!#!Info  Example:       SPHERICAL SHELL UNDER OUTSIDE PRESSURE SECTOR 10 DEG RADIAL Y
!#!Info  Keyword:       tank; rotational symmetry; sherical shell
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$


!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG TEMPLATE urs:6
HEAD Example Description
<TEXT>
Spherical Shell

The ratio of thickness to radius amounts only to 1/1000. Thus the system behaves
essentially as a membrane. Serious disturbances occur at the boundaries.
An effective model is constructed practically with the symmetrical properties of
the structure. Thus it is sufficient to examine a sector of 10 degrees for instance
- see also  -->   nonlinear_quad\concrete_tank_cracked.dat
A refinement at the boundary is suggested due to the disturbances.

Model of the spherical shell:

The inner node has always the constraint ZPMM, since it has no degrees of freedom
except for the displacement in the Z direction. Global conditions can be used
as boundary conditions of the nodes of the first boundary, if the edge is one of the
global coordinate axes. If the coordinate axis, however, is placed along the bisecting
line of the angle, the boundary has to be defined with polar coordinates.
The constraints of the nodes along the boundary can be described with PRMT,
if the horizontal normal of the boundary is selected as direction of the support. The
constraint of the simply supported node, however, requires special considerations.
An additional input of PZ is possible here, but it is not permitted generally
because it may contradict to the coupling condition. It is best therefore to define
the moment boundary condition similarly to the other nodes and subsequently define
a constraint PT (= two directions restrained) in a 90 degrees rotated direction.
The constraints of the nodes of the second boundary can be defined either with
the same method or with symmetric conditions. In the case of a symmetric condition
each node of one boundary has to be coupled with FIX SYM at its partner
node with the same radius at the opposite boundary.
The choice between the various methods is to a certain degree a matter of taste.
Considerations relating to the local coordinate systems may affect the decision
to certain degree.
In the following input the Y axis was placed on the bisecting line of the angle.
</TEXT>
END

+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD SPHERICAL SHELL UNDER OUTSIDE PRESSURE SECTOR 10 DEG RADIAL Y
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
STEE 1 S 235
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD SPHERICAL SHELL UNDER OUTSIDE PRESSURE SECTOR 10 DEG RADIAL Y
$ ASE-Manual, Example 5.2
HEAD REFINEMENT TOWARDS BOUNDARY
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIR NEGZ GDIV 1000
let#w 1.0
NODE    NO   X PHIZ PHIG  FIX    DX     DY
         1  35.  0   180  ZPMM
  ( 3 13 2) 35. 85  (180-4  -4) PRMT   COS(#w) -SIN(#w)
  ( 4 14 2) 35. 95  (180-4  -4) PRMT  -COS(#w) -SIN(#w)
  (15 23 2) 35. 85  (180-25 -1) PRMT   COS(#w) -SIN(#w)
  (16 24 2) 35. 95  (180-25 -1) PRMT  -COS(#w) -SIN(#w)
        25  35. 85   180-30  MT     COS(#w) -SIN(#w)
        25            FIX    PT     SIN(#w)  COS(#w)
        26  35. 95   180-30  MT    -COS(#w) -SIN(#w)
        26            FIX    PT    -SIN(#w)  COS(#w)
GRP 1 titl 'shell'
QUAD 1 1  3  4   T 0.035[m]
loop#1 11
 let#2 #1*2
 QUAD 2+#1 3+#2  5+#2  6+#2  4+#2   T 0.035[m]
endloop
END

PROG SOFILOAD urs:5
HEAD
LC 1 TYPE NONE TITL 'KUGELSCHALE AUSSENDRUCK'
              $ 'SPHERICAL SHELL OUTSIDE PRESSURE'
  QUAD grp 1 TYPE pz 14.5
END

+PROG ASE URS:3
HEAD
LC 1
END

!#!Info  Example:       Single span T-Beam
!#!Info  Keyword:       T-Beam
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
UNIT 0  $ Units in m
CONC 1 C 30      $ C 30  =   C30/37  !
STEE 2 S 500
SREC 1 B 0.30[m] H 0.50[m] HO 0.20[m] BO  2.50[m] MNO 1 $ 2.50 = effective width
END
$ Kindly pay attention to the SOFiSTiK-T-Beam-Philosophy
$ in the ASE Manual theoretical principles
$ and to the examples in folder ase.dat\..\bridge

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD Single span T-Beam ASE manual example 5.3
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000
node no  x   y
    101  0  -2
    102  0   0
    103  0   2
    201  8  -2
    202  8   0
    203  8   2
grp 1
  quad n1 101 102 202 201 t 0.20[m] m 4 n 12
  quad n1 102 103 203 202 t 0.20[m] m 4 n 12
  beam na 102 202 nm fit
boun na 1 titl A
boun na  ne nm=fit type=cz ca=1E6
    101 102
    102 103
    201 202
    202 203
node no  fix
    102  pp
    202  pzpy

$ Group title for WINGRAF:
GRP   1 titl 'Superstructure'

END

+prog sofiload urs:3
head
LC 2 titl 'M-total=3*4m*l^2/8 = 96 kNm'
  quad grp 1 type PG P 3.0
end


!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD
LC 1 FACD 1 $ please check sum of loads =
           $         = 8m*4m*0.20m*25 + 8m*0.30m*(0.50m-0.20)*25 = 178 kN
           $ You see that the double area (beam-flange and slab)
           $ is not applied double in the dead loading FACD 1
           $ You can check this also in WINGRAF
           $ LC 1 beam load = only web-part 0.30m*0.30m*25 = 2.25 kN/m
LC 2
           $ Result WINGRAF M-beam=83.3 kNm, the rest to 96 kNm stays in the outer part
           $ = outside the effective width of the T beam
           $ The reduced beam stiffness itself gets only 64.34 kNm but
           $ the shell bending moment mxx is added in the area of the
           $ effective width: MY-T-beam = 64.01 + 19.29 = 83.3 kNm = WINGRAF-MY !
           $ see ASE-print:
$      STATISTIC BEAM - ADDITIONAL FORCES FROM A SLAB
$      Loadcase    2
$      The printed beam-forces include max. additional forces of a slab:
$        max. beam-force without  slab-addition |   max. slab-addition
$      cnr    bm            N       Vz       My |        N       Vz       My
$            [m]         [kN]     [kN]    [kNm] |     [kN]     [kN]    [kNm]
$         1 2.50 max      0.0    23.59    64.01       0.0     4.95    19.29

END

$ in the ASE Manual theoretical principles
$ and the YOUTUBE Video https://youtu.be/GoT1f0aGdgs   SOFiSTiK T-beam philosophy

+PROG DECREATOR urs:6
HEAD T-Beam Design Sections - integratres forces of beam+quad
ECHO DSLN,FORC,LPLT,SPLT YES
UNIT 5
DSLN NO 1 HDIV 0.5         $Design element with subdivisions
 DGEO BEAM (10001 10012 1) $Selection of sequenced beams
 DSLC MID S 0.0 TYPM SECT  $Design section at mid-span
 DSEL QGRP 1               $Selection of grouped quads
LC 1,2
END

!#!KAPITEL eigenfrequency
+PROG ASE URS:3
HEAD Quick eigenfrequency analysis without further input
MASS 0 $
       $ Deletes possibly the additional masses in the database
EIGE 7
END

+PROG WING URS:4
HEAD
SIZE 4 0 ; STRU 0 0
VIEW ANGL 110 -120 -20
LC 1 ; DEFO YES 1. ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; DEFO NO ; STRU CONT
LC 2 ; DEFO YES 1. ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; DEFO NO ; STRU CONT
LC 3 ; DEFO YES 1. ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; DEFO NO ; STRU CONT
LC 4 ; DEFO YES 1. ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; DEFO NO ; STRU CONT
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:5
HEAD
LC 92 TYPE NONE TITL $ Additional-masses
  QUAD 71 78 1 TYPE pzz P 2.0 $
                              $ 2.0 kN/m2 in front element strips
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:7
HEAD Additional Masses - Input as standard loads
LC 92
$ Attention : Only secondary loads are allowed to be defined in this load case,
$ which subsequently have to be used by a reapplication of the determination of eigen frequency.
$ No dead load factor must be defined because the dead load is automatically activated as mass
$ Besides this, no temperature-, prestress-, or strain loads are to be entered.
$ The elements should not take any prestress from SOFIMSHA otherwise it will produce nodal loads!
$ Loads from SOFILOAD or SOFIPLUS must be analyzed with ASE in advance. Only then
$ they can be used for a mass conversion
$ (because the static ASE run converts element loads into a nodal load/mass vector).
END

+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD Eigenfrequency analysis with additional masses
MASS LC 92 PRZ 100      $ default PRZ = psi2
$ Converts PZ-loads of load case 92 into masses upto 100% (eventually reduces imposed loads)
$ (can be checked with WING by plotting the total nodal loadvector of loadcase 92)
EIGE 7 LC 101
END
$ For a first eigenfrequency check please use Animator.
$
$ Controlling of masses (should be necessarily checked):
$   dead mass of elements(out of first ASE calculation:)  2.222 t
$   sum of loads of LC 92 = 2.32 kN                     = 0.232 t
$                                                       ---------
$   sum of masses for EIGE-LC 101-107                     2.454 t
$                                                       =========
$  SUM OF MASSES
$         TM-X[kg]   TM-Y[kg]   TM-Z[kg] RM-X[kgm2] RM-Y[kgm2] RM-Z[kgm2]
$ total     2454.1     2454.1     2454.1       0.00       0.00       0.00
$
$ For calculation of buckling eigenvalues of a stressed component,
$ kindly see ase9.dat and ase13.dat
$ Cable eigenfrequencies see ase.dat\english\geometric_nonl\cable_eigenfrequencies.dat
$ in time step analysis  see ase.dat\english\dynamics\cable_dynamics.dat
$                        and ase.dat\english\dynamics\whip.dat
$ earthquake analysis see DYNA and ase.dat\english\dynamics\earthquake_jb.dat
$                              and csm.dat\english\csm33_earthquake_bridge.dat


+PROG TEMPLATE -e urs:8
head
sto#lc1 101
sto#neig  7
TXE Modal participation : see DYNA manual  Part "Modal participation factor"
TXE These participation factors are also stored in the database and can be accessed with @key
TXE as follows:
TXE           |  modal part. factor for earthquake |    rotation around system center S |
TXE Loadcase  |        PFX         PFY         PFZ |    phiX[%]     phiY[%]     phiZ[%] |
TXE           | ===================================|====================================|
$ LET#0 2
loop#i0 #neig
  let#lc #lc1+#i0 $ i0 starts with 0-1-2-3-4...
  @KEY LC_CTRL #lc
  STO#PFx @(RX) ! modal part. factor for eq. in X direction
  STO#PFy @(RY) ! modal part. factor for eq. in Y direction
  STO#PFz @(RZ) ! modal part. factor for eq. in Z direction
  STO#RFx 100*@(CRI1) ! rotation around x-axis around S
  STO#RFy 100*@(CRI2) ! rotation around y-axis around S
  STO#RFz 100*@(CRI3) ! rotation around z-axis around S
  TXE #(#lc,8.0)  |#(#PFx,11.3) #(#PFy,11.3) #(#PFz,11.3) |#(#RFx,11.2) #(#RFy,11.2) #(#RFz,11.2) |
endloop
TXE           | ===================================|====================================|
TXE
TXE Sorry, the modal part. factor for earthquake PFX... cannot be printed as
TXE effective modal mass in % because they are stored in a different manner for the push over analysis.
TXE Only the rotational parts are stored as printed in the ASE output and can be printed in % here.
end

!#!Info  Example:       CABLE ELEMENT
!#!Info  Keyword:       cable
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1   C   30      $ C 30  =   C30/37  !
STEE 2   S  500
STEE 3   Y '1860A'          titl 'prestessing steel'
STEE 4   S  '355T' TMAX 0
STEE 8   Y '1860' ES 160000 titl 'cable'
PROF 1 HEA  100    MNO 4
SCIT 2 D 20[mm]    MNO 8 $ tube or cable
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD CABLE ELEMENT - WIND FRAME FROM STAR2 MANUAL
$ ASE-Manual, Example 5.5
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST 2DSS GDIR NEGY GDIV 1000
NODE 1 0 0 fix F ; 2 0 3 ; 3 3 3 ; 4 3 0 fix F
TRUS (1 3 1) (1 1) (2 1) NCS 1 ; CABL 11 1 3 NCS 2 ; CABL 12 2 4 NCS 2
END

PROG SOFILOAD urs:5
HEAD
LC 901 TYPE NONE
  NODE 2 PX 1 $ unit loadcase Px=1
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:3
HEAD Failure at cable 2
SYST - NONL
LC 1 DLY 1 FACT 10.0 titl 'Px 10.0'; LCC 901
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD Smaller load, however, furthe failure at cable 2!!
HEAD Displacements have to be re-initialized at first!!
SYST - NONL PLC 1
LC 2 DLY 1 FACT 9.0 titl 'Px 9.0'; LCC 901
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD Now negative load, cable 2 with a little tensile force
HEAD Failure at cable 1
SYST - NONL PLC 2
LC 3 DLY 1 FACT -1.0 titl 'Px -1.0'; LCC 901
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD Failure with inner cable sag
SYST - TH3
LC 11 DLY 1 FACT 10.0 titl 'Px 10.0 TH3 cable sagging'; LCC 901
END

$ Please compare LC 1 and 11 - having the same load:
$ In LC  1 cable 2 fails due to compression  -> N=0
$ In LC 11 cable 2 gets an inner sag due to gravity load and
$ so generates a normal force N.
$ In geometric analysis TH3 a cable with gravity load will never fail.

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?



!#!Info  Example:       Shell-buckling Silo
!#!Info  Keyword:       inclined position; buckling; Predeformation; imperfection; ultimite load
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$


$ Please also refer to ase13...dat !


!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG TEMPLATE urs:6
HEAD Example Description
<TEXT>
QUADâˆ’Euler Beam

A simple Euler beam fixed at its bottom is used as an example of the analysis
of shells according to secondâˆ’order theory. The geometrically nonâˆ’linear analysis
gets started with CTRL THII.
The small horizontal load at the top is necessary in order to induce an initial horizontal
displacement.

The buckling load according to the theory of elasticity without horizontal load
amounts to 540 kN.

           Pki = Pi^2 * EI / sk^2    (sk=buckling length)
</TEXT>
END


+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD QUAD EULER BEAM
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
STEE 1 S 235 MUE 0.0
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD QUAD EULER BEAM
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000
NODE NO           X        Y    Z
  (1    5    1)  0         0    (0 -1)
  (11  15    1)  0        0.2   (0 -1)
GRP 0
  quad N1   N2   N3   N4  M  N   MNO T=0.1[m]
        1    5   15   11  4  1    1
NODE NO FIX
     1,11 F
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:5
HEAD
LC 901 TYPE NONE TITL 'PZ'
  NODE 5,15 PZ 50
LC 902 TYPE NONE TITL 'PX'
  NODE 5,15 PX 0.01

END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:3
HEAD Condition Load Case for Buckling Mode Shape Determination
LC 100 TITL buckling_eigenvalue_PLC
  LCC 901 $ PZ
END

!#!KAPITEL Buckling eigenvalues
+PROG ASE urs:4

HEAD Buckling Eigenvalues for Stresses of LC 100
SYST PLC 100 FACV 0.0 $
                      $ or   FACV 1.0 if deformations of PLF shall be taken into account!
EIGE 5 BUCK LC 701 LMIN auto   $
                               $ saves the buckling eigenvalues in LC 701-705
END

!#!KAPITEL Ultimate load iteration
+PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD Limit Load Iteration geometrically non-linear
ULTI 30
CTRL BUCK 4 V3 7001 $ Calculate buckling eigenvbalues on last loadlevel and store in LC 7001
SYST PROB TH3
LC  101
  LCC 901 $ PZ
  LCC 902 $ PX
END

+Prog Template urs:9
head Print of last set variables to ULTI
$ - are stored as CADIMP variables in ASE for later usage
$  Usage of ASE_ITER(:)
$  ASE_ITER(0) = first loadcase of ULTI
$  ASE_ITER(1) = last  loadcase of ULTI
$  ASE_ITER(2) = last  load factor
$
$ Usage of  #LAST_LFA and #LAST_LFB  see PROG WING and PROG RESULTS
txb -----------------------------------------
txb Stored variables:
txb -----------------------------------------
let#lc_from #ASE_ITER(0)
let#lc_upto #ASE_ITER(1)
let#lastfact #ASE_ITER(2)
  txb ULTI load factor iteration from loadcase #lc_from up to loadcase #lc_upto last faktor= #(#lastfact,11.6)
STO#LAST_LFA #ASE_ITER(1)   $ -> WING #LAST_LFA
txb -----------------------------------------
END

+PROG ASE URS:22
HEAD with imperfection
OBLI LC 701 VMAX 30[mm] DIRE XX $ imperfection without stresses 30 mm
                               $ scaled at global XX direction
                               $ Multiple OBLI-LC lines are allowed
ULTI 30 FAK1 0.1 DFAK 1.0 FAKE -0.02 $ start at FAC1 0.1 to better recognize predeformation in load-defo plot
SYST PROB TH3 PLC -
LC  301
  LCC 901 $ PZ
END
STO#LAST_LFB #ASE_ITER(1)
END

$ Automatically a deformation curve will be generated in Ursula output.
$
$ A deformation curve can be manually built with DBVIEW
$ Procedure :start DBVIEW.
$ -select (element type) nodal-displacement-UX

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD BRIQ als Luft - volumenkonstante Verformung erzeugt keine Spannung
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
MAT 1 E 0.0006 MUE 0.499999 G 0.0002 K 100 GAM 0.0129 ALFA 1/293/3 TITL Luft
  $ ALFA: bei 293 Grad soll Volumenverdoppelung auftreten,
  $ auf das Volumen bezogener Temp.Ausdehnungskoeffizient daher 1/293
  $ da bei MAT aber die Ausdehnung in einer x-Richtung einzugeben -> 1/293/3 (drei Raumrichtungen) : /3 vgl. LF 11

  $ Anwendung siehe Datei ..\membranes\luftkissen.dat
  $ usage     see   file  ..\membranes\air_cushion.dat

END
END
$  Luft: Gam = 1.29 kg/m3 = 0.0129 kN/m3
$
$  ohne TemperaturerhÃ¶hung gilt: p*v=constant
$   mit p0 = 1 bar = 100 kN/m2 ( 10 m Wasser)
$   und delta-V = 1 % Volumenabnahme folgt
$       delta-p = 1 % von 100 = 1 kN/m2 DruckerhÃ¶hung
$  d.h. Kompressionsmodul K = delta-sigma/delta-eps-V
$                         K = 1/0.01 = 100 kN/m2
$  Die Querdehnzahl sollte eigentlich 0.5 sein.
$  Da 0.5 rechentechnisch nicht zulÃ¤ssig sind wird gewÃ¤hlt:
$  mue=0.499999  (= 0.5-1E-6)
$  und man erhÃ¤lt wegen
$                    E
$          K  =  ---------
$                 3(1-2mue)
$  E = K*(3*(1-2mue)) = 0.0006 KN/m2
$                    E
$          G  =   --------
$                  2(1+m)
$
$  G = E/3            = 0.0002 KN/m2
$
$ Wasser:
$  MATE 1 E 0.0132 MUE 0.499999 G 0.0044 K 2200 GAM 10.0 BEZ Water
$  Kompressionsmodul K = 2.2E8 kN/m2  = 2200 MN/m2
$  Die Querdehnzahl sollte eigentlich 0.5 sein.
$  Da 0.5 rechentechnisch nicht zulÃ¤ssig sind wird gewÃ¤hlt:
$  mue=0.499999  (= 0.5-1E-6)
$  und man erhÃ¤lt wegen
$                    E
$          K  =  ---------
$                 3(1-2mue)
$  E = K*(3*(1-2mue)) = 0.0132 MN/m2
$                    E
$          G  =   --------
$                  2(1+m)
$
$  G = E/3            = 0.0044 MN/m2
$
$      JB 9.8.2018
$

$  Umrechnungsformeln
$
$  In den Stoffgesetzen wird hÃ¤ufig der Kompressionsmodul, der E-Modul und der Steifemodul verwendet. Ein elastischer KÃ¶rper wird jedoch nur durch zwei Parameter beschrieben, so daÃŸ man immer einen Wert durch zwei andere berechnen kann. Im folgenden be
$
$          E     ElastizitÃ¤tsmodul
$          Es    Steifemodul (behinderte Seitendehnung)
$          K     Kompressionsmodul
$          G     Schubmodul
$          m     Querdehnzahl
$
$                    E                      E
$          K  =  ---------        G  =   --------
$                 3(1-2m)                 2(1+m)
$
$                  9Â·KÂ·G                  3K - 2G
$          E  =  ----------       m  =   ----------
$                  3K + G                 6K + 2G
$
$                     1 - m
$          Es  =  E -----------
$                   (1+m)(1-2m)
$
$                  3Â·KÂ·E                  3Â·KÂ·(1-2m)
$          G  =  ---------        G  =   ------------
$                 9Â·K - E                   2Â·(1+m)
$
$
$      JB 31.12.2004
$
+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2

    (11  14 1)  (11 1)  1E12  1E12  1   $ Alle Knoten starr Federgelagert

END

!#!Info Example:    Layered dam, analytical primary state
!#!Info Program:    ASE

+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD 'Material'
MAT   1  E 300000 MUE 0.3 GAM 18.0 GAMA 10.0
NMAT  1  TYPE MOHR  P1 35.0  P2 5.0  P3 0.0  P4 0.0
END

+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:6
HEAD 'Soil body'
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000 POSZ

CTRL MESH 2 ; CTRL HMIN 0.5

$ subsoil:
SPT   101   X   -20.000000 Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT   111   X   -20.000000 Y          0.0 Z         10.0
SPT  1101   X    20.000000 Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT  1111   X    20.000000 Y          0.0 Z         10.0

SLN   1   101   111  $SDIV 0.2 $FIX  PP
SLN   2   111  1111  $SDIV 0.2
SLN   3  1111  1101  $SDIV 0.2 $FIX  PP
SLN   4  1101   101  $SDIV 0.2

SAR   1  GRP 1  MNO 1   MCTL +1  NRA 0  T 0.0  TITL 'Front Surface'
SARB  TYPE OUT NL 1,2,3,4

$ dam:
SPT  2001   X    -6.000000 Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT  2002   X    +6.000000 Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT  2003   X    +2.000000 Y          0.0 Z         -3.0
SPT  2004   X    -2.000000 Y          0.0 Z         -3.0
SPT  3001   X    +4.000000 Y          0.0 Z         -1.5
SPT  3002   X    -4.000000 Y          0.0 Z         -1.5

SLN   11  2001  2002  SDIV 0.2
SLN   12  2002  2003  SDIV 0.2
SLN   13  2003  2004  SDIV 0.2
SLN   14  2004  2001  SDIV 0.2

SLN   21  3001  3002  SDIV 0.2

SAR   2  GRP 2  MNO 1   MCTL +1  NRA 0  T 0.0  TITL 'Layer 1'
SARB  TYPE OUT NL 11,12,21,14

SAR   3  GRP 3  MNO 1   MCTL +1  NRA 0  T 0.0  TITL 'Layer 2'
SARB  TYPE OUT NL 21,12,13,14

END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD 'Extrusion'
UNIT 0 $ m
SYST REST
CTRL REST 2

$ copy temporary layers
GRP 11 TITL 'Back Surface'
QUAD PROP MNO 1 NRA 0  T 0.0
TRAN QUAD GRP 1,2,3 DY 1.0 PROP NEW

$ extrusion
GRP 21 TITL 'Subsoil'
  BRIC PROP MNO 1
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 1 DY 1.0 PROP x2
GRP 22 TITL 'Layer1'
  BRIC PROP MNO 1
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 2 DY 1.0 PROP x2
GRP 23 TITL 'Layer2'
  BRIC PROP MNO 1
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 3 DY 1.0 PROP x2

$ boundary conditions
MOD NODE XMIN -20.0-0.001 XMAX -20.0+0.001  FIX PX
MOD NODE XMIN 20.0-0.001 XMAX 20.0+0.001  FIX PX
MOD NODE YMIN -0.001 YMAX +0.001  FIX PY
MOD NODE YMIN 1.0-0.001 YMAX 1.0+0.001  FIX PY
$MOD NODE ZMIN -0.001 ZMAX +0.001  FIX PZ
MOD NODE ZMIN 10.0-0.001 ZMAX 10.0+0.001  FIX PZ

END



!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST NO
GRP 21 FACD 1.0 FACL 1.0   K 0.6  GAM 18.0  GAMA 10.0  H 0.0
       !                   !--------- parameters of an analytical stress state (-> see manual)
       !-------- the analytical stress state is used as initial stress state and should be
       !         in equilibrium with the actually applied forces (here: gravity load).
       !         check: for perfect equilibrium, the resulting displacements are zero.
LC 1 TITL 'Analytical primary state'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !   URS:3
HEAD
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES PLC 1 FACV 1.0
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST NO
GRP 21 FACD 1.0
GRP 22 FACD 1.0 FACL 1.0  PLC 0  K 0.8  GAM 18.0  GAMA 10.0  H -1.5
                                 !--------- parameters of an analytical stress state
LC 2 TITL 'First Layer'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !   URS:5

ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST NO
GRP 21 FACD 1.0
GRP 22 FACD 1.0
GRP 23 FACD 1.0 FACL 1.0  PLC 0  K 0.8  GAM 18.0  GAMA 10.0  H -3.0
                                 !--------- parameters of an analytical stress state
LC 3 TITL 'Second Layer'
END

!#!Info  Example:       BRIC_BUCL
!#!Info  Keyword:       volume  element, buckling, geometric nonlinear
!#!Info  Program:       ASE




$ To compare with ase12_slab_bucking.dat

$ Siehe auch     ase.dat\..\bric\bric_th2

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM 'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
STEE 1 S 235 ES 210000
END

+prog SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD SLAB BUCKLING
$ German Betonkalendar 1987-I S.435
$ t=1cm a=2.4 b=1.2m E=210000 mue=0.3
$ p-krit= 527 KN/m Uniaxial pressure
$ To compare with ase12_slab_bucking.dat
SYST SPAC GDIV  10000

let#L  2.4  $ length of body
let#W  1.2  $ width of body
let#H  0.01 $ height of body

NODE 1 X  0  0 0
     2 X #L  0 0
     3 X #L #W 0
     4 X  0 #W 0
    11 X  0  0 #H
    12 X #L  0 #H
    13 X #L #W #H
    14 X  0 #W #H
NODE 9 X #L/4 #W/2 0 $ Check point

GRP 1 ; BRIC   -  1 2 3 4 11 12 13 14  MNO 1 M 24 N 12 K 1
GRP 2 ; QUAD   -  1 4 14 11 MNO 1 NRA 0 T 0 M 12 N 1 $ Load surface
GRP 3 ; QUAD   -  2 3 13 12 MNO 1 NRA 0 T 0 M 12 N 1 $ Load surface

$ Only lower nodes are supported:
let#x   0 ; SBOX A1X #x-0.01 0 0  #x+0.01 0 0  A2X 0 -1 0   0 10 0 A3X 0 0 0.009  0 0 0.011 OPT AND
NODE SBOX FIX pz
let#x 2.4 ; SBOX A1X #x-0.01 0 0  #x+0.01 0 0  A2X 0 -1 0   0 10 0 A3X 0 0 0.009  0 0 0.011 OPT AND
NODE SBOX FIX pxpz

let#y   0 ; SBOX A1X -1 0 0   10 0 0  A2X 0 #y-0.01 0  0 #y+0.01 0 A3X 0 0 0.009  0 0 0.011 OPT AND
NODE SBOX FIX pz
let#y 1.2 ; SBOX A1X -1 0 0   10 0 0  A2X 0 #y-0.01 0  0 #y+0.01 0 A3X 0 0 0.009  0 0 0.011 OPT AND
NODE SBOX FIX pypz
END

!#!Info  Example:       BRIC concrete law with explicit rebar beams
!#!Info  Keyword:       material nonlinear; concrete law; cracked stiffness; reduction of stiffness; crack; volume; BRIC
!#!Info  Program:       ASE

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
NORM 'NF' NDC 'en199X-200X'
echo mat,sect full

CONC 1 C   30  $ here unused, therefore material 9 is used for brics!
STEE 3 S  500

$ Here material LADE for cracked bric concrete  TCM    Triple_Crack_Model   see also example   bric_smeared_cracked_girder.dat
MATE  9 E 33000 MUE 0.2 TITL 'LADE C30 SLS fcm 38 fctk 2.03'
NMAT  9 'LADE' P1    89855E3 P2 2.0 P3 2028 P4 50 P6 0.2 $ P3=tensile strength
$     The yielding curve is plotted in ASE in the material output!
$     If you change P3 you also must adapt P1 to get the same uniaxial strength!
$     So best change P3 and look to the Ursula plot, then change P1 - and so on!

$     P1 opening angle and together with P3 the strength
$     P2 curvature in direction of the hydrostatic axis - see  bric_compression_softening.dat
$     P3 tensile strength in kN/m2
$     P4 dilatanz (plastic potential)
$          default is P4=P1/10 or P4=500
$     P5 = max. hydrostatic compression
$          e.g. max. hydrostatic compression = 45.0 N/mm2 ->input P5= 45000
$          It is recommended not to input P5 as concrete can carry very high hydrostatic compression
$     P6 = eps-zu = length of decreasing tensile strength in o/oo (see. ASE CTRL CONC for quads)
$          The length of decreasing tensile strength can also be input in ASE with CTRL CONC!
$
$ Parameter for other strength in SLS:
$ The ASE strength fcm is the stress that the material can carry in ASE
$          for a uniaxial loading - see ASE-material plots!
$ As tensile strength here the lower 5 % fractile value is used - fctk = 0.7*fctm with:
$                 fctm = 0.30 fck^(2/3)          bis C50
$                 fctm = 2.12 ln[1 + (fcm / 10)] ab  C50
$          as on SLS for this tensile stress a cracking must be assumed.
$

$ GZT: Im Grenzzustand der TragfÃ¤higkeit darf der Beton eigentlich keinen Zug mehr aufnehmen.
$      Da er dann aber auch keine KohÃ¤sion mehr hat wÃ¼rde er sich wie Sand verhalten und
$      bei kleinster Belastung 'zerbrÃ¶seln'.
$
$      Der Zug kÃ¶nnte dann mit einer verschmierten Bewehrung (siehe Beispiel bric_smeared_cracked_girder.dat)
$      aufgenommen werden.
$      Mit der hier verwendeten Bewehrung aus Stabelementen wÃ¼rde der Beton aber immer versagen, vor allem
$      im Bereich der Ã¤uÃŸeren Betondeckung. Denn wenn keine Spaltzugspannungen aufgenommen weren kÃ¶nnen
$      kann der Beton auch keine Kraft an die Bewehrung weiterleiten (wie ein Stab in Sand).
$      Es wird daher eine geringere Betonzugfestigkeit angesetzt und zwar 0.5*fctk.

$      fc  = Festigkeitsklasse

$      Betonzugfestigkeit = 0.5*fctk mit fctk= 0.7*fctm

!#!Info  Example:       3D-reference temperature

                      $ Heat conductivity concrete in [W/m*K]

                      $ Bulk density concrete in [kg/mÂ³]

                      $ Loft coefficient concrete = c*rho
HMAT 1 KXX #lambda S #S     $ temp. material  values concrete
STEE 2 S 500
SREC 1 1[m] 1[m] MNO 1 MRF 0 REF UM
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:5
HEAD $ Manual input
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LC 5
  BRIC GRP 0 TYPE DT P 0 Z 0 DPZ 10
             BEAM GRP 5 TYPE DTZ 10
             BEAM GRP 5 TYPE DT   5
LC 6
  BRIC GRP 0 TYPE DT P 0 Z 2 DPZ 10
             BEAM GRP 5 TYPE DTZ 10
             BEAM GRP 5 TYPE DT   5-20
LC 7
  BRIC GRP 0 TYPE DT P 0 Z 4 DPZ 10
             BEAM GRP 5 TYPE DTZ 10
             BEAM GRP 5 TYPE DT   5-40

LC 901 TYPE NONE TITL 'Compare as BEAM'
        BEAM grp 5 TYPE dtz 10
        BEAM grp 5 TYPE dt   5
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+prog ase urs:7
head
LC 1 dlz 1
lc 5,6,7
end


+PROG HYDRA URS:3
HEAD Initial temperature
#define HYDRA_control
LET#alfa     13       $
                      $ Temperature transfer condition = 1./0.04 (alfa-a, by Wind > 2m/s) ... 1/0.13 (alfa-i, without Wind)
LET#eps      0.9      $
                      $ Emission boundary condition (emission), greater at lighter concrete as at darker
LET#temp     0        $
                      $ Average initial temperature complete system
LET#anzTage  4        $
                      $ no. of days, till the temperature behaviour is been leveled

SYST DIMT H DIMQ W ; ECHO POT
#enddef
#include HYDRA_control
sto#teil 1
PLC T 0 HP #temp
LC 101 TITL 'lf 0'
  BOUN H  0 FROM 1 #teil*100+21 1 $ below 0
  $ SURF input see bric_hydra_dt2h_petra.dat
END

+PROG HYDRA URS:4
HEAD
#include HYDRA_control
PLC 10 T CONT
STEP 10 100
LC 102 TITL 'lf 0-10'
  BOUN H  0 FROM            1            #teil*100+21 1 $ below 0
  BOUN H 10 FROM #teil*1000+1 #teil*1000+#teil*100+21 1 $ above 10
  $ SURF input see bric_hydra_dt2h_petra.dat
  $ Only with LC 101 without STEP see bric_hydra_dt2h_petra.dat
END

+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD
LC 4 TITL ''
  TEMP 102 T1 0 T2 10*100*3600 NOG 0 EMOD OFF    $
                                                $ min. max. temperature (size of time step in sek.)
  LCC 901
END

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?


!#!Info  Example:       3D-reference temperature
!#!Info  Keyword:       heat conductivity; temperature; PETRA; Tetraeder
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
UNIT 5
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1 C  30
LET#lambda   2.1      $
                      $ Heat conductivity concrete in [W/m*K]
LET#c        1050     $
                      $ Calorific capacity concrete in [J/kg*K]
LET#rho      2400     $
                      $ Bulk density concrete in [kg/mÂ³]
LET#S        #c*#rho  $
                      $ Loft coefficient concrete = c*rho
HMAT 1 KXX #lambda S #S     $ temp. material  values concrete
STEE 2 S 500
END

+prog sofimshc urs:3
HEAD 3D-reference temperature
SYST SPAC GDIV  10000 gdir negz
CTRL MESH 3+32  $ create volume mesh
sto#HMIN  1.10
CTRL HMIN #HMIN $ mesh density    5.0[m] = super grosse Elem.

sto#L  10.0  $ length of body  wie ASE 9
sto#W  1.00  $ width of body
let#H  1.00  $ height of body

SPT 1 X  0  0 0  fix pz
    2 X #L  0 0  fix pz
    3 X #L #W 0  fix pzpy
    4 X  0 #W 0  fix pp
   11 X  0  0 #H
   12 X #L  0 #H
   13 X #L #W #H
   14 X  0 #W #H

let#nr 100 ; let#dy #w*5
SPT 1+#nr X  0  0+#dy 0
    2+#nr X #L  0+#dy 0
    3+#nr X #L #W+#dy 0
    4+#nr X  0 #W+#dy 0
   11+#nr X  0  0+#dy #H
   12+#nr X #L  0+#dy #H
   13+#nr X #L #W+#dy #H
   14+#nr X  0 #W+#dy #H

$ lines defining the body
SLN 1,2,3,4 NPA 1,2,3,4 NPE 2,3,4,1
SLN 11,13 NPA 11,13 NPE 12,14
SLN 12,14 NPA 12,14 NPE 13,11
SLN 21,22,23,24 NPA 1,2,3,4 NPE 11,12,13,14

$ structural areas
SAR  1 GRP 1 nra 0 t  0.0[mm] mno  -  ; SARB OUT 1,2,3,4     $ must be nra 0 for HYDRA !
SAR  2 GRP 2 nra 0 t  0.0[mm] mno  -  ; SARB OUT 1,11,21,22  $ otherwisse wrong result in HYDRA
SAR  3 GRP 3 nra 0 t  0.0[mm] mno  -  ; SARB OUT 2,12,22,23
SAR  4 GRP 4 nra 0 t  0.0[mm] mno  -  ; SARB OUT 3,13,23,24
SAR  5 GRP 5 nra 0 t  0.0[mm] mno  -  ; SARB OUT 4,14,24,21
SAR  6 GRP 6 nra 0 t  0.0[mm] mno  -  ; SARB OUT 11,12,13,14

$ structural volume
SVO 1 GRP 1 MNO 1
SVOS 1,2,3,4,5,6

END

+PROG HYDRA URS:2
HEAD Initial temperature
#define HYDRA_control
LET#alfa     13       $
                      $ Temperature transfer condition = 1./0.04 (alfa-a, by Wind > 2m/s) ... 1/0.13 (alfa-i, without Wind)
LET#eps      0.9      $
                      $ Emission boundary condition (emission), greater at lighter concrete as at darker
LET#temp     0        $
                      $ Average initial temperature complete system
LET#anzTage  4        $
                      $ no. of days, till the temperature behaviour is been leveled

SYST DIMT H DIMQ W ; ECHO POT
#enddef
#include HYDRA_control
sto#teil 1

LC 101 TITL 'lf 0'
  SURF TYPE SPEC VAL 100000 from 10000 to 19999 VP 0
  SURF TYPE SPEC VAL 100000 from 60000 to 69999 VP 10.0
$ For SURF, surface quads must be input with nra 0 , otherwisse wrong result in HYDRA
END

  TEMP 101

!#!KAPITEL Smeared reinforcement in cracked concrete TCM Triple_Crack_Model
+PROG BEMESS urs:9
HEAD Definition of reinforcement parameters and minimum reinforcement

$ Circular reinforcement see example  volume_meshing_video.dat
$
$ Calcutation of the smeared reinforcement in Brics:
$ for example group 48 = midspan bottom bric layer (thickness= height= 0.14m):
$ In this area 7 bars with diameter 28 exist = AS = 43.05 cm2
$    in an area of 0.80m*0.14m=0.112m2   -> ASO  = AS/0.112m2 = 402.2 cm2/m2
$
$ top  normal nur 7 diameter 20 = 21.98 cm2    ASO  = AS/0.112m2 = 196.2 cm2/m2
$ topmid support 12 diameter 28 = 73.89 cm2    ASO  = AS/0.112m2 = 659.7 cm2/m2
$
$ stirrups diameter 20 alle 15 = as=20.93cm2/m    ASO3 = as/0.14m   = 148.5 cm2/m2
$ stirrups midspan  20 alle 30 = as=10.46cm2/m    ASO3 = as/0.14m   =  74.3 cm2/m2
$ x-bars outside    10 alle 30 = as= 2.61cm2/m    ASO3 = as/0.14m   =  18.7 cm2/m2
$ final disc        20 alle 15 = as=20.93cm2/m    ASO3 = as/0.14m   = 148.5 cm2/m2

DI3D 0[Â°] 0[Â°]  $ = BRIC input in rad , for 10 degree please input 10*3.14/180 or 10[Â°]
$ default
PARA NOG     -    DU 20[mm] 20[mm] 20[mm] ASU  10   ASU2  10    ASU3  10
$ Endscheibe
PARA NOG 11,12,13 DU 28[mm] 20[mm] 20[mm] ASU 196.2 ASU2 148.5  ASU3 148.5
PARA NOG 14,15,16 DU 20[mm] 20[mm] 20[mm] ASU 148.5 ASU2 148.5  ASU3 148.5
PARA NOG 17,18,19 DU 28[mm] 20[mm] 20[mm] ASU 402.2 ASU2 148.5  ASU3 148.5

    Creates a .cdb with the yield surface for animation of the yield surface

 - results - volume elements - nonlinear results - plasticity : positive if yield surface triggered
 - results - volume elements - nonlinear results - tension damage : strain after fctk peak
 - design - volume elements - nonlinear results - reinforcement stress, max-min concrete stress

!#!Info Example:    Uniaxial tensile test for a hardening steel material (tri-linear work law)
!#!Info Program:    ASE
!#!Info Keywords:   Nonlinear static Analysis, 3D continuum elements


!#!Chapter System, materials and loading

$
$ parameters for system
$
#define LENGTH=1.00

$
$ parameters for plots
$
#define LC0_1=1       $ first load case of 1st lc sequence
#define EPSMAX=120    $ maximum range x, strain [0/00] (displacement [mm])
#define SIGMAX=400    $ maximum range y, stress [MPa]

+PROG TEMPLATE urs:11
HEAD
<TEXT>

The numerical softening response should match the analytical curve.

Bar length [m]: $(LENGTH)
</TEXT>
END


+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Structural Steel
$ NORM DIN EN199x-200x
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
ECHO MAT EXTR

STO#AC 0.1*0.1 $[m2]

$ steel -------------------------------------

STO#Es    210000  ! [MPa]
STO#fy     235  ! [MPa]
STO#ft     360  ! [MPa]
STO#epst   100  ! [0/00]
STO#epsy #fy/#Es*1000 ! [0/00]
STO#Et   (#ft-#fy)/(#epst-#epsy)*1000 ! [Mpa] hardening modulus

STEE 1 S 235 ES #Es
!*!Label Explicit definition of work law (serviceability)
SSLA 'SERV'  1.0
SSLA EPS               SIG
             -1000    -#ft
              -100    -#ft
          -(#epsy)    -#fy
                 0       0
          +(#epsy)    +#fy
              +100    +#ft
             +1000    +#ft

! for comparison (bilinear):
!MATE 1 E #Es
!NMAT 1 type vmis p1 #fy*1000  p2 #Et*1000

END


+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:6
HEAD STEEL BAR
UNIT 0 ;
SYST 3D GDIV -1000 GDIR NEGZ
STO#L $(LENGTH)

CTRL MESH 2 ; CTRL HMIN 0.5

SPT   101   X          0.0 Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT   111   X          0.0 Y          0.0 Z          0.1
SPT  1101   X           #L Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT  1111   X           #L Y          0.0 Z          0.1
SPT   201   X          0.0 Y          0.1 Z          0.0
SPT   211   X          0.0 Y          0.1 Z          0.1
SPT  1201   X           #L Y          0.1 Z          0.0
SPT  1211   X           #L Y          0.1 Z          0.1

SLN   1   101   111  !SDIV 0.2 $FIX  PP
SLN   2   111  1111  !SDIV 0.2
SLN   3  1111  1101  !SDIV 0.2 $FIX  PP
SLN   4  1101   101  !SDIV 0.2

SAR   1  GRP 1  MNO 1   MCTL +1  NRA 0  T 0.0  TITL 'Front Surface'
SARB  TYPE OUT NL 1,2,3,4

END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:17
HEAD  EXTRUSION
SYST REST
CTRL REST 2
UNIT 0
$ Hilfsebenen kopieren
GRP 2 TITL 'Back Surface'
QUAD PROP MNO 1 NRA 0  T 0.0
TRAN QUAD GRP 1 DY 0.1 PROP NEW

$ Extrusion
GRP 10 TITL 'Volume Body'
  BRIC PROP MNO 1
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 1 DY 0.1 PROP x1

$ Randbedingungen
MOD NODE XMIN -0.001 XMAX +0.001  FIX PX
!MOD KNOT XMIN 10-0.001 XMAX 10+0.001  FIX PXPYPZ
NODE 101,201 FIX PZ
NODE 101,111 FIX PY

$ delete temporary QUADs
DEL QUAD INC GRP FROM 1,2
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3

  NODE 1101,1111,1201,1211  TYPE WXX  P1 1[mm]    ! corresponds to 1.0[0/00] tensile strain
END


!#!Chapter Simulation of tensile loading response

+PROG ASE urs:2
LET#EPS1 1.0 ! strain (increment) of first load step
LET#NSTEPS 15  !119
let#EPSINC ($(EPSMAX)-#EPS1)/#NSTEPS

HEAD
!*!Label choose serviceability level for work law(s):
NSTR KSV SL

SYST PROB NONL  NMAT YES
LC 1
LCC 1001 FACT #EPS1
END

LOOP#i #NSTEPS !$(EPSMAX)-1
  HEAD
!*!Label choose serviceability level for work law(s):
  NSTR KSV SL

  SYST PROB NONL PLC 1+#i  NMAT YES
  LC 2+#i
  LCC 1001 FACT #EPS1+((#i+1)*#EPSINC)
  END
ENDLOOP

END


!#!Chapter Plot loading response

#define draw_xyCurve

$PROG WING
$ draw curve

    LET#13 (#(Y+0))*#yscal
    LET#14 (#(X+0))*#xscal
    MOVE X #1+2.0+#14      Y #2+2.0+#13         UNIT CM SCHH 0.1; $TEXT ux=#10/sx=#12

    LOOP#9 #npts-1
       LET#13 (#(Y+#9+1))*#yscal
       LET#14 (#(X+#9+1))*#xscal
       DRAW X #1+2.0+#14      Y #2+2.0+#13         UNIT CM C #lineStyle
       MOVE X #1+2.0+#14      Y #2+2.0+#13         UNIT CM SCHH 0.1; $TEXT ux=#10/sx=#12

       if (#markerStyle==1)
                $ mark (cross)
          MOVE X #1+2.0+#14-0.03  Y  #2+2.0+#13        UNIT CM
          DRAW X #1+2.0+#14+0.03  Y  #2+2.0+#13        UNIT CM C #lineStyle
          MOVE X #1+2.0+#14      Y  #2+2.0+#13-0.03    UNIT CM
          DRAW X #1+2.0+#14      Y  #2+2.0+#13+0.03    UNIT CM
                $ go back to intersection point
          MOVE X #1+2.0+#14      Y  #2+2.0+#13         UNIT CM
       endif
    ENDLOOP

   if (#includeOrigin==1)
       $ jump to starting point
       MOVE X #1+2 Y #2+2 UNIT CM
       LET#13 (#(Y+0))*#yscal
       LET#14 (#(X+0))*#xscal
       DRAW X #1+2.0+#14      Y #2+2.0+#13         UNIT CM C #lineStyle
   endif

#enddef

        $ grid lines

    MOVE X #1     Y #2+2     UNIT CM; DRAW #1+22   #2+2  UNIT CM
    MOVE X #1     Y #2+4     UNIT CM; DRAW #1+22   #2+4  UNIT CM

    DRAW X #1+2+0.2   Y #2+10-.5 UNIT CM C 1101  $ continous, schwarz
    MOVE X #1+2       Y #2+10    UNIT CM
    DRAW X #1+2-.2    Y #2+10-.5 UNIT CM

$ ################################################

$    numerical response

$ ################################################

   // determine the number of load cases to depict
   LET#lc0 $(LC0_1)  // first load case to depict
   LOOP#9
      LET#CDB_IER 0
      LET#lc #lc0+#9
      @KEY LC_CTRL #lc
   ENDLOOP #CDB_IER==0
   LET#nlc (#lc-#lc0) // the last lc read did not exist, therefore skip +1

   $ read data:
   LOOP#9 #nlc
      @KEY N_DISP (#lc0+#9) 1101              $ cdb record (nodal disp), load case, node number
      LET#X(#9) @(1)*1000/#L                   $ eps_x [0/00]
      @KEY BRIC_STR (#9+#lc0)  3001            $ cdb record (element results), load case, element number
      LET#Y(#9) @(1)/1000                      $ sigx [MPa]
   ENDLOOP

$ draw curve:
let#lineStyle 4301 $ blue
let#includeOrigin 1
let#markerStyle 1
let#npts #nlc
#include draw_xyCurve



$ ################################################

$    theoretical curve (worklaw)

$ ################################################

   LET#npts 100
   LET#epsmin 0.0
   LET#epsmax #X(#nlc-1)
   LET#epsinc (#epsmax-#epsmin)/(#npts-1) !  #nlc

   LET#epsy #fy/#Es
   LET#Et (#ft-#fy)/(#epst-#epsy)
   LET#getsig_lin '=FUN(eps,#Es*#eps)'
   LET#getsig_hard '=FUN(eps,#fy+#Et*(abs(#eps)-#epsy))'
   LET#getsig_ult '=FUN(eps,#ft)'

   LET#getsig_trilin '=FUN(eps,#Es*#eps)'
   $PRT#wmin ; PRT#wmax ; PRT#winsc
   LOOP#9 #npts
      LET#eps #epsinc*#9
      if (abs(#eps)<=#epsy)
         let#sig #getsig_lin(#eps)
      elseif (abs(#eps)<=#epst)
         let#sig #getsig_hard(#eps)
      else
         let#sig #getsig_ult(#eps)
      endif
      LET#Y(#9) #sig
      LET#X(#9) #eps
   ENDLOOP

$ draw curve:
let#lineStyle 13204 $ dark blue
let#includeOrigin 0
let#markerStyle 0
#include draw_xyCurve


$ something must produce a new page...
STRU NUME NO

END

<TEXT> Variants:
BRIC elements with effects theory 3. order (cable effect, buckling)
  best with load increase via PLC - see LC 1-2-3-4-5

BRIC elements with effects theory 2. order (towers, columns)
  best with TH2 without PLC - sss LC 20

Variant for big systems with SFIX:
  In big systems also the computation optimized SFIX technique is possible:
  Using the stesses of a linear PLC a geometric stiffness can be used with SFIX PLF
  This gives TH2 results in one step (also for a set of load combinations).
  Can be used if the normal force does not change much
  (on cable effect or in buckling the normal forces change extremely)
</TEXT>

!#!KAPITEL ERWAERMUNG DURCH HYDRATATION mit WÃ¤rmeverlust an die Luft

$ ZunÃ¤chst wird in einem HYDRA-Lauf der gesamte Zeitablauf gerechnet
$ um in DYNR die Temperaturen einfach in einem LF 901 darstellen zu kÃ¶nnen:
+PROG HYDRA URS:3
HEAD INSTATIONAERE ERWAERMUNG DURCH HYDRATATION in einem LF 901 fuer DYNR
$ Head UNSTEADY HEATING BY HYDRATION IN LC 901 FOR DYNR
SYST DIMT H DIMQ W
LC  901
STEP N 300 T 1  $  300 * 1 Stunde $ 1hrs.
PLC HP 15 $ Starttemperatur $ start temperature
   $ Die Energieentwicklung wird in AQUA definiert !
#define hyd
CTRL TEFF 1
SURF TYPE SPEC VAL  50 FROM GRP 10 VP 10 $ 10 Grad Aussentemp. $ 10 degree outside temp.
$ surface quads must be input with nra 0 , otherwisse wrong result in HYDRA
HIST FROM 25,43,#node1
END
#enddef
#include hyd
END

+PROG DYNR URS:9
HEAD Zeitverlauf Gesamt
$ Head Time elapsed total
ECHO FULL
HIST 901 T NO1 25 1002 NO2 43 1004 NO3 #node1 1101  ymin 0 ymax 80
END

!#!KAPITEL ErwÃ¤rmung in Lastfallschritten fÃ¼r ASE

$ Jetzt Berechnung in EinzellastfÃ¤llen, damit HYDRA die Reifegrade je Lastfall
$ 1,2,3,4 abspeichert:
$ Now analysis in single load cases,so that the HYDRA saves ripeness degree per load case
$ 1,2,3,4:
$ LF 1 Reifegrad nach 20 Stunde
$ LF 1 Ripeness degree after 20 hrs.
$ LF 2 Reifegrad nach 40 Stunde
$ LF 2 Ripeness degree after 40 hrs.
$ LF 3 Reifegrad nach 60 Stunde
$ LF 3 Ripeness degree after 60 hrs.
$ LF 4 Reifegrad nach 80 Stunde
$ LF 4 Ripeness degree after 80 hrs.
$    ...              ...

+PROG HYDRA URS:6
HEAD INSTATIONAERE ERWAERMUNG DURCH HYDRATATION LF 1
$ HEAD UNSTEADY HEATING BY HYDRATION LC 1
SYST DIMT H DIMQ W ; ECHO STEP 1 ; ECHO POT NO
                   $ ECHO STEP 1   ist im ersten Schritt unbedingt erforderlich,
                   $ damit HYDRA die Temperaturen der Zwischenschritte abspeichert!!
                   $ Sonst kann ASE z.B. die 16-Stunden Temperatur nicht abgreifen!!
                   $ Necessary in first step,
                   $ so that HYDRA saves the temperature of intermediate step!!
                   $ otherwise ASE cannot grip e. g. the 16 hrs temperature.
LC  1
STO#T0 3 $ Zeitintervall fÃ¼r LastfÃ¤lle InstationÃ¤re ErwÃ¤rmung aus Hydratation
LET#T1 2 $ Unterteilung Stundenintervall DT = 1/#T2 bei T2=2 = 30 min, bei T2=3 = 20 min
STEP N #T0*#T1 T 1/#T1 $ maximal Stundenschritte (#T1=1)
PLC HP 15 $ Starttemperatur $ start temperature
#include hyd
END

+PROG HYDRA URS:7
HEAD INSTATIONAERE ERWAERMUNG DURCH HYDRATATION LF 2-15
$ HEAD UNSTEADY HEATING BY HYDRATION LC 2-15
let#plf 1
loop 14
  SYST DIMT H DIMQ W ; ECHO STEP 1 ; ECHO POT NO
  LC  #plf+1
  LET#T1 2
  STEP N #T0*#T1 T 1/#T1 $ jeweils plus 3*2=6 Zeitschritte a 30 min ergibt 3h
  PLC #plf CONT
#include hyd
  let#plf #plf+1
endloop
END

+PROG ASE URS:5

+PROG ASE URS:15

  SYST PLC #plf ; GRP 0,1 ; GRP2 - ALP0 0.125
  LC       #plf+1 TITL $(BEZ); TEMP #lftemp T1 #stunden*3600 T2 (#stunden+#delta)*3600 EMOD OFF
  let#plf #plf+1
  let#lftemp #lftemp+1
  let#stunden #stunden+#delta
  END
endloop
END

$ --------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ ---------------------- LF 301-315: ------------------------------------------
$  Reifegrad-abhÃ¤ngiger E-Modul nach Technischen Empfehlungen Bautechnick BAW / Wesche
$  EMOD 2.84
$
$  nach Technischen Empfehlungen Bautechnick BAW / Wesche
$  Mit der Eingabe TEMP...EMOD=Wert wird die Entwicklung des E-Moduls nach Wesche aktiviert. Als Wert
$  ist c1*w/z einzugeben [fÃ¼r Z25 z.B. Wert=7.1*0.4 = 2.84]. :
$  fbeta=e^(-c1*w/z*(te^-0.55 - 28^-0.55))
$  fE=fbeta^1/3
$  E=fE*E28
$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ ---------------------- LC 301-315: ------------------------------------------
$  Ripeness degree-dependant on E-Modul to technical recommendation of Bautechnick BAW / Wesche
$  EMOD 2.84
$
$  according to technical recommendation of Bautechnick BAW / Wesche
$  With the input of TEMP...EMOD=Value E-Modul's development will be activated according to Wesche. As value
$  add c1*w/z  [for Z25 e. g. Value=7.1*0.4 = 2.84]. :
$  fbeta=e^(-c1*w/z*(te^-0.55 - 28^-0.55))
$  fE=fbeta^1/3
$  E=fE*E28
$---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#define BEZ = 'Wesche/BAW'

END

  let#plf #plf+1
  let#lftemp #lftemp+1
  let#stunden #stunden+#delta
  END
endloop
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA -R urs:3
HEAD Video Volume Meshing

NODE 1 X 0 0  2.00

                                         129  1.900 2.00 $

     101  6.000 0    ; 111  2.300 0    ; 121  1.800 0    ; 131  1.500 0    $
$    ======================================================================$
sto#div 36  $ division in circular direction
$
loop#i0 #div    $ variable loops from 0-1-2-3...7   for #div=8
  let#i1 #i0+1  $ variable loops from 1-2-3-4...8   for #div=8
  TRAN NODE FROM 101 TO 199 DNO #i1*100 phiz #i1*360/#div
endloop

GRP 99 titl 'Test node coordinates'
loop#i0 #div
  let#i1 #i0+1
 $ spri NA #i1*100+1  dz 1 cp 1E6
 $ spri NA #i1*100+31 dz 1 cp 1E6
endloop

loop#i0 #div    $ variable loops from 0-1-2-3...7   for #div=8
  let#i1 #i0+1  $ variable loops from 1-2-3-4...8   for #div=8
  let#plane1 100*#i1            $ plane1 = hundred number of first node plane
  let#plane2 #plane1+100        $ plane2 = hundred number of    2. node plane
  if #i1==#div
         let#plane2 100         $ last bric uses nodeplane 800---100
  endif
  GRP 1 titl 'concrete'
  let#L1 #plane1 ; let#L2 #plane2  $ to have shorter characters
                                BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    M 5 N 2 K 1 MNO 9
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
   $
  let#L1 #plane1+10 ; let#L2 #plane2+10
                                BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    M 2 N 2 K 1 MNO 9
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
$
  let#L1 #plane1+20 ; let#L2 #plane2+20
                                BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
  let#L1 #L1+1 ; let#L2 #L2+1 ; BRIC N1 #L1+1  #L1+11  #L1+12  #L1+2  N5 #L2+1  #L2+11  #L2+12  #L2+2    ==
endloop

$ other elements
loop#i0 #div
  let#i1 #i0+1
  let#plane1 100*#i1            $ plane1 = hundred number of first node plane
  let#plane2 #plane1+100        $ plane2 = hundred number of    2. node plane
  if #i1==#div ; let#plane2 100 ; endif

  GRP 2 titl 'tower'
    QUAD N1 #plane1+28  #plane1+29  #plane2+29  #plane2+28   t 20[mm] M 2 N 1 MNO 3

  GRP 3 titl 'bolt plate'
    QUAD N1 #plane1+27  #plane1+26  #plane2+26  #plane2+27   t 50[mm] M 1 N 1 MNO 3
    QUAD N1 #plane1+26  #plane1+28  #plane2+28  #plane2+26   t 50[mm] M 1 N 1 MNO 3

  GRP 4 titl 'contact springs'
    SPRI NA #plane1+26  #plane1+25  cp 1E6 ct 1E5 CRAC 0

  if MOD(#i1,2)==0    $ only every second node plane:
    GRP 5 titl 'bolts'
      TRUS NA #plane1+26  #plane1+22 NCS 5
  endif

  GRP 7 titl 'bedding quads'
    let#L1 #plane1 ; let#L2 #plane2  $ to have shorter characters
    QUAD N1 #L1+1  N4 #L1+11 N3  #L2+11 N2  #L2+1  T 0 M 1 N 5 c 2E5 ct 1E5
    QUAD N1 #L1+11 N4 #L1+21 N3  #L2+21 N2  #L2+11 T 0 M 1 N 2 c 2E5 ct 1E5
    QUAD N1 #L1+21 N4 #L1+31 N3  #L2+31 N2  #L2+21 T 0 M 1 N 2 c 2E5 ct 1E5
    $ N1-N4-N3-N2 to point local z downwards for nonlinear lifting of bedding

  GRP 8 titl 'stiffening plate'
    TRUS NA #plane1+27  #plane1+29 NCS 8 $ to avoid big rotation of the steel plate

  GRP 9 titl 'coupling to node 1'
    NODE #plane1+29 fix KF 1
endloop
END

!#!KAPITEL Smeared reinforcement in cracked concrete TCM Triple_Crack_Model
+PROG BEMESS urs:13
HEAD Parameters Circular reinforcement
DI3D 0 0  X 0 Y 0 $ BRIC
PARA NOG - DU 20[mm] ASU 100 200 50
END

$  MÃ¶gliche Definitionen:
$  RI3D 0 0
$      1. Bewehrungsrichtung = global-X   2.=global-Y   3.=global-Z
$  RI3D OAL...OAF... ohne Eingabe zu einem Mittelpunkt:
$      Erst Drehung OAL um global-Z
$      dann Drehung um neue 1. Bewehrungsrichtung
$  RI3D mit Eingabe zu einem Mittelpunkt:
$      X und Y sind zusÃ¤tzlich mit OAL+OAF erlaubt.
$      Eingabe Z nur zulÃ¤ssig mit OAL=OAF=0
$
$      Kreisbewehrung um X,Y (ohne Z Eingabe):
$      Standard Fall mit OAL=OAF=0:
$        z.B. Windanlage-Kreisfundament oder BehÃ¤lter:
$        RI3D OAL 0 OAF 0  X 0  Y 0
$           1. Bewehrung = radial
$           2. Bewehrung = tangential
$           3. Bewehrung = global z
$      Spezialfall mit OAL+OAF:
$        ZusÃ¤tzliche Drehung OAL um global-Z
$        dann Drehung um neue 1. Bewehrungsrichtung
$        z.B. Kegel (KlÃ¤rbecken) mit 30 Grad GefÃ¤lle:
$        RI3D OAL 90 OAF 30  X 0  Y 0
$
$      Sonderfall Eingabe Z: nur zulÃ¤ssig mit OAL=OAF=0:
$      Eingabe Y,Z ohne X: Rotationsachse = X um Punkt Y,Z
$      Eingabe X,Z ohne Y: Rotationsachse = Y um Punkt X,Z

+PROG ASE urs:6
HEAD Smeared TCM Triple_Crack_Model
GRP - ; GRP 5 prex 150 $ Prestress bolts
LC 904 DLZ 1 titl 'G_1+PG+MY+Pxx'
  LCC 901,902,903
END

+PROG ASE urs:5
HEAD Smeared TCM Triple_Crack_Model
ECHO RESI no
syst prob nonl nmat yes tol -10.0
GRP - ; GRP 5 prex 150 $ Prestress bolts
LC 914 DLZ 1 titl 'Cracked G_1+PG+MY+Pxx'
  LCC 901,902,903
END

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
MATE no  1 E 500               $ nra-0 quads
CONC no  2 type C    40        $ bottom slab
CONC no  4 type C    40        $ roof
CONC no  5 type C    40        $ wall
STEE no  6 type Y  1770 tmax 0
STEE no  9 type S   500
MATE no 11 E 500        gam 22 $ soil

$ A special water fluid element is implemented in DYNA for eigenvalue analysis (which works bad with ASE water bric).
$ But in time step analysis, if the water will only shake and not move a lot, I found this ASE representation quite good.
$ You can activate loadcase :
$    lc 8000 dlx 0.1 FACD 1 titl 'test FACD and 0.1*DLX'
$ and see that the water really goes up 10 % on the wall!
$ .
$ This is only possible with the bedding surface mat 14.
$ When the water goes up e.g. 1m, the total dead load of the water is 10kN/m2 higher.
$ As this is not automatically done by the BRIC elements, the surface bedding is added.

$ vgl. dyna6_eigenfrequenzen_wasser.dat  -  compare dyna6_natural_frequencies_water.dat
$ optimal for Wasser in ASE: JB 22.12.2010  see wassertest.dat + see Test loadcase 8000
MATE no 13 K 2080 E 0.001  G 0.0003 MUE 0.4999 GAM 10 ALFA 0.21 TITL Water
$ or: MATE 13 E 0.0132 MUE 0.499999 G 0.0044 K 2200 GAM 10.0 BEZ Water
$  Kompressionsmodul K = 2.2E8 kN/m2  = 2200 MN/m2
$  Die Querdehnzahl sollte eigentlich 0.5 sein.
$  Da 0.5 rechentechnisch nicht zulÃ¤ssig sind wird gewÃ¤hlt:
$  mue=0.499999  (= 0.5-1E-6)
$  und man erhÃ¤lt wegen
$                    E
$          K  =  ---------
$                 3(1-2mue)
$  E = K*(3*(1-2mue)) = 0.0132 MN/m2
$                    E
$          G  =   --------
$                  2(1+m)
$
$  G = E/3            = 0.0044 MN/m2
$
$      JB 9.8.2018
$


$ Also very important: Bedding on watersurface:  -> GRP 14  water_bedding
$ A deflection on top of the water of 1 m (boat) causes an uplift force of
$ 1t/m2 = 10 kN/m2 -> CP Bedding = 10 kN/m3
$ Wird die WasseroberflÃ¤che um 1 m nach unten verdrÃ¤ngt, z.B. durch ein Boot,
$ entsteht eine Auftriebskraft von 1t = 10 kN -> Bettung 10 kN/m3
MATE no 14 E 500               $ water_bedding
BMAT no 14 C 10 CRAC 9999

$ grp  6 - prestressing cables  102= 2000.. node numbers
$ for each 1000-node-level one ncs for variation of number of tendons
$ = area of cables
SCIT 102 MNO 6 D 90
SCIT 103 MNO 6 D 90
SCIT 104 MNO 6 D 80
SCIT 105 MNO 6 D 70
SCIT 106 MNO 6 D 60
SCIT 107 MNO 6 D 50
SCIT 108 MNO 6 D 40
SCIT 109 MNO 6 D 30
SCIT (110 119 1) MNO 6 D 20
SCIT 120 MNO 6 D 90    $ roof cable
$

end

$ Umrechnugsformeln TALPA:
$  Die Querdehnzahl sollte eigentlich 0.5 sein.
$  Da 0.5 rechentechnisch nicht zulÃ¤ssig sind wird gewÃ¤hlt:
$  mue=0.4999  (= 0.5-1E-4)
$  und man erhÃ¤lt wegen
$                    E
$          K  =  ---------
$                 3(1-2mue)
$ mit K=2080 :
$  E = K*(3*(1-2mue)) = 1.25 MN/m2
$                    E
$          G  =   --------
$                  2(1+m)
$
$  G = E/3
$
$  Weitere Umrechnungsformeln
$
 $$
$  In den Stoffgesetzen wird hÃ¤ufig der Kompressionsmodul, der E-Modul und der Steifemodul verwendet. Ein elastischer KÃ¶rper wird jedoch nur durch zwei Parameter beschrieben, so daÃŸ man immer einen Wert durch zwei andere berechnen kann. Im folgenden be
$
$          E     ElastizitÃ¤tsmodul
$          Es    Steifemodul (behinderte Seitendehnung)
$          K     Kompressionsmodul
$          G     Schubmodul
$          m     Querdehnzahl
$
$                    E                      E
$          K  =  ---------        G  =   --------
$                 3(1-2m)                 2(1+m)
$
$                  9Â·KÂ·G                  3K - 2G
$          E  =  ----------       m  =   ----------
$                  3K + G                 6K + 2G
$
$                     1 - m
$          Es  =  E -----------
$                   (1+m)(1-2m)
$
$                  3Â·KÂ·E                  3Â·KÂ·(1-2m)
$          G  =  ---------        G  =   ------------
$                 9Â·K - E                   2Â·(1+m)
$
$

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:3
HEAD Water Tank
ctrl node 50000 ; ctrl gtol 0.020 $ 20 mm tolerance for nodes
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 20000 POSZ
sto#r      44.000 $ m radius to wall innersurface
sto#rroof  85.000 $ m roof circle innerline
sto#troof   0.300 $ roof thickness
sto#twall   0.600 $ wall thickness
sto#tbott   0.500 $ bottom slab
sto#dtwater 2.000 $
sto#tsoil  15.000 $ soil
sto#rsoil  70.000 $ soil-outer radius

sto#rwall #r+0.5*#twall $ m radius to wall centerline

$ mesh refinement: insert 2 or 6 :
sto#m 6 $ or 6 - only 2 or 4 or 6 or 12  !!!  number of elements on 45 degree circle
sto#n 6 $ or 6 - only 2 or 4 or 6 or 12  !!!  number of elements from 301-501
$ or:
$ mesh refinement: insert 2 or 6 :

sto#n 2 $ or 6 - only 2 or 4 or 6 or 12  !!!  number of elements from 301-501

sto#s 3 $ 3 mesh refinement soil

let#nnodes #m*8

prt#nnodes
prt#dn

  NODE 800+#node X #rsoil        PHIZ #i*360/#nnodes $ end of soil
  NODE 700+#node X #rwall+1.50   PHIZ #i*360/#nnodes $ end of soil
  NODE 600+#node X #rwall        PHIZ #i*360/#nnodes $ end of soil
  NODE 500+#node X #r            PHIZ #i*360/#nnodes $ end of soil
  let#node #node+#dn
endloop

let#ri 0.75*#r ; tran NODE 401+#dno,425+#dno dno self dz -#zwall_top+#zrroof-sqr(#rroof^2-#ri^2)

GRP 0 titl soil_bottom
  QUAD prop mno 1 t 0.001[m] nra 0
  let#d 0
#define soil
QUAD - 801+#d 813+#d 713+#d 701+#d M12 -807-#d    -    -707-#d    -    M #m N #s
QUAD - 813+#d 825+#d 725+#d 713+#d M12 -819-#d    -    -719-#d    -    M #m N #s
#enddef                              $ ^ - M12  for real circle  (+ for spline)
#include soil
#define bot_slab_out
QUAD - 701+#d 713+#d 613+#d 601+#d M12 -707-#d    -    -607-#d    -    M #m N 1
QUAD - 713+#d 725+#d 625+#d 613+#d M12 -719-#d    -    -619-#d    -    M #m N 1
#enddef
#include bot_slab_out
#define bot_slab_gap
QUAD - 601+#d 613+#d 513+#d 501+#d M12 -607-#d    -    -507-#d    -    M #m N 1
QUAD - 613+#d 625+#d 525+#d 513+#d M12 -619-#d    -    -519-#d    -    M #m N 1
#enddef
#include bot_slab_gap
#define bot_slab_in
QUAD - 501+#d 513+#d 313+#d 301+#d M12 -507-#d +413+#d +307+#d +401+#d M #m N #n
QUAD - 513+#d 525+#d 325+#d 313+#d M12 -519-#d +425+#d +319+#d +413+#d M #m N #n
QUAD - 301+#d 313+#d 325+#d 101+#d M12 +307+#d +319+#d +225+#d +201+#d M #m N #m
#enddef                              $ ^ + M12  for inner nodes to catch nodes exactly in side!
#include bot_slab_in

GRP 1 titl soil_top
  let#d 1000
#include soil
#include bot_slab_out
#include bot_slab_gap
#include bot_slab_in

  QUAD prop mno 2 t #tbott[m] nra 7
  let#d 2000
#include bot_slab_out
#include bot_slab_gap
#include bot_slab_in

GRP 3 titl water_bottom
  QUAD prop mno 1 t 0.001[m] nra 0
  let#d 3000
#include bot_slab_in

#define nwater=6      $ number of water-brics :  attention: also in Extrusion
GRP 14 titl water_bedding
  QUAD prop mno 14 t 0.001[m] nra 0  $  important water_bedding with mno 14  (BMAT) !!
  let#d 3000+1000*$(nwater)
#include bot_slab_in

GRP 4 titl roof
  QUAD prop mno 4 t #troof[m] nra 7
  let#d 20000
#include bot_slab_gap
#include bot_slab_in

GRP 5 titl wall
  QUAD prop mno 5 t #twall[m] nra 7
  let#b    2000 $ bottom nodes
loop 18
  let#t #b+1000 ; QUAD - 601+#b 613+#b 613+#t 601+#t M12 -607-#b - -607-#t - M #m N 1
                  QUAD - 613+#b 625+#b 625+#t 613+#t M12 -619-#b - -619-#t - M #m N 1
  let#b #b+1000                                    $ ^ - M12  for real circle  (+ for spline)
endloop

GRP 6 titl cables
  let#b    2000 $ bottom nodes
loop 18+1
  CABL prop ncs 100+#b/1000 $ -> ncs 102-103-104 ... 120
  let#t #b+1000 ; CABL FIT 601+#b 613+#b
                  CABL FIT 613+#b 625+#b
  let#b #b+1000
endloop

$ insert for testing part above:
$        END

$ copy to half circle :

let#grp  0 ; grp #grp ; tran quad grp #grp dno 0 phiz 90

$ Extrusion

GRP 11 titl soil
  BRIC prop MNO 11
  TRAN quad inc GRP from 0 DNO - dz -#tsoil PROP x2   $ Extrusion der quads zu brics

GRP 13 titl water
  BRIC prop MNO 13
  TRAN quad inc GRP from 3 DNO - dz -#dtwater*$(nwater) PROP x$(nwater)   $ Extrusion der quads zu brics

$ insert for testing:
$        END

$ Interface springs :

grp 21 titl soil_to_slab_interface
  spri QGRP 2 1 cp 200000 ct 100000 crac 0 mue 0.3 dz 1 $ dz 1 otherwise spring gets tension
grp 23 titl water_to_slab_interface
  spri QGRP 3 2 cp 1E6 ct 0.1 crac 1e8 $ linear suffivient  ct only for stability
grp 25 titl water_to_wall
  let#nnodes #m*8
  let#dn 96/#nnodes $ node increment of springs circular direction
  let#b    3000 $ bottom nodes
  loop $(nwater)+1
    let#node 601+#b $ first node number at the wall
    loop #nnodes
      SPRI - na #node ne #node-100 cp 1E6 ct 0.1    $ linear suffivient  ct only for stability
      let#node #node+#dn
    endloop
    let#b #b+1000 $ bottom nodes
  endloop

$ insert for testing:
$        END

$ --------------------- fixings ---------------------------------------------
$ GRP 'A1'  $ secondary group identifier -> SOFILOAD
$ comment: filter all nodes on outer zylinder of soil:
SBOX R #rsoil+0.1 A1X 0 0 -100 0 0 100 $ = all nodes
SBOX R #rsoil-0.1 A1X 0 0 -100 0 0 100 OPT NOT $ not nodes with r<rsoil !
SBOX A1X -100 0 0  100 0 0  A2X 0 -100 0   0 100 0 A3X 0 0 -0.01  0 0 -#tsoil-0.01 OPT AND
         $ ^ to catch only nodes in tsoil without bottom nodes (follow next)
NODE SBOX FIX PP

$ now all soil bottom nodes with z=0
SBOX A1X -100 0 0  100 0 0  A2X 0 -100 0   0 100 0 A3X 0 0 -0.01  0 0 +0.01 OPT AND
NODE SBOX FIX PP
end

+prog sofiload urs:2
head
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
lc 9001 type none titl WX
  $ node grp 'A1' type wxx P1 0.01[mm]  $ secondary group identifier
@KEY NODE 0          $ node element info
LET#CDB_IER 0
LOOP 200000 $ ALL RECORDS
  LET#no @NR ; LET#FIX @KFIX ; LET#x  @XYZ(0) ; LET#y  @XYZ(1) ; LET#z  @XYZ(2)
  TXE node #no FIX= #FIX xyz= #(x,8.3) #(y,8.3) #(z,8.3)
  let#FIX mod(#FIX,8)
  IF (#FIX==0)&(#no>0) $ nur gelagerte Knoten
    node #no type wxx P1 1[mm]  $ node with fixing PP
  endif
ENDLOOP #CDB_IER<2 $ TO TERMINATE THE LOOP
end

$  STEP 1 LCST ... SELE    +8= accelerations

$  STEP 1 LCST ... SELE  +256= QUAD results

$  STEP 1 LCST ... SELE +1024= non-linear QUAD results

$ Important :
<text>
If you switch on the nonlinear effects (nonlinear interface between soil+tank,
the model behaves totally different with much less tank forces !!
-> in the last two ASE runs, activate the lines:   $ syst prob nonl

The eathquake input on the soil is not yet optimal.
Shaking the soil like this, soil waves are created and reflect on the boundary again.
It may be necessary to introduce a boundary with damping.
For this please also notice new DYNA feature with substructure SBFEM:
  'A high performance scaled boundary finite element method'

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation

+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD
$ NORM DIN EN199x-200x
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
ECHO MAT EXTR
CONC 1 C   30  $ here unused, therefore material 9 is used for brics!
STEE 2 S  500
$ Here material LADE for cracked bric concrete  TCM    Triple_Crack_Model   see also example   bric_smeared_cracked_girder.dat
MATE  9 E 33000 MUE 0.2 TITL 'LADE C30 SLS fcm 38 fctk 2.03'
NMAT  9 'LADE' P1    89855E3 P2 2.0 P3 2028 P4 50  P6 0.2 $ P3=tensile strength
END

+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:6
HEAD
UNIT 0 ;
SYST 3D GDIV -1000 GDIR NEGZ
STO#L 1.00

CTRL MESH 2 ; CTRL HMIN 0.5

SPT   101   X          0.0 Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT   111   X          0.0 Y          0.0 Z          0.1
SPT  1101   X           #L Y          0.0 Z          0.0
SPT  1111   X           #L Y          0.0 Z          0.1
SPT   201   X          0.0 Y          0.1 Z          0.0
SPT   211   X          0.0 Y          0.1 Z          0.1
SPT  1201   X           #L Y          0.1 Z          0.0
SPT  1211   X           #L Y          0.1 Z          0.1

SLN   1   101   111  !SDIV 0.2 $FIX  PP
SLN   2   111  1111  !SDIV 0.2
SLN   3  1111  1101  !SDIV 0.2 $FIX  PP
SLN   4  1101   101  !SDIV 0.2

SAR   1  GRP 1  MNO 1   MCTL +1  NRA 0  T 0.0  TITL 'Front Surface'
SARB  TYPE OUT NL 1,2,3,4
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:17
HEAD  EXTRUSION
SYST REST
CTRL REST 2
UNIT 0
$ Hilfsebenen kopieren
GRP 2 TITL 'Back Surface'
QUAD PROP MNO 1 NRA 0  T 0.0
TRAN QUAD GRP 1 DY 0.1 PROP NEW

$ Extrusion
GRP 10 TITL 'Volume Body'
  BRIC PROP MNO 9
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 1 DY 0.1 PROP x1

$ Randbedingungen
MOD NODE XMIN -0.001 XMAX +0.001  FIX PX
!MOD  KNOT XMIN 10-0.001 XMAX 10+0.001  FIX PXPYPZ
NODE 101,201 FIX PZ
NODE 101,111 FIX PY

$grup 91 bez 'Fest'
$   fede ka 1101,1111,1201,1211 dx 1 cp 1E9

$ delete temporary QUADs
DEL QUAD INC GRP FROM 1,2

END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD loads
LC 1001 TITL 'imposed displ.'
  NODE 1101,1111,1201,1211  TYPE WXX  P1 -1[mm]    ! corresponds to 1.0[0/00]  strain
END

!#!KAPITEL HYDRA

+PROG HYDRA urs:10 $ Querschnitt beflammen
HEAD DIN EN 1991-1-2/NA:2010 Anhang CC Validierungs-Beispiel 10
PAGE UNII 0
ECHO FULL no
ECHO MAT extr
ECHO BOUN yes
ECHO FUNC yes
<TEXT> Randbedingungen
Branddauer                           $(MINU) [min]
Brandkurve                           ETK - Einheitstemperaturkurve
WÃ¤rmeÃ¼bergangskoeffizient - Brand    $(ALPHA) [W/mÂ²K]
WÃ¤rmeÃ¼bergangskoeffizient - Luft     $(ALPHA1) [W/mÂ²K]
Emissionsbeiwert                     $(EPS)
</TEXT>
<TEXT> Material Nr.1
Rohdichte                            $(RHO) [kg/mÂ³]
Feuchte                              $(NSP) [%]
Thermische LeitfÃ¤higkeit             Siehe AQUA
Ausgangstemperatur                   20 [Â°C]
</TEXT>
SYST DIMT min DIMQ kw
STEP N $(MINU) T 1.0 // HOPT 25
PLC HP 20.0 $ Ausgangstemperatur
CTRL KITE 0
LC 701 TITL 'HYDRA'
SURF TYPE SPEC VAL $(ALPHA)/1000 FROM GRP 1 VP 1.0 EPS $(EPS) F 1
SURF TYPE SPEC VAL $(ALPHA)/1000 FROM GRP 2 VP 1.0 EPS $(EPS) F 1
$ For SURF, surface quads must be input with nra 0 , otherwisse wrong result in HYDRA
FUNC T $(MINU) F etk NO 1 TITL 'ETK R $(MINU)'
END

VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0.864813 Y -0.422351 Z 0.271511 AXIS POSZ ROTA 0
LC NO 701 T   60 ; BRIC TYPE TEMP UNIT DEFA SCHH NO STYP NODE FILL AREA REPR DISO
LC NO 701 T  600 ; BRIC TYPE TEMP UNIT DEFA SCHH NO STYP NODE FILL AREA REPR DISO
LC NO 701 T 1600 ; BRIC TYPE TEMP UNIT DEFA SCHH NO STYP NODE FILL AREA REPR DISO
LC NO 701 T 5400 ; BRIC TYPE TEMP UNIT DEFA SCHH NO STYP NODE FILL AREA REPR DISO
END

!#!KAPITEL Fire Analysis
+PROG ASE urs:7
HEAD
sto#lf 1 ; sto#time 0 $ Zeitpunkt in Minuten, 0=Ausgangstemperatur
#define blockase
  SYST PLC #lf-1 PROB NONL NMAT YES ITER 120
  GRP - ; GRP 1,2,3,4,51 off $ damit man im Animator diese Gruppen nicht sieht
  LC #lf DLZ 1.00 TITL 'TEMB Zeit #time Minuten'
    TEMB NO 0 T0 20 $ Ausgangstemperatur auch in HYDRA einzugeben
    TEMP 701 T2 #time*60 NOG 11 $ Zeitschritt in sec aus HYDRA Temperaturberechnung, T1 nicht erforderlich !
  LCC 901 $ Auflast PZ
  ECHO RESI no ; NSTR KSV UL $ Sicherheit 1.0 nach EN 1992-1-2 2.3(2)P: Der empfohlene Wert ist:
   $ âŽ¯ MaterialSicherheit von Beton, Betonstahl und Spannstahl: Î³M,fi = 1,0
  if #lf>1 ; echo mat,resi no ; endif
  CTRL BRIC 4 V6 0.05 $ W6=Zugfestigkeit nur in z-Richtung beim LADE FlieÃŸgesetz (StÃ¼tzen)
#enddef
#include blockase
END

#include blockase
END

  BRIC PROP MNO 9
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 1 DY 0.1 PROP x1

+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD
UNIT 0
CTRL REST 1
NORM 'DIN' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'    $ StrassenbrÃ¼cken -> L_U + L_T gammau = 1.35 !
CONC  1 C    40
STEE  2 S   500
STEE 11 Y '1860A'

let#zmax 1.86
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT - 0.00 0.00
     - 3.28 0.00
     - 3.33 0.20
     - 1.60 0.35
     - 1.68 1.14
     - 1.65 1.16
     - 1.60 #zmax
POLY  OPZ MNO 0
VERT - 0.00 0.28
     - 1.15 0.38
     - 1.15 1.62
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$                |
$     *----------|----------*     #zo
$     |          |<---#yo-->|
$     |          |          |
$     |          |          |
$     |          |<---#yu-->|
$     *----------|----------*     #zu
$                z
let#yo  1.50 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
let#yu  1.50 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox unten
let#zo  0.06 $ z-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
let#zu #zmax-0.06 $ " der Torsionsbox unten
LAY 0 'TORS' type min $ default for reinforcement layers
LAY 1 'BOT'  type opt $ 'bot' lower reinforcement 'bot'
LAY 2 'TOP'  type opt $ 'top' upper reinforcement 'top'
LRF  1 #yo #zo   #yu  #zu AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12   $ Durchm.12/15
LRF  2   -   -  -#yu  #zu AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  3   -   -  -#yo  #zo AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  4   -   -   #yo  #zo AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
let#yo 3.20     $ y-Wert HauptlÃ¤ngsbew. oben
let#yu #yu-0.05 $ y-Wert HauptlÃ¤ngsbew. unten
LRF  5 #yu #zu-0.05 -#yu  AS     1 LAY 1       TORS PASS D  20 $ unten
LRF  6 #yo #zo+0.05 -#yo  AS     1 LAY 2       TORS PASS D  20 $ oben
CUT 1 ZB 0.40  LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze oberhalb  Spannglied
CUT 2 ZB 0.60  LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze unterhalb Spannglied
CUT 3 YB -1.75[m]   MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN  $ belt Y neg. to get correct cut direction (cut belt off)
CUT 4 YB  1.00 ZB -1.00 YE  1.00 ZE  1.00 LAY 4 TYPE FLAN VZFK 0.50 $ 1.12.2021 : am besten einen Schubschnitt so anlegen,
CUT 4 YB  0.00 ZB  1.00 YE  0.00 ZE -1.00 LAY 4 TYPE FLAN VZFK 0.50 $ dass der herausgeschnittene Teil einen Hebelarm zur y- und z- Achse hat
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO                                      $ also hier einen Schnitt an der z-Achse herausfÃ¼hren,
                                                                    $ dann liefert auch eine Querkraft QY einen Anteil.
     'BOT'   0.00  #zmax   1 $ Literal BOT muss in Grossbuchstaben
     'TOP'   0.00  0.00    1 $ eingegeben werden

+PROG SOFILOAD URS:4
HEAD actions and loads
$ actions bridge design
$ All actions should be defined here.
$ This can be done in a separate SOFILOAD run as shown here.
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ECHO ACT Full $ Please check GAMU factors, especially for L_U and L_T (in germany GAMU 1.35)
ACT G_1                                                              TITL 'dead load'
ACT G_2                                                              TITL 'dead load'
ACT P                                                            TITL 'prestress'
ACT C                                                                TITL 'C+S'

ACT L_T GAMU   -  0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
ACT L_U GAMU   -  0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
$ The GAMU and PSI factores are taken from the .ini file depending on the design code (-> check)

$ ACT L_U GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'

#define support01
  let#dhspring        0 $ m bearing height
    $ bearing springs
    let#sy 0.5*#b0
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 51000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 53000 ; endif
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 52000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 54000 ; endif
    $ node on top of pier: node 49000...
             tran node #node                 dz #h dno 49000
             node #node+51000 FIX KF #node      $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+53000 FIX KF #node      ; endif $ coupling
             node #node+52000 FIX KF #node+49000 $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+54000 FIX KF #node+49000 ; endif $ coupling
             SPRI #node+0 #node+51000 #node+52000 DZ 1 CP 1E7             $ vertical bearing
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+1 #node+53000 #node+54000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  ; endif
    $ transverse bearing springs:
             SPRI #node+3 #node+51000 #node+52000 dy 1 CP 1E6 $ transverse
    $ longitudinal bearing springs:
    let#cp_long 1.0                       $ weak - to get bearing displacements
    if #logitud ; let#cp_long 1E6 ; endif $ longitudinal fixed bearing
             SPRI #node+7 #node+51000 #node+52000 dx 1 CP #cp_long $ longitudinal
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+8 #node+53000 #node+54000 dx 1 CP #cp_long ; endif $ longitudinal
  $ node bottom of pier: node 50000...
  tran node #node dz #UKpier dno 50000
  BEAM #node 50000+#node 49000+#node NCS 9 KR POSY
  node #node+50000 FIX F                 $ fixed support
#enddef
$
let#node         101 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            1.5 $ m cross section height
let#b0           3.5 $ m bearingspread
let#UKpier         7 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         111 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        1 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         121 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
END

  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

$ of traffic load cases:
$    SUP EXCL - from available load cases a single will be taken
$    SUP CONC - from available load cases all will be taken  , if acting unfavourable

           $
           $ ULS design :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF

           $

           $ see also MAXIMA - Theoretical bases
$ G as generic term action G includes the lower actions

$ Not but Z the ZF and ZS, because no underline follows!

$ Check: Prestressed tendon 1 had systematic angular displacement of 0.75 rad,
$ to add to the unintentional angular displacement of 0.30*42.80m = 12.84 degree,
$ gives a total angular displacement of
$ gamma = 0.75 + 0.30*42.80 * PI/180 = 0.75 + 0.22 = 0.97
$ Therewith it gives a reduction factor e^-mue*gamma(kappa-1) of 0.903.
$ The allowable stress by first strain is hence 0.90*fp0,1k*0.903
$   = 0.90*1500*0.903 = 1219 N/mm2. This is exactly 0.956 times the
$ nominal stress 1275, or as force 0.956*3634kN = 3472 kN.   Printout GEOS:
$
$   prestressing force/Nominal stress ZV:  3634 kN          Nominal stress   ZV/AZ :  1275 N/mm2
$   Maxi. allowable stress              :  3472 kN          Maxi. allowable stress :  1218 N/mm2
$   Middle allow. stress                :  3634 kN          Middle allow. stress   :  1275 N/mm2
$   Elastic limit                       :  1500 N/mm2       E-Modul                :195000 N/mm2
$   Yield stength                       :  1770 N/mm2

$      Given prestressing factor ZVi/ZVnenn          Given prestressing
$      general                 : 1.000               Strain        :
$      by strain               : 0.956               decreases     :
$      at prestressing anchor  : 1.000               restraint     :
$      at fix anchor           : 1.000               Slip          :
$      at slip                 : 0.916

$ The maximum stress will be reached over slippage with 0.916*1275 = 1168 N/mm2.
$ This value (=0.78*fp0,1k) will be determined for prestressing steel relaxation !

$ The regulation to hold an overstress reserve is important for the total strain!

$ Overview of the generated load case and design case numbers
$ Convention :
$    1000-th Number: 1000 = application,     2000 = Fraction
$     100-th Number:  100 = rare effects combination [rare]
$                     200 = not frequent effects combination [nonfrequent]
$                     300 = frequent effects combination [frequent]
$                     400 = quasi constant combination [permanent]
$                     900 = 1.0 times application superposition
$    The superposition of MAXIMA begins with the identification of
$    MAX or MIN, all others are AQB-combination!
$     Further  differences only for STAB-AQB-combination :
$      10-th Number:   00 = 100 % Prestress
$                      90 =  90 % Prestress
$                      10 = 110 % Prestress
$       1-th Number:  0+1 = maxi/mini Vaule state I
$                     5+6 = maxi/mini Value state II
$ therewith yields following STAB-AQB-design case numbers LC-BEME:
.
$ combination of actions   Prestress   State  I      State II
$                                       max LC min    max LC min
$ rare          [rare]   Pk,inf  90%   1190  1191    1195  1196
$                         Pm     100%   1100  1101    1105  1106
$                         Pk,sub 110%   1110  1111    1115  1116
.
$ not frequent     [nonf]   Pk,inf  90%   1290  1291    1295  1296
$                         Pm     100%   1200  1201    1205  1206
$                         Pk,sub 110%   1210  1211    1215  1216
.
$ frequent         [freq]   Pk,inf  90%   1390  1391    1395  1396
$                         Pm     100%   1300  1301    1305  1306
$                         Pk,sub 110%   1310  1311    1315  1316
.
$ quasi constant [perm]  Pk,inf  90%   1490  1491    1495  1496
$                         Pm     100%   1400  1401    1405  1406
$                         Pk,sub 110%   1410  1411    1415  1416
.
$ Fraction state [desi]   Pm     100%      -     -    2105  2106
$

       -    SUMP MY 'Permanent'       G   P  0.90    C     $     ZF  1.0 **

$
$ with the addition of 10% statical indeterminate part the disjunction of
$ statically determinate and indeterminate part achieved,
$ determinate part 90 %, indeterminate part 100 %
$ since in LC  P  both parts are with 90 % responded!
$
$ The permanent stress is defined in combination with type SUMP
$
$ For non-prestressed bridges only the reinforcing steel to be proved.
$ If it is not welded on, may according to german DIN-Fachbericht 102 4.3.7.5 (101) Page 160
$ respectively EN 1992-1-1 6.8.5(3) (6.71)
$ a reasonable resistance against fatigue accepted, if under frequent action the stress range
$ lies under 70 MPa.
$ as prestressing steel is used here, but a check according to german
$ DIN-Fachbericht 102 4.3.7.5 (102)
$ respectively EN 1992-1-1:   6.8.6(1)   with load model 3 necessary -> next AQB-Run.
$ The fatigue design of concrete is at pressure like here is mostly not necessay:
$     (comp. DIN-FB Kap. "" 4.3.7.1(102)
$ respectively EN 1992-1-1:   6.8.6(1)
$ - If stress range check under 70 mPa is sufficient:
NSTR FAT DINF SIGS 70
END
