!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD External prestress with cables
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ CTRL styp BEM
CONC 1  C   40        $ = C40/50
STEE  2 S 500                $ standard reinforcement steel 500
STEE  7    S  '235' $ TMAX  0 $ structural steel for tubes, rolled steel ...
STEE 11    Y '1770' ES 200000 $ prestessing steel or cables
STEE 18    Y '1860'

SECT  1 MNO 1
let#zmax 2.40
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT - 0.00[m] 0.00[m]
     - 3.28[m] 0.00[m]
     - 3.33[m] 0.20[m]
     - 1.60[m] 0.35[m]
     - 1.68[m] 1.14[m]
     - 1.65[m] 1.16[m]
     - 1.60[m] #zmax[m]
POLY  OPZ MNO 0
VERT - 0.00[m] 0.28[m]
     - 1.15[m] 0.38[m]
     - 1.15[m] #zmax-0.25[m]
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$                |
$     *----------|----------*     #zo
$     |          |<---#yo-->|
$     |          |          |
$     |          |          |
$     |          |<---#yu-->|
$     *----------|----------*     #zu
$                z
let#yo  1.50 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
let#yu  1.50 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox unten
let#zo  0.06 $ z-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
let#zu #zmax-0.06 $ " der Torsionsbox unten
LAY 0 'TORS' type min $ default for reinforcement layers
LAY 1 'BOT'  type opt $ 'bot' lower reinforcement 'bot'
LAY 2 'TOP'  type opt $ 'top' upper reinforcement 'top'
LRF  1 #yo[m] #zo[m]   #yu[m]  #zu[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12   $ Durchm.12/15
LRF  2    -     -     -#yu[m]  #zu[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  3    -     -     -#yo[m]  #zo[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  4    -     -      #yo[m]  #zo[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
let#yo 3.20     $ y-Wert HauptlÃ¤ngsbew. oben
let#yu #yu-0.05 $ y-Wert HauptlÃ¤ngsbew. unten
LRF  5 #yu[m] #zu-0.05[m] -#yu[m]  AS     1 LAY 1       TORS PASS D  20 $ unten
LRF  6 #yo[m] #zo+0.05[m] -#yo[m]  AS     1 LAY 2       TORS PASS D  20 $ oben
CUT 1 ZB 0.40[m]  LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze oberhalb  Spannglied
CUT 2 ZB 0.60[m]  LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze unterhalb Spannglied
CUT 3 YB -1.75[m]   MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN  $ belt Y neg. to get correct cut direction (cut belt off)
CUT 4 YB  1.00[m] ZB -1.00[m] YE  1.00[m] ZE  1.00[m] LAY 4 TYPE FLAN VZFK 0.50
CUT 4 YB -1.00[m] ZB  1.00[m] YE -1.00[m] ZE -1.00[m] LAY 4 TYPE FLAN VZFK 0.50
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO
     'BOT'   0.00[m]  #zmax[m]   1 $ Literal BOT muss in Grossbuchstaben
     'TOP'   0.00[m]  0.00[m]    1 $ eingegeben werden

SREC 9 H 1.5[m] B 4[m] $ piers
CABL 3 D 40 MNO 11
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:3
HEAD External prestress with cables
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 POSZ
NODE (101 121 1) X (0 21.4/10)
let#no 101 ; tran NODE #no dno 100 dz 0.60[m] ; node #no+100 fix kf #no
let#no 105 ; tran NODE #no dno 100 dz 2.10[m] ; node #no+100 fix kf #no
let#no 111 ; tran NODE #no dno 100 dz 0.40[m] ; node #no+100 fix kf #no
let#no 117 ; tran NODE #no dno 100 dz 2.10[m] ; node #no+100 fix kf #no
let#no 121 ; tran NODE #no dno 100 dz 0.60[m] ; node #no+100 fix kf #no

GRP 1
  BEAM (101 110 1) (101 1) (102 1) NCS 1 NP -1
GRP 2
  BEAM (111 120 1) (111 1) (112 1) NCS 1 NP -1
  BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec A typm HFAC
  BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec A typm SHEA
  BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec E typm SHEA
  BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec E typm HFAC
$
GRP 3
  CABL no NA  NE NCS=3
        1 201 205
        2 205 211
        3 211 217
        4 217 221
$
GRP 9
$ Den folgenden Block kÃ¶nnen Sie ohne Ã„nderung verwenden und nur die
$ darunter stehenden Variablen let#node ... setzen !
$ (Voraussetzung: Knotennummern im Ãœberbau < 1000)
#define support01
  let#dhspring        0 $ m bearing height
    $ bearing springs
    let#sy 0.5*#b0
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 51000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 53000 ; endif
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 52000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 54000 ; endif
    $ node on top of pier: node 49000...
             tran node #node                 dz #h dno 49000
             node #node+51000 FIX KF #node               $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+53000 FIX KF #node      ; endif  $ coupling
             node #node+52000 FIX KF #node+49000         $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+54000 FIX KF #node+49000 ; endif $ coupling
             SPRI #node+0 #node+51000 #node+52000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  $ vertical bearing
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+1 #node+53000 #node+54000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  ; endif
    $ transverse bearing springs:
             SPRI #node+3 #node+51000 #node+52000 dy 1 CP 1E6 $ transverse
    $ longitudinal bearing springs:
    let#cp_long 1.0                       $ weak - to get bearing displacements
    if #logitud ; let#cp_long 1E6 ; endif $ longitudinal fixed bearing
             SPRI #node+7 #node+51000 #node+52000 dx 1 CP #cp_long $ longitudinal
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+8 #node+53000 #node+54000 dx 1 CP #cp_long ; endif $ longitudinal
  $ node bottom of pier: node 50000...
  tran node #node dz #UKpier dno 50000
  BEAM #node 50000+#node 49000+#node NCS 9 KR POSY
  node #node+50000 FIX F                 $ fixed support
#enddef
$
let#node         101 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            1.5 $ m cross section height
let#b0           3.5 $ m bearingspread
let#UKpier         4 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         111 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        1 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
let#UKpier         9 $ m bottom level pier
#include support01
$
let#node         121 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
let#UKpier         4 $ m bottom level pier
#include support01
$
END

!#!Kapitel Loading, Prestress
+PROG SOFILOAD URS:4
HEAD actions and loads
$ actions bridge design

ACT C

ACT L_2 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 2'
ACT L_3 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 3'
$ The GAMU and PSI factores are taken from the .ini file depending on the design code (-> check)
$ You can also define them nanually here e.g. with:
$ ACT L_T GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
$ ACT L_U GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
  $ Superposition with ELLA traffic loading see more\csm31_design_ella.dat
  $ here SUP COND=special case, since L_U is applied in MAXIMA/AQB without inter superposition!
  $ L_1 with multiple UDL over loads in transvers direction needs EXCL, because only one to be taken
ACT SL  GAMU 1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'loading during construction'
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT FAT GAMU 1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'Fatigue LM3'
ACT SF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'possible settlement'
ACT ZF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'probable settlement'
  $ Acc. DIN FB 101 - C.2.3 for settlements GAMA=1.00.
ACT W                                                                TITL 'wind transvers'
ACT T   GAMU 0.81 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.80 PSI1 0.60 PSI2 0.50 PS1S    - TITL 'temperatur'
  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$
ACT B   GAMU 1.0 1.0 PART G SUP PERM PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'construction stage'
$ The signs SUP PERM,COND,EXCL are necessary and set itself according to
$ the definition of traffic load cases:
$    SUP EXCL - only one out of available load cases
$    SUP CONC - all of the available load cases, if acting unfavourable
           $ Meaning of PSI-Value:
           $
           $ Fraction :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
           $
           $ Rare    : 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
           $ frequent: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
           $ quasi   : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-all
           $ not     : PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
           $
           $ to  : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
           $ See MAXIMA - theoretical basics
$ G if as generic term effects G the under effects
$ G_1 and G_2 combined! alike L the L_U plus L_T combined!
$ not but Z the ZF and ZS, as no underline follows!
$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END
END

     L_U SLS,ULS $  -> MAXIMA: SUP COND     UDL base load
                 $  L_U...L_T in most times better with a MAXIMA pre superposition see csm33_earthquake_bridge.dat
     L_1 SLS,ULS $ UDL oberload span 1 - take only one
     L_2 SLS,ULS $ UDL oberload span 2 - take only one
     L_T SLS,ULS $ for SLS and ULS- checks
  $ Superposition with ELLA traffic loading see more\csm31_design_ella.dat
     T   SLS,ULS $ temperature
     ZF   SLS    $ true settlement SLS
     SF   ULS    $ possible settlement ULS
   $  FAT  FAT    $ activates more exact fatigue design via damage equivalent range of steel stresses.
                 $ A simple fatigue check will be done without this line.

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD External prestress with cables
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ CTRL styp BEM
CONC 1  C   40        $ = C40/50
STEE  2 S 500               $ standard reinforcement steel 500
STEE  7    S  '235' $ TMAX  0 $ structural steel for tubes, rolled steel ...
STEE 11    Y '1860A' $ prestessing steel
                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2
                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max
STEE 18    Y '1860'

SECT  1 MNO 1
let#zmax 2.40
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT - 0.00[m] 0.00[m]
     - 3.28[m] 0.00[m]
     - 3.33[m] 0.20[m]
     - 1.60[m] 0.35[m]
     - 1.68[m] 1.14[m]
     - 1.65[m] 1.16[m]
     - 1.60[m] #zmax[m]
POLY  OPZ MNO 0
VERT - 0.00[m] 0.28[m]
     - 1.15[m] 0.38[m]
     - 1.15[m] #zmax-0.25[m]
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$                |
$     *----------|----------*     #zo
$     |          |<---#yo-->|
$     |          |          |
$     |          |          |
$     |          |<---#yu-->|
$     *----------|----------*     #zu
$                z
let#yo  1.50 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
let#yu  1.50 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox unten
let#zo  0.06 $ z-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
let#zu #zmax-0.06 $ " der Torsionsbox unten
LAY 0 'TORS' type min $ default for reinforcement layers
LAY 1 'BOT'  type opt $ 'bot' lower reinforcement 'bot'
LAY 2 'TOP'  type opt $ 'top' upper reinforcement 'top'
LRF  1 #yo[m] #zo[m]   #yu[m]  #zu[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12   $ Durchm.12/15
LRF  2    -     -     -#yu[m]  #zu[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  3    -     -     -#yo[m]  #zo[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  4    -     -      #yo[m]  #zo[m] AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
let#yo 3.20     $ y-Wert HauptlÃ¤ngsbew. oben
let#yu #yu-0.05 $ y-Wert HauptlÃ¤ngsbew. unten
LRF  5 #yu[m] #zu-0.05[m] -#yu[m]  AS     1 LAY 1       TORS PASS D  20 $ unten
LRF  6 #yo[m] #zo+0.05[m] -#yo[m]  AS     1 LAY 2       TORS PASS D  20 $ oben
CUT 1 ZB 0.40[m]  LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze oberhalb  Spannglied
CUT 2 ZB 0.60[m]  LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze unterhalb Spannglied
CUT 3 YB -1.75[m]   MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN  $ belt Y neg. to get correct cut direction (cut belt off)
CUT 4 YB  1.00[m] ZB -1.00[m] YE  1.00[m] ZE  1.00[m] LAY 4 TYPE FLAN VZFK 0.50
CUT 4 YB -1.00[m] ZB  1.00[m] YE -1.00[m] ZE -1.00[m] LAY 4 TYPE FLAN VZFK 0.50
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO
     'BOT'   0.00[m]  #zmax[m]   1 $ Literal BOT muss in Grossbuchstaben
     'TOP'   0.00[m]  0.00[m]    1 $ eingegeben werden

SREC 9 H 1.5[m] B 4[m] $ piers
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:3
HEAD External prestress with cables
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 POSZ
NODE (101 121 1) X (0 21.4/10)
GRP 1
  BEAM (101 110 1) (101 1) (102 1) NCS 1 NP -1
GRP 2
  BEAM (111 120 1) (111 1) (112 1) NCS 1 NP -1
  BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec A typm HFAC
  BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec A typm SHEA
  BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec E typm SHEA
  BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec E typm HFAC
$
GRP 9
$ Den folgenden Block kÃ¶nnen Sie ohne Ã„nderung verwenden und nur die
$ darunter stehenden Variablen let#node ... setzen !
$ (Voraussetzung: Knotennummern im Ãœberbau < 1000)
#define support01
  let#dhspring        0 $ m bearing height
    $ bearing springs
    let#sy 0.5*#b0
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 51000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 53000 ; endif
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 52000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 54000 ; endif
    $ node on top of pier: node 49000...
             tran node #node                 dz #h dno 49000
             node #node+51000 FIX KF #node               $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+53000 FIX KF #node      ; endif  $ coupling
             node #node+52000 FIX KF #node+49000         $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+54000 FIX KF #node+49000 ; endif $ coupling
             SPRI #node+0 #node+51000 #node+52000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  $ vertical bearing
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+1 #node+53000 #node+54000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  ; endif
    $ transverse bearing springs:
             SPRI #node+3 #node+51000 #node+52000 dy 1 CP 1E6 $ transverse
    $ longitudinal bearing springs:
    let#cp_long 1.0                       $ weak - to get bearing displacements
    if #logitud ; let#cp_long 1E6 ; endif $ longitudinal fixed bearing
             SPRI #node+7 #node+51000 #node+52000 dx 1 CP #cp_long $ longitudinal
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+8 #node+53000 #node+54000 dx 1 CP #cp_long ; endif $ longitudinal
  $ node bottom of pier: node 50000...
  tran node #node dz #UKpier dno 50000
  BEAM #node 50000+#node 49000+#node NCS 9 KR POSY
  node #node+50000 FIX F                 $ fixed support
#enddef
$
let#node         101 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            1.5 $ m cross section height
let#b0           3.5 $ m bearingspread
let#UKpier         4 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         111 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        1 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
let#UKpier         9 $ m bottom level pier
#include support01
$
let#node         121 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
let#UKpier         4 $ m bottom level pier
#include support01
$
END

!#!Kapitel Loading, Prestress
+PROG SOFILOAD URS:4
HEAD actions and loads
$ actions bridge design
$ All actions should be defined here.
$ This can be done in a separate SOFILOAD run as shown here.
ECHO ACT Full $ Please check GAMU factors, especially for L_U and L_T (in germany GAMU 1.35)
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ACT G_1
ACT G_2
ACT P
ACT C
ACT ZC  GAMU 1.00 1 SUP PERM PSI0 1.00 PSI1 1.00 PSI2 1.00           TITL '                            life load creep part'
ACT L_T GAMU   -  0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
ACT L_U GAMU   -  0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
ACT L_1 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 1'
ACT L_2 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 2'
ACT L_3 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 3'
$ The GAMU and PSI factores are taken from the .ini file depending on the design code (-> check)
$ You can also define them nanually here e.g. with:
$ ACT L_T GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
$ ACT L_U GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
  $ Superposition with ELLA traffic loading see more\csm31_design_ella.dat
  $ here SUP COND=special case, since L_U is applied in MAXIMA/AQB without inter superposition!
  $ L_1 with multiple UDL over loads in transvers direction needs EXCL, because only one to be taken
ACT SL  GAMU 1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'loading during construction'
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT FAT GAMU 1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'Fatigue LM3'
ACT SF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'possible settlement'
ACT ZF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'probable settlement'
  $ Acc. DIN FB 101 - C.2.3 for settlements GAMA=1.00.
ACT W                                                                TITL 'wind transvers'
ACT T   GAMU 0.81 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.80 PSI1 0.60 PSI2 0.50 PS1S    - TITL 'temperatur'
  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$
$ The signs SUP PERM,COND,EXCL are necessary and set itself according to
$ the definition of traffic load cases:
$    SUP EXCL - only one out of available load cases
$    SUP CONC - all of the available load cases, if acting unfavourable
           $ Meaning of PSI-Value:
           $
           $ Fraction :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
           $
           $ Rare    : 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
           $ frequent: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
           $ quasi   : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-all
           $ not     : PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
           $
           $ to  : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
           $ See MAXIMA - theoretical basics
$ G if as generic term effects G the under effects
$ G_1 and G_2 combined! alike L the L_U plus L_T combined!
$ not but Z the ZF and ZS, as no underline follows!
$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END
END

!#!Info  Example:       Incremental launching
!#!Info  Keyword:       incremental launching; moving spring
!#!Info  Program:       ASE

$ Please also notice : CSM manual: Theoretical background - Incremental Launching Training

$ Incremental launching:                              JB 02.02.2007
$ Main feature is the free position of support moving springs beyond
$ the superstructure. If the moving spring finds an element in the
$ node sequence of MOVS from to, the spring supports this two
$ node subsystem like a balanced beam: the spring supports the two
$ nodes - only the bending moment peak in the real beam above is missing.
$ But for short superstructure beam elements (1m) this balanced beam
$ represents the real width of the moving support area.
$ Please check this behavior in plot of beam MY in this loadcase 902 !

$ In this example the support springs move beyond the fixed bridge
$ Please note that support positions are independent to superstructure nodes!

$ Alternatively the piers can be fixed while the superstructure moves:

$ Example with moving superstructure on fixed piers:
$                   movs_incremental_launching_2.dat

$ Example with CSM, tendons and creep+shrinkage:
$                   csm42_incremental_launching.dat


!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Movs_incremental_launching_principle
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
UNIT 0  $ Units in m
CONC 1 C 30
STEE 2 S 500
SREC 1 H 2.00[m] B .50[m] HO .40[m] BO 4.0[m]
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Movs_incremental_launching_principle
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC          GDIV   1000
NODE     NO             X
    (1 33 1)         (0 3.00)
TRAN NODE 2,12,22,32 DNO 1000 DZ 3.0
NODE NO FIX
     2    pymx
    12    pymx
    22    pymx
    32  pxpymx
NODE 1002,1012,1022,1032 FIX F
GRP 1
  BEAM NO           NA    NE NCS=1 NP=-1
      (101 132 1)  (1 1) (2 1)
GRP 9
  SPRI 1,2,3,4 NA 1002,1012,1022,1032 DZ -1 CP 1E8
$ There are two different ways to define moving springs.
$ In this example the spring is defined only at one node
$    = no coupling spring
$    and the superstructure is not connected with the springs
$    without an ASE-MOVS input.
$    So without ASE-MOVS this system would be instable !
$    ASE-MOVS L0 must be defined in this case!
$    The advantage is, that you are free in defining support springs
$    completely independant of discretisation of superstructure!
$
$ The second possibility as usually used in all CSM examples -> see CSM incremental launching
$    is to define coupling spings supporting
$    the structure also without an ASE-MOVS input.
$    ASE-MOVS L0 is not necessary in that case because the
$    spring length is defined with the coupling node.
$
$ ASE-MOVS input will then:
$ case 1 : - add a new free coupling node or node-line
$ case 2 : - change the coupling node to a new free coupling node or node-line
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:3
HEAD Define Moving springs - Remain active up to next MOVS blank input
MOVS grp 9 TYPE BGRP 1 L0 3.0[m]
END
+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD Launching position dx 2m
$ If you get instability, first activate the following     step 1 dt 1
$ and check the launching system and the activation of groups
$ in the produced 4000-loadcases (animator)
$ step 1 dt 1 $ for checks of instability
$ Please also check the list of moving spring activation

END
+PROG ASE URS:5

END
+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD Launching position dx 13m

END
+PROG ASE URS:7
HEAD Launching position dx 17m

END

-PROG WING URS:8

SCHH H6 0.30 MMOD OFF MAXN 0 MINN 0 $ no extreme values
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0 Y -1 Z 0 AXIS POSZ ROTA 0
SIZE SC 500
AND MSCA NO $ scale plot to first layer (fixed system)
LC NO 2+900
#define wing1
  GRP LC YES
  NODE TYPE SZ UNIT DEFA SCHH YES FILL NO REPR DVEC
  AND
  BEAM TYPE MY UNIT DEFA SCHH YES STYP BEAM FILL NO REPR DLIN
  DEFO NO
#enddef
#include wing1
LC NO 7+900
#include wing1
LC NO 13+900
#include wing1
LC NO 17+900
#include wing1
END

-PROG ASE URS:9
HEAD Envelope steps
let#length 50
let#dx #length
loop#step 21
  LAUN GRP 9 DX #dx[m] ; LC 1+#step FACD 1
  let#dx #dx-#length/20
  END
endloop
END

-PROG MAXIMA URS:13

END

  LC NO 1+#step
    #include wing1

  AND ; LC NO 802

!#!Info  Example:       M-kappa bending curvature plot of a section

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD M kappa plot
UNIT 5
ECHO SECT full
NORM 'NF' 'en199X-200X'
CONC  1 C    40
STEE  2 S 500

SECT  1 MNO 1
let#ymax 3000
let#zmax 2000
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
let#y #ymax
let#z #zmax
VERT    Y           Z
     0.40*#y -1.00*#z
     0.80*#y -0.70*#z
     1.00*#y -0.20*#z
     1.00*#y  0.20*#z
     0.80*#y  0.70*#z
     0.40*#y  1.00*#z
POLY  OPZ MNO 0
let#y #ymax*0.70
let#z #zmax*0.70
VERT    Y           Z
     0.40*#y -1.00*#z
     0.80*#y -0.70*#z
     1.00*#y -0.20*#z
     1.00*#y  0.20*#z
     0.80*#y  0.70*#z
     0.40*#y  1.00*#z
$
let#y #ymax*0.85
let#z #zmax*0.85
RF      Y           Z  AS=20[cm2] LAY=M1 TORS=ACTI D=16[mm]
     0.00*#y -1.00*#z   $ and 0-0
     0.40*#y -1.00*#z
     0.80*#y -0.70*#z
     1.00*#y -0.20*#z
     1.00*#y  0.20*#z
     0.80*#y  0.70*#z
     0.40*#y  1.00*#z
     0.00*#y  1.00*#z   $ and 0-0
    -0.40*#y -1.00*#z
    -0.80*#y -0.70*#z
    -1.00*#y -0.20*#z
    -1.00*#y  0.20*#z
    -0.80*#y  0.70*#z
    -0.40*#y  1.00*#z

CUT 1 ZB 0.00 LAY 1
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO
     'BOT'   0.00  #zmax   1
     'TOP'   0.00 -#zmax   1
END

S NCS 1 NO  2 X 0.000  N -5000.00  MY 20000.00
S NCS 1 NO  3 X 0.000  N -5000.00  MY 30000.00
NSTR ULTI
END

!#!Kapitel M kappa plot
+PROG AQB urs:11
sto#Nforce   -5000
HEAD M kappa plot for N= #Nforce kN
sto#nsteps 80
loop#i0 #nsteps  $ starting with 0,1,2,3 ...
  let#i1 #i0+1   $ starting with 1,2,3,4 ...
  S NCS 1 NO 100+#i1 X 0.000  N #Nforce  MY 500*#i1
endloop
NSTR ULTI
END

+PROG TEMPLATE urs:4
HEAD Results
TXE Results for N=#Nforce kN
TXE beam-no   Myi (inner bending moment My)    ESZ  (total curvature y)
TXE          [kNm]                             [-]
TXE ------------------------------------------------
$ let#0 2 $ to test CADIMP
let#LC 0 $ loadcase
loop#i0 #nsteps  $ starting with 0,1,2,3 ...
  let#i1 #i0+1   $ starting with 1,2,3,4 ...
  let#no 100+#i1    $ beam-no
  @KEY BEAM_STI  #LC  $ Stiffness of beams
  LET#Myi  @(#no,Myi)  $ read inner Myi  of beam #no

  @KEY BEAM_STR  #LC  $ Stresses in cross-section of beams
  LET#ESZ  @(#no,ESZ)  $ read strain gradient in z-direction   of beam #no

  TXE #(#no,6.0) #(#Myi,8.1)                        #(#ESZ,8.6)
  if #ESZ<0.50
    let#XX1(#i0) #ESZ*1000
    let#YY1(#i0) #Myi
  endif ! otherwise force too high - undesignable
endloop
TXE .
TXE .
TXE .
$
$==========================================================
!*!Label Plot Settings ----
$==========================================================
$
$ picture title
$
let#pic_titl 'My kappa plot for N=#N kN'
$
$ picture dimensions [cm]
$
let#pict_ycm 12.0
let#pict_xcm 13.0
$
$ data labels
$
let#leg1 'N=#Nforce kN'       $ in case of several curves !
let#leg_pos 'NE'   $ SS = line start, EE = line end, NE = north-east, NW = north-west, SE = south-east, SW = south-west
$
$ axis legends
$
$ let#x_leg 'ndof'
let#x_leg 'curvature [o/ooo]'
let#y_leg 'Acting bending moment My [kNm]'
$
$ ticks
$
let#x_tiks 0 1 2 5 10
let#x_tiks_nd 1                    $ number of decimal places
let#y_tiks 0 5000 10000 20000 30000 40000
let#y_tiks_nd 1
$
$ ############################# please change data and ticks above   #######################
$ ##########################################################################################
$ ############################# best do not change following lines  !!!!! ##################
$ ##########################################################################################
$                        In remembrance of Bojan Radmanovic  (JB 26.04.2016)
$
$ axis position
$
let#x_yaxis_pos 0 $ x-coordinate of y-axis
let#y_xaxis_pos 0 $ y-coordinate of x-axis
$
$ grid
$
let#is_grid 1+2 $ 0 = no grid, +1 = x-grid, +2 = y-grid
$
$
$ line and marker type (color, width, type)
$
$ index = 1000 * col + 100 * wid + typ
$
$ line type  : 1 = ___ | 2 = - - | 3 = . . | 4 = . - | 5 = --- | 6 = ... | 7 = .-.
$
$ marker type: 1 = .   | 2 = +   | 3 = *   | 4 = o   | 5 = x
$
let#line_type_1 2*1000+0*100+1
let#mark_type_1 2*1000+0*100+5
$
$
$==========================================================
!*!Label Plot ----
$==========================================================
$
$ Extreme values
$
let#extrX(0) 0.0 ;  let#extrX(1) 0.0
let#extrY(0) 0.0 ;  let#extrY(1) 0.0
$
loop#i XX1
 $
 let#extrX(0)  MIN(#extrX(0),#XX1(#i))
 let#extrX(1)  MAX(#extrX(1),#XX1(#i))
 $
 let#extrY(0)  MIN(#extrY(0),#YY1(#i))
 let#extrY(1)  MAX(#extrY(1),#YY1(#i))
 $
endloop
$
$ also consider specified tik-range
loop#i x_tiks
 $
 let#extrX(0)  MIN(#extrX(0),#x_tiks(#i))
 let#extrX(1)  MAX(#extrX(1),#x_tiks(#i))
 $
endloop
loop#i y_tiks
 $
 let#extrY(0)  MIN(#extrY(0),#y_tiks(#i))
 let#extrY(1)  MAX(#extrY(1),#y_tiks(#i))
 $
endloop
$
let#extrX(0)  MIN(#extrX(0),#x_yaxis_pos)
let#extrX(1)  MAX(#extrX(1),#x_yaxis_pos)
$
let#extrY(0)  MIN(#extrY(0),#y_xaxis_pos)
let#extrY(1)  MAX(#extrY(1),#y_xaxis_pos)
$
let#extrX(0) #extrX(0)*1.1 ; let#extrX(1) #extrX(1)*1.1
let#extrY(0) #extrY(0)*1.1 ; let#extrY(1) #extrY(1)*1.1
$
$ plot data
$
let#PSC #extrY(1)-#extrY(0)
let#FAK #PSC/(#extrX(1)-#extrX(0))
$
$----------------------------------------------------------
<PICT> xcm #pict_xcm ycm #pict_ycm text #pic_titl
$----------------------------------------------------------
$
$ -0.2*#PSC   +0.2*#PSC
$
GNT 1 XMIN #extrX(0)*#FAK XMAX #extrX(1)*#FAK $$
      YMIN #extrY(0)      YMAX #extrY(1)      SC -1
$
$ x-Axis
$
GTXI H 0.3 hali left vali half
GGDP TYPE VEC1   X1 #extrX(0)*#FAK Y1 #y_xaxis_pos X2 (#extrX(1)-#extrX(0))*#FAK  Y2 0.0
GTXT  X  #extrX(1)*#FAK*1.05 Y  #y_xaxis_pos TEXT #x_leg
$ x-Tiks
GPMI TYPE '+' SIZE 2
GTXI H 0.3 hali left VALI top
loop#i x_tiks
  GPM  X1 #x_tiks(#i)*#FAK Y1 #y_xaxis_pos
  $ GTXT  X #x_tiks(#i)*#FAK  Y #y_xaxis_pos VAL #x_tiks(#i) ND #x_tiks_nd
  GTXT  X #x_tiks(#i)*#FAK  Y #y_xaxis_pos VAL #x_tiks(#i) ND #x_tiks_nd
endloop
GTXT  X #x_yaxis_pos*#FAK  Y #y_xaxis_pos VAL #x_yaxis_pos ND #x_tiks_nd
$ y-Axis
GTXI H 0.3 hali cent vali bott
GGDP TYPE VEC1 X1 #x_yaxis_pos*#FAK Y1 #extrY(0) X2 0.0  Y2 (#extrY(1)-#extrY(0))
GTXT  X  #x_yaxis_pos*#FAK Y  #extrY(1)*1.05 TEXT #y_leg
$ y-Tiks
GPMI TYPE '+' SIZE 2
GTXI H 0.3 HALI righ VALI bott
loop#i y_tiks
  GPM  Y1 #y_tiks(#i) X1 #x_yaxis_pos*#FAK
  GTXT  Y #y_tiks(#i)  X #x_yaxis_pos*#FAK  VAL #y_tiks(#i) ND #y_tiks_nd
endloop
GTXT  Y #y_xaxis_pos  X #x_yaxis_pos*#FAK  VAL #y_xaxis_pos ND #y_tiks_nd
$
$ grid
$
GPLI col stan type ndot
if (#is_grid==1)|(#is_grid==3)
  $
  loop#i x_tiks
    GPL X1 #x_tiks(#i)*#FAK Y1 #extrY(0) X2 #x_tiks(#i)*#FAK Y2 #extrY(1)
  endloop
  $
endif
  $
if (#is_grid==2)|(#is_grid==3)
  loop#i y_tiks
    GPL X1 #extrX(0)*#FAK Y1 #y_tiks(#i) X2 #extrX(1)*#FAK Y2 #y_tiks(#i)
  endloop
  $
endif
$
$ plot curve
$
!*!Label Legend define
let#xy_leg 0 0
if     #leg_pos=='NE'
  let#xy_leg(0) #extrX(1)*#FAK*1.05
  let#xy_leg(1) #extrY(1)*1.05
elseif #leg_pos=='NW'
  let#xy_leg(0) #extrX(0)*#FAK*1.05
  let#xy_leg(1) #extrY(1)*1.05
elseif #leg_pos=='SE'
  let#xy_leg(0) #extrX(1)*#FAK*1.05
  let#xy_leg(1) #extrY(0)*1.05
elseif #leg_pos=='SW'
  let#xy_leg(0) #extrX(0)*#FAK*1.05
  let#xy_leg(1) #extrY(0)*1.05
endif
$
#define legend
$
if     #leg_pos=='SS'
  GTXI HALI RIGH
  let#leg_xoffs (#extrX(1)-#extrX(0))*0.01 ! 1% horiz. offset for legend text
  let#xy_leg(0) (#XX(0)-#leg_xoffs)*#FAK
  let#xy_leg(1) #YY(0)
elseif #leg_pos=='EE'
  GTXI HALI LEFT
  let#leg_xoffs (#extrX(1)-#extrX(0))*0.01 ! 1% horiz. offset for legend text
  let#xy_leg(0) (#XX(#nXX-1)+#leg_xoffs)*#FAK
  let#xy_leg(1) #YY(#nXX-1)
elseif #leg_pos=='NE'
  GTXI HALI LEFT
  let#xy_leg(0) #xy_leg(0)
  let#xy_leg(1) #xy_leg(1)-(0.4/#pict_ycm*#PSC)
elseif #leg_pos=='NW'
  GTXI HALI RIGH
  let#xy_leg(0) #xy_leg(0)
  let#xy_leg(1) #xy_leg(1)-(0.4/#pict_ycm*#PSC)
elseif #leg_pos=='SE'
  GTXI HALI LEFT
  let#xy_leg(0) #xy_leg(0)
  let#xy_leg(1) #xy_leg(1)+(0.4/#pict_ycm*#PSC)
elseif #leg_pos=='SW'
  GTXI HALI RIGH
  let#xy_leg(0) #xy_leg(0)
  let#xy_leg(1) #xy_leg(1)+(0.4/#pict_ycm*#PSC)
endif
$
GTXI COL #line_type/1000 H 0.3
GTXT X #xy_leg(0) Y #xy_leg(1) TEXT #leg
$
#enddef
$
!*!Label Curve define
#define plot_curve
$
GPLI ind #line_type
GPMI ind #mark_type
loop#i #nXX
  if #i>0
    GPL X1 #XX(#i-1)*#FAK Y1 #YY(#i-1) X2 #XX(#i)*#FAK Y2 #YY(#i)
  endif
  GPM  X1 #XX(#i)*#FAK Y1 #YY(#i)
endloop
$ legend
#include legend
$
#enddef
$
$==========================================================
!*!Label  f1(x)
$==========================================================
$
let#line_type #line_type_1
let#mark_type #mark_type_1
let#leg       '#leg1'
$
let#nXX 0
loop#i XX1
  let#XX(#i) #XX1(#i)
  let#YY(#i) #YY1(#i)
  let#nXX #nXX+1
endloop
$
#include plot_curve
$
$----------------------------------------------------------
</PICT>
$----------------------------------------------------------
$
$

$ Possibilities in AQB : see file m_kappa_plot.dat

!#!Kapitel first check to get max. capacities
+PROG AQB urs:5
HEAD M-N interaction plot
sto#Ntension   +5000  $ this the section can carry good under tension
sto#Ncompres  -20000  $ this the section can carry good under compression - not too high to get more points at N=0
sto#Mpure      +5000  $ this the section can carry on N=0
 $ ^ please choose values so that all capacity values 'rel' are above 1.00 and no reinforcement is increased !
ECHO desi full
BEAM 1 X 0.00 NCS 1 TYPE SECT $ to get the result 'rel' stored in the database !
lC 1 type 'G_1' ; S NCS - NO 1 X 0.00  N #Ntension  MY 0
lC 2 type 'G_2' ; S NCS - NO 1 X 0.00  N #Ncompres  MY 0
lC 3 type 'G_3' ; S NCS - NO 1 X 0.00  N 0          MY #Mpure
$ tension with LC 1:
let#facN  0.9 ; let#facM 1.-abs(#facN)
  COMB SOLO LC1 1 F1 +#facN      LC2 3 F2 #facM    LCST 1001 $ stores result 'rel' in cdbase 147/1001
let#facN  0.1 ; let#facM 1.-abs(#facN)
  COMB SOLO LC1 1 F1 +#facN      LC2 3 F2 #facM    LCST 1002 $ stores result 'rel' in cdbase 147/1001
let#facN  0.001 ; let#facM 1.-abs(#facN)
  COMB SOLO LC1 1 F1 +#facN      LC2 3 F2 #facM    LCST 1003 $ stores result 'rel' in cdbase 147/1001
$ compression with LC 2:
let#facN -0.1 ; let#facM 1.-abs(#facN)
  COMB SOLO LC1 2 F1 -#facN      LC2 3 F2 #facM    LCST 1004 $ stores result 'rel' in cdbase 147/1001
let#facN -0.9 ; let#facM 1.-abs(#facN)
  COMB SOLO LC1 2 F1 -#facN      LC2 3 F2 #facM    LCST 1005 $ stores result 'rel' in cdbase 147/1001
DESI ULTI AM1 0 0 0 0 SMOD no  $ N and M are increased to find capacity 'rel'
END

!#!Kapitel M-N interaction plot

+PROG AQB urs:11
HEAD M-N interaction plot
BEAM 1 X 0.00 NCS 1 TYPE SECT $ to get the result 'rel' stored in the database !
lC 1 type 'G_1' ; S NCS - NO 1 X 0.00  N #Ntension  MY 0
lC 2 type 'G_2' ; S NCS - NO 1 X 0.00  N #Ncompres  MY 0
lC 3 type 'G_3' ; S NCS - NO 1 X 0.00  N 0          MY #Mpure
 $ ^ please choose #Ntension...#Mpure so that all capacity values 'rel' are above 1.00 and no reinforcement is increased !
sto#nsteps 50
sto#nstep05 #nsteps/2 $ here N shall be 0.0

loop#i0 #nsteps-1  $ starting with 0,1,2,3 ...
  let#i1 #i0+1   $ starting with 1,2,3,4 ...
  let#facN abs((#nstep05-#i1))/#nstep05
  let#facN #facN*#facN ; let#facM 1.-abs(#facN) $ take facN quadratic to get more points for bending My (N nearly zero)
  TXE CADINP test print loop i0=#i0 i1=#i1 facN=#(#facN,6.3) facM=#(#facM,6.3)
  if #i1<#nstep05
    $ tension with LC 1:
    COMB SOLO LC1 1 F1 +#facN      LC2 3 F2 #facM    LCST 100+#i1 $ stores result 'rel' in cdbase 147/1001
  else
    $ compression with LC 2:
    COMB SOLO LC1 2 F1 +#facN      LC2 3 F2 #facM    LCST 100+#i1 $ stores result 'rel' in cdbase 147/1001
  endif
endloop
DESI ULTI AM1 0 0 0 0 SMOD no
END

+PROG TEMPLATE urs:4
HEAD Results
TXE Results M-N interaction plot
TXE LCST   Myi (inner bending moment My)    Ni (Inner normal force N)    'rel'
TXE      [kNm]                            [kN]
TXE ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
sto#rel_error 0
$ let#0 2 $ to test CADIMP
loop#i0 #nsteps-1  $ starting with 0,1,2,3 ...
  let#i1 #i0+1   $ starting with 1,2,3,4 ...
  let#no 1 $ beam-no
  let#LC 100+#i1 $ loadcase
  @KEY BSCT_DES #LC    $ Ultimate/Plastic Design results of loadcase #LC
  LET#Ni   @(#no,Ni)   $ read inner Ni  of beam #no
  LET#Myi  @(#no,Myi)  $ read inner Myi  of beam #no
  LET#rel  @(#no,scf)  $ relative capacity

  TXE #(#LC,5.0) #(#Myi,8.1)                   #(#Ni,10.1)                       #(#rel,8.3)
  let#XX1(#i0) #Myi/1000
  let#YY1(#i0) #Ni/1000
  if #rel<1.01
    sto#rel_error 1 ! reinforcement is increased - #Ntension...#Mpure is too high
  endif
endloop
TXE .
TXE .
TXE .
$

!#!Info Example:    Secondary effect of prestress - prestressed slab
!#!Info Program:    ASE
!#!Info Keyword:    Secondary effect


!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Voided prestressed slab
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
CONC 1 C   30
STEE 2 S  500
STEE 3 S  235
STEE 11 Y '1860A'
                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2
                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max
end

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC GDIR POSZ GDIV 1000
NODE  1 X  0   8 0 $ left lower edge of the slab
NODE  8 X 11  -8 0 $ left upper edge of the slab
NODE NO NR1 NR2    Y
      2   1   8   6.50 $ Edge of haunch
      3   1   8   5.50 $ Bearing axis 1
      4   1   8   2.50 $ Bearing axis 2
      5   1   8  -2.50 $ Bearing axis 3
      6   1   8  -5.50 $ Bearing axis 4
      7   1   8  -6.50 $ Edge of haunche
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 8 DNO 100 DX 0.80
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 8 DNO 200 DX 0.80+20.0
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 8 DNO 300 DX 0.80+40.0
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 8 DNO 400 DX 0.80+40.0+0.80
let#1 200 $ Thickness at cantilever end
let#2 400 $ Thickness at cantilever section
let#3 800 $ Thick slab area
GRP 1
QUAD N1  N2  N3  N4  M  N T1 T2 T3 T4 MNO=1 MRF=2 POSI=BELO
      1 101 102   2  1  2 #1 #1 #2 #2 $ Cantilever
    101 201 202 102 12  2 #1 #1 #2 #2 $ Cantilever

    301 401 402 302  1  2 #1 #1 #2 #2 $ Cantilever

    307 407 408 308  1  2 #2 #2 #1 #1 $ Cantilever

GRP 2 TITL 'Final bearing'

    - 103,104,105,106
    - 203,204,205,206

    - 103,104,105,106           $ Alternatively you can switch off supports completely and use dynamic stabilisation
    - 303,304,305,306

+PROG TENDON urs:7

+PROG TENDON urs:3
HEAD Parabolic Prestress
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ Definition of prestressing system:
$ We recommend to input all data as user defined prestressing system.
$ For the static analysis the following values are sufficient:
SYSP NOPS MAT   ZV       AZ    LITZ MINR   BETA  MUE ECC  SP     DO
        1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 82[mm] $ csm3_parabel and csm32_slab, 12 wires
      $ 1  11 3078[kN] 2250[mm2] 15 7.10[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 92[mm] $            15 wires
      $ 1  11 3848[kN] 2850[mm2] 19 6.50[m] 0.3 0.21 4[mm] 3[mm] 97[mm] $ csm31_beam 19 wires
      $ 1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.0 0.00 0[mm] 0[mm] 10[mm] $ csm3_casting_yard
$
$ reference axis for all tendons = x-axis:
AXES NOH 1  VAL1  0.00 0.00 0.00  TYPE=poly  KIND=QUAD
         1  VAL1 50.00 0.00 0.00  TITL "X-Axis"
$ tendon geometry definition:
let#nr 1   $  Geometry- and String number
let#y 6.30 $  Y-coordinate of this string
#define tendons
TGEO NOG #nr NOH 1 NOPS 1
let#x 11/2-#y*11/16 $ Starting coordinate at slab outer edge
PTUV S        U       V   DVS  RV    RL   type=REFX
    #x       #y      0.25  -   -     -
    #x+10.00 #y      0.70  0   -     -
    #x+20.80 #y      0.15  0  9.5   1.3
    #x+31.60 #y      0.70  0   -     -
    #x+41.60 #y      0.25  -   -     -

CS ICS1 11 12                $ = construction stages
PSIG 'RI' ANWS 9 KAPA - K3 1280 $
        $ k3 = estimated limit to reduce stress at traffic opening (after first creep+shrinkage)
        $      max-sigma-traffic opening in most cases (e.g. to EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)) -> 0.65 fpk (or 0.75 depending on design code)
$ final tendon definition:
TEND NOT #nr NOG #nr NTEN 2 LC 11
                      $   2 Attention: NTEN=2
let#nr #nr+1   $ count up for the next number
#enddef
#include tendons

loop#i0 25
  let#y  6.00-0.50*#i0 $ Y-Koordinate des nÃ¤chsten Stranges       $ Y-coordinate for the next string
  #include tendons
endloop

let#y -6.30
#include tendons

$ ----------------------------------------------------------
echo plot full $ tendon plots:
SIZE URS
PLOT GEOE NO 14 FACH  5 TYPG DUTE
PLOT FACT NO 14 FACH 15
end

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE urs:4
HEAD Mv0+Mv2
GRP -  CS 0  $ netto
GRP 2  full  $ Real support
GRP 9  off

LC 3           TITL    'Mv0+Mv2'
  LCC 903
END

+PROG ASE urs:6
HEAD MV0 - statically determined part
GRP -  CS 0  $ netto
GRP 2  off
GRP 9  full  $ Support without restraint for statically determined analysis
LC 9           TITL    'Mv0'  $ Mv0 without Mv2
  LCC 903
END

+PROG ASE urs:7
HEAD $ Variant without real support springs with weak dynamic mass bearing
STEP 1 dt 1000 $ Creates a weak dynamic mass fixing
               $ A too short time step would give a too big dynamic mass fixing
CTRL WARN 282 $ Switches off a here not relevant error message
GRP -  CS 0  $ netto
GRP 2,9  off $ all supports switched off
LC 19           TITL    'Mv0 dynamic'
  LCC 903
END

PROG MAXIMA urs:9
HEAD
COMB 1 EXTR stan TYPE 'STAN' TITL 'MV2 = MV - MV0'
LC  3 TYPE G FACT  1.00
LC  9 TYPE G FACT -1.00
SUPP ETYP 'QUAD' TYPE 'mxx' LC 1009 EXTR MAX COMB 1
SUPP ETYP 'QNOD' TYPE 'mxx' LC 1009 EXTR MAX COMB 1


COMB 2 EXTR stan TYPE 'STAN' TITL 'MV2 = MV - MV0 dynamic'
LC  3 TYPE G FACT  1.00

LC 1019 ; QUAD TYPE MN UNIT 800 SCHH 0.25 STYP NODE REPR DCUT

<TEXT>
In slabs it is not possible to easily extract the secondary effect of prestress because a quad cannot
be assigned to a tendon. Some quads do not even catch a tendon.

But the secondary effect of prestress can be calculated with a trick:

- Total prestress Mv0+Mv2 calculated with the normal support
- Part Mv0 alone calculated on a system with statically determined support condition -> LC 9 or 19
  A statically determined support can be achieved with a special support condition - here group 9
  or by analyzing the superstructure without any real support with a weak dynamic mass fixing - LC 19
- Then the difference of the two loadcases is the searched part MV' = Mv2 = secondary effect of prestress

For beams see bridge_design_manual_aqb.dat
</TEXT>

$ The GAMU and PSI factores are taken from the .ini file depending on the design code (-> check)
$ You can also define them nanually here e.g. with:
$ ACT L_T GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'

  $ Superposition with ELLA traffic loading see more\csm31_design_ella.dat
  $ here SUP COND=special case, since L_U is applied in MAXIMA/AQB without inter superposition!
  $ L_1 with multiple UDL over loads in transvers direction needs EXCL, because only one to be taken
ACT SL  GAMU 1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'loading during construction'
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT FAT GAMU 1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'Fatigue LM3'
ACT SF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'possible settlement'
ACT ZF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'probable settlement'
  $ Acc. DIN FB 101 - C.2.3 for settlements GAMA=1.00.
ACT W                                                                TITL 'wind transvers'
ACT T   GAMU 0.81 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.80 PSI1 0.60 PSI2 0.50 PS1S    - TITL 'temperatur'
  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$
$ Die Kennzeichnung SUP PERM,COND,EXCL ist wichtig und richtet sich
$ je nach Definition der VerkehrslastfÃ¤lle nach:
$    SUP EXCL - von den verfÃ¼gbaren LastfÃ¤llen wird nur einer genommen
$    SUP CONC - die verfÃ¼gbaren LastfÃ¤lle werden alle genommen, falls ungÃ¼nstig wirkend
           $ Bedeutung der PSI-Werte:
           $
           $ Bruch :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
           $
           $ Selten: 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
           $ hÃ¤ufig: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
           $ quasi : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-alle
           $ nichth: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
           $
           $ nach : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
           $ siehe auch MAXIMA - Theoretische Grundlagen
$ G falls als Oberbegriff Einwirkung G die Untereinwirkungen
$ G_1 und G_2 zusammen! Ebenso faÃŸt L die L_U plus L_T zusammen!
$ Nicht aber Z die ZF und ZS, da kein Unterstrich folgt!
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ The specification SUP PERM,COND,EXCL is important and depends on
$ the definition of the traffic load cases:
$    SUP EXCL - only one of the load cases will be taken
$    SUP CONC - all of the available load cases will be taken, if infavourable effects
                      $ Meaning of the PSI-Values:
                      $
                      $ Fraction :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
                      $
                      $ Seldom: 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
                      $ Often: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
                      $ Quasi : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-any
                      $ Noth: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
                      $
                      $ According to : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
                      $ see also MAXIMA - Theoretical basis
$ G should the generic term effects G the sub effects
$ G_1 and G_2 together! L also sums up L_U plus L_T!
$ But not Z the ZF and ZS, as an underscore doesn't follow!
END

   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 2  $ 2. Axis lane 2
endloop
$ Fall C Fahrstreifen 1 ist links:                   $ Case C lane 1 is at left:
let#ys1 -6.20+1.50      $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 1       $ Middle lane 1
let#ys2 -6.20+1.50+3.00 $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 2       $ Middle lane 2
loop#1 10
 LC #lf TITL 'TS_Ãœberlast'   TYPE L_T ; let#lf #lf+1 ; let#x1 7.90+#1*2.0 $ erste Achse $ first axis
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1      Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 1  $ 1. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 1  $ 2. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1      Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 2  $ 1. Axis lane 2
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 2  $ 2. Axis lane 2
endloop

$ Im Nachweis des Grenzzustandes der TragfÃ¤higkeit sind die mÃ¶glichen Baugrundbewegungen
$ anzusetzen, bei deren Ermittlung dÃ¼rfen aber nach DIN FB 102 II-2.3.2.2(103)P
$ ohne weiteren Nachweis die 0.6-fachen Steifigkeiten des Zustandes I abgesetzt werden
$ (wegen mÃ¶glichem Ãœbergang in den Zustand II).
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ For the check of the limit state of the bearing capacity the possible soil movements
$ have to be taken into consideration, however for their determination according to DIN FB 102 II-2.3.2.2(103)P
$ the 0.6 folded rigidities of state 1 can be disregarded for this check
$ (due to possible transition into state II). According to SOFiSTiK (Dr. Bellmann)
$ the superposition has then to be applied with a load safety coefficient g=1.35.
$----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 81 TITL 'mÃ¶gl.Setzung 1+3'  TYPE SF               $ ' potential settlement'
   NODE NO (110 123 1)  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm] $ entspricht Berechnungen mit 0.6-fachen Steifigkeiten
LC 82 TITL 'mÃ¶gl.Setzung 2'    TYPE SF               $ corresponds to analysis with 0.6 folded rigidities
   NODE NO (210 223 1) TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm]
$ Im Nachweis der GrenzzustÃ¤nde der Gebrauchstauglichkeit sind die wahrscheinlichen
$ Baugrundbewegungen immer als stÃ¤ndige Einwirkung, also 1.0-fach anzusetzen,
$ siehe DIN FB 102 II-2.3.4(110)P  . Hier ist die 0.4-Abminderung nicht zulÃ¤ssig!
$ In der vorliegenden Berechnung werden 1 cm als mÃ¶gliche Setzung und 0.5 cm als
$ wahrscheinliche Setzung angesetzt, jeweils pro StÃ¼tzenachse angesetzt und ungÃ¼nstigst
$ Ã¼berlagert.
$ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ For checking the limit states of the fitnes of purpose the most probable
$ soil movements should always be applied as constant effects, therefore 1.0 folded,
$ see DIN FB 102 II-2.3.4(110)P  . Here the reduction of 0.4 is not allowed!
$ In the present analysis 1 com is applied as possible settlement and 0.5 cm are applied as probable settlement,
$ each per support axis and in the worst case superposed.
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 83 TITL 'wahr.Setzung 1+3'  TYPE ZF      $ ' true settlement'
   NODE NO (110 123 1)  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]
LC 84 TITL 'wahr.Setzung 2'    TYPE ZF
   NODE NO (210 223 1) TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]

$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 85 TITL 'T OBEN  WAERMER'   TYPE T
   QUAD GRP  40             TYPE DTZ P  -7.9 $ positive DTZ = higher Temp. in pos. z
   BEAM GRP (10 #GRPLAST 1) TYPE DTZ PA -7.9
LC 86 TITL 'T UNTEN WAERMER'   TYPE T
   QUAD GRP  40             TYPE DTZ P  +5.0 $ positive DTZ = higher Temp. in pos. z
   BEAM GRP (10 #GRPLAST 1) TYPE DTZ PA +5.0
$ Achtung: wegen der vielen Lager in Querrichtung erzeugt die Temperatur auch
$ starke Querbiegemomente (die vier Lager unterdrÃ¼cken eine QuerkrÃ¼mmung).
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ Attention: due to the numerous structural bearings in transverse direction the temperature also creates
$ strong transverse bending moments (the four bearings suppres a transverse curvature).
$---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END

+PROG SOFILOAD URS:3
HEAD Fresh concrete load - see csm13_quad_weight_lar_activation.dat
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LAR  1 GRP 40  $ create an LAR of existing quad elemente group 0
LC 39 TYPE none TITL concrete_load     $ Fresh concrete load
  AREA LAR 1 TYPE PG #depthsitu*0.001*25 $ dead load of quads on LAR
                             $ Belastung einer ganzen LastverteilungsflÃ¤che

<text> <u><b> Double dead load:</u></b>
    The beam sections the concrete dead load is automatically activated stating at CS 40.
    As from CS 40 beams and quads exist,
    this double dead load must be substracted once!
    In steel_composite_tbeam.dat this is done automatically by the "T-beam philosophy"
</text>
LC 40 TYPE none TITL double_concrete_load
  beam grp (10 #GRPLAST 1) TYPE PG -#depthsitu*0.001*25 $ negative load of section concrete!
  $ Because ASE stage >=40 activates concrete dead load automatically !!!
$ -> Please check WINGRAF - beam loads in loadcase 39+40 !!!
END

+PROG AQUA URS:9
HEAD Steel composite section thin walled
ECHO MAT FULL
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
UNIT 2 $ mm units in AQUA (steel)
$ CTRL styp BEM

CONC 1    C  30 ALFA 1.2E-5  TITL 'in situ concrete' $ deck slab  ALFA 1.2E-5 same as steel to test LC 90-92
STEE 2,3  S 500   TITL 'reinforcement'
$
STEE 4    S 450T  TITL 'shear stud connection'
$
STEE 6    S 450T  TITL 'top steel plate'
STEE 7    S 450T  TITL 'steel web'
STEE 8    S 450T  TITL 'bottom steel plate'
$
$ Material distribution:
$
$   *-------------- y <-----*-----------------------*
$   *                       z                       *
$   *                                               *
$   *===============================================*       in situ concrete
$   *     1+3               |      1+3              *
$   *                       4                       *       shear stud connection
$   *-----------------------------------------------*
$                     ---6-----6---                         top blec
$                           |
$                           |
$                           7                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     ---8-----8---                         bottom blec

CTRL RFCS 2 $ consider reinforcement for stiffness

STO#AS    10    $      cm2/m minimum reinforcement in the in situ concrete

STO#depthsitu  350  $ [mm] in situ deck concrete
STO#widthsitu 1000  $ [mm] concrete width
STO#height     600  $ [mm] steel height
STO#widthtop   500  $ [mm] steel width top
STO#widthbot   500  $ [mm] steel width bottom
 $ blec thickness:
STO#TT          20  $ [mm] blec thickness on top
STO#TW          10  $ [mm] web thickness
STO#TB          30  $ [mm] blec thickness of bottom  slab

SECT  1  MNO 6 MRF 3 TITL  'steel part alone' $ "real"
SV  AK .1 $ ohne Torsionssteifigkeit !
$
$
$   *-------------- y <---*TOPC---------------------*       top blec upper layer (z=0)
$   *                                               *
$   *SITR==================SITU=================SITL*
$   *                       | MNR 4 LNAH            *       shear stud connection
$   *                      LNAX                     *
$   *                       | MNR 4 BLEC            *       shear stud connection
$   *-----------------------*-----------------------*       top blec upper layer (z=0)
$                     TOCR-TOC-TOCL                         top blec center line  C=centerline
$                           |
$                           |
$                           |                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     BOCR-BOC-BOCL                         bottom blec center line
$                          BOT                              bottom blec lowest layer (z=height)
$
$  construction points:
$  concrete
SPT SITU Y  0 Z #depthsitu/2                       MNO 0 $ center in situ concrete   MNR 0 = only construction
SPT SITR Y  0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
SPT SITL Y -0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
$  steel
SPT TOP  Y  0 Z #depthsitu                         MNO 6 $ top-steel center ! MNO 6 = AQB output point
SPT TOC  Y  0 Z #TT/2                    REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ top blec center line  C=centerline
SPT TOCR Y  0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT TOCL Y -0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT BOC  Y  0 Z  #height-#TB/2           REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ variable construction point !!!!!!
SPT BOCR Y  0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOCL Y -0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOT  Y  0 Z  #height                 REFP TOP  MNO 8 $ for AQB:       MNR 8 = for AQB-output material 8

$ SPT LNAX Y  0 Z #depthsitu*0.9                     MNO 4 $ shear connection point
$
$ now all points of above sketch are defined and can be used for steel-parts :
$
$ CS 1
  $ top plate:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=6  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOCR TOC   #TT
       TOC  TOCL  #TT
  $ WEB:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=7  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOC  BOC   #TW
  $ bottom slab
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=8  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       BOCR BOC   #TB
       BOC  BOCL  #TB
  $ without concrete ! 'steel part alone' $ "real"
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:1
HEAD Steel composite bridge - t beam philosophy
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIR POSZ GDIV 10000
NODE  9 X  0   8 0 $ linke untere Ecke der Platte $ left lower edge of the slab
NODE 24 X 11  -8 0 $ linke obere  Ecke der Platte $ left upper edge of the slab
NODE NO NR1 NR2    Y
     10   9  24   6.50 $ Lagerachse 1             $ Bearing axis 1
     11   =   =   5.50 $ Lagerachse 2             $ Bearing axis 2
     12   =   =   4.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     13   =   =   3.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     14   =   =   2.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     15   =   =   1.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     16   =   =   0.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     17   =   =  -0.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     18   =   =  -1.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     19   =   =  -2.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     20   =   =  -3.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     21   =   =  -4.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     22   =   =  -5.50 $ Lagerachse ...           $ Bearing axis ...
     23   =   =  -6.50 $ Kante der Voute          $ Edge of haunche
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 99 DNO 100 DX 0.30
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 99 DNO 200 DX 0.30+21.0
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 99 DNO 300 DX 0.30+21.0+0.30
let#3 #depthsitu*0.001 $ dicker Plattenbereich                $ Thick slab area
$
GRP 40
let#1 9 $ left node 1
loop 15
  let#2 #1+1 $ left node 2
  QUAD N1   N2     N3     N4     M  N T1 T2 T3 T4 MNO=1 MRF=2 POSI=BELO
      0+#1 100+#1 100+#2   0+#2  1  2 #3[m] #3[m] #3[m] #3[m] $
    100+#1 200+#1 200+#2 100+#2 16  2 #3[m] #3[m] #3[m] #3[m] $
    200+#1 300+#1 300+#2 200+#2  1  2 #3[m] #3[m] #3[m] #3[m] $

+PROG SOFILOAD URS:24
HEAD actions and loads
$ actions bridge design
$ All actions should be defined here.
$ This can be done in a separate SOFILOAD run as shown here.
ECHO ACT Full $ Please check GAMU factors, especially for L_U and L_T (in germany GAMU 1.35)
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ACT G_1
ACT G_2
ACT P
ACT C
ACT ZC  GAMU 1.00 1 SUP PERM PSI0 1.00 PSI1 1.00 PSI2 1.00           TITL '                            life load creep part'
ACT L_T GAMU   -  0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
ACT L_U GAMU   -  0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
ACT L_1 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 1'
ACT L_2 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 2'
ACT L_3 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 3'
$ The GAMU and PSI factores are taken from the .ini file depending on the design code (-> check)
$ You can also define them nanually here e.g. with:
$ ACT L_T GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
$ ACT L_U GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
  $ Superposition with ELLA traffic loading see more\csm31_design_ella.dat
  $ here SUP COND=special case, since L_U is applied in MAXIMA/AQB without inter superposition!
  $ L_1 with multiple UDL over loads in transvers direction needs EXCL, because only one to be taken
ACT SL  GAMU 1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'loading during construction'
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT FAT GAMU 1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'Fatigue LM3'
ACT SF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'possible settlement'
ACT ZF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'probable settlement'
  $ Acc. DIN FB 101 - C.2.3 for settlements GAMA=1.00.
ACT W                                                                TITL 'wind transvers'
ACT T   GAMU 0.81 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.80 PSI1 0.60 PSI2 0.50 PS1S    - TITL 'temperatur'
  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$
$ Die Kennzeichnung SUP PERM,COND,EXCL ist wichtig und richtet sich
$ je nach Definition der VerkehrslastfÃ¤lle nach:
$    SUP EXCL - von den verfÃ¼gbaren LastfÃ¤llen wird nur einer genommen
$    SUP CONC - die verfÃ¼gbaren LastfÃ¤lle werden alle genommen, falls ungÃ¼nstig wirkend
           $ Bedeutung der PSI-Werte:
           $
           $ Bruch :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
           $
           $ Selten: 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
           $ hÃ¤ufig: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
           $ quasi : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-alle
           $ nichth: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
           $
           $ nach : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
           $ siehe auch MAXIMA - Theoretische Grundlagen
$ G falls als Oberbegriff Einwirkung G die Untereinwirkungen
$ G_1 und G_2 zusammen! Ebenso faÃŸt L die L_U plus L_T zusammen!
$ Nicht aber Z die ZF und ZS, da kein Unterstrich folgt!
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ The specification SUP PERM,COND,EXCL is important and depends on
$ the definition of the traffic load cases:
$    SUP EXCL - only one of the load cases will be taken
$    SUP CONC - all of the available load cases will be taken, if infavourable effects
                      $ Meaning of the PSI-Values:
                      $
                      $ Fraction :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
                      $
                      $ Seldom: 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
                      $ Often: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
                      $ Quasi : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-any
                      $ Noth: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
                      $
                      $ According to : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
                      $ see also MAXIMA - Theoretical basis
$ G should the generic term effects G the sub effects
$ G_1 and G_2 together! L also sums up L_U plus L_T!
$ But not Z the ZF and ZS, as an underscore doesn't follow!
END

$ Im Nachweis des Grenzzustandes der TragfÃ¤higkeit sind die mÃ¶glichen Baugrundbewegungen
$ anzusetzen, bei deren Ermittlung dÃ¼rfen aber nach DIN FB 102 II-2.3.2.2(103)P
$ ohne weiteren Nachweis die 0.6-fachen Steifigkeiten des Zustandes I abgesetzt werden
$ (wegen mÃ¶glichem Ãœbergang in den Zustand II).
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ For the check of the limit state of the bearing capacity the possible soil movements
$ have to be taken into consideration, however for their determination according to DIN FB 102 II-2.3.2.2(103)P
$ the 0.6 folded rigidities of state 1 can be disregarded for this check
$ (due to possible transition into state II). According to SOFiSTiK (Dr. Bellmann)
$ the superposition has then to be applied with a load safety coefficient g=1.35.
$----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 81 TITL 'mÃ¶gl.Setzung 1+3'  TYPE SF               $ ' potential settlement'
   NODE NO (110 123 1)  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm] $ entspricht Berechnungen mit 0.6-fachen Steifigkeiten
LC 82 TITL 'mÃ¶gl.Setzung 2'    TYPE SF               $ corresponds to analysis with 0.6 folded rigidities
   NODE NO (210 223 1) TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm]
$ Im Nachweis der GrenzzustÃ¤nde der Gebrauchstauglichkeit sind die wahrscheinlichen
$ Baugrundbewegungen immer als stÃ¤ndige Einwirkung, also 1.0-fach anzusetzen,
$ siehe DIN FB 102 II-2.3.4(110)P  . Hier ist die 0.4-Abminderung nicht zulÃ¤ssig!
$ In der vorliegenden Berechnung werden 1 cm als mÃ¶gliche Setzung und 0.5 cm als
$ wahrscheinliche Setzung angesetzt, jeweils pro StÃ¼tzenachse angesetzt und ungÃ¼nstigst
$ Ã¼berlagert.
$ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ For checking the limit states of the fitnes of purpose the most probable
$ soil movements should always be applied as constant effects, therefore 1.0 folded,
$ see DIN FB 102 II-2.3.4(110)P  . Here the reduction of 0.4 is not allowed!
$ In the present analysis 1 com is applied as possible settlement and 0.5 cm are applied as probable settlement,
$ each per support axis and in the worst case superposed.
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 83 TITL 'wahr.Setzung 1+3'  TYPE ZF      $ ' true settlement'
   NODE NO (110 123 1)  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]
LC 84 TITL 'wahr.Setzung 2'    TYPE ZF
   NODE NO (210 223 1) TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]

$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

$---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

+prog template urs:6
head Results and Comparison
<text> <u><b> Results: Please notice:</u></b>

- The last CSM-AQUP plots (also coppied at the end of this file) show the stress development
   for a section in midspan. Please notice that in the last
  creep steps until infinite, the concrete shrinks
  and creates tension in the concrete: stress point PktTOPC and PktBOTC:
  This enforces a compression increase in the top steel flange stress point Pkt TOP:
- Main Listing of CSM_AQB run "Print of stresses in a cross section":
      NORMALSPANNUNGEN    [MPA]
      Q   Lastfall                N       MY       MZ  Pkt TOP  Pkt BOT
                               [kN]    [kNm]    [kNm]    [MPa]    [MPa]
      BA0 10 steel alone        0.0   130.88     0.00   -20.88    15.51
      BA0 39 concrete weig      0.0  1025.79     0.00  -163.66   121.59
      BA0 40 concrete hard     23.6  1032.14     0.20  -163.91   123.11
      BA0 45 creep+shrinka    -11.6  1050.66     0.38  -168.01   124.16
      BA0 50 g_2 asphalt,     271.3  1102.58     0.87  -167.09   139.52
      BA0 55 C+S until tra    231.2  1132.52     1.12  -173.17   141.76
      BA0 65 C+S until t-i     88.2  1214.11     1.72  -190.84   146.78
      BA0 66 C+S until t-i    -12.6  1273.83     2.14  -203.65   150.58
      BA0 67 C+S until t-i    -33.4  1287.33     2.22  -206.48   151.51
      BA0 70 traffic test    1052.3  1479.03     3.75  -201.76   209.54

Comparison of variants:
$ steel_composite_tbeam.dat : "T-beam philosophy" "Plattenbalkenphilosophie"
$ steel_composite_orto.dat  : "orto"  variant with ortotropic quad slab
$ steel_composite_real.dat  : "real"  physically correct variant with excentric steel-section
$
If you compare the stress results at the end of the input files you will see that all
stresses in the steel in the boundary girder 10 (group 10) are nearly identically.
Main differences are:
 - "real" gives physically correct forces in the pure excentric beam section:
          a tension normal force in midspan = physically correct
          The corresponding bending moment MY is related to the center of gravity of the pure beam section.
 - "orto" and "T-beam" create forces of the steel-composite-section, that means:
          N=0 and bending moment MY related to the center of gravity of the composite section.
 Nevertheless the stresses are nearly identically  -> all 3 variants can be used.

Advantages / disadvantages:

 "real"
        + gives physically best stresses (real 3-D force equilibrium)
        - Cannot be used for an ULS design of the composite section.
          Cannot be used for checks in cracked section AQB-NSTR
        - Bond force only extractable via difference of beam normalforce
          (or using double nodes with coupling springs).
        + ELLA influence analysis possible for all elements
        + Slab action optimal
        + Normalforces in the slab optimal

 "orto"
        + in longitudinal direction the loading is carried only by the beams.
        + gives forces related to the center of gravity of the composite section.
        + ULS design and cracked section checks  AQB-NSTR possible on the composite section.
        + Bond force can be plotted in WINGRAF directly.
        - Slab action not optimal - no skew main bending moments in the slab
          Single loads are carried only in transverse direction in the slab
        - transverse bending moments in the slab not very realistic
        - No normal forces in the slab

 "T-beam" with PLEX
        + in longitudinal direction the loading is carried only by the beams
          with the corrections made by the t-beam philosophy
        + gives forces related to the center of gravity of the composite section.
        + ULS design and cracked section checks  AQB-NSTR possible on the composite section.
        + Bond force can be plotted in WINGRAF directly.
        + ELLA influence analysis possible for all elements (using PLEX)
        + Slab bending action realistic
        + transverse direction in the slab realistic
        + Using PLEX also normal forces in the slab appear as in reality

 Dead load problem:
 In  "real" the dead load of the slab is activated with the activation of the quad-group.
          In construction stage 39 only the liquid concrete is load in advance.
 In  "orto" the dead load of the slab is also activated with the activation of the quad-group.
          In the same time in construction stage 40 also the concrete weight in the
          composite beam section is activated -> concrete weight would act twice!
          So via loadcase 40 the double dead load is substracted in construction stage 40.
          Liquid concret loading in advance as in "real".
 In  "T-beam" the dead load of the slab is also activated with the activation of the quad-group.
          In the same time in construction stage 40 also the concrete weight in the
          composite beam section is activated,
          but this part is automtically substracted by the t-beam philosophy!
          So no double dead load must be substracted.
          Liquid concret loading in advance as in "real".

</text>
end

+PROG Template urs:3
HEAD Variables

STO#widthsitu 2000  $ [mm] concrete width
STO#height     900  $ [mm] steel height
STO#widthtop   500  $ [mm] steel width top
STO#widthbot   500  $ [mm] steel width bottom
 $ blec thickness:
STO#TT          20  $ [mm] blec thickness on top
STO#TW          10  $ [mm] web thickness
STO#TB          30  $ [mm] blec thickness of bottom  slab

STO#AS          10  $  [cm2/m] minimum reinforcement in the in situ concrete

+PROG AQUA URS:9
HEAD Steel composite single span girder
NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X'

UNIT 2 $ mm units in AQUA (steel)
$ CTRL styp BEM

CONC 1    C  30   TITL 'in situ concrete' $ deck slab
STEE 2,3  S 500   TITL 'reinforcement'
$
STEE 4    S 355T  TITL 'shear stud connection'
$ The studs are build with a short steel plate MNO 4 and a WELD part -> shear stress gives real connection force
$ as multiple materials are used on top+bottom. Then WING-bond force is not suitable
$
STEE 6    S 355T  TITL 'top steel plate'
STEE 7    S 355   TITL 'steel web'
STEE 8    S 355T  TITL 'bottom steel plate'
$
$ Material distribution:
$
$   *-------------- y <-----*-----------------------*
$   *                       z                       *
$   *                                               *
$   *===============================================*       in situ concrete
$   *     1+3               4      1+3              *     4 shear stud connection WELD
$   *                       4                       *     4 " little PLAT -> shear stress gives real connection force
$   *-----------------------------------------------*
$                     ---6-----6---                         top blec
$                           |
$                           |
$                           7                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     ---8-----8---                         bottom blec

CTRL RFCS 2 $ consider reinforcement for stiffness

SECT  1  MNO 6 MRF 3 TITL  'steel composite'
SV  AK .1 $
$
$
$   *-------------- y <---*TOPC---------------------*       top blec upper layer (z=0)
$   *                                               *
$   *SITR==================SITU=================SITL*
$   *                       | MNR 4 WELD            *       shear stud connection
$   *                      LNAX                     *
$   *                       | MNR 4 PLAT            *       short steel plate
$   *----------------------BOTC---------------------*       TOP = top blec upper layer = bottom concrete BOTC
$                     TOCR-TOC-TOCL                         top blec center line  C=centerline
$                           |
$                           |
$                           |                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     BOCR-BOC-BOCL                         bottom blec center line
$                          BOT                              bottom blec lowest layer (z=height)
$
CS 1
$  construction points:
$  concrete
SPT SITU Y  0 Z #depthsitu/2                       MNO 0 $ center in situ concrete   MNR/MNO 0 = only construction
SPT SITR Y  0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
SPT SITL Y -0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
$  steel
SPT TOP  Y  0 Z #depthsitu                         MNO 6 $ top-steel center ! MNR/MNO 6 = AQB output point
SPT TOC  Y  0 Z #TT/2                    REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ top blec center line  C=centerline
SPT TOCR Y  0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT TOCL Y -0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT BOC  Y  0 Z  #height-#TB/2           REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ variable construction point !!!!!!
SPT BOCR Y  0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOCL Y -0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOT  Y  0 Z  #height                 REFP TOP  MNO 8 $ for AQB:       MNR/MNO 8 = for AQB-output material 8

$
$ now all points of above sketch are defined and can be used for steel-parts :
$
  $ top plate:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=6  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOCR TOC   #TT
       TOC  TOCL  #TT
  $ WEB:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=7  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOC  BOC   #TW
  $ bottom slab
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=8  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       BOCR BOC   #TB
       BOC  BOCL  #TB
CS 40
  $ weld connection -> T not too thin !!!  ---------------------------------------
  $ to better check the connection shear stress between steel and concrete,
  $ we devide the connection LNAH/WELD into a connection LNAH/WELD and a short steel BLEC
  $
SPT LNAX Y  0 Z #depthsitu*0.9                     MNO 4 $ shear connection point
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=4  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOC  LNAX   50
  WELD REFA REFE   T           MNO=4  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       LNAX SITU  -50 $ negative for studs
  $ in situ concrete: -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PANE REFA REFE MNO  AS     LAY TORS T  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0 MRF=3 $ in situ concrete
       SITR SITU 1   #AS/100  M1 PASS #depthsitu
       SITU SITL 1   #AS/100  M1 PASS #depthsitu
  SPT  TOPC Y 0 Z 0           MNO 1      $ for AQB: TOPS=top-Situ  MNR/MNO .. = for AQB-output material ..
  SPT  BOTC Y 0 Z #depthsitu  MNO 1      $ for AQB: TOPS=top-Situ  MNR/MNO .. = for AQB-output material ..
                                         $ concrete AQB points defined later because in later CS construction set !!!!
END

+PROG AQUA URS:9
HEAD Steel composite section thin walled

$

$
STEE 6    S 450T  TITL 'top steel plate'
STEE 7    S 450T  TITL 'steel web'
STEE 8    S 450T  TITL 'bottom steel plate'
$
$ Material distribution:
$
$   *-------------- y <-----*-----------------------*
$   *                       z                       *
$   *                                               *
$   *===============================================*       in situ concrete
$   *     1+3               |      1+3              *
$   *                       4                       *       shear stud connection
$   *-----------------------------------------------*
$                     ---6-----6---                         top blec
$                           |
$                           |
$                           7                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     ---8-----8---                         bottom blec
