STO#depthsitu  350  $ [mm] in situ deck concrete
STO#widthsitu 1000  $ [mm] concrete width
STO#height     600  $ [mm] steel height
STO#widthtop   500  $ [mm] steel width top
STO#widthbot   500  $ [mm] steel width bottom
 $ blec thickness:
STO#TT          20  $ [mm] blec thickness on top
STO#TW          10  $ [mm] web thickness
STO#TB          30  $ [mm] blec thickness of bottom  slab

SECT  1  MNO 6 MRF 3 TITL  'steel composite'
SV  AK .1 $ ohne Torsionssteifigkeit !
$
$
$   *-------------- y <---*TOPC---------------------*       top blec upper layer (z=0)
$   *                                               *
$   *SITR==================SITU=================SITL*
$   *                       | MNR 4 LNAH            *       shear stud connection
$   *                      LNAX                     *
$   *                       | MNR 4 BLEC            *       shear stud connection
$   *-----------------------*-----------------------*       top blec upper layer (z=0)
$                     TOCR-TOC-TOCL                         top blec center line  C=centerline
$                           |
$                           |
$                           |                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     BOCR-BOC-BOCL                         bottom blec center line
$                          BOT                              bottom blec lowest layer (z=height)
$
CS 1
$ do not use CS 0 here, CS 0 is always a complete cross section!
$ Best use CS 1 as first CS (do not start e.g. with CS 10)
$  construction points:
$  concrete
SPT SITU Y  0 Z #depthsitu/2                       MNO 0 $ center in situ concrete   MNR 0 = only construction
SPT SITR Y  0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
SPT SITL Y -0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
$  steel
SPT TOP  Y  0 Z #depthsitu                         MNO 6 $ top-steel center ! MNO 6 = AQB output point
SPT TOC  Y  0 Z #TT/2                    REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ top blec center line  C=centerline
SPT TOCR Y  0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT TOCL Y -0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT BOC  Y  0 Z  #height-#TB/2           REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ variable construction point !!!!!!
SPT BOCR Y  0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOCL Y -0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOT  Y  0 Z  #height                 REFP TOP  MNO 8 $ for AQB:       MNR 8 = for AQB-output material 8

$
$ now all points of above sketch are defined and can be used for steel-parts :
$
  $ top plate:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=6  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOCR TOC   #TT
       TOC  TOCL  #TT
  $ WEB:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=7  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOC  BOC   #TW
  $ bottom slab
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=8  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       BOCR BOC   #TB
       BOC  BOCL  #TB
CS 40
  $ weld connection -> T not too thin !!!  ---------------------------------------
  $ to better check the connection shear stress between steel and concrete,
  $
  $ we devide the connection WELD into a connection WELD and a short steel PLAT
SPT LNAX Y  0 Z #depthsitu*0.9                     MNO 4 $ shear connection point
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=4  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOC  LNAX   50
  WELD REFA REFE   T           MNO=4  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       LNAX SITU  -50 $ negative for bold connections
  $ in situ concrete: -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PANE REFA REFE MNO  AS     LAY TORS T  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0 MRF=3 $ in situ concrete
       SITR SITU 1   #AS/100  M1 PASS #depthsitu
       SITU SITL 1   #AS/100  M1 PASS #depthsitu
  SPT  TOPC Y 0 Z 0           MNO 1      $ for AQB: TOPS=top-Situ  MNR .. = for AQB-output material ..
  SPT  BOTC Y 0 Z #depthsitu  MNO 1      $ for AQB: TOPS=top-Situ  MNR .. = for AQB-output material ..
                                         $ concrete AQB points defined later because in later CS construction set !!!!

ACT L_1 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 1'
ACT L_2 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 2'
ACT L_3 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 3'
$ The GAMU and PSI factores are taken from the .ini file depending on the design code (-> check)
$ You can also define them nanually here e.g. with:
$ ACT L_T GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'

  $ Superposition with ELLA traffic loading see more\csm31_design_ella.dat
  $ here SUP COND=special case, since L_U is applied in MAXIMA/AQB without inter superposition!
  $ L_1 with multiple UDL over loads in transvers direction needs EXCL, because only one to be taken
ACT SL  GAMU 1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'loading during construction'
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT FAT GAMU 1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'Fatigue LM3'
ACT SF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'possible settlement'
ACT ZF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'probable settlement'
  $ Acc. DIN FB 101 - C.2.3 for settlements GAMA=1.00.
ACT W                                                                TITL 'wind transvers'
ACT T   GAMU 0.81 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.80 PSI1 0.60 PSI2 0.50 PS1S    - TITL 'temperatur'
  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$
$ Die Kennzeichnung SUP PERM,COND,EXCL ist wichtig und richtet sich
$ je nach Definition der VerkehrslastfÃ¤lle nach:
$    SUP EXCL - von den verfÃ¼gbaren LastfÃ¤llen wird nur einer genommen
$    SUP CONC - die verfÃ¼gbaren LastfÃ¤lle werden alle genommen, falls ungÃ¼nstig wirkend
           $ Bedeutung der PSI-Werte:
           $
           $ Bruch :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
           $
           $ Selten: 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
           $ hÃ¤ufig: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
           $ quasi : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-alle
           $ nichth: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
           $
           $ nach : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
           $ siehe auch MAXIMA - Theoretische Grundlagen
$ G falls als Oberbegriff Einwirkung G die Untereinwirkungen
$ G_1 und G_2 zusammen! Ebenso faÃŸt L die L_U plus L_T zusammen!
$ Nicht aber Z die ZF und ZS, da kein Unterstrich folgt!
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ The specification SUP PERM,COND,EXCL is important and depends on
$ the definition of the traffic load cases:
$    SUP EXCL - only one of the load cases will be taken
$    SUP CONC - all of the available load cases will be taken, if infavourable effects
                      $ Meaning of the PSI-Values:
                      $
                      $ Fraction :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
                      $
                      $ Seldom: 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
                      $ Often: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
                      $ Quasi : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-any
                      $ Noth: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
                      $
                      $ According to : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
                      $ see also MAXIMA - Theoretical basis
$ G should the generic term effects G the sub effects
$ G_1 and G_2 together! L also sums up L_U plus L_T!
$ But not Z the ZF and ZS, as an underscore doesn't follow!
END

$ Tandemsystem : Fahrstreifen 1:Radlast 150 kN/Rad TS=SOFILOAD-TYP L !
$                  GesamtÃ¼berlast=600 kN
$                Fahrstreifen 2:Radlast 100 kN/Rad
$                  GesamtÃ¼berlast=400 kN
$ =======================================================================
$ Tandem system : Lan 1:Wheel load 150 kN/wheel TS=SOFILOAD-TYP L !
$                  Total over load=600 kN
$                Lane 2:Wheel load 100 kN/wheel
$                  Total over load=400 kN

$ Fall A Fahrstreifen 1 ist rechts:  $ Case A Lane 1 is on right side:
let#lf 301
let#ys1 6.20-1.50      $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 1 $ middle lane 1
let#ys2 6.20-1.50-3.00 $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 2 $ middle lane 2
loop#1 10
 LC #lf TITL 'TS_Ãœberlast'   TYPE L_T ; let#lf #lf+1 ; let#x1 3.50+#1*2.0 $ erste Achse  $ first axis
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1      Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 1         $ 1. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 1         $ 2. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1      Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 2         $ 1. Axis lane 2
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 2         $ 2. Axis lane 2
endloop
$ Fall B Fahrstreifen 1 mittig!                      $ Case B lane 1 is in the middle!
let#ys1 0.0      $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 1             $ Middle lane 1
let#ys2 0.00-3.00 $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 2             $ Middle lane 2
loop#1 10
 LC #lf TITL 'TS_Ãœberlast'   TYPE L_T ; let#lf #lf+1 ; let#x1 6.00+#1*2.0 $ erste Achse $ first axis
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1      Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 1  $ 1. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 1  $ 2. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1      Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 2  $ 1. Axis lane 2
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 2  $ 2. Axis lane 2
endloop
$ Fall C Fahrstreifen 1 ist links:                   $ Case C lane 1 is at left:
let#ys1 -6.20+1.50      $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 1       $ Middle lane 1
let#ys2 -6.20+1.50+3.00 $ Mitte Fahrstreifen 2       $ Middle lane 2
loop#1 10
 LC #lf TITL 'TS_Ãœberlast'   TYPE L_T ; let#lf #lf+1 ; let#x1 7.90+#1*2.0 $ erste Achse $ first axis
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1      Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 1  $ 1. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 1  $ 2. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1      Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 1. Achse Fahrstreifen 2  $ 1. Axis lane 2
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $ 2. Achse Fahrstreifen 2  $ 2. Axis lane 2
endloop

$ Im Nachweis des Grenzzustandes der TragfÃ¤higkeit sind die mÃ¶glichen Baugrundbewegungen
$ anzusetzen, bei deren Ermittlung dÃ¼rfen aber nach DIN FB 102 II-2.3.2.2(103)P
$ ohne weiteren Nachweis die 0.6-fachen Steifigkeiten des Zustandes I abgesetzt werden
$ (wegen mÃ¶glichem Ãœbergang in den Zustand II).
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ For the check of the limit state of the bearing capacity the possible soil movements
$ have to be taken into consideration, however for their determination according to DIN FB 102 II-2.3.2.2(103)P
$ the 0.6 folded rigidities of state 1 can be disregarded for this check
$ (due to possible transition into state II). According to SOFiSTiK (Dr. Bellmann)
$ the superposition has then to be applied with a load safety coefficient g=1.35.
$----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 81 TITL 'mÃ¶gl.Setzung 1+3'  TYPE SF               $ ' potential settlement'
   NODE NO (110 123 1)  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm] $ entspricht Berechnungen mit 0.6-fachen Steifigkeiten
LC 82 TITL 'mÃ¶gl.Setzung 2'    TYPE SF               $ corresponds to analysis with 0.6 folded rigidities
   NODE NO (210 223 1) TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm]
$ Im Nachweis der GrenzzustÃ¤nde der Gebrauchstauglichkeit sind die wahrscheinlichen
$ Baugrundbewegungen immer als stÃ¤ndige Einwirkung, also 1.0-fach anzusetzen,
$ siehe DIN FB 102 II-2.3.4(110)P  . Hier ist die 0.4-Abminderung nicht zulÃ¤ssig!
$ In der vorliegenden Berechnung werden 1 cm als mÃ¶gliche Setzung und 0.5 cm als
$ wahrscheinliche Setzung angesetzt, jeweils pro StÃ¼tzenachse angesetzt und ungÃ¼nstigst
$ Ã¼berlagert.
$ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ For checking the limit states of the fitnes of purpose the most probable
$ soil movements should always be applied as constant effects, therefore 1.0 folded,
$ see DIN FB 102 II-2.3.4(110)P  . Here the reduction of 0.4 is not allowed!
$ In the present analysis 1 com is applied as possible settlement and 0.5 cm are applied as probable settlement,
$ each per support axis and in the worst case superposed.
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 83 TITL 'wahr.Setzung 1+3'  TYPE ZF      $ ' true settlement'
   NODE NO (110 123 1)  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]
LC 84 TITL 'wahr.Setzung 2'    TYPE ZF
   NODE NO (210 223 1) TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]

$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LC 85 TITL 'T OBEN  WAERMER'   TYPE T
   QUAD GRP  40             TYPE DTZ P  -7.9 $ positive DTZ = higher Temp. in pos. z
   BEAM GRP (10 #GRPLAST 1) TYPE DTZ PA -7.9
LC 86 TITL 'T UNTEN WAERMER'   TYPE T
   QUAD GRP  40             TYPE DTZ P  +5.0 $ positive DTZ = higher Temp. in pos. z
   BEAM GRP (10 #GRPLAST 1) TYPE DTZ PA +5.0
$ Achtung: wegen der vielen Lager in Querrichtung erzeugt die Temperatur auch
$ starke Querbiegemomente (die vier Lager unterdrÃ¼cken eine QuerkrÃ¼mmung).
$ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ Attention: due to the numerous structural bearings in transverse direction the temperature also creates
$ strong transverse bending moments (the four bearings suppres a transverse curvature).
$---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END

+PROG SOFILOAD URS:4
HEAD
LC 101 TITL 'temp top-aligned Z0=0'
  QUAD GRP 1 TYPE 'T'  1 Z0  0.00[m]  35 $$
                           1.000[m]   5
  $ In all elements you now have 35 degree on the top surface,
  $ at the bottom side the temperature is varying and depending on the quad thickness,
  $ see animator element-info layer-temperature
  $ This absolute temperature acts taking into accout the erection temperature of 20 degree (ASE-CTRL-NLAY-V3)

LC 102 TITL 'temp bottom-aligned Zend=0'
  QUAD GRP 1 TYPE 'T'  1 Z0 -1.00[m]  35 $$
                            0.00[m]   5
  $ In all elements you now have 5 degree at the bottom surface,
  $ at the upper side the temperature is varying and depending on the quad thickness.

LC 103 TITL 'temperature stretched'
  QUAD GRP 1 TYPE 'T'  1 Z0 -0.20[m]  35 $$
                           +0.20[m] 5
  $ In all elements you now have 35 degree on the top surface and 5 degree at the bottom.
  $ independant of the quad thickness.

$ Please also notice the nice Temp input in t_beam_bridge_excentrict.dat -> CSM-Temperature
END
<TEXT> SOFILOAD manual:
Their are three cases to be distinguished: If
all ordinates are positive, they are referred absolutely to the uppermost fibre of
the QUAD-element, if they are all negative they are referred to the lowermost
fibre. In all othe cases the reference is the mid surface of the QUAD element. If
the real thickness of the QUAD element does not match the load definition, the
definition will be scaled with a warning for the third case.
</TEXT>

$ A .pdf for nonlinear temperature is available in ase.dat\...\special\quads_on_fire_1.pdf

<TEXT> Remarks:
Please notice that no forces or stresses occur in loadcase 101! Only a constant curvature
is created. This represents a temperature loading on a beam section.

If you open Animator loadcase 101 please double klick a thin element.
Then change "stress in x+y direction" into "layer temperature" . Compare with thick element.
See also report browser - Layerelement - Stresses

Further explanations to SOFILOAD-TEMP see ase.dat\english\nonlinear_quad\quads_on_fire.dat
</TEXT>

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD T-beam bridge excentric
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ CTRL styp BEM
echo mat,sect full
!*!Label Material
CONC  1    C    40  $ = C40/50
STEE  2    S 500    $ standard reinforcement steel 500
STEE  7    S  '235' $ TMAX  0 $ structural steel for tubes, rolled steel ...
STEE 11    Y '1860A' $ prestessing steel
                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2
                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max
STEE 12    Y '1860A' $ prestessing steel

!*!Label Section 1
SECT  1 MNO  1
#define section
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT no    Y        Z    EXP
     1  0.00[m] 0.00[m] 0.50 $ air contact
     2 -3.00[m] 0.00[m] 1.00 $ for all following points
     3 -3.00[m] 0.25[m]
     4 -2.50[m] 0.25[m]
     5 -0.80[m] 0.45[m]
     6 -0.80[m] 1.80[m]
let#zmax   1800 $ mm
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$                |
$     *----------|----------*     #ztop
$     |          |<--#ytop->|
$     |          |          |
$     |          |          |
$     |          |<--#ybot->|
$     *----------|----------*     #zbot
$                z
  let#ytop  720 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#ybot  720 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox below
  let#ztop  110 $ [mm] z-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#zbot #zmax-110 $ "       of Torsionsbox below
LAY 0 'TORS' type min $ default for reinforcement layers
LAY 1 'BOT'  type opt $ 'bot' lower reinforcement 'bot'
LAY 2 'TOP'  type opt $ 'top' upper reinforcement 'top'
RF Y #ytop,-#ytop Z #ztop AS 10[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
RF Y #ybot,-#ybot Z #zbot AS 10[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
$ bending reinforcement:
  let#ytop 2500 $ [mm]
  let#ybot  650 $ [mm]
  let#ztop   70 $ [mm]
  let#zbot #zmax-70
RF Y #ytop,#ytop/3,-#ytop/3,-#ytop Z #ztop AS 10[cm2] LAY 2 TORS pass D  20 $ above
RF Y #ybot,#ybot/3,-#ybot/3,-#ybot Z #zbot AS 10[cm2] LAY 1 TORS pass D  20 $ below
CUT 1 ZB  450    MNO 1        LAY 1 $ By  x=3.80 m of the support above the tendon
CUT 2 ZB  700    MNO 1        LAY 1 $ By  x=3.80 m of the support underneath the tendon
CUT 3 YB  820    MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN  $ belt
CTRL WARN 10463
SPT    NO    Y        Z     MNO
     'TOP'   0        0      1
     'BOT'   0       #zmax   1 $ input literal BOT in kapitel letters
     'SIDE' 3000[mm] #zmax   1 $ noneffective part
#enddef
#include section
NEFF YMIN -9000 YMAX -2900  ZMIN -1000 ZMAX +9000 type Z
NEFF YMIN  2900 YMAX  9000  ZMIN -1000 ZMAX +9000 type Z

SECT  2 MNO  1   $ Noneffective width over middle support
#include section
NEFF ymin -9000 ymax -1850  zmin -1000 zmax +9000 type Z
NEFF ymin  1800 ymax  9000  zmin -1000 zmax +9000 type Z


!*!Label Section 5
SECT  5 MNO  1  TITL 'crossgirder end support'
let#bslab05 1.00 ; let#bweb05 0.80
#define crossgirder
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT no    Y        Z    EXP
     1  0.00[m] 0.00[m] 0.50 $ air contact
     2 -#bslab05[m] 0.00[m] 1.00 $ for all following points
     3 -#bslab05[m] 0.35[m]
     5 -#bweb05[m]  0.35[m]
     6 -#bweb05[m]  2.00[m]
let#zmax   2000 $ mm
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$                |
$     *----------|----------*     #ztop
$     |          |<--#ytop->|
$     |          |          |
$     |          |          |
$     |          |<--#ybot->|
$     *----------|----------*     #zbot
$                z
  let#ytop  720 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#ybot  720 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox below
  let#ztop  110 $ [mm] z-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#zbot #zmax-110 $ "       of Torsionsbox below
LAY 0 'TORS' type min $ default for reinforcement layers
LAY 1 'BOT'  type opt $ 'bot' lower reinforcement 'bot'
LAY 2 'TOP'  type opt $ 'top' upper reinforcement 'top'
RF Y #ytop,-#ytop Z #ztop AS 10[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
RF Y #ybot,-#ybot Z #zbot AS 10[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
$ bending reinforcement:
  let#ytop  900 $ [mm]
  let#ybot  650 $ [mm]
  let#ztop   70 $ [mm]
  let#zbot #zmax-70
RF Y #ytop,#ytop/3,-#ytop/3,-#ytop Z #ztop AS 10[cm2] LAY 2 TORS pass D  20 $ above
RF Y #ybot,#ybot/3,-#ybot/3,-#ybot Z #zbot AS 10[cm2] LAY 1 TORS pass D  20 $ below
CUT 1 ZB  370    MNO 1        LAY 1 $ By  x=3.80 m of the support above the tendon
CUT 2 ZB  900    MNO 1        LAY 1 $ By  x=3.80 m of the support underneath the tendon
CTRL WARN 10463
SPT    NO    Y        Z     MNO
     'TOP'   0        0      1
     'BOT'   0       #zmax   1 $ input literal BOT in kapitel letters
#enddef
#include crossgirder

SECT  6 MNO  1  TITL 'crossgirder middle support'
let#bslab05 1.40 ; let#bweb05 1.00
#include crossgirder

!*!Label Section 9
SREC 9 H 1.5[m] B 4[m] TITL 'piers'

SECT 99 MNO  1 TITL 'Test section for ex_q '
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT no    Y        Z    EXP
     1  0.00[m] 0.00[m] 0.50 $ air contact
     2 -3.00[m] 0.00[m] 1.00 $ for all following points
     3 -3.00[m] 0.25[m]
     4 -2.50[m] 0.25[m]
     5 -0.80[m] 0.45[m]
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:4
HEAD T-beam bridge excentric
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC GDIR POSZ GDIV 1000
NODE  1 X  0   6 0 $ left lower edge of the slab
NODE 13 X  8  -6 0 $ left upper edge of the slab
sto#dxdy 8/12 $ dx/dy bridge angle for traffic loads
NODE NO NR1 NR2    Y
      2   1  13   5.50 $ edge of haunch
      3   1  13   3.80 $ web corner
      4   1  13   3.00 $ beam center
      5   1  13   2.20 $ web corner
      6   1  13   0.50 $ edge of haunch
      7   1  13   0.00 $ bridge center
      8   1  13  -0.50 $ edge of haunch
      9   1  13  -2.20 $ web corner
     10   1  13  -3.00 $ beam center
     11   1  13  -3.80 $ web corner
     12   1  13  -5.50 $ edge of haunch
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 13 DNO 100 DX 1.00
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 13 DNO 200 DX 1.00+25.0
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 13 DNO 300 DX 1.00+30.0
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 13 DNO 400 DX 1.00+30.0+5.0
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 13 DNO 500 DX 1.00+30.0+30.0
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 13 DNO 600 DX 1.00+30.0+30.0+1.00
$
TRAN NODE FROM 104,304,504 DNO 1000 DZ 2.20  $ pier head
TRAN NODE FROM 107,307,507 DNO 1000 DZ 2.20
TRAN NODE FROM 110,310,510 DNO 1000 DZ 2.20
TRAN NODE FROM 107,307,507 DNO 2000 DZ 8.00  $ pier bottom

node 2107,2307,2507 fix F

let#1 250 $ Thickness at cantilever end
let#2 450 $ Thickness at cantilever section
let#3 450 $ Thick slab area
GRP 3 titl 'slab'
let#k 0 ; let#m  1
#define slab
QUAD N1     N2     N3     N4      M  N T1 T2 T3 T4 MNO=1 MRF=2 POSI=BELO
      1+#k 101+#k 102+#k   2+#k  #m  1 #1 #1 #1 #1 $ cantilever
      2+#k 102+#k 103+#k   3+#k  #m  2 #1 #1 #2 #2 $ haunch
      3+#k 103+#k 104+#k   4+#k  #m  1 #3 #3 #3 #3 $ web
      4+#k 104+#k 105+#k   5+#k  #m  1 #3 #3 #3 #3 $ web
      5+#k 105+#k 106+#k   6+#k  #m  2 #2 #2 #1 #1 $ haunch
      6+#k 106+#k 107+#k   7+#k  #m  1 #1 #1 #1 #1 $ cantilever
      7+#k 107+#k 108+#k   8+#k  #m  1 #1 #1 #1 #1 $ Cantilever
      8+#k 108+#k 109+#k   9+#k  #m  2 #1 #1 #2 #2 $ haunch
      9+#k 109+#k 110+#k  10+#k  #m  1 #3 #3 #3 #3 $ web
     10+#k 110+#k 111+#k  11+#k  #m  1 #3 #3 #3 #3 $ web
     11+#k 111+#k 112+#k  12+#k  #m  2 #2 #2 #1 #1 $ haunch
     12+#k 112+#k 113+#k  13+#k  #m  1 #1 #1 #1 #1 $ cantilever
#enddef
#include slab
let#k 100 ; let#m 12
#include slab
let#k 200 ; let#m  4
#include slab
let#k 300 ; let#m  4
#include slab
let#k 400 ; let#m 12
#include slab
let#k 500 ; let#m  1
#include slab

!+!Kapitel Define Excentric T-beam philosophy !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
+PROG ASE urs:3
HEAD T-beam philosophy definition
TBEX NOG AUTO $ Activates T-beam philosophy 2020 also for excentric beam elements - cathes also group 5+6 cross girderes
TBEX NOG 1  neff 0.01 $ superstructure_beams midspan
TBEX NOG 2  neff 0.22 $ superstructure_beams middle support
       $ NEFF is used to scale the bending moments over the inner columns:
       $ for this best calculate LC 8+9 (9=beams without quads : 8=PLEX) and then:
       $ a bigger NEFF       in midspan reduces the beam        midspan moment in LC 8
       $ a bigger NEFF over the columns reduces the beam middle support moment in LC 8
       $ Best do not touch all other parameter, only in case you get
       $ instability, then first F_GZ

       $  YOUTUBE Video  ->   https://youtu.be/GoT1f0aGdgs         SOFiSTiK T-beam philosophy    How to model a T-beam or composite beam


             $ The neff factor takes into account that the compression in the quad slab
             $ cannot immediately reach the quad boundary and outer parts and so the slab
             $ is not fully acting, especially over inner supports.
             $ This represents the effect of non acting width in the a section.
             $ Please look to the quad principle normal forces in loadcase 8 for this effect.
             $ The neff factor has been adjusted here with the help of test loadcase 7 and 8
             $ by comparing the beam bending moment in loadcase 7 and 8.
             $
             $ Only in case the automatic extraction of the average deck slab thickness does not work properly  (->report listing)
             $ you can also input the area and excentricity exactly, e.g.
             $ TBEX NOG 1 area 2.16[m2] ex_q 0.188[m] neff 0.01
             $     (please input area and ex_q with dimensions)
             $ area 2.16[m2] and ex_q here taken from test section 99
             $          = 2*(0.80*0.45+1.70*0.35+0.50*0.25)[m2]
             $ But to scale the dead load bending moment better use NEFF
             $
             $ If you do not like these manipulations you could also try to run the quad slab
             $ without normal force stiffness (GRP2 3 QUEA 1E-6)
             $
             $ NEFF definition see also test example t_beam_excentric_test.dat
<TEXT>
The TBEX definition should be made in a separate ASE run just following the system definition.
All following ASE runs then use this definion without new TBEX input, also in a CSM run
or an ASE induced by a SSD task (eigenvalue task).
</TEXT>
END

ACT SF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'possible settlement ULS'
ACT ZF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'probable settlement SLS'
  $ Acc. DIN FB 101 - C.2.3 for settlements GAMA=1.00.
ACT W                                                                TITL 'wind transvers'
ACT T   GAMU 0.81 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.80 PSI1 0.60 PSI2 0.50 PS1S    - TITL 'temperatur'
  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT B   GAMU 1.35 1 PART G SUP PERM PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'construction stage'
END

+prog CSM urs:20
head Temperature
<TEXT> Special treatment using TBEX
A statically determined supported bridge superstructure shall not get internal restraint stresses.
All elements shall get a constant curvature - and at the same time in the cross direction (double curvature).

You best fix the curvature for the most important element, here the superstructure beam with a heigth of 1.80 m.
If we want to apply e.g. a dT/h of +7Â°C we have to apply 7Â°/1.80m.
In the height of the center of gravity of the main girder at  SM=0.656 m no longitudinal strain shall occur,
dt shall be 0.0 there. This leads to a surface temperature of -0.656m*7Â°/1.80m = -2.53Â°

To get the same curvature in the 0.45m thick slab we must apply only 1.75Â°/0.45m (=7Â°/1.80m).
The 0.25m thick slab may only get 1.00Â°/0.25m.
To get the same longitudinal elongation on the top of the bridge we get:
- top of main beam   -2.53Â°C      bottom +4.47Â°C
- top 0.25m slab     -2.53Â°C      bottom -1.53Â°C   (-2.53+1.00)
- top 0.45m slab     -2.53Â°C      bottom -0.78Â°C   (-2.53+1.75)

A uniform temperature TN must be added constant of course.

Such a temperature on a haunched quad can be input in absolute temperatures with  QUAD TYPE 'T'.
But this is quit complicated and so we implemented a feature in CSM to define such a temperature field:
</TEXT>

<TEXT> Additional Explanations

According to EN1991-1-5 chapter 6 temperature loads belong to the variable actions.


Constant temparature (relative to erection temperature T0)
  delta TN,con = dT    =      -27.0Â°C  (con...contraction) Te,min=-17Â°C - T0=+10Â°C erection
  delta TN,exp = dT    =      +27.0Â°C  (exp...expansion)   Te,max= 37Â°C - T0=+10Â°C erection

A temperature gradient will be applied according to table 6.1
  delta TM,heat = DTZ  =   12.3Â°C  top surface warmer (15*0.82)
                                   including surface factor k_sur 0.82
  delta TM,cool = DTZ  =   -8.0Â°C  bottom surface warmer

Positive values of DTY and DTZ mean that the temperature raises in the positive
direction of the corresponding Y resp.  Z axis.  This load type is only applicable
for sections having a distinct extension or geometry

  ---> x |===============|  Top = 40Â°C
  |      |               |
  |      |===============|
  V  z   |               |  DTZ = 30Â°C - 40Â°C = -10Â°C
         |               |
         |               |
         |===============|  Bottom = 30Â°C

A simultaneous application of constant and variable temperature results in
8 combination according to EN1991-1-5 chapter 6.1.5:
   delta TN    + wm*delta TM and
   wn*delta TN + delta TM

The combination factors are:
             wn =     0.35
             wm =     0.75
</TEXT>

TEMP LC 90      TN +27.0*1.00     DT -12.3*0.75   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T summer posdt TN+wm*dT' $ top=hot
TEMP LC 91      TN +27.0*1.00     DT  +8.0*0.75   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T summer negdt TN+wm*dT' $ top=cold

TEMP LC 92      TN -27.0*1.00     DT -12.3*0.75   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T winter posdt TN+wm*dT'
TEMP LC 93      TN -27.0*1.00     DT  +8.0*0.75   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T winter negdt TN+wm*dT'

TEMP LC 94      TN +27.0*0.35     DT -12.3*1.00   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T summer posdt wn*TN+dT'
TEMP LC 95      TN +27.0*0.35     DT  +8.0*1.00   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T summer negdt wn*TN+dT'

TEMP LC 96      TN -27.0*0.35     DT -12.3*1.00   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T winter posdt wn*TN+dT'
TEMP LC 97      TN -27.0*0.35     DT  +8.0*1.00   HM 1.80[m]    SM 0.656[m]  GRP 1 TO 6  TITL 'T winter negdt wn*TN+dT'

CTRL FILE 'temp' $ filename for the created input file
END

!#!Kapitel CSM Stage Analysis

+PROG ELLA urs:42.1
HEAD Traffic over influence lines evaluation - UDL+TS part

ECHO LPOS $ for following SOFILOAD COPY ELLA
ECHO EVAL,RES no
$ ECHO stat extr $ to show what ELLA is doing

LSEL 'AX_1' INT 7 DZ 0.1
$ ------------------------ evaluation for beam forces:  ---------------------------
CALC MY  1  2     $ definition of loadcase sub-numbers 1-12
CALC VZ  3  4   $ to save time only MY + VZ
$ CALC MT  5  6
$ CALC  N  7  8
$ CALC MZ  9 10
$ CALC VY 11 12
$ ------------------------ evaluation for beam forces:  ---------------------------

CALC MXX LMAX 1  2 $ definition of loadcase sub-numbers 1-12
CALC MYY LMAX 3  4 $ to save time only MXX + MYY
$ CALC VXX LMAX 5  6
$ CALC VYY LMAX 7  8
$ ------------------------ evaluation for beam forces:  ---------------------------

$  Here three lanes are placed on the width!  - so AX_1.10 to AX_1.12 must be loaded !
SAVE TYPE L_U LCB 850 TITL 'ELLA-UDL'          $ 850 = head number of envelope UDL
    CASE 1 GRU        $ GRU = only UDL area loads
      POSL 'AX_1.10' TRAI 901 $ SYNC ON $ lane 1
      POSL 'AX_1.11' TRAI 902 $ SYNC ON $ lane 2
      POSL 'AX_1.12' TRAI 903 $ depending on country: here 3.0 kN/m UDL on lane 3
    $ POSL 'AX_1.13' TRAI 903 $ depending on country: here 3.0 kN/m UDL on lane 4
      POSL 'AX_1.0'  TRAI 909 $ only additional basic area pedestrians from WR to YRA
    CASE 2 GRU $ left: main vehicle standing left = internal lane 20:
      POSL 'AX_1.20' TRAI 901 $ SYNC ON
      POSL 'AX_1.21' TRAI 902 $ SYNC ON
      POSL 'AX_1.22' TRAI 903 $ depending on country: here 3.0 kN/m UDL on lane 3
    $ POSL 'AX_1.23' TRAI 903 $ depending on country: here 3.0 kN/m UDL on lane 4
      POSL 'AX_1.0'  TRAI 909 $ only additional basic area pedestrians from WR to YRA
SAVE TYPE L_T LCB 950 TITL 'ELLA-Tandemsystem' $ 950 = head number of envelope L_T
    CASE 1 GR0        $ GR0 = only tandem axle loads
      POSL 'AX_1.10' TRAI 901 $ SYNC ON
      POSL 'AX_1.11' TRAI 902 $ SYNC ON
      POSL 'AX_1.12' TRAI 903 $ SYNC ON
    CASE 2 GR0 $ left: main vehicle standing left = internal lane 20:
      POSL 'AX_1.20' TRAI 901 $ SYNC ON
      POSL 'AX_1.21' TRAI 902 $ SYNC ON
      POSL 'AX_1.22' TRAI 903 $ SYNC ON
      $ depending on country: here no tandem axle in lane 4
END

<TEXT> Comments to CSM DESI:
To not get confused by the huge amount of results we recommend to let them run separate (here only DESI ULTI).
Then you can better check the results separate and you have a better overview.
Using SSD you best insert multiple CSM-DESIGN tasks with only one design task each.
Using Teddy you can also open the created _gzt.dat file and run and check the results separate.
Please notice that with every CSM-DESI run also a WINGRAF .gra file is created.
In this file the actual result plots are already prepared for interactive changes (box, groups):
   Please open windows explorer and double klick on file _uls.gra
   Or open WINGRAF and from there open file _uls.gra
   Then please immediately store the .gra file under another name to keep your changes.
   Or in SSD: insert task 'Interactive graphics' and from there open file _gzt.gra
With a CSM-DESI STAN run (here at the end) you can also get an overview over the possible design tasks.
</TEXT>

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Steel composite section thin walled
!
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ CTRL styp BEM
echo mat,sect full
!*!Label Material
CONC 1    C  40  $ = C40/50
CONC 2    C  40  EC 10000 titl 'cracked'
STEE 3    S 500   TITL 'reinforcement'
$
STEE 4    S 450T  TITL 'shear stud connection'
$
STEE 6    S 450T  TITL 'top steel plate'
STEE 7    S 450T  TITL 'steel web'
STEE 8    S 450T  TITL 'bottom steel plate'

!*!Label Section 1
$
$ Material distribution:
$
$   *-------------- y <-----*-----------------------*
$   *                       z                       *
$   *                                               *
$   *===============================================*       in situ concrete
$   *     1+3               |      1+3              *
$   *                       4                       *       shear stud connection
$   *-----------------------------------------------*
$                     ---6-----6---                         top blec
$                           |
$                           |
$                           7                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     ---8-----8---                         bottom blec

CTRL RFCS 2 $ consider reinforcement for stiffness

STO#AS    10    $      cm2/m minimum reinforcement in the in situ concrete

STO#depthsitu  450  $ [mm] in situ deck concrete   at steel connection
STO#d_average  350  $ [mm] in situ deck concrete  (average deck)
STO#widthsitu 6000  $ [mm] concrete width
STO#zmax      2400 $ mm
STO#height #zmax-#depthsitu  $ [mm] steel height
STO#widthtop   400  $ [mm] steel width top
STO#widthbot   700  $ [mm] steel width bottom
 $ blec thickness:
STO#TT          22  $ [mm] blec thickness on top
STO#TW          20  $ [mm] web thickness
STO#TB          50  $ [mm] blec thickness of bottom  slab

SECT  1  MNO 6 MRF 3 TITL  'steel composite'
let#concrete 1 $ uncracked concrete
#define section
SV  AK .1 $ ohne Torsionssteifigkeit !
$
$
$   *-------------- y <---*TOPC---------------------*       top blec upper layer (z=0)
$   *                                               *
$   *SITR==================SITU=================SITL*
$   *                       | MNR 4 LNAH            *       shear stud connection
$   *                      LNAX                     *
$   *                       | MNR 4 BLEC            *       shear stud connection
$   *-----------------------*-----------------------*       top blec upper layer (z=0)
$                     TOCR-TOC-TOCL                         top blec center line  C=centerline
$                           |
$                           |
$                           |                               steel web
$                           |
$                           |
$                     BOCR-BOC-BOCL                         bottom blec center line
$                          BOT                              bottom blec lowest layer (z=height)
$
CS 1
$ do not use CS 0 here, CS 0 is always a complete cross section!
$ Best use CS 1 as first CS (do not start e.g. with CS 10)
$  construction points:
$  concrete
SPT SITU Y  0 Z #d_average/2                       MNO 0 $ center in situ concrete   MNR 0 = only construction
SPT SITR Y  0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
SPT SITL Y -0.5*#widthsitu Z 0           REFP SITU MNO 0
$  steel
SPT TOP  Y  0 Z #depthsitu                         MNO 6 $ top-steel center ! MNO 6 = AQB output point
SPT TOC  Y  0 Z #TT/2                    REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ top blec center line  C=centerline
SPT TOCR Y  0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT TOCL Y -0.5*#widthtop  Z 0           REFP TOC  MNO 0
SPT BOC  Y  0 Z  #height-#TB/2           REFP TOP  MNO 0 $ variable construction point !!!!!!
SPT BOCR Y  0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOCL Y -0.5*#widthbot  Z 0           REFP BOC  MNO 0
SPT BOT  Y  0 Z  #height                 REFP TOP  MNO 8 $ for AQB:       MNR 8 = for AQB-output material 8

$
$ now all points of above sketch are defined and can be used for steel-parts :
$
  $ top plate:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=6  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOCR TOC   #TT
       TOC  TOCL  #TT
  $ WEB:
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=7  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOC  BOC   #TW
  $ bottom slab
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=8  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       BOCR BOC   #TB
       BOC  BOCL  #TB
CS 40
  $ weld connection -> T not too thin !!!  ---------------------------------------
  $ to better check the connection shear stress between steel and concrete,
  $
  $ we devide the connection WELD into a connection WELD and a short steel PLAT
SPT LNAX Y  0 Z #depthsitu*0.9                     MNO 4 $ shear connection point
  PLAT REFA REFE   T           MNO=4  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       TOC  LNAX   50
  WELD REFA REFE   T           MNO=4  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0
       LNAX SITU  -50 $ negative for bold connections
  $ in situ concrete: -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PANE REFA REFE MNO          AS     LAY TORS T  YB=0 ZB=0 YE=0 ZE=0 MRF=3 $ in situ concrete
       SITR SITU #concrete   #AS/100  M1 PASS #d_average
       SITU SITL #concrete   #AS/100  M1 PASS #d_average
  SPT  TOPC Y 0 Z 0           MNO #concrete      $ for AQB: TOPS=top-Situ  MNR .. = for AQB-output material ..
  SPT  BOTC Y 0 Z #depthsitu  MNO #concrete      $ for AQB: TOPS=top-Situ  MNR .. = for AQB-output material ..
                                                 $ concrete AQB points defined later because in later CS construction set !!!!
SPT    NO    Y        Z     MNO
     'TOP1'   0        0      1
     'BOT1'   0       #zmax   1 $ input literal BOT in kapitel letters
     'SIDE' 3000[mm] #zmax   1 $ noneffective part
     CTRL WARN 346 $ to avoid warning: Stress point SIDE in cross section  1 construction stage  40 is inside of a non effective area.
#enddef
#include section
NEFF YMIN -9000 YMAX -2900  ZMIN -1000 ZMAX +9000 type Z
NEFF YMIN  2900 YMAX  9000  ZMIN -1000 ZMAX +9000 type Z

SECT  2  MNO 6 MRF 3 TITL  'steel composite 2' $ Noneffective width over middle support
let#concrete 2 $ cracked concrete
#include section
NEFF ymin -9000 ymax -1850  zmin -1000 zmax +9000 type Z
NEFF ymin  1800 ymax  9000  zmin -1000 zmax +9000 type Z


!*!Label Section 5
SECT  5 MNO  1  TITL 'crossgirder end support'
let#bslab05 1.00 ; let#bweb05 0.80
#define crossgirder
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT no    Y        Z    EXP
     1  0.00[m] 0.00[m] 0.50 $ air contact
     2 -#bslab05[m] 0.00[m] 1.00 $ for all following points
     3 -#bslab05[m] 0.35[m]
     5 -#bweb05[m]  0.35[m]
     6 -#bweb05[m]  2.00[m]
let#zmax   2000 $ mm
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$                |
$     *----------|----------*     #ztop
$     |          |<--#ytop->|
$     |          |          |
$     |          |          |
$     |          |<--#ybot->|
$     *----------|----------*     #zbot
$                z
  let#ytop  720 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#ybot  720 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox below
  let#ztop  110 $ [mm] z-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#zbot #zmax-110 $ "       of Torsionsbox below
LAY 0 'TORS' type min $ default for reinforcement layers
LAY 1 'BOT'  type opt $ 'bot' lower reinforcement 'bot'
LAY 2 'TOP'  type opt $ 'top' upper reinforcement 'top'
RF Y #ytop,-#ytop Z #ztop AS 10[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
RF Y #ybot,-#ybot Z #zbot AS 10[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
$ bending reinforcement:
  let#ytop  900 $ [mm]
  let#ybot  650 $ [mm]
  let#ztop   70 $ [mm]
  let#zbot #zmax-70
RF Y #ytop,#ytop/3,-#ytop/3,-#ytop Z #ztop AS 10[cm2] LAY 2 TORS pass D  20 $ above
RF Y #ybot,#ybot/3,-#ybot/3,-#ybot Z #zbot AS 10[cm2] LAY 1 TORS pass D  20 $ below
CUT 1 ZB  370    MNO 1        LAY 1 $ By  x=3.80 m of the support above the tendon
CUT 2 ZB  900    MNO 1        LAY 1 $ By  x=3.80 m of the support underneath the tendon
CTRL WARN 10463
SPT    NO    Y        Z     MNO
     'TOP'   0        0      1
     'BOT'   0       #zmax   1 $ input literal BOT in kapitel letters
#enddef
#include crossgirder

SECT  6 MNO  1  TITL 'crossgirder middle support'
let#bslab05 1.40 ; let#bweb05 1.00
#include crossgirder

!*!Label Section 9
SREC 9 H 1.5[m] B 4[m] TITL 'piers'

SECT 99 MNO  1 TITL 'Test section for ex_q '
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT no    Y        Z    EXP
     1  0.00[m] 0.00[m] 0.50 $ air contact
     2 -3.00[m] 0.00[m] 1.00 $ for all following points
     3 -3.00[m] 0.25[m]
     4 -2.50[m] 0.25[m]
     5 -0.80[m] 0.45[m]
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:8
HEAD Definition secondary group area for cracked concrete
SYST REST ; CTRL REST 2
GRP 'A1'  $ secondary group identifier
  SBOX A1X   31[m] 0 0 B1X  39[m] 0 0       A2X 39[m] -6[m] 0 B2X 31[m] 6[m] 0       T 1[m]
  $ Attention: this area for quad elements must match with the beam group defintion:
  $ means: when the beams change from material concrete 1 to 2 ,
  $        also the quads must change from stiffness factor GRP2 ... QUEA 1.0    to  GRP2 'A1' QUEA 0.3 !!!!
END

$    END

!+!Kapitel Define Excentric T-beam philosophy !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
+PROG ASE urs:3
HEAD T-beam philosophy definition
TBEX NOG AUTO $ Activates T-beam philosophy 2020 also for excentric beam elements - cathes also group 5+6 cross girderes
TBEX NOG 1  neff 0.00 $ superstructure_beams midspan
TBEX NOG 2  neff 0.01 $ superstructure_beams middle support
       $ NEFF is used to scale the bending moments over the inner columns:
       $ for this best calculate LC 8+9 (9=beams without quads : 8=PLEX) and then:
       $ a bigger NEFF       in midspan reduces the beam        midspan moment in LC 8
       $ a bigger NEFF over the columns reduces the beam middle support moment in LC 8
       $ Best do not touch all other parameter, only in case you get
       $ instability, then first F_GZ

             $ The neff factor takes into account that the compression in the quad slab
             $ cannot immediately reach the quad boundary and outer parts and so the slab
             $ is not fully acting, especially over inner supports.
             $ This represents the effect of non acting width in the a section.
             $ Please look to the quad principle normal forces in loadcase 8 for this effect.
             $ The neff factor has been adjusted here with the help of test loadcase 7 and 8
             $ by comparing the beam bending moment in loadcase 7 and 8.
             $
             $ All other parameters should not be touched. Only in case you get
             $ an instable system you can reduce F_GZ
             $
             $ Only in case the automatic extraction of the average deck slab thickness does not work properly  (->report listing)
             $ you can also input the area and excentricity exactly, e.g.
             $ TBEX NOG 1 area 2.16[m2] ex_q 0.188[m] neff 0.01
             $     (please input area and ex_q with dimensions)
             $ area 2.16[m2] and ex_q here taken from test section 99
             $          = 2*(0.80*0.45+1.70*0.35+0.50*0.25)[m2]
             $ But to scale the dead load bending moment better use NEFF
             $
             $ If you do not like these manipulations you could also try to run the quad slab
             $ without normal force stiffness (GRP2 3 QUEA 1E-6) also using TBEX
             $
             $ NEFF definition with secondary groups see also test example t_beam_excentric_test.dat
<TEXT>
Attention: the area and the excentricity should be not too big, otherwise instable systems
           can occur due to the negative stiffness of the correction beam!
           Best view the bridge in animator in global x direction, switch off the transverse girders
           and check if the beam section and the quad thickness overlap well.

The TBEX definition should be made in a separate ASE run just following the system definition.
All following ASE runs then use this definion without new TBEX input, also in a CSM run
or an ASE induced by a SSD task (eigenvalue task).
</TEXT>
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:25
HEAD
LC  2          TITL 'g_2'             TYPE none
   BEAM GRP 1,2 TYPE PZZ 3.50
LC  9          TITL 'Test beam load'  TYPE none
   BEAM GRP 1,2 TYPE PZZ 100
LC 39          TITL 'Concrete load'   TYPE none
   BEAM GRP 1,2 TYPE PZZ 0.35*6.00*25 $ 35 cm concrete
END
+PROG ASE URS:16
HEAD Comparison pure beam anaylsis - if necessary skaling NEFF input in TBEX
grp - ; grp 3 off

  LCC 9
END
HEAD
grp - ; grp 3 yes
GRP2 'A1' QUEA 0.3 $  over the middle support for cracked concrete
$ Attention: as this is a secondary group definition, this line must be input in every ASE run and in
$            the CSM input with
$
LC 8 TYPE NONE titl 'Test result with quad slab and TBEX'
  LCC 9
END      $ Please compare beam bending MY of LC 7 and LC 8 in WINGRAF
         $ and then scale NEFF until the bending moments come together

Attention: the area for quad elements must match with the beam group defintion:
means: when the beams change from material concrete 1 to 2 ,
       also the quads must change from stiffness factor GRP2 ... QUEA 1.0    to  GRP2 'A1' QUEA 0.3 !!!!
So better do not use attribute areas but better use real groups in SOFIPLUS for beams and quads to
better separate the uncracked - cracked parts!

!#!Info Example:    Voided slab
!#!Info Program:    ASE
!#!Info Keyword:    bubble deck; layer; voided slab

$  Please use animator and select loadcase 1, find element info and
$  klick an element in midspan to check layered element behaviour.
$
$ For design see bemess.dat\english\special\bubble_deck.dat

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Voided prestressed slab
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
echo mat full
CONC 1 C   30
STEE 2 S  500
STEE 3 S  235
STEE 11    Y '1860A' $ prestessing steel
                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2
                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max
CONC 8 C   30    EC 5 GAM 0.0 $ Bubble deck inner layer - without stiffness EC 5
SSLA SERV 1.00 ; let#fcr -5/1000 $definiton of work law so that it fits to EC for nonlinar analysis
SSLA    EPS     SIG       TYPE
        0       0         POL     $-------------
       -1.0    #fcr       POL     $
       -3.5    #fcr       POL     $ compressive zone
       -9.0     0
SSLA ULTI 1.50
SSLA    EPS     SIG       TYPE
        0       0         POL     $-------------
       -1.0    #fcr       POL     $
       -3.5    #fcr       POL     $ compressive zone
       -9.0     0
       $ see also bemess.dat\english\special\bubble_deck.dat
MLAY no 9 t0 0.180[m] 1 $$
          t1 0.340[m] 8 $$
          t2 0.180[m] 1
$           -------
$ total h =  0.700 m  = 0.18+0.34+0.18
$        Material number  1    8    1
$
end

+PROG TENDON urs:9
HEAD Parabolic Prestress
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ Definition of prestressing system:
$ We recommend to input all data as user defined prestressing system.
$ For the static analysis the following values are sufficient:
SYSP NOPS MAT   ZV       AZ    LITZ MINR   BETA  MUE ECC  SP     DO
        1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 82[mm] $ csm3_parabel and csm32_slab, 12 wires
      $       2* two tendons - better here than  TEND NSP 2
      $ 1  11 3078[kN] 2250[mm2] 15 7.10[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 92[mm] $            15 wires
      $ 1  11 3848[kN] 2850[mm2] 19 6.50[m] 0.3 0.21 4[mm] 3[mm] 97[mm] $ csm31_beam 19 wires
      $ 1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.0 0.00 0[mm] 0[mm] 10[mm] $ csm3_casting_yard
$
$ reference axis for all tendons = x-axis:    $ Bezugsspur = X-Achse $ Reference lane  = X-Axis
AXES NOH 1  VAL1   0.00 0.00 0.00  TYPE=poly  KIND=QUAD
         1  VAL1 100.00 0.00 0.00  TITL "X-Axis"
let#NO 1             $ number of tendon
let#y  2.7*11/18     $  y coordinate of this tendon -- Geometry

#define tendons
 TGEO   NOG #NO  NOH 1  NOPS 1
 PTUV    S      U       V      DUS  type=REFX
        #x1    #y      0.25     -
        #x1+10 #y      0.60    0.0
        #x1+20 #y      0.25     -
        #x1+22 #y      0.14    0.0
        #x1+24 #y      0.25     -
        #x1+34 #y      0.60    0.0
        #x1+44 #y      0.25
 CS ICS1 11 12                $ = construction stages
 PSIG 'RI' ANWS 9 KAPA - K3 1280 $
        $ k3 = estimated limit to reduce stress at traffic opening (after first creep+shrinkage)
        $      max-sigma-traffic opening in most cases (e.g. to EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)) -> 0.65 fpk (or 0.75 depending on design code)
 $ final tendon definition:
 TEND NOT #NO NOG #NO NTEN 2 LC 3 LC0 0  $ Attention NTEN=2 !
 let#NO #NO+1   $ fÃ¼r nÃ¤chste Nummer hochzÃ¤hlen         $ count up for the next number

!#!Info  Example:       Dynamic overview
!#!Info  Keyword:       earthquake; time step analysis; impulse; crash; impact; acceleration
!#!Info  Program:       ASE

+PROG TEMPLATE urs:1
HEAD

<TEXT>

Dynamic overview:
================================================================================================

Important:
DYNA is the specialist for modal analyis and linear dynamics.

In ASE usually nonlinear dynamic is calculated.

Therefore the complete stress state including dead load must be generated.
It is best to calculate the steady state g_1+g_2 already nonlinear but statically
and then uses this static state as primary loadcase for the nonlinear time step analysis.

As different load components must be added with or without  time functions (FUNC),
it is recommended to combined the loading in ASE with LCC.

Usage see a2_introduction_earthquake.dat and step_sofiload_ase.dat.

================================================================================================

Earthquake with modal analysis:
=============================

  - see dyna.dat\..\dyna41_three_storey_frame_resp.dat

  incl. design:
  - see ase.dat\..\dynamics\earthquake_jb.dat
  - see csm.dat\..\csm33_earthquake_bridge.dat
  - see csm.dat\..\more\csm32_earthquake_quad.dat

================================================================================================

earthquake in time step analysis (most times nonlinear):
=====================================================

  main criteria - differences:
  ==============================
  - Earthquake can be input in a load-time-table (a3_introduction_base_acceleration.dat)
  - or can be generated artificially (a2_introduction_earthquake.dat)
  - topic free field acceleration and response see a4_erdbeben_single_mass_response.dat

  - It can be applied as an acceleration of the elementes (a2_introduction_earthquake.dat)
  - or as given base point movement (ase_nstr_pld_earthquake_frame.dat)
      (in DYNA also as an acceleration of a big base point mass)

  examples:
  ==========
    - a2_introduction_earthquake.dat
      - artificial synthetic earthquake according EC2
      - using g_2 as additional mass and additional dead load
      - Using the acceleration input of SOFILOAD in ASE with LCC, the acceleration
          is applied on all system- und additional masses (acce noda 0 in SOFILOAD)
      - time step analysis on one loadcase e.g. 102
          LC 102 then contains results after N time steps)
          Storage of main results in evaluation loadcases (STEP...LCST...SELE)
          Simple continue function to add time steps
          So you can first check 50 time steps and then continue on demand
      - nonlinear quad analysis (cracked concrete quads)

    - a3_introduction_base_acceleration.dat
      - element acceleration from a given earthquake table
      - Comparison of different methods of acceleration input:
        - EFM Effective force method - acce noda 0 - system acceleration
        - LMM Large Mass Method - acce noda 1 - base point acceleration

    - a4_erdbeben_single_mass_response.dat
      - how to input the magnitude of acceleration -> RESP AG
      - AG free field acceleration and response
      - check with SDOF single degree of freedom beams - see last WING-plot

    - ase_nstr_pld_earthquake_frame.dat
      - Given earthquake acceleration table
      - Converting the acceleration values into displacement values:
          Integration of the dynamic equation in a template with
          following base line correction
          (in order to get acceptable displacements at the end)
      - Applying these displacements as given support displacements
          (base point displacement)
      - advantage: earthquake looks realistic in the animator
          (also in reality the ground moves)
          But results should be identically the method
          of  horizontal substitute loads
      - steel frame with beam plasticity (ase_dehn_pld_earthquake_rahmen.dat)

    - earthquake 22.3.57 SAN FRANCISCO (ase.dat\deutsch\ase1_dam_wall.dat)
      - simple DLX acceleration from a table (commented ASE at the end of the file)

    - earthquake in  a water tank:  (ase.dat\..\bric\water.dat)
      - can be switched with nonlinear bedding
          see also dyna.dat\..\dyna6_natural_frequencies_water.dat
================================================================================================

Other dynamic analysis:
===============================
  A dynamic loading can also be:
  ==================================================

  - given load-time function:
    - pedestrians on swinging footbridge (step_sofiload_ase.dat)
    -  " without SOFILOAD FUNC in an ASE-CADIMP-loop (step_bridge_nonl_lifting_support.dat)
    - explosion load (explosion_on_th3_quad_girder.dat)
      cracked concrete quad grider including TH3 cable effect of the reinforcement
    - wind

  - intelligent load (load adapts to swing movement):
    - aggressive pedestrians on a footbridge (step_intelligent_load.dat)
      The pedestrians jump adapted to the changing eigenfrequency
    - wind gust on a tower (step_intelligent_load_nonl.dat)
      Due to nonlinear lifting of the bedding the eigenfrequency chjanges.
      The wind gust is adjusted to this (unfavorable load-time function)

  - Impact:
    - ship impact with v0 impact velocity (ase_nstr_pld_pile_crash.dat)
    - car crash with v0 and moving springs (movs_car_collision.dat)
    - as simple given load-time function

  - train passing:
    - With train bridge interaction (movs_train_interaction.dat)

</TEXT>



<TEXT>
Comments to load functions  (refer to step_sofiload_ase.dat):
==========================
In ASE usually nonlinear dynamic is calculated. Therefore the complete stress state
including dead load must be generated.
To the permanent part (dead load) the variable part of the loading
(earthquake, impulse, initial velocity) must be added.
It is best to combine the loading directly in ASE, e.g.:

SYST PLC 101 $ static state
STEP N 100 DT 0.01 LCST 1001
LC 102 FACD 1
  LCC 801 $ permanent additional dead load without load function
  LCC 901 $ variable load with load function from SOFILOAD

When the variable load starts, the static state already exists.
If you first analyze the steady state in a separate loadcase without
time dynamic (e.g. loadcase 101) you can then continue with the time dynamic analysis
using the steady state as a primary loadcase - see SYST PLC 101 above.
If you would activate the dead load in the time step analysis for the first time,
the system would accelerate from the unstressed start state and then swing around
the steady state.
This would be the case if you would suddenly remove the formwork from a concrete girder,
see ase.dat\english\dynamics\ step_nonl_concrete_girder.dat

In order to avoid large databases for the time step method the calculation can be made
only with two load cases which vary in each case.
This takes place automatically using STEP N>1 and LCST. The results which are important
for the user can be stored then in separate storage load cases with
STEP ... LCST ... SELE ... (bit pattern).

</TEXT>



<TEXT>
With Echo stat yes the "Statistic nonlinear effects" can be printed in all time steps

If nonlinear effects occured or not can be seen
also on the number of iterations ITER in:
     Summary of time step dynamic analysis !

</TEXT>

END

<TEXT>

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:5
HEAD Set up load vector g_2 - additional dead load
LC 92 $ see comment above
END

+PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD Set up mass vector g_1+g_2 for SOFILOAD
$
$  With the masses assembled here, the following SOFILOAD acce node would sets up the horizontal nodal eathquake forces
$
$
$  But the recommended input is SOFILOAD acce noda where in SOFILOAD only the acceleration
$  function es defined and in ASE LCC automatic all system- and additional masses are accelerated!
MASS LC 92 PRZ 100 $ Add masses from g_2. Systemmasses from gamma are applied automatically!
EIGE 9 LC 6001 $ Set up mass vector and analyze eigenfrequencies
$ please check sum of masses
END



+PROG SOFILOAD urs:6
HEAD Artificial earthquake: definition of acceleration with acce noda
echo func
$ Definitions for trap function - defines the earthquake intensity in time 0-t sec.
lc 7001 TYPE NONE titl 'influence func. trap'   $ intensity function
  func s trap t 20.0 t2 3.0 t3 3.0
$ eurocode 8, type 1, ground type a, xi=5%, ag=g=9.81 m/sÂ²
lc 7002 TYPE NONE titl 'EC8 acceleration response spectrum' $ following values for german Bodensee (AG 0.4 AH 1.4):
  RESP TYPE DIN  CLAS B-R ZONE I MOD - SA 1.250 SB 3.125 SMIN 0.0 TB 0.050 TC 0.250 TD 2.000 TE 0.0 K1 1.000 K2 2.000 AG 0.4*1.4 AH 1.0
  $ The factor AH for horizontal acceleration only works for modal analys up to now, so here as factor to AG !
$
$ Definitions for synthetic accelerogram
sto#DT 0.0005     $ Time step for resulting function
sto#TMIN 0.001 $ Smallest period
sto#TMAX 3 $ jbjbjb 10.00  $ Largest period
sto#NFREQ 500   $ Number of frequencies
sto#ITER 20     $ Number of iterations
sto#ZETA 2[%]   $ Target damping ratio    damping in command   RESP,  SIMQ  and template Rayleigh damping !!!
$ calculate simulated accelelogram corresponding to the defined spectrum:
lc 7003 TYPE NONE titl 'simulated accelelogram'
  sto#alpha 30 ; ACCE TYPE NODA no 0 AX cos(#alpha) AY sin(#alpha) $ Uses the mass vector of previous EIGE run and with this creates nodal
                              $
  SIMQ  LSPE 7002  LINT 7001 DT #DT TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX NFRE #NFREQ ITER #ITER D #ZETA ag -1
lc 7004  TYPE NONE titl '2. random SIMQ'
  sto#alpha 30 ; ACCE TYPE NODA no 0 AX cos(#alpha) AY sin(#alpha)
  SIMQ  LSPE 7002  LINT 7001 DT #DT TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX NFRE #NFREQ ITER #ITER D #ZETA ag -1
lc 7005  TYPE NONE titl '3. random SIMQ'
  sto#alpha 30 ; ACCE TYPE NODA no 0 AX cos(#alpha) AY sin(#alpha)
  SIMQ  LSPE 7002  LINT 7001 DT #DT TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX NFRE #NFREQ ITER #ITER D #ZETA ag -1
<TEXT>
LC 7003-7004 7005: here three different time functions are created with a random generator.
As the random generator depends on the LC number, the three functions are different!
The TRAP Intensity function and the SIMQ settings were choosen in a way,
that in the check generated function LF 7013 the desired spectrum is reached,
here with a maximum acceleration of 1.4*0.4 m/sec2.
In ground view 6 directions should be checked, see sto#alpha  30
so usually 6 directions:    0-30-60-90-120-150 degree

On how to input the magnitude of acceleration (free field acceleration and response   )
  see a4_erdbeben_single_mass_response.dat
</TEXT>

$ calculate spectrum from simulated accelelogram
$ check generated function:
LC no 7013 TYPE NONE  TITL 'Simulated FRF 7003'
  REVA TIME AA 7003 TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX D1 #ZETA REF1 7002 2001  TDIF 10*#DT
LC no 7014 TYPE NONE  TITL '2. random SIMQ'
  REVA TIME AA 7004 TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX D1 #ZETA REF1 7002 2001  TDIF 10*#DT
LC no 7015 TYPE NONE  TITL '3. random SIMQ'
  REVA TIME AA 7005 TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX D1 #ZETA REF1 7002 2001  TDIF 10*#DT
end
end
end

sto#ITER 20     $ Number of iterations
sto#ZETA 3[%]   $ Target damping ratio    damping in command   RESP,  SIMQ  and template Rayleigh damping !!!
$ calculate simulated accelelogram corresponding to the defined spectrum:
lc 7003 TYPE NONE titl 'simulated accelelogram'
  acce type noda no 0  ax 2.5 $ Uses the mass vector of previous EIGE run and with this creates nodal loads incl. time function
  simq  lspe 7002  lint 7001 dt 0.01 tmin 0.02 tmax 4.00 nfre 200 iter 4 d 5[%]
  SIMQ  LSPE 7002  LINT 7001 DT #DT TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX NFRE #NFREQ ITER #ITER D #ZETA
$ check generated function
LC no 7004 TYPE NONE  TITL 'Simulated FRF, X-dir.'
REVA TIME AA 7003 TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX D1 #ZETA REF1 7002 2001  TDIF #DT
end

+prog template urs:22 $ Rayleigh damping
head Rayleigh damping
$ -------- rayleigh damping ---------
$ frequencies
let#f1     1.5                    $ [Hz]  1st eigenfreq.
let#f2     5.0                    $ [Hz]  2nd eigenfreq.
$ viscous damping ratios
let#xi1 0.02 ; prt#xi1     $ [-] 0.02 = 2% damping at frequency f1 (1% for steel, 3-7% for concrete)
let#xi2 0.02 ; prt#xi2     $ [-] at frequency f2                   (2-3% for prestressed concrete)
$
let#w1 2*#pi*#f1; sto#w2 2*#pi*#f2;
$ calculate rayleigh coeff. for steel
sto#rada 2*#w1*#w2*(#xi1*#w2-#xi2*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2); prt#rada   $ mass proportional
sto#radb 2*(#xi2*#w2-#xi1*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2)        ; prt#radb   $ stiffness proportional
$
end

+PROG ASE urs:7
HEAD Steady state g_1+g_2 already nonlinear
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES
LC 101 FACD 1.00 TITL 'Steady state g_1+g_2'
  LCC 92 $ G_2
END

+PROG ASE URS:10
HEAD Time step analysis with horizontal accelerations from SOFILOAD
STEP N 50 DT 0.02 LCST 1002 SELE 1+4+8+64+256+512+1024 LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  $ Here to test only 50 steps - for real analysis set N to 1000 = 20 seconds
  $ DT is not #DT of SOFILOAD! There DT is smaller for synthetic analysis and plot.
CTRL CONC V4 2.50 $ tensile strength reduced to enforce cracks
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES PLC 101
grp - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
MASS LC 92 PRZ 100 $ g_2 mass - is applied as dynamic mass and immediately also as static load
                  $ via dead load factor LC...FACD! No more LCC 7001 necessary !
                  $ (only on LC-FACD - not on GRP...FACD )
                  $ The structural mass is automatic applied as mass with LC-DLZ
ctrl WARN (350 353 1)   $ to get over 3.5 Promille strain limitation
LC  102 FACD 1 $ After the analysis, LC 102 contains the result after 50 time steps due to LCST!
  LCC 7003  $ copies the load using the loadfunction FUNC defined in SOFILOAD !
            $ For a real check also LCC 7004 and LCC 7005 and other directions #alpha must be analyzed!
  $      - Using the acceleration input of SOFILOAD in ASE with LCC, the acceleration
  $          is applied on all system- und additional masses (acce noda 0 in SOFILOAD)
  $          (acce noda - not - acce node !)
END

+PROG ASE URS:9
HEAD go on 40 time steps with dt 0.05 sec - swing off
$ echo stat yes $Statistic nonlinear effects in all time steps
STEP N 40 DT 0.05 THE 0.70 LCST CONT SELE 1+4+8+64+256+512+1024 LCSM 9900 $ CONT=continue
CTRL CONC V4 2.50 $ tensile strength reduced to enforce cracks
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES PLC 102
grp - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
MASS LC 92 PRZ 100
ctrl WARN (350 353 1)   $ to get over 3.5 Promille strain limitation
LC  103 FACD 1 $ Wegen LFSP Eingabe enthÃ¤lt LF 103 am Ende das Ergebnis nach 100 Zeitschritten ! After the analysis, LC 103 contains the result after 100 time steps due to LCST!
  LCC 7003
END

+PROG ASE URS:11
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat  or a3...dat
PLOT 1002 NNO 1 DIRE UX TYPE TIME
PLOT 1002 NNO 1 DIRE AX TYPE TIME $ only available if STEP...SELE +8 is set !
END
$ stresses in nonlinear quads available in Animator elementinfo due to STEP...SELE

!#!Chapter EFM Effective force method - acce noda 0 - system acceleration

+prog sofiload urs:6
head EFM Effective force method - acce noda 0 - system acceleration
sto#nt 1000
#include timetable
lc 101 type none titl 'EFM acce noda 0 ag(t)'
acce type noda no 0 ax -1.0 $ -1.0 for system - because base acceleration is positive +1
loop#i #nt
 func t #time(#i) f #a(#i)
endloop
end

+prog ase urs:3
head EFM Effective force method - acce noda 0 - system acceleration
syst PLC 100
grp - rada #rada radb #radb
grp 9 full
mass 0 ; mass LC 11 $ MASS and FACD - see remarks in a2...dat
sto#nstep 150 $
step #nstep dt 0.02 lcst 1001 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00  $ ... time-history saved in loadcases starting from LCST
lc 201 FACD 1.0 titl 'EFM' $ all results from the last time step are saved in this load case (for eventual restart).
  lcc 101
  $      - Using the acceleration input of SOFILOAD in ASE with LCC, the acceleration
  $          is applied on all system- und additional masses (acce noda 0 in SOFILOAD)
  $          (acce noda - not - acce node !)
end

+prog ase urs:14
head EFM with simple ASE dead load factor - old method
#include timetable
let#plf 100 ; let#lf 9001
loop#i #nstep
  step 1 dt 0.02 lcst - THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  syst plc #plf
  grp - rada #rada radb #radb
  mass 0 ; mass LC 11
  lc #lf dlx -0.1*#a(#i+1) DLZ 1.0
  let#plf #lf
  let#lf #lf+1
  end
endloop
end

!#!Chapter LMM Large Mass Method - acce noda 1 - base point acceleration

+prog sofiload urs:8
head LMM Large Mass Method - acce noda 1 - base point acceleration
sto#nt 1000
#include timetable
lc 102 type none titl 'LMM acce noda 1 ag(t)'
acce type noda no 1 ax 1.0
loop#i #nt
 func t #time(#i) f #a(#i)
endloop
end

+prog ase urs:11
head LMM Large Mass Method - acce noda 1 - base point acceleration
syst PLC 100
grp - rada #rada radb #radb
grp 9 off
mass 0 ; mass LC 11
step #nstep dt 0.02 lcst 2001 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00 $ ... time-history saved in loadcases starting from LCST
lc 202 FACD 1.0 titl 'LMM' $ all results from the last time step are saved in this load case (for eventual restart).
  lcc 102
end

!#!Chapter Results
+prog ase urs:10
head Results
plot lc 1001 nno 4 dire ux $ EFM noda 0
plot lc 9001 nno 4 dire ux $ EFM with simple ASE dead load factor - old method
plot lc 2001 nno 1 dire ux $ LMM noda 1
plot lc 2001 nno 1 dire ax $ LMM noda 1 = input base acceleration !
plot lc 1001 nno 1 dire PX $ EFM noda 0
plot lc 2001 nno 1 dire PX $ LMM noda 1

PLOT LC 1001 NO -1 dire Estr $ strain energy of all groups
PLOT LC 1001 NO -1 dire Ekin $ kinetic energy of all groups
PLOT LC 1001 NO -1 dire Esum $  energy of all groups

$ plot lc 2001 nno 4 dire ux $ LMM noda 1
$ plot lc 1001 nno 4 dire ax $ EFM noda 0
$ plot lc 2001 nno 4 dire ax $ LMM noda 1
end

$ Overview output of results with PROG RESULTS see ase.dat\english\ase1_overview.dat

<TEXT> Conclusion:
All three methods give nearly the same bending moment
 (1. and 2. have exact same results)

Method 1 : EFM Effective force method - acce noda 0 - system acceleration
           - SOFILOAD defines the time - acceleration curve (time function)
           - SOFILOAD also only sets the acceleration direction ax (no nodal loads)
           - ASE uses the acceleration direction ax like a dead load in x and
             applies this using the time function
           - so all free nodes of the system accelerate in x direction
           - the support nodes stand still
           - this gives animations as if the camera is fixed with the soil
             and accelerated together with the soil

Method 2 : EFM with simple ASE dead load factor - old method
           - same as Method 1 but without SOFILOAD
           - ASE directly uses the dead load input in x direction with
             the time function in the manually defined CADINP array #a(#i+1)

Method 3 : LMM Large Mass Method - acce noda 1 - base point acceleration
           - SOFILOAD defines the time - acceleration curve (time function)
           - SOFILOAD also only sets the acceleration direction ax (no nodal loads)
             but now also specifies a node 1.
             So this acceleration is only applied on node 1
           - ASE recognizes that this is a support node and sets
             this node free in x-direction (removes the PX-fixing).
             Then it applies a large mass LMM 1E20 tons and
             accelerates this mass in x direction with the time function
           - so node 1 accelerates like the original earthquake and the
             (not accelerated) system above must follow
           - this gives animations like in reality (camera standing still - not accelerated)

Method 4 : Real support displacement input
           - shown in dynamics/ase_nstr_pld_earthquake_frame.dat  (ase_dehn_pld_erdbeben_rahmen.dat)
             by first integrating the acceleration time function
             into a displacement time function
             and then really applying the displacement as support movement

For comparision with DYNA please ask for a3_introduction_ase_dyna_compare.dat
                                        (a3_einfuehrung_ase_dyna_vergleich.dat)
</TEXT>

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD

CONC 1 C 30 GAM 0
STEE 2

let#f 0.056622/10  ; SVAL 1 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
let#f 0.056622/4   ; SVAL 2 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
let#f 0.056622/2   ; SVAL 3 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
let#f 0.056622*1   ; SVAL 4 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
let#f 0.056622*2   ; SVAL 5 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
let#f 0.056622*4   ; SVAL 6 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
let#f 0.056622*10  ; SVAL 7 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
let#f 0.056622*100 ; SVAL 8 MNO 1 A 0.1[m2] ay 0 az 0 IT 1[m4] IY 0.001*#f*#f[m4] IZ 1[m4]
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD Earthquake SDOF single degree of freedom response factor
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000 POSZ
NODE   (1   8 1) X (0 1) Z -2.0
NODE (101 108 1) X (0 1) Z  0.0 FIX F
BEAM fit NA (101 108 1) NE (1 1) KR negy DIV 5 NCS (1 1)
MASS   (1   8 1) MX 1.0

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD  Eigenfrequencies
EIGE 12 LC 6001
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:14
HEAD Artificial earthquake: definition of acceleration with acce noda
ECHO FUNC

$ Definitions for trap function (T = 45s) - defines the earthquake intensity in time 0-45 sec.
sto#F2 1.7      $ Defines start exponential curve
sto#F3 1.8      $ Defines end exponential curve
sto#T45 45.0    $ T = Duration of
sto#T2_45 4.5   $ T = Peak start
sto#T3_45 30.5  $ T = Peak end
LC no 7001  TYPE NONE  TITL 'Intensity function - COMP'
 FUNC S COMP T #T45 T2 #T2_45 T3 #T3_45 F2 #F2 F3 #F3

LC NO 7002  TYPE NONE  TITL 'acceleration response spectrum'
RESP AG 0.3*9.81  AH   1.00 AV 0.00 MOD 0.03 TITL 'Response spectrum' $ <--- Response spectrum command (MOD 0.03 here without action -> SIMQ)
$ in europa usually  AG between 0.1 - 0.3  *9.81
$ Here used 0.3*9.81  : loadcase 1 for compare: 30% DLX dead load in X direction
$ free field acceleration: a nice map of the earth see
$   http://www.kernenergie.de/kernenergie-wAssets/docs/fachzeitschrift-atw/2009/atw2009_12_sadegh_bautechnische_auslegung_erdbeben.pdf
$ AH shoult be set to 1.0 - important is AG and the direction in ACCE
        FUNC 0.00    1.00
        0.01    1.15 ;       0.02    1.30 ;       0.03    1.45 ;       0.04    1.60 ;       0.05    1.75
        0.06    1.90 ;       0.07    2.05 ;       0.08    2.20 ;       0.09    2.35 ;       0.10    2.50
        0.14    2.50 ;       0.18    2.50 ;       0.22    2.50 ;       0.26    2.50 ;       0.30    2.50
        0.34    2.50 ;       0.38    2.50 ;       0.42    2.50 ;       0.46    2.50 ;       0.50    2.50
        0.68    1.92 ;       0.85    1.57 ;       1.03    1.35 ;       1.20    1.19 ;       1.38    1.07
        1.55    0.98 ;       1.73    0.90 ;       1.90    0.84 ;       2.08    0.79 ;       2.43    0.71
        3.48    0.57 ;       4.60    0.46 ;       6.70    0.32 ;       8.50    0.25 ;       10.00   0.21
$ Definitions for synthetic accelerogram
sto#DT 0.01     $ Time step for resulting function
sto#TMIN 0.0001 $ Smallest period
sto#TMAX 10.00  $ Largest period
sto#NFREQ 500   $ Number of frequencies
sto#ITER 20     $ Number of iterations
sto#ZETA 3[%]   $ Target damping ratio    damping in command   RESP,  SIMQ  and template Rayleigh damping !!!
$
$ calculate simulated accelelogram corresponding to the defined spectrum:
LC no 7003  TYPE NONE  TITL 'simulated accelelogram'
  ACCE TYPE NODA NO 0  AX 1.0 $ Uses the mass vector of previous EIGE run and with this creates nodal loads incl. time function
                              $
                              $
  SIMQ  LSPE 7002  LINT 7001 DT #DT TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX NFRE #NFREQ ITER #ITER D #ZETA

$ check generated function
LC no 7004  TYPE NONE  TITL 'Simulated FRF, X-dir.'
REVA TIME AA 7003 TMIN #TMIN TMAX #TMAX D1 #ZETA REF1 7002 2001  TDIF #DT
end

+prog template urs:22 $ Rayleigh damping
HEAD Rayleigh damping
$ -------- rayleigh damping ---------
$ frequncies
sto#f1     0.333                  $ [Hz]  1st eigenfreq.
sto#f2     3.0                    $ [Hz]  2nd eigenfreq.
$ viscous damping ratios
sto#xi1 0.03 ; prt#xi1     $ [-] at frequency f1
sto#xi2 0.03 ; prt#xi2     $ [-] at frequency f2
$
sto#w1 2*#pi*#f1; sto#w2 2*#pi*#f2;
$ calculate rayleigh coeff. for steel
sto#rada 2*#w1*#w2*(#xi1*#w2-#xi2*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2); prt#rada   $ mass proportional
sto#radb 2*(#xi2*#w2-#xi1*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2)        ; prt#radb   $ stiffness proportional
$
END

+PROG ASE urs:7
HEAD Steady state g_1+g_2  and LC 1 30% DLX dead load in X direction for compare
LC   1 DLX 0.30 TITL '30% ' $ zum Vergleich   30% DLX dead load in X direction' $ for compare
END
LC 101 FACD 1.00 TITL 'Steady state g_1+g_2'
END

+PROG ASE URS:10
HEAD Time step analysis with horizontal accelerations from SOFILOAD
  STEP N  100 DT #DT DIV 0 LCST 1002 SELE - LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
$ STEP N 4500 ... $ Please set STEP N 4500 steps for final run
SYST PLC 101
GRP - RADA #rada RADB #radb  $ damping
LC  102 FACD 1 $ After the analysis, LC 102 contains the result after 50 time steps due to LCST!
  LCC 7003  $ copies the load using the loadfunction FUNC defined in SOFILOAD !
  $      - Using the acceleration input of SOFILOAD in ASE with LCC, the acceleration
  $          is applied on all system- und additional masses (acce noda 0 in SOFILOAD)
  $          (acce noda - not - acce node !)
END

END
