<TEXT> Checks:
Please first look to the compare loadcase 1: 30% deadload in X direction:
All beams have a bottom moment of 6.0 kNm

Beam 8 has high stiffness 100 Hz T= 0.01 sec -> response factor 1.00 -> MY = 1.0 * MY of LC 1 -> MY= 6.0 kNm  OK

Beam 5 gets resonance       2 Hz T= 0.50 sec -> response factor 2.50 -> MY = 2.5*6kNm = about 15 kNm          OK
                                                                           = 2.50 times the result of LC 1
                                                                           = 2.50 * 30% earth acceleration in X direction

Beam 2 is rather weak    0.25 Hz T= 4.00 sec -> response factor 0.50 -> MY = 0.5*6kNm = about  3 kNm          OK

Main check: depending on the stiffness of a beam, it gets a bending moment of
response factor * bending moment of  AG horizontal loaded static loadcase

Juergen Bellmann 27.02.2017

+prog template urs:1
head Integration nach Newmarkâˆ’Wilson und base line correction
$ FÃ¼r die Geschwindigkeit und Verschiebung am Ende des Zeitintervalls wird
$ der Ansatz nach DYNA 2.2 gemacht.
$ Intgrieren:
sto#dis2(2688) 0 $ Feld #dis2(0:2688) anlegen  a 0.02 sec  (UNITS: MM)
sto#vel2(2688) 0 $ Feld #vel2(0:2688) anlegen  a 0.02 sec  (UNITS: MM/sec)
sto#dis2(0) 0    $ Startelement (0)
sto#vel2(0) 0    $ Startelement (0)
let#i -7         $ dann beginnt folgende erste Zeile mit acce(1:8)

let#dt 0.02
let#delta 0.50
let#beta  1/6    $ or 0.25
$
let#d1 1-#delta
let#b5 0.5-#beta
loop#i 2688
  let#j #i+1     $ t+dt
  sto#vel2(#j) #vel2(#i)+#dt*(#d1*#acce(#i)+#delta*#acce(#j))
  sto#dis2(#j) #dis2(#i)+#dt*#vel2(#i)+#dt*#dt*(#b5*#acce(#i)+#beta*#acce(#j))
endloop

sto#maxacce 0
sto#maxvel2 0
sto#maxdis2 0

$ base line correction:
let#dvend #vel2(2688)
let#ddend #dis2(2688)
prt#dvend
prt#ddend
TXB Max displacement before base line correction = #(ddend,9.3)
loop#i 2688
  let#j #i+1     $ t+dt
  sto#vel2(#j) #vel2(#j)-#j*#dvend/2688
  sto#dis2(#j) #dis2(#j)-#j*#ddend/2688
  if  #acce(#j)>#maxacce ; sto#maxacce=#acce(#j)  ; endif
  if -#acce(#j)>#maxacce ; sto#maxacce=-#acce(#j) ; endif
  if  #vel2(#j)>#maxvel2 ; sto#maxvel2=#vel2(#j)  ; endif
  if -#vel2(#j)>#maxvel2 ; sto#maxvel2=-#vel2(#j) ; endif
  if  #dis2(#j)>#maxdis2 ; sto#maxdis2=#dis2(#j)  ; endif
  if -#dis2(#j)>#maxdis2 ; sto#maxdis2=-#dis2(#j) ; endif
endloop

loop#i 20
  prt#dis2(#i)     $ testprint
endloop

loop#i 20
  let#j #i+2688-20
  prt#dis2(#j)     $ testprint
endloop

TXB Max values after base line correction:
TXB Max acceleration = #(maxacce,9.3)
TXB Max velocity     = #(maxvel2,9.3)
TXB Max displacement = #(maxdis2,9.3)
end

+PROG ASE URS:7
HEAD Earthquake - Input as base point excitation - displacement-time-process

LOOP#1 180 $ max. 2688
  ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,LOAD NO
  ECHO GRP YES ! activates storage of strain and kinetic energy
  SYST PROB NONL PLC 100+#1 ; NSTR S1 KSV PLD
  MASS LC 2 $ Convert loads of LC 2 in mass
  STEP 1 0.02 div 0 LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  GRP (0 99 1) RADA 0.05 RADB 0.00005
  $ Determination of RADA-RADB factors see in DYNA manual
  LC 101+#1 DLY 1
    $ lc 2 Attention: Do not determine load case 2 here, because in the
    $ STEP-Dynamic-Analysis the additional mass by the conversion of load case 2
    $ in mass now, due to egy 1, these loads can be equally applied in dead loads!
    $ Check over displacement - the displacement at the length of the bar
    $ must not accelerate in the first 3 load cases !! JB 04.04.2003
  LCC 9001 fact #dis2(#1)*3 $ *3 to get higher effect
    sto#wx_last #dis2(#1)*3
  END
  sto#lf_last 101+#1 $ Save this variable in the .cdb for Post vibration
ENDLOOP
$
TXB Test print out variable ..lf_last = #lf_last
END

+PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD Post vibration too examine remaining deformations
TXB Test print out variable ..lf_last = #lf_last
  ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,LOAD NO
SYST PROB NONL PLC #lf_last ; NSTR S1 KSV PLD
MASS lc 2 $ Convert loads of LC 2 in mass
STEP 30 0.02 div 0 LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
GRP (0 99 1) RADA 5 RADB 0.0010 $ high damping, so that
               $ still state can be achieved!
LC #lf_last+1 DLY 1
  $ lc 2 Attention: Do not determine load case 2 here, see above
  LCC 9001 fact #wx_last
sto#lf_end #lf_last+30
TXB Test print out variable ..lf_end = #lf_end
END

END

!#!Info  Example:       Impact at pile with ASE NSTR PLD
!#!Info  Keyword:       time step analysis; impact; collision; plastic hinge
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$
$ english file name: ase_nstr_pld_pile_crash.dat
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:3
HEAD Impact at pile with ASE NSTR PLD
$
<TEXT>
Overview: see -> a1_dynamic_overview.dat

Explanation
Basis:
- The non-linear beams are only possible in the dynamic of ASE with a limitation
  of full plastic internal forces and moments (DEHN...KSV PLD).
  The program just limits the forces in the non-linear iteration to
  the full plastic forces (ideal plastic behavior)
  (Sum of quadratic utilization factors  <= 1.0).

- Therewith no non-linear cracked concrete sections analysis is possible
  in a non-linear dynamic run. Reason: A non-linear stress distribution of cross section
  is required using a primary load case.
  This is at present only possible with the QUAD-shell model CONCRETE
  See example  step_nonl_concrete_girder.dat or a2_introduction_earthquake.dat
.
  Non-linear concrete model see in ASE-manual.

- Quick run:
  - Run through the example (Animator can start automatically at the end)
  - Page through the created images with Ursula:
    You can observe, that the moment does not rise over 222 kNm, plastic
    curvatures appear and a distorted system remains at the end.
Tips to non-linear dynamic:
- Beam division : Instead of dividing a beam STAB...TEIL always apply
  short beams with true intermediate nodes. Reason:
  1. The masses are concentrated at nodes and a distribution
     of masses at midspan can only be mapped with true intermediate nodes.
  2. The non-linearities of the plastic beam leads to a better
     iteration by using short beams rather than long subdivided beams.
  3. The animation uses only the deformation of nodes.
- Contact springs should be entered preferably soft, otherwise a short
  time step will be necessary!
  Avoid extreme short contact compression.
- Contact springs should have adequate length, so that the length
   of the springs by a deformation is not at zero or negative
  (foremost by the geometrical non-linear analyses)
- To define damping separately place the elements in different groups
   (see ASE below).
.
Secondary masses:
- Generally the secondary masses are separately computed in ASE-run e. g.
  as g_2-loadcase and then converted into masses.
  But attention should be paid that the normal element mass is set automatically!
  See example     ase_DEHN_PLD_Erdbeben_Rahmen.dat
- For impact mass it is easier to input a massive cross section
  in AQUA (alike in this example) -> better animator view.
.
To difficulty of convergence:
- Convergence of every step of load must be ensured and controlled!
- Reasonable residual forces have no importance in a time period,
  because these will be superimposed in the next time period, so these are not lost.
- If negative stiffness are reported within the iterations,
  with
  ASE ... ctrl iter 0
  this stiffness update can be disabled.
  However in normal case the presetting ctrl iter 3
  is better by the systems with crack springs.
- The time period can be reduced by a bad convergence.
- A long time period can be used if oscillations occur.
  Solely it is unattractive that in the time axis in animation
  appears quasi accelerated.
.
Furhter examples with ASE-beams   DEHN...PLD:
- ase_DEHN_PLD_Anprall_an_Pfahl.dat $ Specimen example dynamic with plastic beams
- ase_DEHN_PLD_Erdbeben_Rahmen.dat  $ Earthquake- frame   "
.
Further examples see also:
  ase.dat\deutsch\dynamics\a1_dynamic_overview.dat
. JB 07.04.2003
</TEXT>
$
NORM DIN 18800
STEE 1 ST 37 TMAX 0
STEE 9 ST 37 TMAX 0 gam 0
PROF 5 HEA 500
SCIT 9 D 1000[mm] T 30[mm] MNO 9 $ tube or cable
$ MNO 0 has gamma 0 - Impact mass is defined via MASS in SOFIMSHA !
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE urs:1
HEAD Primary load case
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,BEDD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
LC 1 DLY 1
END

+PROG ASE urs:2
HEAD Impact
HEAD For observation: URSULA delivers here a nice plot
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,BEDD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
ECHO GRP YES ! activates storage of strain and kinetic energy
CTRL WARN 193 $ energy convergence is OK
CTRL ITER 0   $ quicker
STEP 60 0.05 LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00  $ 100- base number for corresponding forces
SYST PROB NONL PLC 1
GRP -                        $ At first activate all Elements
GRP  1  RADA 0   RADB 0      $ Beams are plastic in themselves!
                             $ Therefore no extra damping!
GRP  2  RADA 1.0 RADB 0.005  $ Soil springs
GRP 3,4 RADA 0   RADB 0      $ The coupling spring has got a damping in SOFIMSHA to damp the strike!
  $ Determination of RADA-RADB factors see DYNA manual

$ Attention: the piles and the elements of the ship may not get a RADA damping!
$ Otherwise energy could be absorbed by the environment (the water).
$ Then the energy equation 1/2 m v^2  =  force*displacement would not be fulfilled!
$ Check via energy:
$   mass = 80 t  (ship mass calculated per pile)
$   E-ship = 1/2 m v^2 = 0.5*80*1000*3.5^2 = 490 KNm
$     moment of a pile M-pl = 860 kNm
$     averaged moment of the pile on top of soil = 830 kNm
$       (4.0m below impact point, average of time step results during impact)
$     Force against the ship = M/leverarm = 830kNm/4.0m = 207 kN
$   energy piles = force*displacement = 207kN*2.40m = 498 kNm >= 490kNm ship energy
LC 2 DLY 1 TITL 'Impact'
V0 GRP 3 VX 3.5 $ m/s velocity
NSTR S1 KSV PLD
END

+PROG ASE urs:6
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT LC 1 NNO 3,1003 DIRE UX
PLOT LC 1 NNO 3,1003 DIRE VX
PLOT LC 1  NO -1     DIRE Estr $ strain energy of all groups
PLOT LC 1  NO -1     DIRE Ekin $ kinetic energy of all groups
PLOT LC 1  NO -1     DIRE Esum $  energy of all groups
PLOT LC 1            DIRE N,v NO 44001
PLOT LC 1            DIRE BMY NO 10006 xi 999
END

$  Parameter
$ **********************************************

#define h=70.245       $ HÃ¶he                    [m]
#define l=140.843      $ Laenge                  [m]

#define D=114.796      $ Durchmesser Ersatzvollquerschnitt [mmÂ²]

        let#1 1+#m
        let#f #1/$(n)

        CABL NO    NA    NE    NCS
             1+#m  1+#m  2+#m  1

     1      pp
     1+$(n) pp

  sto#dtgust 1./#f $ time for one gust
  FUNC  T          F
      0.000    .0
   #dtgust/4  1.0     $ 1. impulse   as one period has 4 loadsteps 0-1-1-0
      -       1.0
      -        .0
      -        .0
      -       1.0     $ 2. impulse
      -       1.0
      -        .0
  loop 3
      -        .0
      -       1.0     $ ... impulse  3 more gust
      -       1.0
      -        .0
  endloop
  $   100       .0     $ End of FUNC
END

!#!Info  Example:       Dynamic Relaxation air cushion
!#!Info  Keyword:       time step analysis; membranes; dynamic_relaxation
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
MATE 1 E 50 E90 - MUE 0.40  G -  GAM 10          TITL Membran $ isotrop PVC !
NMAT 1 MEMB P1 10 $ defines material as membrane - P1=10 kN/m yielding force to avoid astronomic residual forces in iterations
END

-PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Dynamic Relaxation air cushion - quarter system
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000
NODE NO      X        Y
     1,2   0,0.50   0.00
    11,12  0,0.50  -0.50
GRP 1
    QUAD -  1 2 12 11 M 16 16 T 0.2[mm]
node fit  1  2 fix PZ
node fit  1 11 fix PZ
node fit  2 12 fix PX
node fit 11 12 fix PY
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:3
HEAD Dynamic Relaxation air cushion
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000
NODE NO          X             Y
     1,2,3    -0.50,0.50,0   0.50
    11,12,13  -0.50,0.50,0  -0.50
    21,22     -0.50,0.50     0
GRP 1
    QUAD -  1 2 12 11 M 16*2 16*2 T 0.2[mm]
node fit  1  2 fix PZ
node fit  1 11 fix PZ
node fit  2 12 fix PZ
node fit 11 12 fix PZ
node 3,13 fix PX
node   21 fix PY
END

<TEXT> Dynamic relaxation:
The final target is a static solution.
If a normal load increase does not work, a decreasing dynamic stiffness
can be added - this method is called 'dynamic relaxation'.
.
To achieve convergence in the first critical load path, the first
time steps are choosen short.
To decrease the dynamic fixing effect, the time step then increases.
With RADA a high damping can be activated for the first critical
time steps. For the last long time steps, the effect of RADA can be neglected.
.
To avoid oszillations the load can be increased using a load function in
sofiload (soft load increase).
.
It is also possible to start with a steady state (static primary load case)
as shown e.g. in step_sofiload_ase.dat.
</TEXT>

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+prog ase urs:6
HEAD Dynamic relaxation
CTRL ITER 3 V2 1
let#lf 1 ; let#plf 0
loop#i0 20
  let#i1 #i0+1         $ 1,2,3, 4, 5... 20
  let#i2 #i1*#i1       $ 1,4,9,16,25...400
  let#dt 0.001*#i2     $ 0.001,0.004, ...  0.400 sec.
  let#tol4 1.0/#i2     $ 1,0.25,0.11,0.075...     $ tolerance    " -> speed up first steps
  STEP 1 DT #dt DIV 0 BET 0.4 0.55 1.0 $ THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  SYST PLC #plf PROB TH3 TOL -0.01 TOL4 #tol4 TOL8 -#tol4 NMAT YES
  VOLU 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 0.25 $ P0 input -> air pressure is fixed - will not change ! See ase.dat\..\membranes\air_volume_tennis.dat
  GRP - RADB 0.05 $ nicht RADA verwenden, sonst zu hohe DÃ¤mpfung(Festhaltung) bei t>10 sec !
      $ RADB 0.001 : DÃ¤mpfung ca. 100 bei 0.01sec, DÃ¤mpfung ca. 2 bei 1.0sec,
  LC #lf FACD 1.0 TITL 'Dynamic relaxation'
  END
  let#plf #lf ; let#lf #lf+1
endloop
END

+PROG ASE URS:11
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT   1 NNO 12 DIRE Z TYPE TIME
PLOT   1 NNO  2 DIRE Y TYPE TIME
END

<TEXT> Dynamic relaxation:
The final target is a static solution for a load that is higher (2.0) than
the linear buckling load of 1.45 (1. buckling eigenvalue).
If a normal load increase does not work, a decreasing dynamic stiffness
can be added - this method is called 'dynamic relaxation'.
.
To achieve convergence in the first critical load path, the first
time steps are choosen short.
To decrease the dynamic fixing effect, the time step then increases.
With RADA a high damping can be activated for the first critical
time steps. For the last long time steps, the effect of RADA can be neglected.
.
To avoid oszillations the load can be increased using a load function in
sofiload (soft load increase).
.
It is also possible to start with a steady state (static primary load case)
as shown e.g. in step_sofiload_ase.dat.
</TEXT>

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+prog ase urs:6
HEAD Dynamic relaxation
let#lf 1 ; let#plf 0
loop#i0 20
  let#i1 #i0+1         $ 1,2,3, 4, 5... 20
  let#i2 #i1*#i1       $ 1,4,9,16,25...400
  let#dt 0.01*#i2      $ 0.01,0.04, ...  4.00 sec.
  let#iter MIN(80,#i2) $ 1,4,9,16,25... 80        $ convergence not critical in first time steps
  let#tol4 1.0/#i2     $ 1,0.25,0.11,0.075...     $ tolerance    " -> speed up first steps
  STEP 1 DT #dt DIV 0 BET 0.4 0.55 1.0 $ THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  CTRL WARN 2581       $ first time steps have small ITER
  SYST PLC #plf PROB TH3 TOL4 #tol4 TOL8 -#tol4 ITER #iter
  GRP - RADB 0.001 $ nicht RADA verwenden, sonst zu hohe DÃ¤mpfung(Festhaltung) bei t>10 sec !
      $ RADB 0.001 : DÃ¤mpfung ca. 100 bei 0.01sec, DÃ¤mpfung ca. 2 bei 1.0sec,
  LC #lf TITL 'Dynamic relaxation load 2.0'
    LCC 911 FACT 2.0   $ 2.0 = over the linear buckling load of 1.45 !
  END
  let#plf #lf ; let#lf #lf+1
endloop
END

PLOT   1 NNO 101 DIRE Y TYPE TIME
END

!#!Info  Example:       Interpretation of modal analysis
!#!Info  Keyword:       dynamic; earthquake; modal analysis; mass; modal mass
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ english file name: erdbeben_jb.dat

$ Overview: see -> a1_dynamic_overview.dat

$ JB- Interpretation of modal analysis :

$ The natural frequency 1001 is activated with factor 0.1049
$ the internal forces and moments of 1001 are therefore contained together
$ with this factor in Dyna results:  (Moment Mz 4785 kNm see in WINGRAF MZ LC 1001)
$ 4789*0.1049 = 503 kNm = internal forces and moments of DYNA-analysis LF 907
$                                    (Moment Mz  503 kNm see in WINGRAF MZ LC  907)
                 $ JB 06.05.2015

$ Factor to be found under:

$ Modal Response
$ Response of periodic loading is exact including the phases
$ Contributions of all functions will be added as sum of squares
$ Fkt.  Mode    Response   Phase          Mode    Response   Phase
$   11     1  -1.049E-01 S=    2.988         2   4.289E-03 S=    2.988
$               ^^^^^^^^
$          3  -1.935E-03 S=    2.880         4  -3.910E-09 S=    1.222
$          5  -6.597E-08 S=    1.218         6  -2.980E-05 S=    1.209

$ The earthquake directions X and Y are combined directly in DYNA.
$

Task:
This example shows the use of nonlinear cracked concrete combined with
dynamic effects. Hysterese is included.

   load ^
 factor |    /\
        |   /  \
        |  /    \
        | /      \
        |/        \
        *---------------------------->  time
           0.025  0.050 sec.

Real accurate explosion loading curve see DYNA - dyna_blast.dat
and dyna_blast_nonl.dat    or SOFiSTiK Seminar 2012


$ Impact in concrete girder see also  -->   step_nonl_betonbalken.dat  !!!!!


+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD Nonlinear dynamic impact
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,LOAD NO
ECHO GRP yes ! activates storage of strain and kinetic energy
ECHO MAT - $ please look at least one time to the material output+plots of ASE !!
CTRL WARN 350,351,352,353  $ deactivates error messages
                           $ "maximun strain or capacity is reached"
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 2.0 $ pure tensile strength reduced
$
let#dt  0.005  $ seconds time increment
let#plc 1
$
loop#1 90    $ number of time steps   #1 counts starting from  0:  0,1,2,3,4 ....
  let#step #1+1
  let#timea #dt*#1      $ time beginning of time step
  let#timee #timea+#dt  $ time at end of this time step
  let#time (#timea+#timee)/2.0   $ time in the middle of this time step
  let#factor 0.0001           $ factor must not be zero !
  if #time < 0.025
    let#factor #time/0.025         $ load increasing
  else
    if #time < 0.050
      let#factor (0.050-#time)/0.025  $ load descending
    endif
  endif
  STEP 1 dt #dt THE 0.7 DIV 0 LCSM 9900 $ THE 0.7 = alpha-method - alpha= -0.30
  SYST PROB th3 NMAT YES TOL -2.0 PLC #plc
  LC #plc+1 FACD 1.0 FACT #factor titl 'factor= #factor'
    LCC 9001
  END
  let#plc #step
endloop
END
END

+PROG ASE URS:7
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT 1 NNO 2 DIRE UZ TYPE time
PLOT 1 NNO 2 DIRE VZ TYPE time
PLOT 1 NNO 2 DIRE AZ TYPE time
PLOT 1 NNO 3 DIRE PX TYPE time
PLOT 1  NO -1     DIRE Estr $ strain energy of all groups
PLOT 1  NO -1     DIRE Ekin $ kinetic energy of all groups
PLOT 1  NO -1     DIRE Esum $  energy of all groups

$ Plot in layers :
PLOT lc 1 DIRE  sx TYPE ex NO 7 xi -1.0
PLOT lc 1 DIRE ss1 TYPE ex NO 7 xi  1.0
$ For stress in reinforcement, choose ss1 or ss2 and
$ select upper/lower side just with xi= -1/+1
END

$ numerical damping: see ase.dat\...\dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat

$ The picture:
$    PLOT 1 NNO 3 DIRE PX TYPE lcno
$ Shows an increasing compression in the first steps (group 1+2 active for compression arch)
$ and then a tensile cable net in the next steps until the girder is
$ nearly completely damaged and a crashed shape remains.
$ The iteration is relatively good due to the dynamic stiffening of the time step analysis.
$

</TEXT>

+PROG ASE urs:3
HEAD MOVS
$ Radfedern
MOVS grp 6 TYPE QGRP 0 L0 $(z)[m]  $ aus STO#z=-0.4   $ STO damit in ASE vefÃ¼gbar !
$ Anprallfedern
MOVS grp 9 TYPE BGRP 2 L0 0.1[m]

+PROG ASE urs:4
HEAD PrimÃ¤rlastfall schon mal mit Koppelfedersuchen
CTRL WARN 183
SYST PROB NONL 31 ; ctrl warn 2581
GRP -
GRP 9 OFF
LC 1 FACD 1
END

+PROG ASE urs:5
HEAD Anfangsgeschwindigkeit
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,BEDD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results

STEP 60 0.01 LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
CTRL ITER 0 $ = schneller bei nonl
SYST PROB NONL ITER 90 PLC 1 tol -5 tol4 0.002 $ first iterations with 5 kN tolerance, then 0.002 %
LC 2 FACD 1
let#vo=100 $km/h (Anprallgeschwindigkeit)
let#alpha=20 $Anprallwinkel [Grad]
V0 GRP 5 VX #vo*cos(#alpha)/3.6 VY -#vo*sin(#alpha)/3.6
NSTR S1 KSV pld
END

                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2
                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max

   - 3.28 0.00
   - 3.33 0.20

   - 1.60 #h1

     - +1.15 0.38

     - -1.15 #h1-0.2
     - -1.15 0.38

let#21 0.05 $ z-Werte der Torsionsbox oben
let#22 #h1-0.05 $ z-Werte der Torsionsbox unten
LRF  1 -#11  #21  #11  #21 AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D 16
LRF  2  #11  #21  #11  #22 ==   $
LRF  3  #11  #22 -#11  #22 ==   $  Torsionsbox:  *-------------------------> y
LRF  4 -#11  #22 -#11  #21 ==   $                |                   |
                                 $     *----------|----------*   #21  |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     |<--#11--->|<---#11-->|        |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     *----------|----------*       #22
                                 $                z
let#11 #11-0.05          $ y-Werte Hauptlaengsbew.
let#21 #21+0.02,#22-0.03 $ z-Werte Hauptlaengsbew.
LRF  5 -#11  #22  #11  #22 AS     - LAY 1       TORS PASS D  20 $ unten
LRF  6 -3.20 #21 3.20  #21 AS     - LAY 2       TORS PASS D  20 $ oben

$ QS 4 YA  1.00 ZA -1.00 YE  1.00 ZE  1.00  MNR 1 MBW 11 RANG 4 TYP Gurt QZFK 0.50

     'UMI'   0.00   #h1    1 $ Literal UMI muss in Grossbuchstaben

   - 4.00 0.40

              -      -        0[mm]              0[mm]          30[mm]

!#!Info  Example:       train interaciton
!#!Info  Keyword:       time step analysis; contakt; moving spring
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!Info  Date:          09.07.2010


$ Beschreibung der Animation:
$ ZugÃ¼berfahrt Doppelzug Ã¼ber eine BrÃ¼cke
$ Dieses Testbeispiel soll nur die Verarbeitung der
$ "Moving Springs" testen, die sich den Kontaktpunkt des Fahrzeuges

+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Moving Springs - loads moving over a bridge - without mass interaction

NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'

                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max
SECT  1 MNO  1 MRF 11
sv it -0.05 $ to better see torsional deformation
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
let#h1 2.50
VERT - 0.00 0.00
   - 3.28 0.00
   - 3.33 0.20
   - 1.60 0.35
   - 1.68 1.04
   - 1.65 1.06
   - 1.60 #h1
POLY      MNO 0
VERT -  0.00 0.28
     - +1.40 0.38
     - +1.40 #h1-0.2
     - -1.40 #h1-0.2
     - -1.40 0.38
let#11 1.50 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox
let#21 0.05 $ z-Werte der Torsionsbox oben
let#22 #h1-0.05 $ z-Werte der Torsionsbox unten
LRF  1 -#11  #21  #11  #21 AS 1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D 16
LRF  2  #11  #21  #11  #22 ==   $
LRF  3  #11  #22 -#11  #22 ==   $  Torsionsbox:  *-------------------------> y
LRF  4 -#11  #22 -#11  #21 ==   $                |                   |
                                 $     *----------|----------*   #21  |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     |<--#11--->|<---#11-->|        |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     |          |          |        |
                                 $     *----------|----------*       #22
                                 $                z
let#11 #11-0.05          $ y-Werte Hauptlaengsbew.
let#21 #21+0.02,#22-0.03 $ z-Werte Hauptlaengsbew.
LRF  5 -#11  #22  #11  #22 AS     - LAY 1       TORS PASS D  20 $ unten
LRF  6 -3.20 #21 3.20  #21 AS     - LAY 2       TORS PASS D  20 $ oben
CUT 1 ZB 0.40     MNO 1 MRF 11      LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze oberhalb  Spannglied
CUT 2 ZB 0.60     MNO 1 MRF 11      LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze unterhalb Spannglied
CUT 3 YB -1.75[m]   MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN  $ belt Y neg. to get correct cut direction (cut belt off)
$ QS 4 YA  1.00 ZA -1.00 YE  1.00 ZE  1.00  MNR 1 MBW 11 RANG 4 TYP Gurt QZFK 0.50
$ QS 4 YA -1.00 ZA  1.00 YE -1.00 ZE -1.00  MNR 1 MBW 11 RANG 4 TYP Gurt QZFK 0.50
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO
     'UMI'   0.00   #h1    1 $ Literal UMI muss in Grossbuchstaben
     'OMI'   0.00  0.00    1 $ eingegeben werden
END

    BEAM na (20 49 1)   ne (21 1)  NCS  1 NP    -1

    BEAM na (51 99 1)   ne (52 1)  NCS  1 NP    -1

!#!Kapitel System
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD

CONC  1  C   40        $ = C40/50
STEE  2  S  500
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Train passing along an axis - with mass interaction
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC          GDIV   1000
NODE NO 1,2,3,4 X 10,150,150,10 Y 50,50,-50,-50
GRP 1 TITL Superstructure
  QUAD - N1 1 2 3 4 MNO 2 POSI BELO T 0.30[m] C 1e4 CT 1e2 M 20 N 10
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:10
HEAD Separate run e.g.after SOFIPLUS to create train (moving springs)
SYST REST ; CTRL REST 2
sto#dzmovs 4.00
sto#uz_bedding 2.355/1000 $ as slab already deflects in bedding by 2.355 mm
NODE     201 X    -4.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ attention:
NODE     202 X    -1.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ center of train to be coppied
NODE     203 X     1.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ must be at point x=0, y=0 !!!
NODE     204 X     4.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding
NODE     205 X    -4.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding
NODE     206 X    -1.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding
NODE     207 X     1.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding
NODE     208 X     4.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding

NODE     301 X    -4.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ attention: also fro train 2, the center must
NODE     302 X    -1.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ must be at point x=0, y=0 !!!
NODE     303 X     1.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ So here two points are defined at the same location!
NODE     304 X     4.5 Y -1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ So point 301 has the same coordinate as 201 !
NODE     305 X    -4.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ But they are not connected and can be coppied
NODE     306 X    -1.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding  $ with a different dx !
NODE     307 X     1.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding
NODE     308 X     4.5 Y  1   Z  -#dzmovs+#uz_bedding

GRP 3  titl 'Moving springs + masses'
    SPRI NA (201 208 1) DZ 1 CP 1E3 CT 1E6 CRAC 0 dp 60 $ Moving mass with interaction - damping for first train
    MASS NO (201 208 1) MX 20 $ 8*20 t = 160 t train load
GRP 4  titl 'train 2
    SPRI NA (301 308 1) DZ 1 CP 1E3 CT 1E6 CRAC 0 dp -  $ no damping on 2. train
    MASS NO (301 308 1) MX 20 $ 8*20 t = 160 t train load

END

+PROG SOFIMSHC URS:3
HEAD  Definition of the axis
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST REST ; CTRL REST 1
$ ------------------------------------- axis : ------------------------------
GAX 'AX_1'
  GAXA S  0 X 0[m] 0 0 SX 1 0 0 $ first starting point with starting direction
  GAXA L 10 RA   0 RE   80
  GAXA L 40 R   80
  GAXA L 20 RA  80 RE   0
  GAXA L 20 RA   0 RE -35
  GAXA L 90 R -35
  GAXA L 90 R -35
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis

+PROG ASE urs:7
HEAD Vertical eigenfrequency of masses
grp - ; grp 1 off
eige 5            $ gives 1.13 Hertz -> time step not longer that 0.2 sec !!
END

+PROG ASE urs:9
HEAD Define MOVS moving springs
MOVS grp 3,4 TYPE QGRP 1 L0 #dzmovs[m] OUTF 'fix'
END

+prog sofiload urs:8
head
lc 806 titl 'line load to create a little sagging in the slab'
  line ref qgrp 1 type PG P1 300 x1 90 y1 -50   x2 dxy 0 100
end

+PROG ASE urs:4
HEAD Primary load case without time step !
SYST PROB LINE $ no nonlinear effects
grp - ; grp 3,4 prex -200 $ to achieve that deformation is 0 on spring force -200 kN !
LC 1001 FACD 1 TITL 'Start with dead load'
  LCC 806 $ line load to create a little sagging in the slab -> interaction with mass of train
          $ you see the changing contact spring force in the last ASE plot when train passes the saggings !
END

+PROG ASE urs:5

STEP 250  dt 0.20 THE 0.70 LCST 8001 LCSM 9900
SYST PROB LINE PLC 1001
LC 1002 FACD 1
  LAUN GRP 3 dx    0[m] VX 5[m/sec] ref 'AX_1' $ actual train position = 0[m] + time*vx
  LAUN GRP 4 dx  -65[m] VX 6[m/sec] ref 'AX_1' $ means train 2 (grp 4) goes 65 m behind train 1 : but faster
  LCC 806 $ line load to create a little sagging in the slab
END

+PROG ASE urs:6
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT LC 8001 NNO 208 DIRE uz
PLOT LC 8001 NNO 301 DIRE uz
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD Pendulum impact test
UNIT 6 $ mm
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 POSZ
sto#h  876
sto#b 1938
NODE  NO      X       Z
     101    -#b/2   -#h/2         $  contact springs:
     102    -100    -#h/2         $        203 204 205
     103     -50    -#h/2         $    302 303 304 305 306
     104       0    -#h/2         $    402 403 404 405 406
     105     +50    -#h/2         $    502 503 504 505 506
     106    +100    -#h/2         $        603 604 605
     107    +#b/2   -#h/2
TRAN node 101 107 dno 100 dz #h/2-100
TRAN node 101 107 dno 200 dz #h/2-50
TRAN node 101 107 dno 300 dz #h/2
TRAN node 101 107 dno 400 dz #h/2+50
TRAN node 101 107 dno 500 dz #h/2+100
TRAN node 101 107 dno 600 dz #h

TRAN node 202 606 dno 1000 dy 200[mm]
TRAN node 1404    dno 1000 dy  10[mm]
TRAN node 1404    dno 2000 dy 210[mm]
NODE 1404,2404,3404 fix ypmm

GRP 1
    let#n1  4 $ center area 5*5 nodes - do not change '4'
    let#n2  8 $ above center area  - change allowed
    let#n3 10 $ beside center area - change allowed
    QUAD PROP T 8[mm]
    QUAD -  101 201 202 102 M #n2 #n3
    QUAD -  102 202 206 106 M #n2 #n1
    QUAD -  106 206 207 107 M #n2 #n3

    QUAD -  201 601 602 202 M #n2 #n3
    QUAD -  202 602 606 206 M #n2 #n1
    QUAD -  206 606 607 207 M #n2 #n3

    QUAD -  601 701 702 602 M #n2 #n3
    QUAD -  602 702 706 606 M #n2 #n1
    QUAD -  606 706 707 607 M #n2 #n3

sto#cftot 400 $ Sum of spring stiffness of all springs 400 kN\m.
sto#cfi 0.70*#cftot/9  $  9 springs inside
sto#cfo 0.30*#cftot/12 $ 12 springs outside
GRP 2
  $ 9 inner springs:
  let#nodes 9,303,304,305,403,404,405,503,504,505
  loop#i #nodes(0)
    SPRI #nodes(#i+1) NA #nodes(#i+1) NE #nodes(#i+1)+1000 CP #cfi CRAC 0 GAP  5[mm]
    if #nodes(#i+1)<>404
      NODE #nodes(#i+1)+1000 FIX KF 1404
    endif
  endloop
  $ 12 outer springs: with a GAP t simulate later contact !
  let#nodes 12,203,204,205,302,402,502,306,406,506,603,604,605
  loop#i #nodes(0)
    SPRI #nodes(#i+1) NA #nodes(#i+1) NE #nodes(#i+1)+1000 CP #cfo CRAC 0 GAP 25[mm]
    NODE #nodes(#i+1)+1000 FIX KF 1404
  endloop
GRP 9
  SPRI - NA 2404 NE 1404 CP 1E9 $ for plot use only
  TRUS - NA 3404 NE 2404 NCS 9  $ for animation (without mass - gamma=0)
  MASS 3404 MX 50[kg]

$ --------------------- fixings ---------------------------------------------
GRP 0
SBOX A1X   -1000 0 0     1000 0 0  A2X 0 -1000 0   0 1000 0 A3X 0 0 -#h/2-1   0 0 -#h/2+1
SBOX A1X   -1000 0 0     1000 0 0  A2X 0 -1000 0   0 1000 0 A3X 0 0 +#h/2-1   0 0 +#h/2+1 OPT OR
SBOX A1X -#b/2-1 0 0  -#b/2+1 0 0  A2X 0 -1000 0   0 1000 0 A3X 0 0   -1000   0 0   +1000 OPT OR
SBOX A1X +#b/2-1 0 0  +#b/2+1 0 0  A2X 0 -1000 0   0 1000 0 A3X 0 0   -1000   0 0   +1000 OPT OR
NODE SBOX FIX PY
spri SBOX DY 1 CT 100
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD Primary load case
LC 1 FACD 1
END

HEAD Federelemente mit exponentieller DÃ¤mpfung

$ Achtung: bei hohem Exponenten ist das Verhalten der DÃ¤mpfer eher voll-plastisch:
$          Eine minimale Ã„nderung der Geschwindigkeit von z.B.
$          vz= +1.E-6 m/sec nach -1.E-6 m/sec hat eine
$          sehr groÃŸe KraftÃ¤nderung zur Folge :

$          vz= +1.E-6 m/sec -> DÃ¤mpferkraft= 100*+1.E-6^0.015 = +81.2 kN
$          vz= -1.E-6 m/sec -> DÃ¤mpferkraft= 100*-1.E-6^0.015 = -81.2 kN
$
$ Die erzeugt praktisch eine Sprungstelle in der Kraft-Verformungskurve !
$ vgl. AQUA
END

END
$ Ergebnis:
$ Aufgrund der ersten hohen Last rutscht der DÃ¤mpfer bei ca. -100 kN
$ Druckkraft auf ca. 900 mm durch.
$ Dann wird die Geschwindigkeit kleiner, die DÃ¤mpferkraft bleibt aber hoch
$ wegen des hohen Exponenten:
$ z.B. dp 100 expp 0.015 :
$          vz= -1.E-6 m/sec -> DÃ¤mpferkraft= 100*-1.E-6^0.015 = -81.2 kN
$
$ Dadurch wird die statische Endlage praktisch nicht erreicht bzw. erst
$ sehr spÃ¤t.

$ Task:
$ This example shows the input of dynamic loading with
$ user defined formula in ASE-CADINP.
$ The load shall act from time 0.20-0.40,
$                    from time 1.00-1.20,
$                    from time 1.80-2.00 and
$                    from time 2.60-2.80:
$
$    load ^     _        _        _        _
$  factor |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         *-------------------------------------->  time
$             .2 .3    .6 .7    .9 1.0  1.3 1.4
$
$ or sinus-load: e.g.
$  let#factor sin(360*#time/0.300)+0.0001   $ +0.0001 factor must not be zero !
$                           $ 0.300 = 0.300 seconds period
$
$ see also:
$ step_sofiload_ase.dat
$ explosion_on_th3_quad_girder.dat
$ step_intelligent_load.dat
$ step_intelligent_load_nonl.dat
$
$
$ numerical damping: to avoid numerical oszillations
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.25 0.50 1.00 $ Original Newmark without numerical damping               '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 1/6  1/2  1.40 $ Original Wilson with large damping in higher modes       '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.4  0.55 1.00 $ good numerical damping of high freq. for nonlinearities  '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET  -  - THE 0.70 $ alpha method acc. Hilber-Hughes-Taylor input THE= 1 - |alpha|.
                                    $ example alpha -0.3   --> THE=0.7

+PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD
ctrl solv 998 $ do not make stiffness new during iterations
              $ normal nonlinear effects (springs or quad-nmat) are
              $ iterated via redidual iteration (no stiffness update necessary)
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,BEDD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
<TEXT,file=step_testprint.txt>
 Testprint: written to file step_testprint.txt - Initialize result file = write first line
</TEXT>

let#dt  0.04 $ seconds time increment
let#plf 1
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,LOAD,GRP NO
ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
$
loop#1 120 $ number of time steps   #1 counts starting from  0:  0,1,2,3,4 ....
  let#step #1+1
  let#timea #dt*#1     $ time beginning of time step
  let#timee #timea+#dt $ time at end of this time step
  let#time (#timea+#timee)/2.0   $ time in the middle of this time step
  let#factor 0.000001              $ factor must not be zero !

  if (#time>0.201)&(#time<0.301) ; let#factor 1.0 ; endif
  if (#time>0.601)&(#time<0.701) ; let#factor 1.0 ; endif
  if (#time>0.901)&(#time<1.001) ; let#factor 1.0 ; endif
  if (#time>1.301)&(#time<1.401) ; let#factor 1.0 ; endif
  if (#time>1.701)&(#time<1.801) ; let#factor 1.0 ; endif
  $ see also step_intelligent_load.dat
  $ or use a sinusfunktion:
  $ let#factor sin(360*#time/0.300)+0.0001   $ +0.0001 factor must not be zero !

  <TEXT,file=+step_testprint.txt> $ Testprint: written to file step_testprint.txt :
    step #step time= #(timea,8.3)sec.  load factor= #(factor,5.2)
  </TEXT>
  STEP 1 DT #dt LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  SYST prob nonl PLC #plf ; let#plf #plf+1
  MASS LC 7001 PRZ 100 $ g_2 mass - is applied as dynamic mass and also as static load
                  $ via dead load factor LC...FACD! No more LCC 7001 necessary !
                  $ (only on LC-FACD - not on GRP...FACD )
                  $ The structural mass is automatic applied as mass with LC-FACD
  LC #plf FACD 1.0
    $ lc 7001 nicht nochmal ansetzen, da durch MASS-Satz und EGZ auch dessen Gewicht aktiviert wird (nicht bei GRUP-FAKG)!
    LCC 7002 #factor
  END
endloop
END

$ Task:
$ The load+mass is moving over the bridge. The load-value
$ depends on the velocity of the center node of the span.
$ .
$ If the velocity is z-direciton is positive, the load is
$ high because the man wants to bring the bridge into
$ vibration!

$ numerical damping: to avoid numerical oszillations
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.25 0.50 1.00 $ Original Newmark without numerical damping               '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 1/6  1/2  1.40 $ Original Wilson with large damping in higher modes       '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.4  0.55 1.00 $ good numerical damping of high freq. for nonlinearities  '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET  -  - THE 0.70 $ alpha method acc. Hilber-Hughes-Taylor input THE= 1 - |alpha|.
                                    $ example alpha -0.3   --> THE=0.7

$ another example: step_bridge_nonl_lifting_support.dat
$ That example shows the input of dynamic loading with
$ user defined formula in ASE-CADINP.
$ The load shall act from time 0.20-0.40,
$                    from time 1.00-1.20,
$                    from time 1.80-2.00 and
$                    from time 2.60-2.80:
$    load ^     _        _        _        _
$  factor |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         |    | |      | |      | |      | |
$         *-------------------------------------->  time
$             .2 .4     1 1.2  1.8 2.0  2.6 2.8


$ AuflagerkrÃ¤fte werden in Wingraf zu einer Summe zusammengefasst (Bild-Titel)
$ Dabei werden derzeit auch die DÃ¤mpfungskrÃ¤fte einer
$ massenproportionalen GRUP RADA DÃ¤mpfung als Auflagerkraft mitgenommen.

+prog template urs:22 $ Rayleigh damping
head Rayleigh damping
$ -------- rayleigh damping ---------
$ frequencies
let#f1     #f0                 $ [Hz]  1st eigenfreq.
let#f2    3.03                 $ [Hz]  2nd eigenfreq.
$ viscous damping ratios
let#xi1 0.01 ; prt#xi1     $ [-] 0.01 = 1% damping at frequency f1 (1% for steel, 3-7% for concrete)
let#xi2 0.01 ; prt#xi2     $ [-] at frequency f2                   (2-3% for prestressed concrete)
$
let#w1 2*#pi*#f1; sto#w2 2*#pi*#f2;
$ calculate rayleigh coeff. for steel
sto#rada 2*#w1*#w2*(#xi1*#w2-#xi2*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2); prt#rada   $ mass proportional
sto#radb 2*(#xi2*#w2-#xi1*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2)        ; prt#radb   $ stiffness proportional
$
$ read dead load dirction from database:
@KEY SYST
let#IACHS @(IACHS)
sto#GDIR +1.0             $ gravity direction: +1 = global z axis goes down - a positive load factor must give a load into this direction !
if #IACHS<0
  sto#GDIR -1.0 $ gravity direction: -1 = global z axis goes up
endif
prt#GDIR
end

$ numerical damping: to avoid numerical oszillations
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.25 0.50 1.00 $ Original Newmark without numerical damping               '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 1/6  1/2  1.40 $ Original Wilson with large damping in higher modes       '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.4  0.55 1.00 $ good numerical damping of high freq. for nonlinearities  '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET  -  - THE 0.70 $ alpha method acc. Hilber-Hughes-Taylor input THE= 1 - |alpha|.
                                    $ example alpha -0.3   --> THE=0.7

!#!KAPITEL Non-Intelligent load method - fixed sinus FUNC from SOFILOAD
+PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD Time Step analysis Non-Intelligent load method - fixed sinus FUNC from SOFILOAD
let#dt  0.05 $ seconds time increment
let#plf 1001
let#v 0.9*#f0 $ m/s velocity according (NA.7.105.2)
ECHO DISP,FORC,NOST,BEDD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
ECHO GRP yes ! activates storage of strain and kinetic energy
$
loop#1 280 $ number of time steps   #1 counts starting from  0:  0,1,2,3,4 ....
  let#timea #dt*#1     $ time beginning of time step
  let#timee #timea+#dt $ time at end of this time step
  let#time (#timea+#timee)/2.0   $ time in the middle of this time step
  $ location of load (passanger) for the animation:
  let#x 10.0+#time*#v $ position starting at 10.0m - then it gets interesting !
  STEP 1 DT #dt LCSM 11000 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  SYST PLC #plf ; let#plf #plf+1
  MASS LC 7001 PRZ 100 $ structural dead load is automatically activated as mass !
  grp  - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
  grp 99 rada 0     radb 0      $ no damping     also activates Mass+load of passanger !
  LC #plf FACD 1.0 TITL 'method 1 Non-Intelligent'
    $ don't activate lc 7001 - as it is also activated as load by MASS and LC FACD!
    LCC 7005 $ +- 180 N passanger load   with FUNC function from SOFILOAD
    LAUN GRP 99 dx #x[m] $ passanger position together with grp also activates Mass+load of passanger !
  END
endloop
end

+PROG ASE URS:28
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT 1001 NNO     221     DIRE UZ TYPE TIME
PLOT 1001 NNO     221     DIRE AZ TYPE TIME    $ allowable AZ see SOFILOAD
PLOT 1001 NO 2102 DIRE N
PLOT 1001  NO -1     DIRE Estr $ strain energy of all groups
PLOT 1001  NO -1     DIRE Ekin $ kinetic energy of all groups
PLOT 1001  NO -1     DIRE Epot $ potential energy of all groups
PLOT 1001  NO -1     DIRE Esum $ sum of all energies of all groups
END

$ Alternatively you can also create a single load with wavying load position in SOFILOAD
$ and apply a separate load copy for each step in ASE.

!#!KAPITEL Intelligent load method 2 block load - necessary for nonlinear approach as eigenfrequencies may change
-PROG ASE URS:7
HEAD Time Step analysis - Intelligent load method 2 block load
let#dt  0.05 $ seconds time increment
let#plf 2001
let#v 0.9*#f0 $ m/s velocity according (NA.7.105.2)
ECHO DISP,FORC,NOST,BEDD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
ECHO GRP yes ! activates storage of strain and kinetic energy
<TEXT,file=testprint_method2.txt>
 Testprint: written to file testprint_method2.txt - Initialize result file = write first line
</TEXT>
$
loop#1 280 $ number of time steps   #1 counts starting from  0:  0,1,2,3,4 ....
  let#timea #dt*#1     $ time beginning of time step
  let#timee #timea+#dt $ time at end of this time step
  let#time (#timea+#timee)/2.0   $ time in the middle of this time step
  $ location of load (passanger) for the animation:
  let#x 10.0+#time*#v $ position starting at 10.0m - then it gets interesting !
  if #time<0.2/#f0
    let#velo #GDIR  $ first steps with load to enforce bridge to start to go down
  else
    $ read velocity VZ of last time step at the detector node:
    $ detector node = center node of span, where the passanger just is positioned:
    let#node 208                    $ span 1
    if #x>11 ; let#node 221 ; endif $ span 2
    if #x>27 ; let#node 235 ; endif $ span 3
    @KEY N_VELO #plf ; LET#velo @(#node,VZ) $ read VZ of node #node in #plf
  endif
  let#factor -1.0 $ passangers feet are in the air - no contact = negative load (+- 0.18 kN)
  if #velo*#GDIR>0. ; let#factor +1.0 ; endif $ passanger feet has contact.
  $ Assuming 50% in the air with factor -1.00 : factor on ground = -1.0
  let#factor #factor*SQR(2.0/3.1416) $ effective load to compare with sinus load: Integral(sin) < integral block-function !
  <TEXT,file=+testprint_method2.txt> $ Testprint: written to file testprint_method2.txt :
    time= #(timea,8.3)sec. at x= #(x,9.2)m velocity= #(velo,7.4)m/s -> new load factor= #(factor,6.3)
  </TEXT>
  $
  STEP 1 DT #dt LCSM 12000 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  SYST PLC #plf ; let#plf #plf+1
  MASS LC 7001 PRZ 100 $ structural dead load is automatically activated as mass !
  grp  - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
  grp 99 rada 0     radb 0      $ no damping
  LC #plf FACD 1.0 TITL 'method 2 intelligent block load'
    $ don't activate lc 7001 - as it is also activated as load by MASS and LC FACD!
    LCC 7004 fact #factor $ +- 180 N passanger load
    LAUN GRP 99 dx #x[m] $ passanger position
  END
endloop
end

-PROG ASE URS:9
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT 2001 NNO     221     DIRE UZ TYPE TIME
PLOT 2001 NNO     221     DIRE AZ TYPE TIME    $ allowable AZ see SOFILOAD
PLOT 2001 NO 2102 DIRE N
PLOT 2001  NO -1     DIRE Estr $ strain energy of all groups
PLOT 2001  NO -1     DIRE Ekin $ kinetic energy of all groups
PLOT 2001  NO -1     DIRE Esum $  energy of all groups
END
!#!KAPITEL Method 3 intelligent sinus
-PROG ASE URS:10
HEAD Time Step analysis - Method 3 intelligent sinus
let#dt  0.05 $ seconds time increment
let#plf 3001
let#v 0.9*#f0 $ m/s velocity according (NA.7.105.2)
ECHO DISP,FORC,NOST,BEDD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
ECHO GRP yes ! activates storage of strain and kinetic energy
<TEXT,file=testprint_method3.txt>
 Testprint: written to file testprint_method3.txt - Initialize result file = write first line
</TEXT>

let#T_walk 1./1.67 ; let#T_update #T_walk $ period of 1. eigenfrequency g1+g2 without mass of passanger - start value - will be updated
$
loop#1 280 $ number of time steps   #1 counts starting from  0:  0,1,2,3,4 ....
  let#timea #dt*#1     $ time beginning of time step
  let#timee #timea+#dt $ time at end of this time step
  let#time (#timea+#timee)/2.0   $ time in the middle of this time step
  $ location of load (passanger) for the animation:
  let#x 10.0+#time*#v $ position starting at 10.0m - then it gets interesting !
  $
  if #time<0.2*#T_walk
    let#factor       1.0         $ first steps with load to enforce bridge to start to go down
    let#velolast     #GDIR       $ last velo: +1 in case global Z goes down (#GDIR=+1.0)
    let#T_lastchange 0.2*#T_walk $ last time of change velocity-z VZ from negative to positive
    let#velo 0                   $ for testprint
  else
    $ read velocity VZ of last time step at the detector node:
    $ detector node = center node of span, where the passanger just is positioned:
    let#node 208                    $ span 1
    if #x>11 ; let#node 221 ; endif $ span 2
    if #x>27 ; let#node 235 ; endif $ span 3
    @KEY N_VELO #plf ; LET#velo @(#node,VZ) $ read VZ of node #node in #plf
    if (#velo*#GDIR>0.)&(#velolast*#GDIR<0.) $ in case both conditions are true -> direction change from upwanrds to downwards
      let#T_now (#time-#dt)-#T_lastchange $ new time T_walk - (#time-#dt)=plc time
      if #T_now>0.2*#T_update $ only if it is senseful - to neglect oszillations during the VZ change
        let#T_lastchange #time-#dt*abs(#velo)/(abs(#velo)+abs(#velolast)) $ start a new sinus cycle at this time
        let#T_update 0.9*#T_update+0.1*#T_now $ slowly adjust the walking step time #T_update
      endif
    endif
    let#velolast #velo
    let#dt_since_change #time-#T_lastchange
    if #dt_since_change<#T_update
      $ we apply a sinus wave from time #T_lastchange up to #T_lastchange+#T_update :
      let#factor sin(360*#dt_since_change/#T_update)+0.0001 $ +0.0001 because factor must not be zero !
    else
      let#factor 0.0001 $ = zero , wait until we get the next direction change
    endif
  endif
  <TEXT,file=+testprint_method3.txt> $ Testprint: written to file testprint_method3.txt :
    time= #(timea,8.3)sec at x= #(x,9.2)m velocity= #(velo,7.4)m/s T_lastchange= #(T_lastchange,6.3)sec -> new load factor= #(factor,6.3) T_update= #(T_update,6.3)sec
  </TEXT>
  $
  STEP 1 DT #dt LCSM 13000 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  SYST PLC #plf ; let#plf #plf+1
  MASS LC 7001 PRZ 100 $ structural dead load is automatically activated as mass !
  grp  - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
  grp 99 rada 0     radb 0      $ no damping
  LC #plf FACD 1.0 TITL 'Method 3 intelligent sinus'
    $ don't activate lc 7001 - as it is also activated as load by MASS and LC FACD!
    LCC 7004 fact #factor $ +- 180 N passanger load
    LAUN GRP 99 dx #x[m] $ passanger position
  END
endloop
end

-PROG ASE URS:11
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT 3001 NNO     221     DIRE UZ TYPE TIME
PLOT 3001 NNO     221     DIRE AZ TYPE TIME    $ allowable AZ see SOFILOAD
PLOT 3001 NO 2102 DIRE N
PLOT 3001  NO -1     DIRE Estr $ strain energy of all groups
PLOT 3001  NO -1     DIRE Ekin $ kinetic energy of all groups
PLOT 3001  NO -1     DIRE Esum $  energy of all groups
END


<TEXT> Result comments:
Method 1: we apply a fixed predefine dsinus wave.
          Problem: we cannot be shure that the system really reacts exactly in the same frequency as the load frequency.
          Especially with nonlinear effects or moving mass the system frequency will change and the fixed load frequency
          will not remain in resonance.
Method 2: the intelligend load method applies the positive load only in case a controlling node goes down
          and applies a negative load in case the node goes up.
          So the load is always pushing the system and remains in resonance.
          Problem: in method 2 this gives a block load and little peak accelerations on the load jump
Method 3: we start a sinus wave cycle when the controlling node jumps from going up to going down.
          When the next change comes, the next sinus wave is triggered.
          The length of the sinus wave starts with an estimated value and is adjusted in dependance of the cycles.

The analysis does not run quick because due to the moving load (mass) the command LAUN was used and so
in every time step the system stiffness must be made new.

Dr. Juergen Bellmann - SOFiSTiK - 13.06.2018

!#!Info  Example:       intelligent load on nonlinear bedded tower
!#!Info  Keyword:       eigenfrequency; time step analysis; damping; resonance,intelligent load
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!Info  Date:          02.06.2010

$    In diesem Beispiel wird das Bauwerk wie bei einer Schaukel immer nur
$    im richtigen Moment angestossen (aufgeschaukelt).
$
$    In this example the building is pushed always in the right moment to
$    increase the amplitude - like pushing a swing.
$
$ Problem:
$ A modal analysis detects, that the bedding would lift.
$ What effect has this ?
$
$ Answer:
$ You can calculate, what happens if the bedding lifts,
$ only in a nonlinear time step analysis.
$ -> the first eigenfrequency will get smaller (lower frequency)
$ This can be checked in the last plot of this analysis -> Plot after analysis
$
$ The following results are obtained with AQUA - STO#jump 0   :
$
$ - linear first eigenfrequency: LC 5001       1.95 Herz
$ - nonlinear: first swingings: dt=0.56sec. == 1.78 Herz (load is alternating ->
$                                                         decrease load to achieve 1.95)
$ - nonlinear: first swingings: dt=0.90sec. == 1.11 Herz = lower frequency
$
$      dt=0.56sec meaured from time  0.56 - 1.12 sec
$      dt=0.90sec meaured from time  3.24 - 4.14 sec
$
$ The problem is that the load shall build up the swinging (aufschaukeln).
$ Like for a normal children swing, the adult only pushes in the time when the swing
$ goes away from him.
$ This is modelled with an intelligent load. The ASE-loop
$ looks in each time step whether:
$  - the velocity is positive -> apply positive horizontal load
$  - the velocity is negative -> apply negative horizontal load
$
$ In case of STO#jump 1, I tuned the values so that the first nonlinear vertical eigenfrequency
$ is nearly the same as the first nonlinear horizontal eigenfrequency -> system jumps
$ J. Bellmann 2.6.2010

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD
GRP -
LC 1 FACD 1  TITL 'primary loadcase g1+g2'
  lcc 901

LC 6001 FACD 1  TITL 'test g_1'
LC 6002        TITL 'g_2 for additional mass'
  lcc 901

LC 6003 FACD 1  TITL 'test g_1+g_2+horizontal'
  lcc 901
  lcc 902
END

+PROG ASE urs:5
HEAD Eigenfrequencies [without damping]
MASS LC 6002 PRZ 100 $ additional mass - structural dead load is automatically activated as mass !
EIGE 6 LC 5001       $ Please check sum of masses!
END

$ numerical damping: to avoid numerical oszillations
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.25 0.50 1.00 $ Original Newmark without numerical damping               '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 1/6  1/2  1.40 $ Original Wilson with large damping in higher modes       '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET 0.4  0.55 1.00 $ good numerical damping of high freq. for nonlinearities  '/
$ step  N.. DT.. BET  -  - THE 0.70 $ alpha method acc. Hilber-Hughes-Taylor input THE= 1 - |alpha|.
                                    $ example alpha -0.3   --> THE=0.7
+PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD
ctrl solv 998 $ do not make stiffness new during iterations - quicker
              $ normal nonlinear effects (springs or quad-nmat) are sufficiently
              $ iterated via redidual iteration (no stiffness update necessary)
let#dt  0.04 $ seconds time increment
let#plf 1
ECHO DISP,REAC,FORC,NOST,LOAD NO ; ECHO SPRI YES $ activates only the output for spring and cable results
ECHO GRP yes ! activates storage of strain and kinetic energy
$
loop 150 $ number of time steps
  let#node 10605  $ controlling node
  let#velo 0.1    $ read velocity of last time step:
  if #plf>1 $ not possible for first because first step is no dynamic one!
        @KEY N_VELO #plf    $  velocity of loadcast #plf
        LET#velo @(#node,Vy) $ read VZ of node #node
        $ velocity and acceleration can also be plotted in WINGRAF !
  endif
  let#factor 1.00
  if #velo<0.0 ; let#factor -1.00 ; endif   $ most interesting line !! intelligent load !
                                            $ for a sinus load see step_intelligent_load.dat method 3
  STEP 1 DT #dt LCSM 9900 THE 0.70 $ BET 0.25 0.50 1.00
  SYST prob nonl PLC #plf
  MASS LC 6002 PRZ 100 $ additional mass - structural dead load is automatically activated as mass !
  LC #plf+1 FACD 1.0
    lcc 901              $ g_2
    lcc 902 fact #factor $ horizontal_load (intelligent)
  END
  let#plf #plf+1
endloop
END
$ explanation: see comments on top of AQUA

+PROG ASE URS:28
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT LC 1 NNO 10605 DIRE UY TYPE TIME
PLOT LC 1 NNO 10605 DIRE VY TYPE TIME
PLOT LC 1 NNO   609 DIRE UZ TYPE TIME
PLOT LC 1  NO -1     DIRE Estr $ strain energy of all groups
PLOT LC 1  NO -1     DIRE Ekin $ kinetic energy of all groups
PLOT LC 1  NO -1     DIRE Esum $  energy of all groups
$ PLOT LC 1 NNO   609 DIRE PZ TYPE TIME  $ plot only correct with ASE >= version 16.62
END

!#!Info  Example:       CYLINDRIC DAM
!#!Info  Keyword:       eigenfrequency; time step analysis; concrete law; cracked eigenfrequency; damping; hysteresis
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ This example shows eigenfrequencies in cracked state !!!!

$ english file name: step_nonl_concrete_girder.dat

$ Overview: see -> a1_dynamic_overview.dat

$ Impact in concrete girder see also
$             \..\dynamics\ step_nonl_betonbalken.dat
$             \..\dynamics\ explosion_on_th3_quad_girder.dat
$             \..\special\  collaps_element_deactivation.dat

!#!Kapitel System input
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1  C  40 MUE 0
STEE 2  S 500
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Einfeldtraeger beim Ausschalen nichtlinear dynamisch
$ Head single-span beam - removing formwork - nonlinear dynamic study
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000
NODE NO      X          Y
     1,2,3   0,2.5,5   .5
    11,12,13 0,2.5,5  -.5
NODE NO FIX ;  1 pypz ; 3 pypz ; 11,13 pz
GRP 1
  QUAD -  1 2 12 11 M 6 1 T 0.20[m]
  QUAD -  2 3 13 12 M 6 1 T 0.20[m]
GRP 2
  SPRI 1,11 1,11 DX  1 CP 100
  SPRI 3,13 3,13 DX -1 CP 100
END

+PROG BEMESS URS:3
HEAD Definition of reinforcement parameters and minimum reinforcement
GEOM - HA 40 DHA 10 HB 40 DHB 10
DIRE  0 0
PARA NOG - DU 12 16 DL 12 16 ASU 0[cm2/m] 0[cm2/m] ASL 4[cm2/m] 4[cm2/m]
              $ ^ minimum reinforcement for nonlinear analysis
              $ ^ Please check this input with WINGRAF - reinforcement loadcase 99
END

+prog template urs:22 $ Rayleigh damping
kopf Rayleigh damping
$ -------- rayleigh damping ---------
$ frequencies
let#f1     0.1                   $ [Hz]  1st eigenfreq.
let#f2     0.3                   $ [Hz]  2nd eigenfreq.
$ viscous damping ratios
let#xi1 0.01 ; prt#xi1     $ [-] 0.02 = 2% damping at frequency f1 (1% for steel, 3-7% for concrete)
let#xi2 0.01 ; prt#xi2     $ [-] at frequency f2                   (2-3% for prestressed concrete)
$
let#w1 2*#pi*#f1; sto#w2 2*#pi*#f2;
$ calculate rayleigh coeff. for steel
sto#rada 2*#w1*#w2*(#xi1*#w2-#xi2*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2); prt#rada   $ mass proportional
sto#radb 2*(#xi2*#w2-#xi1*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2)        ; prt#radb   $ stiffness proportional
$
ende


!#!Kapitel Sudden crack due to reducing concrete tensile strength

+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD
STEP 50 0.005 THE 0.7 LCSM 9900 LCST 201 $ THE 0.7 = alpha-method - alpha= -0.30
SYST PROB NONL ITER 80 NMAT YES TOL -0.2 TOL4 0.002
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 4.00 $ nackte Betonzugfestigkeit  $ pure tensile strength
LC 101 FACD 1.0
END

+PROG ASE URS:5
HEAD Now suddenly crack induced by reducing concrete tensile strength
ECHO MAT - $ please look at least one time to the material output+plots of ASE !!
STEP 100 0.005 THE 0.7 LCSM 9900 LCST CONT $ THE 0.7 = alpha-method - alpha= -0.30
SYST PROB NONL ITER 80 NMAT YES TOL -0.2 TOL4 0.002 PLC 101
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 2.00 $ fctk reduced to enforce girder to crack
                          $ or:   ELEM QUAD no 8 FCTK 0.50  $ Collaps Analyse with induced crack only in Elem 8
LC 102 FACD 1.0
END

+PROG ASE URS:13
HEAD Now damping to see energy to get constant
ECHO MAT - $ please look at least one time to the material output+plots of ASE !!
STEP 100 0.005 THE 0.7 LCSM 9900 LCST CONT $ THE 0.7 = alpha-method - alpha= -0.30
SYST PROB NONL ITER 80 NMAT YES TOL -0.2 TOL4 0.002 PLC 102
grp - rada #rada #radb
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 2.00 $ fctk reduced to enforce girder to crack
                          $ or:   ELEM QUAD no 8 FCTK 0.50  $ Collaps Analyse with induced crack only in Elem 8
LC 103 FACD 1.0
END

!#!Kapitel Impact loading

-prog sofiload urs:10
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LC 8001 TYPE none titl 'impact load'
  AREA type PG P1 85 x1 2.1 -0.4 x2 dxy 0.8 0.8
END

-PROG ASE URS:11
HEAD Impact Primary loadcase
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 2.0 $ pure tensile strength reduced
LC 1001 FACD 1.0 TITL PLC_steady
sto#lc_start 1001
END

-PROG ASE URS:12
HEAD Nonlinear dynamic impact
CTRL WARN 350,351,352,353  $ deactivates error messages  "maximun strain or capacity is reached"
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 2.0 $ pure tensile strength reduced
sto#DT 0.01
        let#nsteps 5
        sto#plc #lc_start
        sto#lc_impact #plc+#nsteps
STEP #nsteps DT #dt THE 0.7 DIV 0 LCSM 9801 $ THE 0.7 = alpha-method - alpha= -0.30
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES PLC #plc TOL -0.2 TOL4 0.002
LC #plc+1 FACD 1.0
  LCC 8001
END

-PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD Swinging goes on
CTRL WARN 350,351,352,353  $ deactivates error messages  "maximun strain or capacity is reached"
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 2.0 $ pure tensile strength reduced
        let#nsteps 30
        sto#plc #lc_impact
        sto#lc_swing #plc+#nsteps
STEP #nsteps DT #dt THE 0.7 DIV 0 LCSM 9801 $ THE 0.7 = alpha-method - alpha= -0.30
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES PLC #plc TOL -0.2 TOL4 0.002
LC #plc+1 FACD 1.0
sto#plc #plc+30
END

-PROG ASE URS:9
HEAD Final swinging with high damping to get remaining deformation
CTRL WARN 350,351,352,353  $ deactivates error messages  "maximun strain or capacity is reached"
CTRL CONC V3 4.50 V4 2.0 $ pure tensile strength reduced
        let#nsteps 40
        sto#plc #lc_swing
STEP #nsteps DT #dt THE 0.7 DIV 0 LCSM 9801 $ THE 0.7 = alpha-method - alpha= -0.30
SYST PROB NONL NMAT YES PLC #plc TOL -0.2 TOL4 0.002
GRP - RADA 1.5 RADB 0.0015  $ 15 % decrement for 5 Herz
LC #plc+1 FACD 1.0
END

-PROG ASE URS:7
HEAD Plot after analysis  $ see also time step plots with RESULTS -> dynamics\step_sofiload_ase.dat
PLOT LC 1001 NNO 2 DIRE UZ TYPE TIME
$ Plot in layers :
PLOT LC 1001 DIRE  SX TYPE TIME NO 1007 XI -1.0
PLOT LC 1001 DIRE  SX TYPE EX   NO 1007 XI -1.0 $ -> Hysterese
PLOT LC 1001 DIRE SS1 TYPE EX   NO 1007 XI  1.0
$ For stress in reinforcement, choose ss1 or ss2 and
$ select upper/lower side just with xi= -1/+1
END

+PROG SOFILOAD URS:3
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LC 2 TITL 'G_2'
  QUAD GRP 0 TYPE PZZ P 3.0 $ additional dead load for additional mass g_2

$ pedestrians with time function FUNC
LC 7001        TITL 'pedestrians'
  NODE 216,217,218,219,220 TYPE PG 25.00
  sto#f 3.08 $ frequency (from eigenvalues)
  sto#dtjump 1./#f $ time for one jump
  FUNC  T          F
      0.000    .0
   #dtjump/4  1.0     $ 1. impulse   as one period has 4 loadsteps 0-1-1-0
      -       1.0
      -        .0
      -        .0
      -       1.0     $ 2. impulse
      -       1.0
      -        .0
  loop 30
      -        .0
      -       1.0     $ ... impulse  30*1/3.08 = 10 sec
      -       1.0
      -        .0
  endloop
  $   100       .0     $ End of FUNC
END

+prog template urs:22 $ Rayleigh damping
head Rayleigh damping
$ -------- rayleigh damping ---------
$ frequencies
let#f1     1.5                    $ [Hz]  1st eigenfreq.
let#f2     5.0                    $ [Hz]  2nd eigenfreq.
$ viscous damping ratios
let#xi1 0.02 ; prt#xi1     $ [-] 0.02 = 2% damping at frequency f1 (1% for steel, 3-7% for concrete)
let#xi2 0.02 ; prt#xi2     $ [-] at frequency f2                   (2-3% for prestressed concrete)
$
let#w1 2*#pi*#f1; sto#w2 2*#pi*#f2;
$ calculate rayleigh coeff. for steel
sto#rada 2*#w1*#w2*(#xi1*#w2-#xi2*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2); prt#rada   $ mass proportional
sto#radb 2*(#xi2*#w2-#xi1*#w1)/(#w2**2-#w1**2)        ; prt#radb   $ stiffness proportional
$
end

+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD Steady state g_1+g_2
SYST PROB NONL
LC 101 FACD 1 TITL 'Steady state g_1+g_2'
  LCC 2 $ G_2
END

<TEXT>
Loadfunctions:
In ASE usually nonlinear dynamic is calculated. Therefore the complete stress state
including dead load must be genereated.
To the permanent part (dead load) the variable part of the loading
(earthquake, impuls, initial velocity) must be added.
It is best to combine the loading directly in ASE, e.g.:

LC 102 FACD 1
  $ LCC 2 $ permanten additional dead load without load function - with MASS LC 2 and FACD 1 already included
  LCC 901 $ variable load with load function from SOFILOAD

When the variable load starts, the static state already exists.
If you first analyze the steady state in a separate loadcase without
time dynamic (e.g. loadcase 101) you can then continue with the time dynamic analysis
using the steady state as a primary loadcase - see SYST PLC 101 above.
If you would activate the dead load in the time step analysis for the first time,
the system would accelerate from the unstressed start state and then swing arround
the steady state.
This would be the case if you would suddenly remove the formwork from a concrete girder,
see ase.dat\english\dynamics\ step_nonl_concrete_girder.dat

In order to avoid large databases for the time step method the calculation can be made
only with two load cases which vary in each case.
This takes place automatically using STEP N>1 and LCST. The results which are important
for the user can be stored then in separate storage load cases with
STEP ... LCST ... SELE ... (bit pattern).

</TEXT>

+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD
STEP N 50 DT 0.02 THE 0.70 LCST 1002 SELE 1+64 LCSM 9900
SYST PROB NONL PLC 101
CTRL ITER 0 $ quicker for simple nonlinear effects
grp - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
grp 5 rada 0     radb 0      $ springs have damping in nonlinear effect alone
MASS LC 2 PRZ 100 $ g_2 mass - is applied as dynamic mass and also as static load
                  $ via dead load factor LC...FACD! No more LCC 7001 necessary !
                  $ (only on LC-FACD - not on GRP...FACD )
                  $ The structural mass is automatic applied as mass with LC-FACD
LC  102 FACD 1 $ After the analysis, LC 102 contains the result after 50 time steps due to LCST!
  LCC 7001  $ copies the load using the loadfunction FUNC defined in SOFILOAD ! -> see loads e.g. in Wingraf
END

HEAD adding 50 time steps

SYST PROB NONL PLC 102

grp - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
grp 5 rada 0     radb 0      $ springs have damping in nonlinear effect alone
MASS LC 2 PRZ 100
LC  103 FACD 1 $ Wegen LFSP Eingabe enthÃ¤lt LF 103 am Ende das Ergebnis nach 100 Zeitschritten ! After the analysis, LC 103 contains the result after 100 time steps due to LCST!
  LCC 7001
END

$ echo stat yes $Statistic nonlinear effects in all time steps

SYST PROB NONL PLC 103
CTRL ITER 0 $ quicker for simple nonlinear effects
grp - rada #rada radb #radb  $ damping
grp 5 rada 0     radb 0      $ springs have damping in nonlinear effect alone

  LCC 7001

+prog template urs:3
head read masses mr-xx of all nodes
let#0 2             $ full test of CADIMP
sto#lc 2001            $ first eigenvalue LC number

sto#maxnode  9999
sto#mrxxnode(#maxnode)   0 $ predefine array #mrxxnode(0:99999) for max. #maxnode nodes
$  LET#LOOPSIZE #maxnode+100
loop#i0 10000 $ LOOPSIZE 10000
  let#i1 #i0+1 $ as #i0 starts with 0-1-2-3  -> #i1 starts with 1-2-3-4..99
  sto#mrxxnode(#i1) 0   $ set array to zero
endloop #i1 < #maxnode

txe masses of all nodes:
$ let#0 2             $ full test of CADIMP
let#summx 0
let#summrxx 0
let#CDB_IER 0       $ prepare for loop
@key MASS_EFF #lc+1000
LOOP $ ALL records
  let#nr     @(NR)                     $ get x of node #n1 of cdbase
  if #cdb_ier<2   $ if next element successful read:
    if #nr>0
      let#mx    @(MT)
      let#mrxx  @(MR)
      let#mryy  @(MR+1) $ for myy ...
      txe Node #(#nr,6.0) mass m-xx=  #(#mx,10.3) tons  rot-mr-xx=  #(#mrxx,10.3) tons*m
      let#summx   #summx+#mx
      let#summrxx #summrxx+#mrxx
      if #nr<#maxnode+1
        sto#mrxxnode(#nr) #mrxx
      endif
    endif
  endif
ENDLOOP #CDB_IER < 2
txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
let#nr 0
txe Sum  #(#nr,6.0) mass m-xx=  #(#summx,10.3) tons  rot-mr-xx=  #(#summrxx,10.3) tons*m

END

+prog template urs:8
head read displacements and compute phix^2*mrxx


txe To detect critical rotational eigenmode:
txe Compare rotational factor sum(phix^2*mrxx) of a series of eigenmodes
txe -
sto#lc_torsion 0
sto#maxvalue   0

sto#nlc 20            $ number of eigenmodes
loop#ilc0
  let#ilc1 #ilc0+1 $ as #ilc0 starts with 0-1-2-3  -> #ilc0 starts with 1-2-3-4
  let#lceige #lc+#ilc0


        $ let#0 2             $ full test of CADIMP
        let#sumff    0
        let#sumplus  0
        let#summinus 0
        let#CDB_IER 0       $ prepare for loop
        @key N_DISP #lceige
        LOOP $ ALL records
          let#nr     @(NR)                     $ get x of node #n1 of cdbase
          if #cdb_ier<2   $ if next element successful read:
            if #nr>0
            if #nr<#maxnode+1
              let#phix @(URX)
              let#mrxx #mrxxnode(#nr)
              let#ff   #phix*#phix*#mrxx
              $ txe LC #lceige Node #(#nr,6.0) phix= #(#phix,9.6) mrxx=  #(#mrxx,10.3) ff=  #(#ff,12.6)
              let#sumff   #sumff+#ff
              if  #phix>0 ; let#sumplus    #sumplus+#ff   ; endif
              if  #phix<0 ; let#summinus   #summinus+#ff  ; endif
            endif
            endif
          endif
        ENDLOOP #CDB_IER < 2
        $ txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        let#nr 0
        let#CDB_IER 0       $ prepare for loop
        let#sumsign #sumplus
        if  -#summinus>#sumplus ; let#sumsign -#summinus ; endif
        txe eigenmode #lceige rotational factor sum(phix^2*mrxx)=#(#sumff,12.6) sumsign=#(#sumsign,12.6)
        if #sumsign>#maxvalue
          sto#lc_torsion #lceige
          sto#maxvalue   #sumsign
        endif

endloop #ilc1 < #nlc
txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
txe -
txe Controlling eigenmode for torsion found in eigenvalue loadcase #lc_torsion
txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END

+prog WING urs:1
head Controlling eigenmode for torsion
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0.864813 Y -0.422351 Z 0.271511 AXIS POSZ
MOVE X DEL DTYP TEXT; MOVE X 25 14 UNIT PR SCHH .6 C 1001
TEXT Controlling eigenmode for torsion found in eigenvalue loadcase #lc_torsion
LC #lc_torsion
beam mt schh 0.35
end

!#!Info  Example:       Cable sag
!#!Info  Keyword:       cable; sag
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ Ein Seil zur Abspannung eines hohen Mastes wird unter BerÃ¼cksichtigung
$ des Seildurchhanges berechnet. Das zunÃ¤chst gerade eingegebene Seil
$ erhÃ¤lt dabei unter Eigengewicht und unter einer Anfangsvorspannung
$ eine hohe Normalkraft (ohne Anfangsvorspannung wÃ¤re die eingegebene
$ Kettenlinie instabil). Der Durchhang ist entspechend gering. Um den
$ Durchhang den gewÃ¼nschten realen Gegebenheiten anzupassen wird im
$ vorliegenden Beispiel das Seil schrittweise nachgelassen - dabei wird
$ die Technik der PrimÃ¤rlastfallverarbeitung ausgenutzt. Nach AbschluÃŸ
$ dieser Formfindung wird eine horizontale Windbelastung auf das Seil
$ aufgebracht. Der GRAF-Plot zeigt die Normalkraft angetragen an der
$ unverformten Seilachse sowie die wahre Verschiebung im Endzustand,
$ also den Durchhang (ÃœberhÃ¶hungsfaktor 1.0).

$PROG
$-------------------------------------------------------------------------
h=350        $ bauhoehe                             [m]
l=300        $ Laenge im Grundriss                  [m]
n=10         $ Anzahl Zwischenpunkte
Deff=32      $ effektive Seildurchmesser            [mm]
gam=78.5     $ spez. Gewicht Seil-Material          [kN/m3]
ISOLATOR=4.0 $ Gewicht Isolator                     [KN]
vor=100      $ Vorspannung (bei geradem  Einbau)    [kN]
windx=0.3    $ Windlast pro projezierte Laenge      [kN/m]

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Seile
NORM din 18800
STEE 1 ST 37
STEE 2 PST 1770 ES 160000 GAM $(gam)
SCIT 7,9 MNO 2 D $(Deff) $ tube or cable
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Seil mit Isolatoren
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000

NODE 1      X     0   Y 0  Z 0
GRP 0
loop#m $(n)
        let#1 1+#m
        let#f #1/$(n)
        NODE 1+#1 X  -$(l)*#f  Y 0  Z -$(h)*#f
        CABL NO    NA    NE    NCS
             1+#m  1+#m  2+#m  9
endloop
NODE NO     FIX
     1      pp
     1+$(n) pp
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:10
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LC 901 TYPE NONE TITL 'nodal load'
  NODE (2 $(n) 1) PZZ $(ISOLATOR)
LC 902 TYPE NONE TITL 'elongation'
  CABL FROM 1 TO 999 INC 1 TYPE EX PA 3
LC 903 TYPE NONE TITL 'wind'
  CABL FROM 1 TO 999 INC 1 TYPE PXX PA $(windx)
END


!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:3
HEAD Formfindung
$ steu seil 0
$ steu iter 0
SYST PROB TH3 ITER 100
GRP 0 FACS 1 PREX $(vor)
LC 1 FACD 1
  LCC 901
END

+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD Kontrolle Primaerlastfall
$ steu seil 0
$ steu iter 0

GRP 0 FACS 1
LC 2 FACD 1
  LCC 901
END

+PROG ASE URS:5
HEAD Seile nachlassen 3 %o Laengenzugabe
$ steu seil 0
$ steu iter 0
SYST PROB TH3 ITER 100      PLC 2
GRP 0 FACS 1
ctrl warn 256 $ strain load additive - OK
LC 3 FACD 1
  LCC 901
  LCC 902
END

+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD Seile weitere 3%o nachlassen +3 %o Laengenzugabe
$ steu seil 0
$ steu iter 0
SYST PROB TH3 ITER 100      PLC 3
GRP 0 FACS 1
ctrl warn 256 $ strain load additive - OK
LC 4 FACD 1
  LCC 901
  LCC 902
END

+PROG ASE URS:7
HEAD erneut Kontrolle Primaerlastfall nur echte Lasten!!
$ steu seil 0
$ steu iter 0
SYST PROB TH3 ITER 100      PLC 4

ctrl warn 256 $ strain load additive - OK

  LCC 901
END

+PROG ASE URS:8

$ steu iter 0

  LCC 901
  LCC 903 $ wind

!#!Info  Example:       Cable eigenfrequencies
!#!Info  Keyword:       cable; eigenfrequency
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ Cable eigenfrequencies
$
$ Cable eigenfrequencies see also  ase.dat\english\dynamics\cable_dynamics.dat
$                              and ase.dat\english\dynamics\whip.dat
$ earthquake analysis see DYNA and ase.dat\english\dynamics\earthquake_jb.dat
$                              and csm.dat\english\csm33_earthquake_bridge.dat

$PROG
$-------------------------------------------------------------------------
#define h=50         $  [m]
#define l=100        $  [m]
#define n=10         $
#define vor=30       $  [kN]
$

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Seile
NORM din 18800
STEE 1 ST 37
STEE 2 PST 1770 ES 160000
CABL 1 D 50
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Cable eigenfrequencies
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000

NODE 1      X     0   Y 0  Z 0
GRP 1
loop#m $(n)
        let#1 1+#m
        let#f #1/$(n)
        NODE 1+#1 X  -$(l)*#f  Y 0  Z -$(h)*#f
        CABL NO    NA    NE    NCS
             1+#m  1+#m  2+#m  1
endloop

     1      pp
     1+$(n) pp
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE URS:3

LC 1 FACD 1
END

+PROG ASE URS:4

EIGE 10 LC 1001
END
