!#!Info  Example:       Buckling eigenvalues with devided cables
!#!Info  Keyword:       cable; buckling eigenvalue
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+prog aqua urs:1
HEAD Mast
NORM din 18800
UNIT 5
STEE 1 ST 37
STEE 2 ST 52
STEE 8 PST 1770 ES 160000
SCIT 1 MNO 1 D 500 T 4 $ Mast
SCIT 2 MNO 8 D 10 $ tube or cable
END

+prog sofimsha urs:2
HEAD MAST - Buckling eigenvalues with devided cables
UNIT 5
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000
NODE (101 120 1) X 0 Y 0 Z (0 -2)
NODE 101 FIX ppmz
let#r 18.0
let#phi   0 ; NODE 1 X #r*sin(#phi) Y #r*cos(#phi) Z 0 FIX pp
let#phi 120 ; NODE 2 X #r*sin(#phi) Y #r*cos(#phi) Z 0 FIX pp
let#phi 240 ; NODE 3 X #r*sin(#phi) Y #r*cos(#phi) Z 0 FIX pp
GRP 1
  BEAM (101 119 1) (101 1) (102 1) NCS 1
GRP 2
  CABL fit 1,2,3 119 NCS 2 DIV 1
  CABL fit 1,2,3 110 NCS 2 DIV 4     $ devision in 4 separate cables
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LC 901 TITL 'little load for e-modulus analysis'
  BEAM GRP 1 TYPE  PY PA  0.5
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG ASE urs:4
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3
GRP -
GRP 2 PREX 5.00
LC 1 FACD 1
END
SYST PROB TH3 PLC 1
GRP -
LC 2 FACD 1 TITL 'little load for e-modulus analysis'
  LCC 901
END

+PROG ASE urs:6
HEAD BUCK lmin auto
SYST PLC 1
EIGE 10 BUCK LC 2101 lmin auto
END

+PROG ASE urs:5
HEAD alternativ
SYST PLC 1
GRP2 2 GEOM 0 $ alternative: geometric stiffness of cables not scaled
EIGE 10 BUCK LC 3101
END

<TEXT>
Please notice, that as a test, the bottom cables are devided and the top cables are not devided!


For the analysis of real cable eigenfrequencies, a cable must be devided to get active masses inside the cable.

In Wingraf see cable elements - cable sag
</TEXT>

+prog template urs:7
head Analysis of effective cable E-moduls
$ let#0 2             $ full test of CADIMP
let#lc1 1  $ two loadcases to extract     e= delta-N / delta-vx
let#lc2 2
#define cableemod
txe Analysis of effective cable E-moduls
txe E-modulus= delta-N / delta-vx of the load cases #lc1 and #lc2
txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
txe Cableno.     N-LC1     N-LC2    vx-LC1    vx-LC2    vq-LC1    vq-LC2 E-modulus
txe               [kN]      [kN]      [mm]      [mm]      [mm]      [mm]    [kN/m]
let#CDB_IER 0
@key CABL_RES #lc1
if #CDB_IER<2       $ if elements available:
  loop
    let#nr @(NR)    $ read element number
    if #cdb_ier<2   $ if next element successful read:
    if #nr>0        $ header has #nr=0
      let#N1  @(N)      $ normal force
      let#vx1 @(#nr,V)  $  axial displacement
      let#vq1 @(#nr,VQ) $  sagging
        $ now read results of lc2 for this cable #nr :
        let#CDB_IER_lc1 #CDB_IER
        @key CABL_RES #lc2
        let#N2  @(#nr,N)      $ normal force
        let#vx2 @(#nr,V)  $  axial displacement
        let#vq2 @(#nr,VQ) $  sagging
        let#CDB_IER #CDB_IER_lc1
        @key CABL_RES #lc1    $ switch back to lc1
        let#N0  @(#nr,N)      $ reread to set pointer to this cable
      LET#E (#N2-#N1)/(#vx2-#vx1)
      LET#vx1 #vx1*1000 ! print in mm
      LET#vx2 #vx2*1000 ! print in mm
      LET#vq1 #vq1*1000 ! print in mm
      LET#vq2 #vq2*1000 ! print in mm
      txe #(#nr,8.0) #(#N1,9.1) #(#N2,9.1) #(#vx1,9.1) #(#vx2,9.1) #(#vq1,9.1) #(#vq2,9.1) #(#E,9.1)
    endif
    endif
  endloop #cdb_ier<2 $ end - if all elements read -> end this loop
endif
txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
txe vx= axial displacement vq= sagging transverse to the cable
txe In LC1 and LC2 the same cable dead load must act and no further cable loads are allowed!
#enddef
#include cableemod
end

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?




!#!Info  Example:       Cable unstressed length
!#!Info  Keyword:       cable; sag; unstressed length
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ cable_unstressed_length.dat

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM DIN 18800
STEE 1 TYPE S   CLAS 355  ES 210000
STEE 2 TYPE PST CLAS 1770 ES 160000
SCIT 1 MNO 1 D 600 T 30 $ tube or cable
CABL NO 2 MNO 2 D 30
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD cable_unstressed_length input LEN0
$  Cables geometric nonlinear analysis: With LEN0 now an unstressed length can be
$  input for cables:
$  LEN0 NO L0 TYPE
$  ETYP:TRUS or CABL (default CABL)
$  NO: elementnumber
$  TYPE=TOTA: input of total cable installation length L0 (default)
$  TYPE=DELT: input difference L0 to the system length in the undeformed system
$  example: cable_unstressed_length.dat:
$  LEN0 CABL 101001 -0.100 TYPE DELT $ install cable 100 mm shorter than system length
$  LEN0 CABL 102001 67.000 TYPE TOTA $ install cable with length 67.000 m
$  Funktion: If a cable is activated in a CS for the first time and a LEN0 input
$  is found for it, the cable is installed stressfree with this length, independant
$  of deformations in the primary loadcase PLC!
$  Internally it gets an additional prestress that shortens it so that the
$  desired length appears.
$  Without LEN0 (normal behaviour) a cable is installed in that way that on the PLC deformations
$  it has force 0 (without prestress and load on internal cable sagging).
$ JÃ¼rgen Bellmann 23.06.2008
$
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 GDIR POSZ
NODE (10 20 1)  X (0  6) Y 0 Z   0
NODE  901                    Z -25
NODE  902                    Z -30
NODE 10,901,902 FIX f
GRP 1
  BEAM NO (10 15 1) NA (10 1) NE (11  1) NCS 1
GRP 101
  CABL NO 1 NA 901 NE 16 NCS 2
GRP 2
  BEAM NO (16 19 1) NA (16 1) NE (17  1) NCS 1
GRP 102
  CABL NO 1 NA 902 NE 20 NCS 2
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LC 2 TITL 'g2'
  BEAM GRP 1,2 TYPE  PG PA  5
LC 3 TITL 'Single load'
  NODE NO 20   TYPE PZZ P1 30
LC 32 TITL 'little load for e-modulus analysis'
  BEAM GRP 1,2 TYPE  PG PA  1
LC 42 TITL 'little load for e-modulus analysis'
  BEAM GRP 1,2 TYPE  PG PA  1

LC 12 TITL 'shortening cable 1 mm'
  CABL 101001 TYPE WX PA -1[mm] $ 1 mm cable shortening - StabverkÃ¼rzung
LC 22 TITL 'shortening cable 1 mm'
  CABL 102001 TYPE WX PA -1[mm] $ 1 mm cable shortening - StabverkÃ¼rzung
LC 901 TYPE NONE TITL 'little lifting'
  NODE 16 PZZ -5
END

+prog template urs:5
head Analysis of effective cable E-moduls
$ let#0 2             $ full test of CADIMP
let#lc1 4030  $ two loadcases to extract     e= delta-N / delta-vx
let#lc2 4032
#define cableemod
txe Analysis of effective cable E-moduls
txe E-modulus= delta-N / delta-vx of the load cases #lc1 and #lc2
txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
txe Cableno.     N-LC1     N-LC2    vx-LC1    vx-LC2    vq-LC1    vq-LC2 E-modulus
txe               [kN]      [kN]      [mm]      [mm]      [mm]      [mm]    [kN/m]
let#CDB_IER 0
@key CABL_RES #lc1
if #CDB_IER<2       $ if elements available:
  loop
    let#nr @(NR)    $ read element number
    if #cdb_ier<2   $ if next element successful read:
    if #nr>0        $ header has #nr=0
      let#N1  @(N)      $ normal force
      let#vx1 @(#nr,V)  $  axial displacement
      let#vq1 @(#nr,VQ) $  sagging
        $ now read results of lc2 for this cable #nr :
        let#CDB_IER_lc1 #CDB_IER
        @key CABL_RES #lc2
        let#N2  @(#nr,N)      $ normal force
        let#vx2 @(#nr,V)  $  axial displacement
        let#vq2 @(#nr,VQ) $  sagging
        let#CDB_IER #CDB_IER_lc1
        @key CABL_RES #lc1    $ switch back to lc1
        let#N0  @(#nr,N)      $ reread to set pointer to this cable
      LET#E (#N2-#N1)/(#vx2-#vx1)
      LET#vx1 #vx1*1000 ! print in mm
      LET#vx2 #vx2*1000 ! print in mm
      LET#vq1 #vq1*1000 ! print in mm
      LET#vq2 #vq2*1000 ! print in mm
      txe #(#nr,8.0) #(#N1,9.1) #(#N2,9.1) #(#vx1,9.1) #(#vx2,9.1) #(#vq1,9.1) #(#vq2,9.1) #(#E,9.1)
    endif
    endif
  endloop #cdb_ier<2 $ end - if all elements read -> end this loop
endif
txe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
txe vx= axial displacement vq= sagging transverse to the cable
txe In LC1 and LC2 the same cable dead load must act and no further cable loads are allowed!
#enddef
#include cableemod
end

                                 $ If not -> apply a little correction prestress for the hangers

<text>

what has to be done:
In LC 701 the girder is defined to be very soft.
The reason for doing this is that the full girder weight acts on the hanger
and gives correct hanger forces.
This is the only purpose of LC701. The estimated prestressing force in LC701 reduces the main cable deformation.
ITER 1 is used because a first equation solving (ITER 1) gives immediately and correctly the
necessary hanger forces for the deck deadload.
Further iterations would only disturb this quasi-linear result for the hangers.
.
In LC702 we now take the found (and almost correct) hanger forces in a system where now the hangers are all very soft.
The hangers pull down with an almost constant force being in equilibrium with the girder weight.
This pulls the main cable in the correct form.
In order to correct the small horizontal inaccuracy you can also add a small hanger prestressing force.
The purpose of prex 0 for the hanger in LC 702 is to overtake the above calculated hanger forces.
The hanger forces will not change due to deformations of the upper main cable.
.
We now activate all elements with real stiffness and check equilibrium for LC101.
LC101 is now having all cable forces and the structure in the wanted position and acts as basic LC (PLF) for all subsequent LCs.
.
Using CTRL DIFF 2000 we can store only the difference of other loads to the PLF.

The above technique only works for vertical hangers - if you have inclined hanges you must use CSM-optimization.
See also csm.dat\..\opimize\csm28_suspension_bridge_real.dat

J. Bellmann SOFiSTiK AG

<\text>

!#!Info  Example:       Warping torsion - Interpretation of torsional parts
!#!Info  Keyword:       warping
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$ See also  ase11_girder_overturning.dat

$   The total torsional moment Mt has 3 parts (MT= MTp +MTs +MTn) :
$   MTp primary torsional moment from Saint Venant shear stresses
$   MTs secondary torsional moment from longitudinal warping stresses
$   MTn theory 2. order torsional moment from twisted normal stresses
$

$   Interpretation see below and in the ASE manual Theoretical background beam element

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:8
HEAD Material, cross section
NORM DIN 18800  $ din for steel structures
ECHO SECT FULL
STEE 1 S 355
SECT 1 MNO 1  TITL 'GENERAL I-BEAM'
 $ SV   cm 506884[CM6]    IT 44.18[CM4]  only if you want to adjust them !

VERT    1 150 200
        2  =  186
        3  4  =
        4  = -186
        5 150 =
        6  = -200
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2

     2 X 2.0
     3 X 4.0
BEAM MESH 1 2 NCS 1  DIV 5
BEAM MESH 2 3 NCS 1  DIV 5
END

  NODE 2 PXX +1000 ;  NODE 3 MXX  10.0 $ PXX for TH3 !

END

Please notice that at the cantlever end (beam 10 x= 0.4) already a part of the load MT= 10 kNm
is carried by warping although there are no longitudinal warping stresses at that location (free end)
refer to PROG RESULTS Cross section stresses!

You can imagine this in the following way:
The top flange longitudinal warping stresses at beam 1 x=0 want to pull pack the top flange at the cantilever.
The bottom flange longitudinal warping stresses want to pull pack the bottom flange as well.
This pair of forces (flange shear from warping longitudinal stresses) carries a part of the MT loading.
So the longitudinal warping stresses at the beginning of the beam create a MTs at the end - and oposite.
An MTs at a beam section x1 creates longitudinal warping stresses at another beam section x2.

$   The total torsional moment Mt has 3 parts (MT= MTp +MTs +MTn) :
$   MTp primary torsional moment from Saint Venant shear stresses
$   MTs secondary torsional moment (flange shear from warping longitudinal stresses)
$   MTn theory 2. order torsional moment from twisted normal stresses
$   Mb warping moment (from warping longitudinal stresses - creates MTs at other beam sections)


Interpretation:
- beam 1    : MT carried nearly completely by longitudinal warping stresses. As rotation is small also MTn is small
- beam 5    : rotation bigger  -> MTn gets bigger -> a part of MT is carried by twisted normal force stresses
- beam 6-10 : normal force = 0 -> MTn3 nearly 0.0
- beam   10 : MT carried mainly by Saint Venant shear stresses                JB 05.11.2013

See also  ase11_girder_overturning.dat
  Interpretation see also in the ASE manual Theoretical background beam element
</TEXT>

!#!Info  Example:       Excavator Analysis of rotated systems
!#!Info  Keyword:       kinematics, rotation, rigid body rotation
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ Please notice additional remarks in file kinematic_1.dat

$ Further remarks at the end of this file

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+prog aqua urs:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
CONC 1 C 30
STEE 2
STEE 3 S 355 $ Steel
STEE 7 S 355 GAM 0 $ Connection to single mass MASS 6 without gamma to easy check the load
$
SREC 1 H 500[mm] 200[mm] MNO 1
SCIT  2 MNO 3 D 550 T 3 $ tube or cable
SCIT  7 MNO 7 D 200 T 3 $ tube or cable

SECT 9 MNO 1 TITL 'excentric'
  let#h  300
  let#b  300
  POLY TYPE OPZ
  VERT   1  Y #b/2 Z  0
       2  Y #b/2 Z  +#h
SECT 10 MNO 1 TITL 'without add. weight'
  let#h  300
  let#b  300
  POLY TYPE OPZ
  VERT   1  Y #b/2 Z  -#h/2
       2  Y #b/2 Z  +#h/2
SECT 11 MNO 1 TITL 'with add. weight'
  let#h  200
  let#b  200
  POLY TYPE OPZ
  VERT   1  Y #b/2 Z  -#h/2
       2  Y #b/2 Z  +#h/2
  SV AG 0.50 $ total g = 0.25 + 0.50 = 0.75 kN/m (0.50= add. weight)
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:3
HEAD Kinematics test beam rotation - Analysis of rotated systems
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 POSZ XREF 0 0 0 T11 1 0 0 T12 0 -1 0
NODE        1 X          0.0  FIX f
NODE        2 X    2.4000000
NODE        3 X    2.5000000
NODE        4 X    5.0000000
NODE        5 X    5.0000000 Z -1.90
NODE        6 X    5.0000000 Z -2.00

NODE     101 X 0 0 1.00 fix pp $ Quad plane
NODE     102 X 7 0 1.00 fix pp
NODE     103 X 0 7 1.00 fix pp
NODE     104 X 7 7 1.00 fix pp
GRP 1 ; BEAM 1 1 2 NCS  9    ZA -0.15  ZE -0.15  $ buztwithout NP -1 - thus center of gravity placed at ZA-ZE !
        BEAM 2 2 3 NCS  2
GRP 2 ; BEAM 1 3 4 NCS  9 NP -1
GRP 3 ; BEAM 1 4 5 NCS 11
        BEAM 2 5 6 NCS  7 $ Connection to single mass MASS 6 without gamma to easy check the load
GRP 4 ; MASS 6 MX 0.5
GRP 9 ; quad - 101 102 104 103  $ Quad plane
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+prog ase urs:2
HEAD
LC 1 FACD 1
END
HEAD
loop#1 6
  let#dphi (#1+1)*15
  LAUN GRP 1,2,3,4 PHI  #dphi[Â°] XM 0[m] YM 0[m] $ rot um ZZ
  LC 11+#1 FACD 1
  END
endloop

loop#1 6
  let#dphi (#1+1)*15
  LAUN GRP 1,2,3,4 PHI     90[Â°] XM 0[m] YM 0[m] $ rot um ZZ
  LAUN -1
  LAUN GRP 1,2,3,4 PHI -#dphi[Â°] YM 0[m] ZM 0[m] $ rot um XX
  LC 21+#1 FACD 1
  END
endloop

loop#1 6
  let#dphi (#1+1)*15
  LAUN GRP 1,2,3,4 PHI     90[Â°] XM 0[m] YM 0[m] $ rot um ZZ
  LAUN -1
  LAUN GRP 1,2,3,4 PHI    -90[Â°] YM 0[m] ZM 0[m] $ rot um XX
  LAUN -1
  LAUN GRP 1,2,3,4 PHI -#dphi[Â°] XM 0[m] ZM 0[m] $ rot um YY
  LC 31+#1 FACD 1
  END
endloop
END

System:

Verstelltes System:
  - Der runde Querschnitt unten (Stab 1002) soll die Verschub- oder Drehachse symbolisieren.
      Sein lokales Koordinatensystem definiert das Bezugssystem fÃ¼r Richtung der Beschleunigungen
      So ist in Lastfall 301 dieses lokale Koordinatensystem mit TRAN um 60 Grad
      um die globale Z-Achse verstellt
      -> siehe Animator Lastfall 301 - der Stab 1002 zeigt in diese verstellte Richtung

Beschleunigung im verstellten System:
  - In Lastfall 301 wird nun berechnet, dass eine Presse in Stab 1002 das vordere Teilsystem
      Gruppe 2,3,4 (ohne 1) in diese Richtung (Stab 1002 lokal x verstellt) beschleunigt.
      (LÃ¤ngsverschub)
      Die Einzelmasse wird dadurch in diese Richtung mit 10 m/sec^2 beschleunigt und
      erzeugt eine entgegengesetzt gerichtete TrÃ¤gheitskraft von
      F=a*m = 10m/sec^2 * 0.5t = 5 kN
      -> siehe WINGRAF LF 301(verstellt) 5 kN am obersten Knoten

  - ReaktionskrÃ¤fte:
      In Stab 1001+1002 sowie am Stabanfang von 2001 findet man eine Normalkraft von -13.5 kN
      Mit dieser Kraft muss die Presse arbeiten um die Beschleunigung zu erzeugen.

Drehbeschleunigung im verstellten System:
  - In Lastfall 311 wird berechnet, dass eine Verdrehung in Stab 1002 erfolgt und
      das vordere Teilsystem um diese Drehachse beschleunigt wird (rechtsdrehend).
      Da die Drehbeschleunigung 2.5 rad/sec^2 betrÃ¤gt wird die 2.0m von der Drehachse
      entfernte Einzelmasse mit 5.0 m/sec^2 nach rechts beschleunigt und
      erzeugt eine entgegengesetzt gerichtete TrÃ¤gheitskraft von
      F=a*m = 5m/sec^2 * 0.5t = 2.5 kN
      -> siehe WINGRAF LF 311(verstellt) 2.5 kN am obersten Knoten nach links (bezogen auf Stab 1002)

  - Das letzte Bild zeigt NUR die Stablasten:
      Zu Stab 2001 (erster exzentrischer Stab nach der Presse)
      Der Schwerpunkt dieses Stabes liegt 150 mm unter der Drehachse (da exzentrischer Stab)
      also auf der anderen Seite der Drehachse wie die Einzelmasse.
      Seine Masse wird daher nach rechts beschleunigt und erzeugt eine nach links
      gerichtete TrÃ¤gheitskraft
      -> siehe WINGRAF letztes Bild.

  - ReaktionskrÃ¤fte:
      In Stab 1002 findet man ein Torsionsmoment von -6.10 kNm
      Mit diesem Drehmoment muss der Dreh-Antrieb arbeiten um die Dreh-Beschleunigung zu erzeugen.

Man kann also mit WINGRAF-Lasten-Stablasten die StÃ¤be kontrollieren.

!#!Info  Example:       Kinematics Analysis of rotated systems
!#!Info  Keyword:       kinematics, rotation, rigid body rotation
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!Info  Date:          09.06.2010


! Attention: if an element is shortened or lengthened by a kinematic movement,
! it is not allowed to use a beam element !
! -> in this example the element in group 81 must be a truss (or cable)
!    but not a beam, because the element changes its length !
! The elements in GRP 71 only rotates but keeps the length - beam allowed
!
! Also in example bagger/excavator the pneumatic cylinders are truss elements !
!
! Using big rotations in a real geometric nonlinear analsis TH3 (with dynamic or not),
! the total rotation of beams is limited to +-90 degree. But you can bend a
! beam in TH3 up to a rotation of +-90 degree!
! Truss, cable and QUADs can rotate more than 90 degree, because they update the
! local coordinate system with the real 3d nodal coordinates.
!
! In kinematic usage TAKT/LAUN the rotation is unlimited also for beams
! - see example bagger/excavator
!
! SOFILOAD: local element loadings must be defined as
!    SOFILOAD QUAD, BEAM local loadings to act in the rotated element coordinate system!
!    Free loads in SOFILOAD (POIN, LINE, AREA) are processed to nodal forces
!    in SOFILOAD using the origin local coordinate systems only!

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'

PAGE 3 UNII 2           $  input in mm
STEE 1 S 235

SCIT  1 MNO 1 D 80 T 10 $ tube or cable
PROF 2 HEB 160
PROF 3 HEB 120
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD Kinematics Analysis of rotated systems
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 100 GDIR NEGY $ rotation best around z-axis !

NODE NO    X    Y    Z     FIX
     1     0    0    0     PPZM
     2    -0.5  0.5  0
     3    -1    1    0
     4     0    1    0
     5     1.5  0.9  0     PPZM
GRP 71 TITL rotation_part
    BEAM NO    NA    NE    KR   NCS
         1     1     2     POSZ 3
         2     2     3     POSZ 3
         3     2     4     POSZ 2
GRP 81 TITL trus
    TRUS NO    NA    NE    NCS
         4     4     5     1
$ Attention: see comments on top of this file !
END

  LCC 9
END

+prog template urs:4
head
#define sincos
  let#alpha #k*180./3.1416 $ Winkel in Grad
  prt#alpha
  let#sink sin(#alpha)
  let#cosk cos(#alpha)
#enddef

#define crossnorm
  let#c(1)  #a(2)*#b(3)-#a(3)*#b(2)
  let#c(2)  #a(3)*#b(1)-#a(1)*#b(3)
  let#c(3)  #a(1)*#b(2)-#a(2)*#b(1)
     let#xl #c(1)*#c(1)+#c(2)*#c(2)+#c(3)*#c(3)
     let#c(1) #c(1)/#xl ; let#c(2) #c(2)/#xl ; let#c(3) #c(3)/#xl $ normiert
#enddef

#define matmul
$ jetzt tm1=t1*dt Matrixmultiplikation:
  let#tm1(1) #dt1(1)*#t1(1)+#dt1(2)*#t2(1)+#dt1(3)*#t3(1)
  let#tm1(2) #dt1(1)*#t1(2)+#dt1(2)*#t2(2)+#dt1(3)*#t3(2)
  let#tm1(3) #dt1(1)*#t1(3)+#dt1(2)*#t2(3)+#dt1(3)*#t3(3)

  let#tm2(1) #dt2(1)*#t1(1)+#dt2(2)*#t2(1)+#dt2(3)*#t3(1)
  let#tm2(2) #dt2(1)*#t1(2)+#dt2(2)*#t2(2)+#dt2(3)*#t3(2)
  let#tm2(3) #dt2(1)*#t1(3)+#dt2(2)*#t2(3)+#dt2(3)*#t3(3)

  let#tm3(1) #dt3(1)*#t1(1)+#dt3(2)*#t2(1)+#dt3(3)*#t3(1)
  let#tm3(2) #dt3(1)*#t1(2)+#dt3(2)*#t2(2)+#dt3(3)*#t3(2)
  let#tm3(3) #dt3(1)*#t1(3)+#dt3(2)*#t2(3)+#dt3(3)*#t3(3)
#enddef
end

loop#zeile0
  let#pos0 #zeile0*#ndatas; let#kapx #geodata(#pos0+0)
  txe Zeile #zeile0 kapx #kapx
  let#pos1 #pos0+#ndatas  ; let#kapx #geodata(#pos1+0)
endloop #kapx<998

$ prt#geodata
end

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Roller Coaster
UNIT 5 $ Einheiten: Querschnitte in mm, Geometrie+Lasten in m
SYST SPAC GDIR POSZ GDIV 1000

sto#dnr1 10000 $ Rohr 1
sto#dnr2 20000 $ Rohr 2

sto#dnr3 30000 $ Test Koordsystem
sto#dnr4 40000 $ Test Koordsystem
sto#dnr5 50000 $ Test Koordsystem
sto#dnr6 60000 $ Test Koordsystem

sto#dy12 0.500 $ halber Abstand der Rohre
sto#dz12 +1.20 $ z Abstand Achse-Rohre

sto#ds 0.50    $ Abstand der Stationen

sto#x 0 ; sto#y 0 ; sto#z -30 $ aktuelle Position der Achse
sto#t1 0    1 0 0                             $ aktuelle Transformationsmatrix t1(1:3) t1(0) unbenutzt
sto#t2 0    0 1 0                             $ aktuelle Transformationsmatrix
sto#t3 0    0 0 1                             $ aktuelle Transformationsmatrix
sto#tm1 0    0 0 0                             $ Vektor tm1(0:3) anlegen
sto#tm2 0    0 0 0                             $
sto#tm3 0    0 0 0                             $

sto#a 0    0 0 0                             $ Vektor vx(0:3) anlegen
sto#b 0    0 0 0                             $ Vektor vy(0:3) anlegen
sto#c 0    0 0 0                             $ Vektor vz(0:3) anlegen

sto#lastlager -1


sto#knr 1 $ aktuelle Knotennummer
NODE #knr       x #x #y        #z        $ Achsknoten (in BrusthÃ¶he der Passagiere)
NODE #knr+#dnr1 x #x #y+#dy12  #z+#dz12 $ Rohrknoten
NODE #knr+#dnr2 x #x #y-#dy12  #z+#dz12 $ Rohrknoten


loop
  sto#knr0 #knr   $ Knotennummer am Anfang
  sto#knr  #knr+1 $ next Knotennummer
  sto#sA (#knr0-1)*#ds    $ Station am Anfang
  sto#sM #sA+0.5*#ds  $ Station in der Mitte
  sto#sE #sA+#ds      $ Station am Ende
  let#zeile0 div(#sM,1) ; let#pos0 #zeile0*#ndatas ; let#pos1 #pos0+#ndatas ; let#xi #sM-#zeile0

  let#kx 0.01*(#geodata(#pos0+0)+#xi*(#geodata(#pos1+0)-#geodata(#pos0+0))) $ KnÃ¼mmung in der Mitte
  let#ky 0.01*(#geodata(#pos0+1)+#xi*(#geodata(#pos1+1)-#geodata(#pos0+1))) $ KnÃ¼mmung in der Mitte
  let#kz 0.01*(#geodata(#pos0+2)+#xi*(#geodata(#pos1+2)-#geodata(#pos0+2))) $ KnÃ¼mmung in der Mitte

  txe Stab von Knoten #knr0 bis #knr Station #(#sA,6.3) bis #(#sE,6.3) Zeile #zeile0 xi #(#xi,6.3) kapx #(#kx,9.6) kapy #(#ky,9.6) kapz #(#kz,9.6)
  let#k #kx
                 #include sincos
                 let#sx #sink ; let#cx #cosk $ Ãœbertrag der sinus und cosinus aus Block sincos
  let#k #ky
                 #include sincos
                 let#sy #sink ; let#cy #cosk $ Ãœbertrag der sinus und cosinus aus Block sincos
  let#k #kz
                 #include sincos
                 let#sz #sink ; let#cz #cosk $ Ãœbertrag der sinus und cosinus aus Block sincos

  $ neuer Vektor T1-T2: Inkrement von
  sto#dt1 0    1*#cy*#cz     0+#sz*#cy  0-#sy*#cz  $ T2 - LÃ¤nge etwas kÃ¼rzer wegen cosinus
  sto#dt2 0    0-#sz*#cx     1*#cx*#cz  0+#sx*#cy  $  Richtung der 2. Achse von T2
  sto#dt3 0    0 0 0                               $ erst mal Feld nur angelegt dt3(0:3)

     let#xl #dt1(1)*#dt1(1)+#dt1(2)*#dt1(2)+#dt1(3)*#dt1(3)
     let#dt1(1) #dt1(1)/#xl ; let#dt1(2) #dt1(2)/#xl ; let#dt1(3) #dt1(3)/#xl $ dt1 normiert
     let#xl #dt2(1)*#dt2(1)+#dt2(2)*#dt2(2)+#dt2(3)*#dt2(3)
     let#dt2(1) #dt2(1)/#xl ; let#dt2(2) #dt2(2)/#xl ; let#dt2(3) #dt2(3)/#xl $ dt2 normiert

  let#a(1) #dt1(1) ; let#a(2) #dt1(2) ; let#a(3) #dt1(3)
  let#b(1) #dt2(1) ; let#b(2) #dt2(2) ; let#b(3) #dt2(3)
                 #include crossnorm  $ cross 1*2 -> 3
  let#dt3(1) #c(1) ; let#dt3(2) #c(2) ; let#dt3(3) #c(3)

  let#a(1) #dt3(1) ; let#a(2) #dt3(2) ; let#a(3) #dt3(3)
  let#b(1) #dt1(1) ; let#b(2) #dt1(2) ; let#b(3) #dt1(3)
                 #include crossnorm  $ cross 3*1 -> 2
  let#dt2(1) #c(1) ; let#dt2(2) #c(2) ; let#dt2(3) #c(3)

  $ tm1=t1*dt Matrixmultiplikation:
  #include matmul

  sto#x #x+#ds*#tm1(1) ; sto#y #y+#ds*#tm1(2) ; sto#z #z+#ds*#tm1(3)

  sto#t1(1) #tm1(1) ; sto#t1(2) #tm1(2) ; sto#t1(3) #tm1(3)  $ t1 ist jetzt erst die Transformation bei ds/2 !!
  sto#t2(1) #tm2(1) ; sto#t2(2) #tm2(2) ; sto#t2(3) #tm2(3)
  sto#t3(1) #tm3(1) ; sto#t3(2) #tm3(2) ; sto#t3(3) #tm3(3)

  $ jetzt t nochmal mit dt Matrixmultiplikation bearbeiten, dann hat man die t am Ende des Abschnittes (bisher bei ds/2)
  $ tm1=t1*dt Matrixmultiplikation:
    #include matmul
  sto#t1(1) #tm1(1) ; sto#t1(2) #tm1(2) ; sto#t1(3) #tm1(3)  $ t1 ist jetzt die Transformation bei ds !!
  sto#t2(1) #tm2(1) ; sto#t2(2) #tm2(2) ; sto#t2(3) #tm2(3)
  sto#t3(1) #tm3(1) ; sto#t3(2) #tm3(2) ; sto#t3(3) #tm3(3)

  NODE #knr       x #x                             y #y                             z #z $ Achsknoten (in BrusthÃ¶he der Passagiere)
  NODE #knr+#dnr1 x #x+#dy12*#t2(1)+#dz12*#t3(1) y #y+#dy12*#t2(2)+#dz12*#t3(2) z #z+#dy12*#t2(3)+#dz12*#t3(3) $ Rohrknoten
  NODE #knr+#dnr2 x #x-#dy12*#t2(1)+#dz12*#t3(1) y #y-#dy12*#t2(2)+#dz12*#t3(2) z #z-#dy12*#t2(3)+#dz12*#t3(3) $ Rohrknoten
  grp 1 titl 'rohr1'
    beam na  #knr+#dnr1-1 ne #knr+#dnr1 drx #tm2(1) #tm2(2) #tm2(3) ncs 1
  grp 2 titl 'rohr2'
    beam na  #knr+#dnr2-1 ne #knr+#dnr2 drx #tm2(1) #tm2(2) #tm2(3) ncs 1
  if 0.02+mod(#sA,2.00)<0.04
    grp 7 titl 'querrohr'
      beam na  #knr+#dnr1-1 ne #knr+#dnr2-1 ncs 7
        $ grup 8 bez 'Test Koordsysteme'
        $   knot #knr+#dnr3 x #x+#t1(1) #y+#t1(2) #z+#t1(3)
        $   knot #knr+#dnr4 x #x+#t2(1) #y+#t2(2) #z+#t2(3)
        $   knot #knr+#dnr5 x #x+#t3(1) #y+#t3(2) #z+#t3(3)
        $   stab ka  #knr ke #knr+#dnr3 qnr 7
        $   stab ka  #knr ke #knr+#dnr4 qnr 7
        $   stab ka  #knr ke #knr+#dnr5 qnr 7
  endif
  let#lagertyp #geodata(#pos0+4)
  if #lagertyp>0
    if #zeile0>#lastlager
      let#supp #geodata(#pos0+3) ; if #supp<1 ; let#supp 2.0 ; endif $ Lagerspreizung
      grp 7 titl 'Stuetze'
      let#a(1) #t1(1) ; let#a(2) #t1(2) ; let#a(3) #t1(3)
      let#b(1)    0.0 ; let#b(2)    0.0 ; let#b(3)    1.0 $ global Z
                     #include crossnorm  $ cross 1*2 -> lokal Y im Grundriss
      let#a(1)   #c(1) ; let#a(2)   #c(2) ; let#a(3)   #c(3)
                     #include crossnorm  $ cross 3*1 -> lokal X im Grundriss
      let#tt1(1)  #c(1) ; let#tt1(2)  #c(2)  $ lokal X im Grundriss
      let#tt2(1) -#a(1) ; let#tt2(2) -#a(2)  $ lokal Y im Grundriss
      if #lagertyp==1
        node #knr+#dnr3 x #x+#tt2(1)*#supp #y+#tt2(2)*#supp z 0 fix pp $ F wenn es zu stark wackelt
        node #knr+#dnr4 x #x-#tt2(1)*#supp #y-#tt2(2)*#supp z 0 fix pp
          beam na #knr+#dnr1-1 ne #knr+#dnr3 ncs 5
          beam na #knr+#dnr2-1 ne #knr+#dnr4 ncs 5
      else
        node #knr+#dnr3 x #x+#tt2(1)*#supp+#tt1(1)*#supp #y+#tt2(2)*#supp+#tt1(2)*#supp z 0 fix pp
        node #knr+#dnr4 x #x-#tt2(1)*#supp+#tt1(1)*#supp #y-#tt2(2)*#supp+#tt1(2)*#supp z 0 fix pp
        node #knr+#dnr5 x #x+#tt2(1)*#supp-#tt1(1)*#supp #y+#tt2(2)*#supp-#tt1(2)*#supp z 0 fix pp
        node #knr+#dnr6 x #x-#tt2(1)*#supp-#tt1(1)*#supp #y-#tt2(2)*#supp-#tt1(2)*#supp z 0 fix pp
          beam na #knr+#dnr1-1 ne #knr+#dnr3 ncs 5
          beam na #knr+#dnr1-1 ne #knr+#dnr5 ncs 5
          beam na #knr+#dnr2-1 ne #knr+#dnr4 ncs 5
          beam na #knr+#dnr2-1 ne #knr+#dnr6 ncs 5
      endif
      sto#lastlager #zeile0 $ damit wegen einer Zeile nur ein Lager entsteht, auch wenn Schrittweite ds<1m
    endif
  endif


  let#kapx #geodata(#pos1+#ndatas) $ next kapx
endloop #kapx<998


node 90001 x -30 -30 0
node 90002 x -30  30 0
node 90003 x  30 -30 0
node 90004 x  30  30 0
grp 99 titl 'Theresienwiese'
  quad - 90001 90002 90004 90003 mno 99 m 10 n 10 t 200[mm]
END

tran node     1       dz -0.05+0.08           dno 8000 $ Kopf                       8001

tran node 8001,18001,28001 dx 3.60 dno 3     dz 0.30

  $ jetzt rechts siehe Knotenplot 10 Zeile  weiter oben :

  beam no 600+#k na 29100+#k 29200+#k ncs 8  $ = Richtung Hauptfeder rechts alt
  beam no 700+#k na 29100+#k 29200+#k ncs 8  $ = Richtung Hauptfeder rechts alt

  beam no 800+#k na 19000+#k  9000+#k ncs 12 ahin mymz ehin mymz  $ = Richtung Querfeder  links  neu alt 200
  beam no 900+#k na 29000+#k  9000+#k ncs 12 ahin mymz ehin mymz  $ = Richtung Querfeder  rechts neu alt 500
  $ achterbahn15 hat gezeigt, dass :
  $ die StÃ¤be 301,601 stellen sich etwas schief und bremsen dadurch den ganzen Zug ab
  $ Oder in achterbahn14quadvoll beschleunigt der Zug im Korkenzieher vermutlich,
  $ weil sich einige StÃ¤be schiefstellen. Quads bleiben aber eher unschief

  grp 8 titl 'Wagen sonstige StÃ¤be'
  if #i0>0
    if mod(#i0,2)>0
      quad n1  18000+#k-1 19000+#k-1  19000+#k   18000+#k   mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Wagen aussen

      quad n1  19000+#k-1  9000+#k-1   9000+#k   19000+#k   mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Bodenplatte
      quad n1   9000+#k-1 29000+#k-1  29000+#k    9000+#k   mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Bodenplatte
      quad n1  19000+#k-1  9000+#k-1   8000+#k-1 18000+#k-1 mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Platte hinten
      quad n1   9000+#k-1 29000+#k-1  28000+#k-1  8000+#k-1 mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Platte hinten
      quad n1  19000+#k    9000+#k     8000+#k   18000+#k   mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Platte vorne
      quad n1   9000+#k   29000+#k    28000+#k    8000+#k   mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Platte vorne

      quad n1  19100+#k-1 19000+#k-1  19000+#k 19100+#k mno 6 t 50[mm]  $ Schienenkontakt
      quad n1  19200+#k-1 19100+#k-1  19100+#k 19200+#k mno 6 t 50[mm]  $
      quad n1  29100+#k-1 29000+#k-1  29000+#k 29100+#k mno 6 t 50[mm]  $
      quad n1  29200+#k-1 29100+#k-1  29100+#k 29200+#k mno 6 t 50[mm]  $
    else
      trus na  9000+#k-1  9000+#k ncs 10 $ Fach Verbinder zweier Wagen
    endif
  endif
  mass 18000+#k 0.05 $ oben
  mass 28000+#k 0.05 $ oben
  grp 11 titl 'Kontaktfeder V Schiene 1'

   $  FEDE  CP 1000 CQ 10 RISS 0 MUE 0.0100000 DP 60   movs_train_interaction

  grp 22 titl 'Kontaktfeder H Schiene 2'
    spri 500+#k na 29200+#k cp 500 DP 0 dy  1 $ horizontal

+PROG ASE URS:3
Head MOVS
$
$ Es zeigte sich:
$ Wenn man die Federn immer senkrecht auf die Schiene ausrichtet kommt der Zug
$ oft zum Stillstand, da z.B. eine Feder etwas nach vorne zeigt und eine etwas nach hinten.
$ Daher hier:
$ Die Federn haben immer eine feste Richtung und zwar die Richtung eines Stabelementes,
$ z.B. Feder 11301 hat als Richtung die Richtung des Stabes 9301
$
CTRL WARN 945 $  Search direction
let#i 1
MOVS 11300+#i type BGRP 1 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9400+#i $ vertikal links
MOVS 12200+#i type BGRP 1 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9800+#i $ H        links
MOVS 21600+#i type BGRP 2 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9400+#i $ vertikal rechts
MOVS 22500+#i type BGRP 2 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9900+#i $ H        rechts

MOVS 11300+#i type BGRP 1 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9400+#i
MOVS 12200+#i type BGRP 1 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9800+#i
MOVS 21600+#i type BGRP 2 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9400+#i
MOVS 22500+#i type BGRP 2 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9900+#i

MOVS 12200+#i type BGRP 1 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9800+#i
MOVS 21600+#i type BGRP 2 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9400+#i
MOVS 22500+#i type BGRP 2 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9900+#i
let#i 4

MOVS 12200+#i type BGRP 1 L0 #L0 tolt 0.60 dire 9800+#i

+PROG ASE URS:7
Head Start
sto#iter 60 ; sto#rada 0 ; sto#radb 0
sto#plf   1 ; sto#dt 0.10
#define 10steps
ctrl solv 4
step 10 dt #dt DIV 0   the 0.7   $
SYST prob TH3 iter #iter tol -4 tol4 -10 tol8 -30 plc #plf ; ctrl warn 2581 $ wenig Iterationen = schneller
grp - rada #rada radb #radb ; grp 49 off ; grp 11,12,21,22 rada 0 radb 0 ; CTRL  WARN 183 $ falls Zwischenschritt divergent
grp 9 off $ ohne StÃ¤be : StÃ¤be dienen aber trotzdem als Richtungszeiger fÃ¼r die MOVS (Knoten KA-KE)
LC #plf+1 DLZ 1
  if #plf==1
    v0 grp 8,9 vx 3.0 $ Anfangsgeschwindigkeit
  endif
#enddef
#include 10steps
END

!#!Info  Example:       Slip-Cable  block and tackle system
!#!Info  Keyword:       slip-Cable; block and tackle system; cable
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ english file name: slip_cable.dat     JB 17.10.2005
$
$ Slip-Cable. Die zu einem Gesamt-SLIP-Seil zusammengesetzten Einzelseile
$ werden in ASE in einer Substructure-Ã¤hnlichen Gesamtsteifigkeit verarbeitet.
$ Dadurch kann bereits in einem linearen Lauf der Effekt komplexer SLIP cable
$ Strukturen z.B. Ã¼ber Umlenkrollen berechnet werden und nichtlineare Berechnungen
$ konvergieren deutlich schneller.
$ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ Slip cables: Global SLIP cable elements (built of single cables connected with
$ block and tackles) are analyzed with an overall combined stiffness like a substructure
$ stiffness in ASE. This produces correct results of slip cable structures
$ also in one linear run. Nonlinear iterations now have a much better convergence.
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:4
HEAD

STEE 3 ST 52
STEE 9 PST 1570 ES 160000
PROF 1 hea 500
PROF 2 hea 200
SECT 3 ; PROF 3 hea 140 ; SV IT -5 $ otherwise the torsion weak beam drills in TH3
CABL 9 D 10 MNO 9
END

                  $ erhalten die gleiche Kraft trotz unterschiedlicher
                  $ Knotenverschiebungen (kokale Verschiebungen)
                  $ --------------------------------------------------------
                  $ all cables of group 9 will get the same force
                  $ although they have different local elongations

  LCC 910

-PROG WING URS:6
HEAD
SIZE -urs SPLI '4X1'
LC NO 1; DEFO TYPE YES FAC 5 LC CURR ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; LOAD
LC NO 2; DEFO TYPE YES FAC 5 LC CURR ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; LOAD
LC NO 3; DEFO TYPE YES FAC 5 LC CURR ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; LOAD
LC NO 4; DEFO TYPE YES FAC 5 LC CURR ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; LOAD
LC NO 1; BEAM TYPE N UNIT 2 SCHH YES STYP CABL FILL NO REPR DLIN
LC NO 2; BEAM TYPE N UNIT 2 SCHH YES STYP CABL FILL NO REPR DLIN
LC NO 3; BEAM TYPE N UNIT 2 SCHH YES STYP CABL FILL NO REPR DLIN
LC NO 4; BEAM TYPE N UNIT 2 SCHH YES STYP CABL FILL NO REPR DLIN
END
END
Effect: in loadcase 1 the cable cannot slip and only the two inner cables
        have a high stress.

        in loadcase 3 all loads have a constant stress =
        cable slipped over the block and tackle   rolls.

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation

  LCC 901,902
END

slip 2 nog 2

  LCC 901,902
END

  LCC 901,902
END

syst prob TH3
slip 2 nog 2 mue 0.20
LC 4 FACD 1 titl 'SLIP mue TH3 +inner cable sagging'
  LCC 901,902
END

+PROG WING urs:7
HEAD
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0 Y 1 Z 0 AXIS NEGZ ROTA 0
loop#i0 4
  let#i1 #i0+1
  LC NO #i1 ; BEAM TYPE  N UNIT DEFA SCHH 0.50 STYP CABL FILL NO REPR DLIN
    AND ; NODE TYPE UX UNIT DEFA SCHH 0.50 FILL NO REPR DVEC
    AND ; NODE TYPE SX UNIT DEFA SCHH 0.50 FILL NO REPR DVEC
endloop
BEAM TYPE UZ UNIT DEFA SCHH 0.50 STYP CABL FILL NO REPR DLIN

END

$
MATE 1 E  400/0.8 E90  300/0.8 G   5/0.8 MUE 0.2 GAM 12/0.8  TITL 'Membran  PVC 0.8 mm' $ Max-Plank
NMAT 1 MEMB $ definiert das Material als Membran
END

$ ErlÃ¤uterungen Membranberechnungen siehe innenhof.dat

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:1
HEAD Tennis court
$
$ In this file we input the curved geometry in SOFIMSHA to get a good height a curvature in the corner.
$ This shape can only be achieved with a stress that is almost zero in the corner !
$
$ An isotropic perstress would lead to a double curvature and no height in the corner,
$ see file tennis_isotropic_prestress.dat
$
$ Juergen Bellmann, SOFiSTiK, 23.11.2022
$
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 NEGZ

STO#width   22.0 $ [m] dome width
STO#length  58.0 $ [m] dome length
STO#nlength 10.0 $ [m] number of elements length
STO#exponent 4
STO#expot 1.0/#exponent
STO#w05 0.5*#width
STO#l05rest 0.5*(#length)-#w05 $ from corner-part to midspan of length
prt#l05rest
$
$
$        xi=0                        xi=1
$           |---------> xi (01)         |
$
$                                       *
$                              *        |
$                         *             |
$                     *                 |
$                  *                    |
$                * |  *                 |
$              *   |     * r=1          |
$             *    |        *           |
$            *     |h1         *        |
$            *     |              *     |
$           *      |                 *  |
$           *---------------------------|--------------------------*
$                          eta <--------|
$       eta=1                           0
$
$       Pytagoras: h1^2 + eta^2 = 1.0  -> h1=SQR(1.0-eta^2)

$ STO#xi  0.00   0.01   0.02   0.04   0.08   0.15   0.30   0.55   1.00  $ 9 elements, creates #xi(0) ... #xl(8)
$ STO#xi  0.00   0.02   0.04   0.07   0.12   0.20   0.40   0.70   1.00  $ 9 elements, creates #xi(0) ... #xl(8)
STO#xi  0.00   0.005  0.02   0.04   0.07   0.11   0.18   0.26  0.36   0.49    0.62   0.80   1.00  $ 9 elements, creates #xi(0) ... #xl(8)
  $    #xi(0) #xi(1) #xi(2) #xi(3) #xi(4) #xi(5)
prt#xi


$ ========================== corner area ==================================
GRP 11
loop#i0       xi  $ loop runs for all elements of array xx   #i0 has values 0-1-2-3-4-5
  let#i1 #i0+1    $ variable #i1 starts at 1 and has values 1-2-3-4-5-6
  loop#j0       xi
    let#j1 #j0+1
    let#no 100*#i1+#j1 $ 100-steps in x, 1-step in y
    let#xix #xi(#i0)    ; let#xiy #xi(#j0)
    let#etax 1-#xix     ; let#etay 1-#xiy
    let#h1x SQR(1.0-#etax^2)
    let#h1y SQR(1.0-#etay^2)
    let#h1 min(#h1x,#h1y)
    let#dij abs(#i1-#j1)
    if #dij==0 ; let#h1 #h1-#etax*0.20*#h1 ; endif
    if #dij==1 ; let#h1 #h1-#etax*0.10*#h1 ; endif
    if #dij==2 ; let#h1 #h1-#etax*0.05*#h1 ; endif
    if #dij==3 ; let#h1 #h1-#etax*0.02*#h1 ; endif
    let#h1a #h1 $ Variante a

    let#xixy #xix*#xiy
    let#eta 1.0-#xixy
    let#h1b SQR(1.0-#eta^2) $ Variante b

    let#etamin min(#etax,#etay)
    let#f #etamin^0.3
    let#f 0.6*#f
    let#h1 #f*#h1a+(1-#f)*#h1b $ mix of Variante a+b

    let#z  #h1*#w05
    let#x   #xix*#w05   ; let#y   #xiy*#w05
    NODE #no X #x #y #z
    TXB Node #(#no,5.0) etax= #(#etax,6.3) etay= #(#etay,6.3) etamin= #(#etamin,6.3)  f= #(#f,6.4) h1 #(#h1,6.4) x= #(#x,6.3) y= #(#y,6.3) z= #(#z,6.3)
                            $ print with format 6 characters and 3 digits
    if (#i1>1)&(#j1>1)
      QUAD - #no #no-100 #no-101 #no-1 T 0.8[mm] MNO 1
    endif
  endloop
endloop
sto#nxbase 100*#i1 $ last 100-node base number

$ ========================== mid area - constant curvature ==================================
GRP 12
loop#i0 #nlength/2
  let#i1 #i0+1
  loop#j0       xi  $ loop runs for all elements of array xx   #i0 has values 0-1-2-3-4-5
    let#j1 #j0+1
    let#no #nxbase+100*#i1+#j1 $ 100-steps in x, 1-step in y
    let#xix 1.000000    ; let#xiy #xi(#j0)      $ xix=1.000 !!!!!!!!!!!
    let#eta 1.0-#xiy
    let#h1 SQR(1.0-#eta^2) ; let#z #h1*#w05
    let#x  #w05+(#l05rest*#i1)/(#nlength/2)
    let#y  #xi(#j0)*#w05
    NODE #no X #x #y #z
    TXB N222 #(#no,5.0) xiy= #(#xiy,5.3) eta= #(#eta,5.3) h1 #(#h1,5.3) x= #(#x,6.3) y= #(#y,6.3) z= #(#z,6.3)
    if (#j1>1)
      QUAD - #no #no-100 #no-101 #no-1 T 0.8[mm] MNO 1
    endif
  endloop
endloop

$ END $ please first activate this 2*END to see what happens
$ END $ please first activate this 2*END to see what happens

GRP 21 ; MIRR QUAD GRP 11   A 1 DIST 0.5*#length
GRP 22 ; MIRR QUAD GRP 12   A 1 DIST 0.5*#length

GRP 31 ; MIRR QUAD GRP 11   B 1 DIST #w05
GRP 32 ; MIRR QUAD GRP 12   B 1 DIST #w05

GRP 41 ; MIRR QUAD GRP 21   B 1 DIST #w05
GRP 42 ; MIRR QUAD GRP 22   B 1 DIST #w05

$ now all bottom nodes with z=0
SBOX A1X -100 0 0  100 0 0  A2X 0 -100 0   0 100 0 A3X 0 0 -0.01  0 0 +0.01 OPT AND
NODE SBOX FIX PP
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:4
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ LC 901 TYPE NONE TITL 'airpressure'
$   QUAD GRP 11,12,21,22,31,32,41,42 TYPE PZ P -0.20  better take VOLU
LC 902 TYPE NONE TITL 'wind in global y'
  AREA PROJ ZZ WIDE 99 TYPE PZ P1 +0.15 X1  0    0 0 X2 DXY #length #w05
  AREA PROJ ZZ WIDE 99 TYPE PZ P1 -0.15 X1  0 #w05 0 X2 DXY #length #w05
END

!+!KAPITEL Formfinding
+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES
VOLU 1 GRP 11,12,21,22,31,32,41,42 V0 #length*0.5*#w05*#w05*3.14 P0 0.20
GRP - ; GRP 11,12,21,22,31,32,41,42 PREX 1.0 1.0 $ sligth prestress to avoid vertical elements
LC 1 FACD 1 TITL 'g_1 and air pressure'
END

+PROG ASE urs:7
HEAD Koordinaten-Update
$ Main reason: only then you will see wind deformations in the Animator
$ swinging around the formfinding system!
SYST PLC 1 STOR YES
END

!+!KAPITEL Wind
+PROG ASE urs:2
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES iter 200 PLC 1 tol -0.20 tol8 -3.0
VOLU 1 P0 0.20 $ constant inner air pressure (take other data from already defined volume number)
$ alternatively to VOLU 1 P0 0.20 :
$ VOLU 1 $ without GRP,POSI,MNO,V0 input:
$        $ air volume would be constant and air pressure would change !!
LC 11 FACD 1 TITL 'Wind, inner air pressure constant'
  LCC 902 $ Wind
END

+PROG ASE urs:3
HEAD
CTRL SOLV 4
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES iter 200 PLC 1 tol -0.20 tol8 -2.0
$ alternatively to VOLU 1 P0 0.20 :
VOLU 1 $ without GRP,POSI,MNO,V0 input:
$        $ air volume would be constant and air pressure would change !!
LC 12 FACD 1 TITL 'Wind, inner air volume constant'
  LCC 902 $ Wind
END

!#!KAPITEL Cutting analysis
+PROG TEXTILE URS:11
HEAD Definition of cutting pattern lines
$ Geodetical lines can be defined in 3 different ways - see manual
$
$ The cutting pattern lines according to standard are defined in plan:
$ Here lines  respectively to y=0 till y=50 m at x=:
let#x 0.4*#w05 ; let#xi #x-2.00 ; LINE XA #x  -1.0        XE #xi 2.50
                                  LINE XA #xi  2.50       XE #xi #width-2.50
                                  LINE XA #xi #width-2.50 XE #x  #width+1.0
let#x 0.6*#w05 ; let#xi #x-1.40 ; LINE XA #x  -1.0        XE #xi 2.50
                                  LINE XA #xi  2.50       XE #xi #width-2.50
                                  LINE XA #xi #width-2.50 XE #x  #width+1.0
let#x 0.8*#w05 ; let#xi #x-1.10 ; LINE XA #x  -1.0        XE #xi 2.50
                                  LINE XA #xi  2.50       XE #xi #width-2.50
                                  LINE XA #xi #width-2.50 XE #x  #width+1.0
let#x     #w05              ; LINE XA #x -1.0    XE #x #width+1.0 type fix
let#x     #w05+0.4*#l05rest ; LINE XA #x -1.0    XE #x #width+1.0 type fix
let#x     #w05+0.8*#l05rest ; LINE XA #x -1.0    XE #x #width+1.0 type fix
let#x     #w05+1.2*#l05rest ; LINE XA #x -1.0    XE #x #width+1.0 type fix
let#x     #w05+1.6*#l05rest ; LINE XA #x -1.0    XE #x #width+1.0 type fix
let#x     #w05+2.0*#l05rest ; LINE XA #x -1.0    XE #x #width+1.0 type fix

let#x #length-0.8*#w05 ; let#xi #x+1.10 ; LINE XA #x  -1.0        XE #xi 2.50
                                          LINE XA #xi  2.50       XE #xi #width-2.50
                                          LINE XA #xi #width-2.50 XE #x  #width+1.0
let#x #length-0.6*#w05 ; let#xi #x+1.40 ; LINE XA #x  -1.0        XE #xi 2.50
                                          LINE XA #xi  2.50       XE #xi #width-2.50
                                          LINE XA #xi #width-2.50 XE #x  #width+1.0
let#x #length-0.4*#w05 ; let#xi #x+1.00 ; LINE XA #x  -1.0        XE #xi 2.50
                                          LINE XA #xi  2.50       XE #xi #width-2.50
                                          LINE XA #xi #width-2.50 XE #x  #width+1.0


$ Attention: If you change something here you must close interactive WINGRAF without saving
$            or best delete the .gra file because otherwise WINGRAF uses older cutting lines !!
END

+PROG TEXTILE urs:12
HEAD Prepare cutting Lines for next WING
PREP    $ necessary if you export the cutting lines from AUTOCAD/SOFIPLUS !
END

+prog  WING URS:14
HEAD Analysis of geodetical lines and the 3D-cutting pattern surfaces
SIZE lp SC 0
VIEW STAN 0 0 -1 POSY $ (for prjects of cutting pattern lines)
$ BOX  XMIN -0.854357 YMIN -2.794463 ZMIN -0.0001104 XMAX 59.35840 YMAX 11.24391 ZMAX 11.02979 TYPE BWIN OPER AND BGRP 0
LC   1 ; DEFO YES 1
MOVE IMPO DTYP CUT   $ read cutting lines from .cdb lesen + remember corresponding loadcase
$ Cutting pattern surfaces analysis: CUTP
CUTP LC 1 GRP no
VIEW TYPE  STAN 5 -7 +4 AXIS  NEGZ
STRU NUME CUT NUMN QUAD $ FILL YES
END

+PROG TEXTILE URS:18
HEAD Cutting - development of surface + compensation without decompensation
CUTT expo 1.70 EDGE 0.30  SEAM 0.10 BOUN 0.20  $ Cutting analysis with cutting area definition of WINGRAF
$    effect of EDGE 0.30 see example textile7_edge.dat
                                                $ Explosion factor can also be applied additionally in WINGRAF
$ Realistic compensation added to elastic material strain in percent:
COMP DE1 -  1.50 $ Percent additional strain in warp direction
COMP DE2 -  1.50 $ Percent additional strain in fill direction
END

$ Attention : in case error due to wrong elements occur:
$ I added a GRP ... PREX - sligth prestress to avoid vertical elements !


!#!KAPITEL Representation
+prog  WING URS:19
HEAD Representation of geodetic lines
SIZE lp SC 0
VIEW TYPE  STAN 5 -7 +4 AXIS  NEGZ
$ Representation of cutting pattern surfaces:
STRU NUME CUT NUMN QUAD FILL YES
$ 3D-representation of geodetical lines:
STRU 0 0
END

+prog  WING URS:9
HEAD Representation of cutted tracks
HEAD Dashed A=strained surface, filled eA= relaxed surface
SIZE lp SC 0
VIEW TYPE  STAN 0 0 -1 AXIS  NEGY
$
COLO C27 -7017 -7017
COL2 C5 -2071 C25 -3017 -3017
$ 2S-cutting pattern surface (A= Surface, eA= relaxed surface):
SELE NUMB 0
STRU NUME CP2C FILL AREA REPR DTXT UNIT DEFA SCHH 0                  $ with filled surface
MOVE X DEL DTYP TEXT; MOVE X 1 26 UNIT PR SCHH .6 C 1001
STRU NUME CP2C FILL NO REPR DTXT UNIT DEFA SCHH 0.33 $ Struktur
STRU NUME CP2S FILL NO REPR DTXT UNIT DEFA SCHH 0.33 $ mit Elementlinien
STRU NUME CP2W FILL NO REPR DTXT UNIT DEFA SCHH 0.33 $ mit Kettrichtung
END

+PROG ASE URS:10
HEAD Export cutting areas and 3D_geodetic lines (seam lines) to autocad.dxf:
SYST PLC 1 STOR CUTT $ or ACAD for total FE-mesh
$    With this ASE command the following .dxf files are created:
$   -   $(name)_cutting_areas_mm.dxf         (and as _m.dxf in [m])
$   -   $(name)_3D_geodetic_lines_mm.dxf
$   Then best move the file $(name)_cutting_areas_mm.dxf from the explorer into the Autocad Window

$   With SYST STOR ACAD also a .dxf file of the complete 3D mesh lines can be created,
$   e.g. also with columns and walls.
END

!#!Info  Example:       Air cushion
!#!Info  Keyword:       geometric nonlinear; membrane; formfindung; air_cushion; VOLU
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!Info  Date:          09.04.2011

$ materials and info see atrium.dat

$ Application see also air_cushion.dat, air_volume_tennis.dat und air_volume_sphere.dat
$
$ Please also ask for the corresponding SOFiSTiK paper contributed to the CIMNE Membranes 2011 conference.

#define laenge=8.00  $ m
#define breite=4.00  $ m
#define abstand=0.01 $ m
#define druck=0.20   $ kn/m2
#define vorsp=0.60   $ kn/m

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+prog aqua urs:1
HEAD Air cushion with VOLU air volume technique
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
MATE 1 E 650 E90 - MUE 0.45  G -  GAM 10          TITL Membran $ isotrop !
NMAT 1 MEMB $ defines material as membrane

$ MATE in N/mm2, MAT in kN/m2 :
$ MAT  2 E 0.0006 MUE 0.499999 G 0.0002 K 100 GAM 0.0129 ALFA 1/293/3 TITL AIR $ air for bric elements
  $
  $ usage     also see   file  ..\membranes\air_volume_tennis.dat    and ..\bric\air.dat
  $ ALFA 1/293/3 : bei 293 Grad soll Volumenverdoppelung auftreten,
  $ auf das Volumen bezogener Temp.Ausdehnungskoeffizient daher 1/293
  $ da bei MAT aber die Ausdehnung in einer x-Richtung einzugeben -> 1/293/3 (drei Raumrichtungen)
END

+prog sofimsha urs:2
HEAD Air cushion with VOLU air volume technique
CTRL KNOT 10000
UNIT 0 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000
NODE NO    X       Y          Z
      1    0       0
     21  $(laenge) 0
    101    0       $(breite)
    121  $(laenge) $(breite)
   9001   -1       0     -1
   9002   -1       0     +1
TRAN NODE FROM 1 999 1 DNO 2000 DZ $(abstand)[m]
    $ node 1 - 999 : top       GRP 1  Quads with z going down
    $ node >  2000 : bottom    GRP 2  Quads with z going up

GRP 1 ; QUAD -    1  101  121   21 T 0.2[mm] M 10 N 20
GRP 2 ; QUAD - 2001 2021 2121 2101 T 0.2[mm] M 20 N 10

NODE FIT    1   21 FIX pp
NODE FIT   21  121 FIX pp
NODE FIT  121  101 FIX pp
NODE FIT  101    1 FIX pp

NODE FIT 2001 2021 FIX pp
NODE FIT 2021 2121 FIX pp
NODE FIT 2121 2101 FIX pp
NODE FIT 2101 2001 FIX pp
END

!+!KAPITEL Formfinding
+prog ase urs:3
HEAD
$ CTRL SOLV 4 $ Please activate if ISOL licence available (parallel computing)
$ Parallel OPEN-MP element analysis best with CTRL SOLV 4
$ see also CTRL CORE : limit number of processors
$   (or set this in SSD/TEDDY-SOFISTIK-globale_options-sofistik.def- parameter SOF_NUM_THREADS )
CTRL WARN 10208 $ uninteresting warning
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES $ $ NMAT YES not really necessary for FACS 1e-10
GRP      - $ switches on all groups initially
GRP 1,2 FACS 1E-10   PREX $(vorsp) PREY $(vorsp) $ Membran
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1,2 V0 $(laenge)*$(breite)*$(abstand) P0 $(druck)
LC 1 FACD 1 TITL 'Formfindung'
END
$      QUAD VOLUME RESULTS (VOLU)
$      Loadcase    1   Formfindung
$         NO       V0    V-now       P0    P-now   area-0 area-now
$                [m3]     [m3]  [kN/m2]  [kN/m2]     [m2]     [m2]
$          1    0.320   21.389     0.00     0.20   64.000   67.581
$          P: positive values = pressure

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD Coordinates-update
$ Main reason: only then you will see wind deformations in the Animator
$ swinging around the formfinding system!
SYST PLC 1 STOR YES
END

+prog sofiload urs:6
head
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
lc 901 type none
  area ref qgrp 1 proj zz wide 99 type pz P1 0.80 X1 1.00 1.00 Z1 -1.0 X2 DXY 2.00 2.00
END

+prog ase urs:5
HEAD
$ CTRL SOLV 4 $ Please activate if ISOL licence available (parallel computing)
VOLU NO 1 OPT 'full'
CTRL WARN 10208 $ uninteresting warning
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES PLC 1 ITER 200 TOL -0.001 TOL8 -0.01 ! VOLU needs more iterations and good accuracy
LC 11 FACD 1 TITL 'Wind gust on upper folio' $ 'Windboe auf obere Folie'
  LCC 901
END
END

+prog ase urs:8
HEAD
$ CTRL SOLV 4 $ Please activate if ISOL licence available (parallel computing)
VOLU NO 1 OPT 'iter'
CTRL WARN 10208 $ uninteresting warning
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES PLC 1 ITER 200 TOL -0.001 TOL8 -0.01 ! VOLU needs more iterations and good accuracy
LC 12 FACD 1 TITL 'Compare with VOLU OPT iter'
  LCC 901
END
END
$      QUAD volume results (VOLU)
$      Loadcase     12   Compare with VOLU NONL Y
$         NO       V0    V-PLC    V-now    P-PLC  P-start    P-now area-PLC area-now
$                [m3]     [m3]     [m3]  [kN/m2]  [kN/m2]  [kN/m2]     [m2]     [m2]
$          1    0.320   21.474   21.412     0.20     0.20     0.49   67.616   67.938
$          P: positive values = pressure
$          P-start = P-PLC + k*DP/V-PLF + k*DT*alphaT   with k=compression modulus

-PROG WING urs:7
HEAD
SCHH H6 -0.3
LC 11
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0 Y 0 Z 1 AXIS POSY ROTA 0
BOX  XMIN -0.162339 YMIN 2.535919 ZMIN -5 XMAX 8.280136 YMAX 1.899181 ZMAX 5 TYPE BWIN OPER AND BGRP 0
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0 Y -1 Z 0 AXIS POSZ ROTA 0
NODE TYPE UV UNIT DEFA SCHH NO FILL NO REPR DVEC
and
LC 901
and ; LOAD TYPE ALL UNIT DEFA SCHH YES SING VECT FILL NO REPR DREP ETYP ALL GTYP ELEM

END

$ Only the upper folio is loaded, the air pressure inside arises
$ and the unloaded bottom folie also gets deformation and stress increase!
$

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?



!#!Info  Example:       Air cushion with plasticity formfinding
!#!Info  Keyword:       geometric nonlinear; membrane; formfindung; air_cushion; VOLU
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!Info  Date:          09.04.2011

$ english file name     air_cushion_formfinding_with_plasticity.dat

#define laenge=8.00  $ m
#define breite=4.00  $ m
#define abstand=0.01 $ m

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+prog aqua urs:1
HEAD Air cushion with plasticity formfinding
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
ECHO MAT full
STEE  1 S 500 ES  800 FY 25 FT 40 titl 'ETFE'   $ see AQUA plot worklaw
$ see AQUA  SLS service worklaw:
$ eps=31 o/oo - 25 N/mm2
$ eps=59 o/oo - 40 N/mm2 - or input own worklaw
$
STEE 11 S 500 ES 5000 FY 5 FT 12 titl 'PVC'    $ PVC - see AQUA plot worklaw

$ important: use of STEEL for membrane requires QUAD... NRA 2 in SOFIMSHA !!!!

END

+prog sofimsha urs:2
HEAD Air cushion with plasticity formfinding
CTRL KNOT 10000
SYST SPAC GDIV 10000
NODE NO    X          Y          Z
      1    0          0
     21  $(laenge)[m] 0
    101    0          $(breite)[m]
    121  $(laenge)[m] $(breite)[m]
GRP 1 ; QUAD -    1  101  121   21 T 0.2[mm] M 10 N 20 NRA 2 $ membrane

NODE FIT    1   21 FIX pp
NODE FIT   21  121 FIX pp
NODE FIT  121  101 FIX pp
NODE FIT  101    1 FIX pp
END

!+!KAPITEL Formfinding
+prog ase urs:3
HEAD $ Slight prestress
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES
GRP      - $ switches on all groups initially
GRP 1 PREX 0.01 PREY 0.01 $ Membran
LC 1  TITL 'prestress'
END

+PROG ASE     urs:4 $ without GRP settings:
HEAD $ Air pressure
CTRL WARN 351 $ big strains allowed
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES  PLC 1
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 +2
LC 2 FACD 1 TITL 'pressure'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES  PLC 2
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 +3
CTRL WARN (350 353 1) $ to avoid error due to high damage strain
LC 3 FACD 1 TITL 'pressure'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES  PLC 3
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 +4
CTRL WARN (350 353 1) $ to avoid error due to high damage strain
LC 4 FACD 1 TITL 'pressure'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES  PLC 4
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 +1
CTRL WARN (350 353 1) $ to avoid error due to high damage strain
LC 5 FACD 1 TITL 'release'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES  PLC 5
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 +0.05
CTRL WARN (350 353 1) $ to avoid error due to high damage strain
LC 6 FACD 1 TITL 'release'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES  PLC 6 tol -0.01 iter 200
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 +0.02
CTRL WARN (350 353 1) $ to avoid error due to high damage strain
LC 7 FACD 1 TITL 'release'
END

$ +PROG ASE $ runs quicker in one ASE !
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES  PLC 7 tol -0.01 iter 200
VOLU NO 1 GRP 1 V0 1 P0 +0.20
CTRL WARN (350 353 1) $ to avoid error due to high damage strain
LC 8 FACD 1 TITL 'refill with slight pressure'

!#!Info  Example:       Volu

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
MATE 1 E  400/0.8 E90  300/0.8 G   5/0.8 MUE 0.2 GAM 12/0.8  TITL 'Membran  PVC 0.8 mm'
NMAT 1 MEMB $ defines material as membrane
$
MAT 31 E 0.0006 MUE 0.499999 G 0.0002 K 100 GAM 0.0129 ALFA 1/293/3 TITL Luft
  $ Anwendung siehe auch Datei ..\membranes\luft*.dat    und ..\bric\luft.dat
  $ usage     also see   file  ..\membranes\air*.dat   and ..\bric\air.dat
  $ ALFA 1/293/3 : bei 293 Grad soll Volumenverdoppelung auftreten,
  $ auf das Volumen bezogener Temp.Ausdehnungskoeffizient daher 1/293
  $ da bei MAT aber die Ausdehnung in einer x-Richtung einzugeben -> 1/293/3 (drei Raumrichtungen)

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:3
HEAD Blow up a sphere
UNIT 5
ctrl node 50000 $ ctrl gtol 0.020 $ 20 mm tolerance for nodes
SYST SPAC GDIV 20000 POSZ
sto#r       9.000 $ m radius

$ mesh refinement: insert 2 or 6 :
sto#m 6 $ or 6 - only 2 or 4 or 6 or 12  !!!  number of elements on 45 degree circle
sto#n 6 $ or 6 - only 2 or 4 or 6 or 12  !!!  number of elements from 301-501

let#nnodes #m*8
let#dn 96/#nnodes $ node increment in circular direction
prt#nnodes
prt#dn
let#node 1
$ let#0 2
loop#i #nnodes
  NODE 500+#node X #r            PHIZ #i*360/#nnodes FIX PP
  let#node #node+#dn
endloop
NODE  401,425    X 0.75*#r       PHIZ  0,90
NODE  413        X 0.80*#r       PHIZ 45
NODE  301,325    X 0.50*#r       PHIZ  0,90
NODE  307,319    X 0.55*#r       PHIZ 22.5,67.5
NODE  313        X 0.60*#r       PHIZ 45
NODE  201,225    X 0.25*#r       PHIZ  0,90
NODE  101        X 0.00*#r       PHIZ  0
<text>
$  nodes for circular mesh:
$  3 macro-areas with 8 nodes (quad N1-N4 + N12+N23...) define 1/4 of a circle:
$        101           201           301         401        501 601 701      801
$        *-------------*-------------*-----------*----------*   *   *         *  ----> X
$        |                          /                       |
$        |                         /                        |
$        |                        /                         |
$        |                       /                         |
$        |                      *307                       |
$     225*                     /                          |
$        |                    /                          |
$        |                   /                          |
$        |                  /                          |
$        |               _*313                        /
$        |            --   \                         *507
$        |       -*-        \                      /
$     325*------  319        \                    /
$        |                    \                 /
$        |                     \              /
$        |                      \          /
$        |                       \      /
$     425*                        \  /
$        |                     ----*513
$        |               ------
$        |           -*--
$        |       ---- 519
$        *------
$     525
</text>
$                                         nodes 1-999 :  $ bottom of soil

GRP 0 titl membrane
    QUAD prop mno 1 T 0.8[mm]
    QUAD -  513  501  301  313  M12 -507   M #m N #n
    QUAD -  525  513  313  325  M12 -519   M #m N #n
    QUAD -  313  301  101  325  M12  -     M #m N #m

$ copy to half circle :
let#grp  0 ; grp #grp ; tran quad grp #grp dno 0 phiz 90
$ copy to full circle :
let#grp  0 ; grp #grp ; tran quad grp #grp dno 0 phiz 180
end

+prog sofiload urs:6

  quad grp 0 type pz P -0.6  ! Last lokal z definiert

!+!KAPITEL Formfinding
+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD
$ Achtung: eine als Last (aus SOFILOAD) definierter Luftdruck
$ behÃ¤lt wÃ¤hrend der ASE-Iteration seine Richtung bei !
$ Es ist daher dann erforderlich zumindest einmal die Richtung
$ upzudaten, indem man auf den PLF aufsetzt und Formfindung wiederholt -> LF 10 und LF 11 !

$ NUR der VOLU-Luftdruck ASE-VOLU-P0 wird wÃ¤hrend der ASE-Iteration
$ upgedatet und Ã¤ndert seine Richtung und GrÃ¶ÃŸe,
$ je nach Verdrehung der Quads und FlÃ¤chenzunahme der Quads -> LF 21 arbeitet in einem ASE-Lastfall !

SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES
GRP      - $ switches on all groups initially
GRP 0 FACS 1E-8  FACL 0 PREX 3 PREY 3 $ Membran
VOLU NO 1 GRP 0 V0 5000 P0 0.60        $ V0 = original volume input !
LC 21 FACD 0.0001 TITL 'VOLU: Soll-vz= 5.641 m #r m' $ = 10m - SQRT(10^2 - 9^2)
                                              $ 10m Radius_memb = 0.60/(2*3) zweifache KrÃ¼mmung
                                              $ 9m =Radius Grundkreis
        $ vgl. Wingraf : es kommen fast genau 5.64 m heraus !
END

-PROG ASE URS:5
HEAD blow up
let#plc 21
loop 3
  SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES PLC #plc tol -1 tol4 -2 tol8 -3
  VOLU NO 1 GRP 0 V0 5000 DV 1000 $ V0 = original volume input !
  LC #plc+1 FACD 0.0001 TITL 'blow up'
  END
  let#plc #plc+1
ENDLOOP
END

-PROG ASE URS:8
HEAD
let#plc 24
loop 7
  SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES PLC #plc tol -1 tol4 -2 tol8 -3
  VOLU NO 1 GRP 0 V0 5000 DV 1000 $ V0 = original volume input !
  LC #plc+1 FACD 0.0001 TITL 'blow up more'
  END
  let#plc #plc+1
ENDLOOP
END

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:5
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
MATE 1 E  400/0.8 E90  300/0.8 G   5/0.8 MUE 0.2 GAM 12/0.8  TITL 'Membran  PVC 0.8 mm'
NMAT 1 MEMB $ defines material as membrane
$
MAT 31 E 0.0006 MUE 0.499999 G 0.0002 K 100 GAM 0.0129 ALFA 1/293/3 TITL Luft
  $ Anwendung siehe auch Datei ..\membranes\luft*.dat    und ..\bric\luft.dat
  $ usage     also see   file  ..\membranes\air*.dat   and ..\bric\air.dat
  $ ALFA 1/293/3 : bei 293 Grad soll Volumenverdoppelung auftreten,
  $ auf das Volumen bezogener Temp.Ausdehnungskoeffizient daher 1/293
  $ da bei MAT aber die Ausdehnung in einer x-Richtung einzugeben -> 1/293/3 (drei Raumrichtungen)

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:1
HEAD Tennis court with VOLU air volume
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 POSZ
NODE 1 X  0.0 Y 33.5 Z 0.0 FIX PP
NODE 2 X 37.5 Y 33.5 Z 0.0 FIX PP
NODE 3 X 37.5 Y  0.0 Z 0.0 FIX PP

  QUAD - 1 2 3 4 NRA 2 T 0.8[mm] M 16 N 16

node fit 1 2 fix pp

END

+prog sofiload urs:6
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
LC 801 TYPE none TITL 'partial areaload'
  AREA TYPE PZ P1 0.80 x1 5 15 x2 dxy 6 12 ! in local z
LC 901 TYPE none TITL 'air pressure in local z'
  QUAD GRP 1 TYPE PZ P -0.25
LC 902 TYPE NONE TITL 'wind'
  QUAD GRP 1 TYPE PX 0.60
END
<TEXT>
Attention:

AREA:
  A global load AREA is directly converted into nodal loads in sofiload.
  This load always remains the global direction!
  Only if the system is updated with ASE-SYST STOR and then the load is
  recomputed with sofiload...LC REST, the load will be updated
  to a new quad orientation.

QUAD...pz:
  A local quad load with QUAD is NOT converted into nodal loads in sofiload!
  If ASE runs on a PLC primary load case, the load is updated to the actual
  quad orientation of the primary load case PLC.
  But it will not be updated in the ASE iteration! It keeps the
  orientation of the primary load case PLC!
  So for big rotations you can first run the loadcase e.g. 11, and then rerun
  this load level again on loadcase 12 with PLC 11 to update the load direction!

VOLU pressure:
  The air pressure processed by the VOLU feature is automatically updated
  also during the ASE iterations. So you can be shure that the pressure on the
  deformed mesh is in equilibrion with the stresses in the deformed shape!
  As also the quad area is updated the technique works for big geometric effect.
  In this example the surface area of the membrane changes during formfinding
  and gets bigger! ASE also reports the actual surface area in the VOLU output.
</TEXT>

HEAD Formfindung
$ CTRL SOLV 4 $ Please activate if ISOL licence available (parallel computing)
$ Parallel OPEN-MP element analysis best with CTRL SOLV 4
$ see also CTRL CORE : limit number of processors
$   (or set this in SSD/TEDDY-SOFISTIK-globale_options-sofistik.def- parameter SOF_NUM_THREADS )
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES $ $ NMAT YES not really necessary for FACS 1e-10

GRP      - $ switches on all groups initially
GRP      0    FACS 1e-10 PREX  2 PREY  2 $ Membran 2 KN/m
GRP      2    FACS 1e-10 PREX 20*2       $ Randseile

  LCC 901
END

END

!#!Info  Example:       Cable fishnet
!#!Info  Keyword:       geometric nonlinear; cable; formfindung
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:5
HEAD Cable Tube
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
conc 1
STEE 2 S  355
STEE 3 Y 1770 ES 160000  TMAX 0

SCIT   1 D   3[mm]          MNO 3 $ cable
SCIT   9 D  50[mm] T 10[mm] MNO 3 $steel ring

END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:1
HEAD Cable Tube
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000 NEGZ
let#r    12.000 $ m radius
let#dz    0.100 $ delta-z from one node ring to next
let#n    20     $ number of nodes in ring
let#m    10     $ number of cables in z

let#dphi 360/#n
grp 1
loop#iz0 #n
  let#iz1 #iz0+1
  let#kz1000 #iz0*1000
  let#z -#iz0*#dz
  let#phi0 #iz0*0.5*#dphi
        loop#i0 #n
          let#i1 #i0+1
          let#phi #phi0+#i0*#dphi
          node #kz1000+#i1 x sin(#phi) y cos(#phi) z #z
          if #iz0==0 ; node #kz1000+#i1 fix pp ; endif
        endloop
  if #iz0>0
        loop#i0 #n
          let#i1 #i0+1
         let#k1 #kz1000-1000+#i1 ; let#k2 #kz1000+#i1 ; cabl - #k1 #k2 ncs 1 ; let#k1 #k2
          let#k2 #kz1000-1000+#i1+1 ; if #i0==#n-1 ; let#k2 #kz1000-1000+1 ; endif ; cabl - #k1 #k2 ncs 1
        endloop
  endif
endloop

$
grp 9
        loop#i0 #n
          let#i1 #i0+1
          let#k1 #kz1000+#i1 ; let#k2 #kz1000+#i1+1
          if #i0==#n-1 ; let#k2 #kz1000+1 ; endif
          beam - #k1 #k2 ncs 9
        endloop
sto#n1 #kz1000+1
sto#n2 #kz1000+1+#n/2

end

+prog sofiload urs:3
head
lc 902
  node #n1     type wxx P1 1000
  node #n1,#n2 type wzz P1 0.001
lc 909
  beam grp 9 type PXX PA 0.04
end

!+!KAPITEL Formfinding
+PROG ASE URS:2
HEAD Formfindung
CTRL SOLV 4 ; ctrl cabl 1 ; ctrl iter 3 v2 1
SYST PROB TH3 PLC -
LC 1 FACD 1 TITL 'Formfindung'
END

+PROG ASE URS:9
HEAD Formfindung
CTRL SOLV 4 ; ctrl cabl 1 ; ctrl iter 3 v2 1
SYST PROB TH3 PLC 1 iter 350 - tol -0.003 $ to get sagging stressfree cables ! see upper cables on pos. X
LC 9 FACD 1 TITL 'pxx'
  LCC 909
END

+PROG WING urs:8
HEAD Cable Elements , Normal force Nx  LC:          9
LC   NO 9
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0.650305 Y -0.638062 Z -0.412287 AXIS NEGZ ROTA 0
DEFO TYPE FULL FAC 1 LC CURR EXPO 0 SMOV NO
STRU NUME DSGN NUMN NO
BEAM TYPE N UNIT -1002.906 SCHH NO STYP CABL FILL VERT REPR DLIN
END

<TEXT> Please notice:
Under horizontal load the whole structure hangs mainly on only 2 cables.
The upper cables on pos. X are nearly stressfree and hang nearly free on upper nodes
.
The inner cable sagging (CTRL CABL 1) helps a little bit.
It avoids totally stressfree cables. Each cable has at least a litte tension due to the inner sagging.
Juergen Bellmann 13.11.2015
</TEXT>

+sys del $(project).$d?


!#!Info  Example:       Membrane analysis
!#!Info  Keyword:       geometric nonlinear; membrane; formfindung; highpoint; textile; Pavillon
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!KAPITEL Variable, Material und System
+PROG AQUA URS:5
HEAD Materials
ECHO MAT,SECT FULL
NORM 'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
STEE 104 S  355
STEE 105 Y 1770 ES 160000  TMAX 0
$
$ Membrane stiffness is usually given in kN/m.
$ If you have a 0.8 mm membrane and define SOFiSTiK-QUAD thickness with 0.8 mm,
$ the E-Modulus must be input as E= Membranestiffness/thickness!
$ (If MATE is used (dimension MN/mm2), the input kN/m/mm gives the correct dimension MN/m2)
$ e.g.
MATE 201 E 1000/0.8 E90  720/0.8 G  40/0.8 MUE 0.2 GAM 14/0.8  TITL 'Membran PTFE 0.8 mm' $ Spinne,Mexiko
NMAT 201 MEMB $ defines material as membrane
$
MATE 202 E  400/0.8 E90  300/0.8 G   5/0.8 MUE 0.2 GAM 12/0.8  TITL 'Membran  PVC 0.8 mm' $ Max-Plank
NMAT 202 MEMB $ defines material as membrane
$
MATE 211 E 1200/0.8 E90  400/0.8 G  40/0.8 MUE 0.2 GAM 14/0.8  TITL 'Membran PTFE 0.8 mm' $ Bahnhofshalle Dresden
NMAT 211 MEMB $ defines material as membrane
$

SCIT 901 D 24[mm] MNO 104 $ Rundstahl
CABL 910 D 10[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105     $ cable
CABL 912 D 12[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105
CABL 914 D 14[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105
CABL 916 D 16[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105
CABL 918 D 18[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105
CABL 920 D 20[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105
CABL 922 D 22[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105
CABL 924 D 24[mm] TYPE 1x7 MNO 105
$
$ ################################################################################
$
$ material used in this example:
MATE 1 E  400/0.8 E90  300/0.8 G  5/0.8 MUE 0.2 GAM 12/0.8  TITL 'Membran  PVC 0.8 mm' $ Max-Plank
NMAT 1 MEMB $ defines material as membrane

SCIT 2 MNO 104 D 50 T 2 $ tube or cable
SCIT 3 MNO 104 D 50 T 2 $ tube or cable
SCIT 4 MNO 104 D 50 T 2 $ tube or cable
SCIT 5 MNO 104 D 50 T 2 $ tube or cable
SCIT 6 MNO 104 D 50 T 2 $ tube or cable

CABL 9 D 12 TYPE 1x7     MNO 105 $ cable

END

+PROG Template urs:1
Head Variables
sto#breite 5.00 $ m
sto#hoehe  2.70 $ m  height
sto#radius 0.20 $ m  ring above
sto#dzo    1.20 $ m  heigth highpoint
sto#dzu    0.40 $ m  dz cables below
sto#dicke  0.8  $ mm membrane t
end

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000
$ upper ring 0 circle
loop#i0 8 $ variable #i0 starts with value 0
  let#phi #i0*360/8 ; NODE NO #i0+1 X #radius*cos(#phi) Y #radius*sin(#phi) Z -#hoehe-#dzo
endloop
$
$ upper steel frame
let#b05 #breite*0.5
NODE NO 11 X  #b05 Y  0    Z -#hoehe
NODE NO 12 X  #b05 Y  #b05 Z -#hoehe
NODE NO 13 X  0    Y  #b05 Z -#hoehe
NODE NO 14 X -#b05 Y  #b05 Z -#hoehe
NODE NO 15 X -#b05 Y  0    Z -#hoehe
NODE NO 16 X -#b05 Y -#b05 Z -#hoehe
NODE NO 17 X  0    Y -#b05 Z -#hoehe
NODE NO 18 X  #b05 Y -#b05 Z -#hoehe
$
$ support nodes:
TRAN node 12,14,16,18 dz #hoehe dno 10
Node 22,24,26,28 fix PZ ; Node 22 fix PP ; Node 24 fix PZPY $ fixings
$
NODE  9 X 0 Y 0 Z -#hoehe-#dzo+1.5*#radius $ compression strud top
NODE 19 X 0 Y 0 Z -#hoehe+#dzu             $ " bottom
$ elemtents
GRP 1
  QUAD -  2 12 14 4 M41 3   M 18 N 6 T #dicke[mm] MNO 1 KR 9 $ lokal x axis is very important !
  QUAD -  4 14 16 6 M41 5   M 18 N 6 T #dicke[mm] MNO 1 KR 9
  QUAD -  6 16 18 8 M41 7   M 18 N 6 T #dicke[mm] MNO 1 KR 9
  QUAD -  8 18 12 2 M41 1   M 18 N 6 T #dicke[mm] MNO 1 KR 9
GRP 2 TITL 'upper ring'
  BEAM fit 8 1 ncs 2
  BEAM fit (1 7 1) (2 1) ncs 2
GRP 3 TITL 'steel frame'
  BEAM fit 18 11 ncs 3
  BEAM fit (11 17 1) (12 1) ncs 3
GRP 4 TITL 'columns'
  BEAM fit 12 22 div 4 ncs 4
  BEAM fit 14 24 div 4 ncs 4
  BEAM fit 16 26 div 4 ncs 4
  BEAM fit 18 28 div 4 ncs 4
GRP 5 TITL 'air column'
  BEAM - 2  9 ncs  6
  BEAM - 4  9 ncs  6
  BEAM - 6  9 ncs  6
  BEAM - 8  9 ncs  6
  BEAM - 9 19 ncs 5
GRP 9 TITL 'cables'
  CABL - 12 19 ncs 9
  CABL - 14 19 ncs 9
  CABL - 16 19 ncs 9
  CABL - 18 19 ncs 9
GRP 99 TITL 'temporary support FOFI'
  SPRI - NA 9,19 dz 1 ct 1e6 cm 1e6
END

!+!KAPITEL Formfinding
+PROG ASE URS:6
HEAD Formfinding
SYST PROB TH3 - tol -0.01 NMAT YES
GRP      - $ switched on all groups
GRP      1    FACS 1e-10  $ membrane
GRP      9       PREX 2   $ to press it up just in the beginning
let#vtvr 0.1 ; HIGH 0 0 0 pr1 0.5 ptpr 0.1
LC 1 DLZ 1             TITL 'Form vtvr=0.1'
END

HEAD Rerun HIGH input with actualized dead load area and FACL 0
SYST PROB TH3 - tol -0.01 NMAT YES PLC 3

!+!KAPITEL Formfinding
+PROG ASE URS:5
HEAD Iter 1 Relaxation method - very stable but membrane nodes may shift on surface from step to step
let#lf1 101 ; let#plf 0 ; let#f_iter1 1 ; CTRL CABL 0 ; CTRL WARN 296
loop 8
  SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES ITER 1 PLC #plf
  $ elements with given length: factor stiffness 1.0, overtake stress from PLC (default FACL 1)
  GRP     -   FACS 1    FACL 1                  $ switches on all elements $ schaltet erst mal alle Gruppen ein
  GRP 20,30   FACS 1    FACL 1                  $ bending beam
  GRP 40      FACS 1    FACL 1 PREX 10*#f_iter1 $ truss with prestress in first step
  $ elements with desired given prestress:
  GRP 10      FACS 1E-2 FACL 0 PREX 40 $ cable just try to reach this prestress
  GRP 50      FACS 1E-2 FACL 0 PREX 20 $ cable just try to reach this prestress
  GRP 60      FACS 1E-2 FACL 0 PREX 50 $ cable just try to reach this prestress
  GRP 70      FACS 1E-2 FACL 0 PREX 40 $ cable just try to reach this prestress
  GRP 90      FACS 1E-2 FACL 0 PREX 70 $ cable just try to reach this prestress
  $ membrane:
  GRP 1,2,3,4 FACS 1E-2 FACL 0 PREX  0 $ membrane with given prestress - just try to reach this prestress, here via HIGH:
  HIGH  0.0[m]  +2.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3  $ high point prestress
  HIGH  0.0[m]   0.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3
  HIGH  0.0[m]  -2.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3
  LC #lf1 FACD 1 TITL 'Iter 1 Relaxation'
  END
  let#lf1 #lf1+1 ; let#plf #lf1-1 ; let#f_iter1 0
endloop
END

+prog ase urs:2
HEAD Post iteration - necessary to guarantee real equilibrium
CTRL CABL 0
  SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES ITER - PLC 104 TOL -0.2 ; CTRL WARN 296
  GRP        - FACS 1 $ switches on all elements $ schaltet erst mal alle Gruppen ein
  $ membrane:
  GRP 1,2,3,4  FACS 1E-10 FACL 0 PREX 0 $ just try to reach this prestress, here HOCH:
  HIGH  0.0[m]  +2.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3  $ = Definition der Vorspannung   $ Definition of prestress
  HIGH  0.0[m]   0.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3  $ = Definition der Vorspannung   $ Definition of prestress
  HIGH  0.0[m]  -2.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3  $ = Hochpunktanteil              $ high point proportion
  LC 150 FACD 1 TITL 'Post iteration'
  END
END

+prog ase urs:6
HEAD Compare in one ASE with new FIXZ=6
  SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES
  GRP        - FACS 1 $ switches on all elements $ schaltet erst mal alle Gruppen ein
  $ membrane:
  GRP 1,2,3,4  FACS 1E-10 FACL 0 PREX 0 $ just try to reach this prestress, here HOCH:
  HIGH  0.0[m]  +2.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3  $ = Definition der Vorspannung   $ Definition of prestress
  HIGH  0.0[m]   0.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3  $ = Definition der Vorspannung   $ Definition of prestress
  HIGH  0.0[m]  -2.0[m]  PR1 30 PTPR 0.3  $ = Hochpunktanteil              $ high point proportion
  LC 156 FACD 1 TITL 'Without Iter 1 Relaxation method'
  END
END

+sys del $(project).$d?

$ Parallel OPEN-MP element analysis best with CTRL SOLV 4

GRP      - $ switches on all groups initially

HIGH  7.5[m]  4.5[m] PR1 7 PTPR 0.12 $ #21  Definition der Vorspannung mit HOCH
     20.5[m]  4.5[m] PR1 7 PTPR 0.15 $ #22  Bei sehr hohen Hochpunkte darf der
     14.0[m] 14.0[m] PR1 7 PTPR 0.2  $ #23  tangentiale Anteil VTVR nicht zu hoch sein
      7.5[m] 22.5[m] PR1 7 PTPR 0.15 $ #24  sonst schnÃ¼rt sich die Membran eine und
     20.5[m] 22.5[m] PR1 7 PTPR 0.35 $ #25  reisst ab!!

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:7
HEAD Wind
unit 0 $ all in [m]
sto#ri    1.0    $ inner radius of the load
sto#rmax 15.0    $ outer radius of the load
sto#p0    1.20   $ basic value

LC   921 'NONE' TITL "Wind from X"
let#winkel 0.0
#define wind
$ loadfactors all 10 degree
$ #A(0) = 0 degree ... #A(18) = 180 degree:    + = pressure,    - = tension
let#A(0) +0.80,+0.70,+0.50,+0.20,-0.20,-0.50,-0.70,-0.80,-0.90
let#A(9) -1.00,-1.00,-1.00,-1.00,-0.95,-0.90,-0.85,-0.80,-0.75,-0.75
$
loop#1 36
  let#alfa1 #winkel    ; let#sn1 sin(#alfa1) ; let#cs1 cos(#alfa1)
  let#alfa2 #winkel+10 ; let#sn2 sin(#alfa2) ; let#cs2 cos(#alfa2)
  let#x1 #rmax*#cs1 ; let#y1 #rmax*#sn1
  let#x2   #ri*#cs1 ; let#y2   #ri*#sn1
  let#x3   #ri*#cs2 ; let#y3   #ri*#sn2
  let#x4 #rmax*#cs2 ; let#y4 #rmax*#sn2
  let#i1 #1 ; let#i2 #1+1
  if #i1 > 18
    let#i1 36-#1
  endif
  if #i2 > 18
    let#i2 36-#1
  endif
  let#p1 #(A+#i1) ; let#p2 #(A+#i2) ;  let#p 0.5*#p1+0.5*#p2+0.000001 $ to avoid 0.00
  area 'qgrp' PROJ ZZ WIDE 99[m] TYPE pz P1 #p*#p0   x1 #x1 #y1   x2 #x2 #y2   x3 #x3 #y3   x4 #x4 #y4
  let#winkel #winkel+10
endloop
#enddef
#include wind

LC   922 'NONE' TITL "Wind from Y"
let#winkel 90
#include wind

LC   923 'NONE' TITL "Wind from 135 degree "
let#winkel 135
#include wind
end

+PROG ASE URS:5
HEAD
SYST PROB TH3 NMAT YES TOL 0.001 PLC 2
LC 23 FACT 1.0 FACD 1 TITL 'Wind from 135 degree'
  LCC 923
END
