+PROG TEMPLATE urs:8
HEAD SOFILOAD Eingabe Generator - siehe .lst Datei nach der Berechnung
PAGE LINE 9000
let#vb1(32) 0  ! array dimesionieren (0:32)
let#vb2(32) 0  ! array dimesionieren (0:32)
let#vb(32) 0  ! array dimesionieren (0:32)

loop#it0 #ntime
  let#it1 #it0+1
  let#t #time(#it1)*60 $ Zeit in Sekunden

@KEY HIST_VAL 1    $ Transient data
LET#CDB_IER 0
LOOP $ ALLE SAETZE
let#tt @tt
if #tt<#t-0.01
  let#tt1 #tt
  loop#i0 #nxi
    let#vb1(#i0) @(vb+#i0) ! #vb1(0:#nlay)
  endloop
else
  let#tt2 #tt
  loop#i0 #nxi
    let#vb2(#i0) @(vb+#i0) ! #vb1(0:#nlay)
  endloop
  let#CDB_IER 2 ! Ende
endif
ENDLOOP #CDB_IER<2 $ SONST KEIN ENDE

let#dt #tt2-#tt1
if #dt>0
  let#f1 (#tt2-#t)/#dt
  let#f2 1.0-#f1
else
  let#f1 1.0
  let#f2 0.0
endif
$    let#w0 #vb1(0)
$    let#w1 #vb1(1)
$    let#w2 #vb1(2)
$    $ Testprint:
$    TXE tt1=#(tt1,8.0) sec.     vb=#(w0,8.1) vb=#(w1,8.1) vb=#(w2,8.1)
$    let#w0 #vb2(0)
$    let#w1 #vb2(1)
$    let#w2 #vb2(2)
$    TXE tt2=#(tt2,8.0) sec.     vb=#(w0,8.1) vb=#(w1,8.1) vb=#(w2,8.1)

$    $ Testprint:
$    TXE f1=#(f1,8.3)  f2=#(f2,8.3)

$    let#w0 #f1*#vb1(0)+#f2*#vb2(0)
$    let#w1 #f1*#vb1(1)+#f2*#vb2(1)
$    let#w2 #f1*#vb1(2)+#f2*#vb2(2)
$    $ Testprint:
$    TXE tt1=#(t,8.0) sec.     vb=#(w0,8.1) vb=#(w1,8.1) vb=#(w2,8.1)
  loop#i0 #nxi
    let#vb(#i0) #f1*#vb1(#i0)+#f2*#vb2(#i0)
  endloop

  let#lf #lf0+#it1
  let#min #time(#it1) $ Zeit in Minuten
  TXE LF #(lf,4.0) TYP none BEZ  #(#min,5.0)_min_Temperatur
  let#ii 0 ; if #seite>0 ; let#ii #nxi-1 ; endif
    let#xx -#seite*#xi(#ii)*#thick/2
    let#vv #vb(#ii)
  TXE   QUAD GRP #grp TYP TEMP 1 Z0 #(xx,6.3) #(vv,6.1) ''$$''
  loop#i0 #nxi-1
    let#ii #ii-#seite
    let#xx -#seite*#xi(#ii)*#thick/2
    let#vv #vb(#ii)
    if #i0<#nxi-1-1
            if #ii<10
              TXE                         Z#(ii,1.0) #(xx,6.3) #(vv,6.1) ''$$''
            else
              TXE                         Z#(ii,2.0) #(xx,6.3) #(vv,6.1) ''$$''
            endif
    else
            if #ii<10
              TXE                         Z#(ii,1.0) #(xx,6.3) #(vv,6.1)
            else
              TXE                         Z#(ii,2.0) #(xx,6.3) #(vv,6.1)
            endif
    endif
  endloop
  TXE ''$''
endloop ! time
END

!#!Info  Example:       LNG Tank - SOFIMSHA rotational symmetric sector shell
!#!Info  Keyword:       material nonlinear; concrete law; cracked stiffness; reduction of stiffness; tank; rotational symmetry
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$

$ Processing with low temperature material curves:
$ All temperatures are defined relative to the absolute zero point -273 degree.
$ So all temperatures ase positiv and can be handled in AQUA.
$
$ If you do not need own material curves please use
$ example   concrete_tank_cracked.dat    without new defined material laws
$ and with temperature input in degree celsius !
$
$ Comments to sector model - see ase.dat\..\nonlinear_quad\sector_modelling.pdf:
$ For a good preanalysis of a tank it is always good
$ not to model the whole 3D shell but to use a rotation symmetric sector model.
$ The major influence of the stiffness reduction due to cracking can
$ be studied much better in such a small model.
$ Furthermore this model converges much better.


!#!KAPITEL Material and System Generation
+prog aqua urs:1
HEAD LNG Tank - Definition of low temperature material curves
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'

<TEXT>
      Temp   0 epsor  -3.081500
      Temp   1 epsor  -3.071500
      Temp 103 epsor  -2.050000
      Temp 173 epsor  -1.350000
      Temp 223 epsor  -0.850000
      Temp 253 epsor  -0.550000
      Temp 293 epsor  -0.150000
      Temp 363 epsor   0.550000

</TEXT>

sto#Ref_Temp_273    273.15 $ Reference temperature = -273.15 Grad
                           $ All temperatures are defined relative to the absolute zero point -273 degree
sto#Start_Temp 35+#Ref_Temp_273 $ Erection temperature (zero strain)
conc  1 C fcn 40
  #define arblbruc
     let#epsor -1.E-5*(#Start_Temp-#temp)*1000 ; txe Temp #temp epsor #(#epsor,10.6)
     ssla ULTI TEMP #temp $ EPST #epsor   EPST not yet running for negative values -> ASE CTRL NLAY V4 1
        let#eps_max -3.00-#fact_fck*2.00 $
        ssla eps #eps_max    sig    0            type spl
        ssla eps -3.50       sig  -30*#fact_fck  type spl
        ssla eps -2.32       sig  -48*#fact_fck  type spl
        ssla eps -0.40       sig  -20*#fact_fck  type spl
        ssla eps     0       sig    0            type pol
        ssla eps  0.06       sig 2.09*#f_tension type pol
        ssla eps  0.18       sig    0            type pol
  #enddef
  $
  $
  $
  let#temp    0               ; let#fact_fck 0.50 ; let#f_tension 0.40 $    0 Grad absolut
                    #include arblbruc
  let#temp    1               ; let#fact_fck 0.50 ; let#f_tension 0.40 $    1 Grad absolut
                    #include arblbruc
  let#temp -170+#Ref_Temp_273 ; let#fact_fck 0.65 ; let#f_tension 0.60 $ -170 Grad Celsius
                    #include arblbruc
  let#temp -100+#Ref_Temp_273 ; let#fact_fck 0.80 ; let#f_tension 0.75
                    #include arblbruc
  let#temp  -50+#Ref_Temp_273 ; let#fact_fck 0.90 ; let#f_tension 0.90
                    #include arblbruc
  let#temp  -20+#Ref_Temp_273 ; let#fact_fck 0.95 ; let#f_tension 0.95
                    #include arblbruc
  let#temp  +20+#Ref_Temp_273 ; let#fact_fck 1.00 ; let#f_tension 1.00 $  +20 Grad Celsius
                    #include arblbruc
  let#temp  +90+#Ref_Temp_273 ; let#fact_fck 1.00 ; let#f_tension 1.00
                    #include arblbruc
stee 2 S 500
  #define arblstahl
     ssla ULTI TEMP #temp EPST -1.E-5*(#Start_Temp-#temp)*1000
                       ssla eps   -25.00 sig -525 $ trilineare
        let#sig -500 ; ssla eps #sig/200 sig #sig $ mit E=200000
                       ssla eps     0.00 sig    0
        let#sig  500 ; ssla eps #sig/200 sig #sig
                       ssla eps    25.00 sig  525
  #enddef
  let#temp    0
                    #include arblstahl
  let#temp    1
                    #include arblstahl
  let#temp  +90+#Ref_Temp_273
                    #include arblstahl
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD LNG Tank - SOFIMSHA rotational symmetric sector shell
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC            GDIV  1000 GDIR POSZ
$
$
$           *11
$              --*--12
$                  -----
$                       -----
$                            ---*18
$                                  * 19
$                                  |
$                                  |
$                                  |
$                                  |
$                                  |
$                                  |
$                                  |
$            51   52            58 |
$           *----*---------------*-* 59     ------> X
$           |
$           |
$           v
$           Z
$
$ --------------------- nodes ---------------------------------------------
NODE    NO   X   Z
        11   0  -12
        19   6  -10
        59   6    0
        51   0    0
NODE NO 12 NR1 11 NR2 19 NR3 SS X 0.1   $ interpolate node 12  on line 11-19
NODE NO 18 NR1 11 NR2 19 NR3 SS X 0.95  $ to get fine mesh at the corner
NODE NO 52 NR1 51 NR2 59 NR3 SS X 0.1
NODE NO 58 NR1 51 NR2 59 NR3 SS X 0.95
$
STO#alfa 5.0 $ sektor angle
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 999 DNO 1000 PHIZ -#alfa $ minus because then
                                             $ support conditions look better in animator!
$ --------------------- elements ---------------------------------------------
GRP 1 TITL roof ; QUAD PROP MNO 1 T 0.20[m]
 $ from 12-18:
  let#1 12,18 ; QUAD N1 #1 #2 #2+1000 #1+1000 M 10  $ = QUAD K1 12 18 1018 1012
  let#1 18,19 ; QUAD N1 #1 #2 #2+1000 #1+1000 M  2
  ctrl Warn 121
                QUAD N1 11 12 1012 $ triangle - if you want

GRP 2 TITL wall ; QUAD PROP MNO 1 T 0.40[m]
 $ from 19-59:
  let#1 19,59 ; QUAD N1 #1 #2 #2+1000 #1+1000 M 30  $ = QUAD K1 19 59 1059 1019

GRP 3 TITL slab ; QUAD PROP MNO 1 T 0.60[m] C 50000 $ bedded bottom slab
 $ from 52-58:
  let#1 52,58 ; QUAD N1 #1 #2 #2+1000 #1+1000 M 10
  let#1 58,59 ; QUAD N1 #1 #2 #2+1000 #1+1000 M  2
                QUAD N1 51 52 1052 $ triangle - if you want
$
$ --------------------- fixings ---------------------------------------------
$ you can use this block without change because nodes selected without node numbers:
$ comment: filter all nodes on the x-Axis with a box and assign FIX PYYM
$          then filter all angle nodes and assign FIX PRMT
SBOX A1X 0 0 0  100 0 0  A2X 0 0 -100  0 0 100  A3X 0 0 0  0 100 0
NODE SBOX FIX PYYM $ rotational symmetry condition x-Achse
$
$ rotational symmetry condition on angle axis:
SBOX A1X 0 0 0  100 0 0  A2X 0 0 -100  0 0 100  A3X 0 -100 0  0 -0.03 0
NODE SBOX FIX PRMT DX sin(#alfa) DY cos(#alfa) $ rotational symmetry condition !
$
$ Attention: if you change TRAN KNOT...PHIZ -#alfa    to   +#alfa,
$            you also must change of sign DX sin(#alfa) !
END

                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2

                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max

+PROG TENDON urs:2
HEAD Parabolic Prestress
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ Definition of prestressing system:
$ We recommend to input all data as user defined prestressing system.
$ For the static analysis the following values are sufficient:
SYSP NOPS MAT   ZV       AZ    LITZ MINR   BETA  MUE ECC  SP     DO
        1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 82[mm] $ csm3_parabel and csm32_slab, 12 wires
      $ 1  11 3078[kN] 2250[mm2] 15 7.10[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 92[mm] $            15 wires
      $ 1  11 3848[kN] 2850[mm2] 19 6.50[m] 0.3 0.21 4[mm] 3[mm] 97[mm] $ csm31_beam 19 wires
      $ 1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.0 0.00 0[mm] 0[mm] 10[mm] $ csm3_casting_yard

AXES NOH 1  VAL1  0.00 0.00 0.00  TYPE=poly  KIND=QUAD
         1  VAL1 20.00 0.00 0.00  TITL "tendon_axis"
$ or use existing axis with   AXES NOH 1 TYPE REFS 'AX_3' KIND QUAD
TOPP NOH 1 KIND REFX S 0,20 SP 1,2
$ tendon geometry definition:  NOPS = prestressing system for max-min radius parameters + duct-excentricities

PTUV    S     U     V   DVS    TYPE=SPAN
        1     0   0.5     -
      1.50    -   0.9     0  $  1.50 = midspan ( xi=0.5 in span 1 )
        2     0   0.5     -
CS ICS1 11 12                $ = construction stages
$ prestress-procedure  $ Anspann-Vorgehen
PSIG 'RI' ANWS 'TS' KAPA - K3 1280 $
        $ k3 = estimated limit to reduce stress at traffic opening (after first creep+shrinkage)
        $      max-sigma-traffic opening in most cases (e.g. to EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)) -> 0.65 fpk (or 0.75 depending on design code)
$ final tendon definition:
TEND NOT 1 NOG 1 NTEN 3 LC 93 LC0 0

echo plot full $ tendon plots:

$                             mm         N/mm2       N/mm2
$ mit  Stahlfaserbeton :    25.2          385        0.60
$ ohne Stahlfaserbeton :    31.2          435        0.00
$
$
$ Wesentlich interessanter ist aber die MÃ¶glichkeit von Stahlfaserbeton-Bauteilen,
$ durch Rissbildung SchnittgrÃ¶ÃŸen umzulagern. Diese Berechnungen werden auch oft im
$ GZG durchgefÃ¼hrt um die Gebrauchstauglichkeit sicherzustellen. Hier fallen nach der
$ nichtlinearen ASE-Berechnung auch die Stahlspannungen im Zustand II an.
$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ Results of 0.9 times load:
$                                 Deformation  sigma-Steel  Concrete tension
$                                     mm         N/mm2       N/mm2
$ with steel fibre concrete :       25.2          385        0.60
$ without steel fibre concrete :    31.2          435        0.00
$
$
$ To besieged the internal forces and moments through cracking is significantly an interesting
$ possibility of steel fibre concrete-elements. These analysis are been often conducted to ensure

                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max

$ Tandemsystem : Lane 1:Wheel load 150 kN/Rad TS=SOFILOAD-TYP L !
$                  Total excess load=600 kN    (Please check safety factor GAMU ! 1.35/1.50)
$                Lane 2:Wheel load 100 kN/Rad
$                  Total excess load=400 kN
$ =======================================================================
$ Case EYA1 Lane 1 is at right     all xx m a Node position!

let#lf 301
let#ys1 6.20-1.50      $  middle lane 1

let#ys2 0.00-3.00 $  Middle lane 2
loop#1 10
 LC #lf TYPE L_T TITL 'TS_overload'
   let#lf #lf+1 ; let#x1 6.00+#1*2.0 $
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1      Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $  2. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1      Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $  1. Axis lane 2
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $  2. Axis lane 2
endloop
$  Case C lane 1 is at left:
let#ys1 -6.20+1.50      $  Middle lane 1
let#ys2 -6.20+1.50+3.00 $  Middle lane 2
loop#1 10
 LC #lf TYPE L_T TITL 'TS_overload'
   let#lf #lf+1 ; let#x1 7.90+#1*2.0 $  first axis
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1      Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $  1. Axis lane 1
   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 150 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys1+1.0,#ys1-1.0 $  2. Axis lane 1

   POIN QGRP TYPE PZZ P 100 X #x1+1.20 Y #ys2+1.0,#ys2-1.0 $  2. Axis lane 2
endloop

TEND NOT #nr NOG #nr NTEN 1 LC 3 LC0 0

  #include tendons

$ Max. perm. stress  po,max:
                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2

                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2

                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent

!#!Info  Example:       Cracked arch without reinforcement
!#!Info  Keyword:       material nonlinear; concrete law; arch; reduction of stiffness; crack; tunneling
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!Info  Date:          23.07.2010



$---------------------------------------------------------------
$ Parameterdefinition
$---------------------------------------------------------------

$ Bodenparameter
#define   E=(120*1000)                  $ Ev des Gebirges in kN/mÂ³
#define phi=(22.5)                      $ Reibungswinkel des Gebirges in Grad (tang. Bettung)
#define coh=(100)                       $ KohÃ¤sion ds Gebirges in kN/mÂ² (tang. Bettung)
#define   p=(260*0.85*0.60*1.0)         $ Gebirgslast pv (85%) in kN/mÂ²
#define   k=(0.4)                       $ Erddruckbeiwert gem. TBS

$ Systemeingabe
#define  rk=(5.56)                      $ Systemradius Kalotte in m
#define  ru=(3.26)                      $ Systemradius Ulme in m
#define rst=(3.56)                      $ Systemradius Strosse in m
#define  rs=(5.79)                      $ Systemradius Sohle in m

#define dk=(0.30)                       $ Spritzbetondicke Kalotte in m
#define ds=(0.60)                       $ Spritzbetondicke Sohle in m


+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Tunnelschale
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'

CONC 1 C 25 MUE 0.0 $ Kalotte    $ mue 0.0 : um Interaktion mit Quad-LÃ¤ngsrichtung zu vermeiden
CONC 2 C 25 MUE 0.0 $ Strosse
CONC 3 C 25 MUE 0.0 $ Ulme       $ Zur Beachtung:  FÃ¼r Temperaturbeanspruchungen
CONC 4 C 25 MUE 0.0 $ Sohle      $ ist der Tunnel lÃ¤ngs-verschieblich !

STEE 5 S 500  $ fÃ¼r die QUAD-Bewehrung

BMAT NO 1 C $(E)/$(rk)*0.5      CT 0.5*$(E)/$(rk)*0.5    MUE tan($(phi))  COH $(coh)  CRAC 0  $ Kalotte 90Â° Firstbereich
BMAT NO 2 C $(E)/$(ru)          CT 0.5*$(E)/$(ru)        MUE tan($(phi))  COH $(coh)  CRAC 0  $ Kalotte Ulmenbereich
BMAT NO 3 C $(E)/$(rst)         CT 0.5*$(E)/$(rst)       MUE tan($(phi))  COH $(coh)  CRAC 0  $ Ulme
BMAT NO 4 C $(E)/$(rs)          CT 0.5*$(E)/$(rs)        MUE tan($(phi))  COH $(coh)  CRAC 0  $ Strosse

SVAL 1,2,3,4 1 A 0.001 $ HilfsstÃ¤be Gruppe 91-98 SOFIMSHC
END

+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:2
HEAD Tunnelschale
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV    10000

CTRL MESH 1
CTRL HMIN 0.4

let#nrx 0 ; let#x 0
#define ring
SPT NO       Y      Z     X=#x
     1+#nrx  0.00  -5.23      $ rechte Seite
     2+#nrx  3.05  -4.34      $ rechte Seite
     3+#nrx  4.51  -1.57      $ rechte Seite
     4+#nrx  2.59   1.59      $ rechte Seite
     5+#nrx  0.00   2.21      $ rechte Seite

     6+#nrx -2.59   1.59      $ linke Seite
     7+#nrx -4.51  -1.57      $ linke Seite
     8+#nrx -3.05  -4.34      $ linke Seite

SLN 1+#nrx 1+#nrx 2+#nrx GRP 91 SNO 1 ; SLNB R  $(rk)  Nx 1 $ Kalotte
SLN 2+#nrx 2+#nrx 3+#nrx GRP 92 SNO 2 ; SLNB R  $(ru)  Nx 1 $ Ulme
SLN 3+#nrx 3+#nrx 4+#nrx GRP 93 SNO 3 ; SLNB R  $(rst) Nx 1 $ StroÃŸe
SLN 4+#nrx 4+#nrx 5+#nrx GRP 94 SNO 4 ; SLNB R  $(rs)  Nx 1 $ Sohle
SLN 5+#nrx 5+#nrx 6+#nrx GRP 95 SNO 3 ; SLNB R  $(rs)  Nx 1 $ Sohle
SLN 6+#nrx 6+#nrx 7+#nrx GRP 96 SNO 3 ; SLNB R  $(rst) Nx 1 $ StroÃŸe
SLN 7+#nrx 7+#nrx 8+#nrx GRP 97 SNO 2 ; SLNB R  $(ru)  Nx 1 $ Ulme
SLN 8+#nrx 8+#nrx 1+#nrx GRP 98 SNO 1 ; SLNB R  $(rk)  Nx 1 $ Kalotte Strosse
#enddef
#include ring
let#nrx 1000 ; let#x 1.0
#include ring
END

+prog sofimsha urs:5
HEAD
SYST REST
GRP 1 ; QUAD fit 1 1001 1002 2 DRX 1 0 0 MNO 1 T $(dk)[m]
GRP 2 ; QUAD fit 2 1002 1003 3 DRX 1 0 0 MNO 2 T $(dk)[m]

GRP 4 ; QUAD fit 4 1004 1005 5 DRX 1 0 0 MNO 4         T1 $(dk)[m] $(dk)[m] $(ds)[m] $(ds)[m]
GRP 5 ; QUAD fit 5 1005 1006 6 DRX 1 0 0 MNO 4         T1 $(ds)[m] $(ds)[m] $(dk)[m] $(dk)[m]

+prog sofiload urs:4
HEAD
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ Erddruckansatz
LC 2 TYPE none TITL 'Erdruck vertikal'
QUAD GRP 1,2,7,8 TYPE PZP  P  $(p)             $ Erdruck vertikal

LC 3 TYPE none TITL 'Erdruck horizontal'
QUAD GRP 1,2,3,4 TYPE PYP  P -$(p)*($(k))      $ Erdruck rechts
QUAD GRP 5,6,7,8 TYPE PYP  P +$(p)*($(k))      $ Erdruck links

LC 81 TYPE none TITL 'Erdruck Bettungsvorspannung'
    QUAD GRP (1 8 1) TYPE 'ex' P 0.1  $ ex kann in diesem Beispiel entfallen, allgemein bei 3D aber lieber ex+ey
    QUAD GRP (1 8 1) TYPE 'ey' P 0.1

<TEXT> Comment
Beim klassischen Verfahren wie hier angewendet kann man zwar den Erddruck exakt aufbringen,
das Aufbringen des radialen Druckes fÃ¼hrt allerdings zu einer ZusammendrÃ¼ckung des Ringes
und damit zunÃ¤chst zu Zugspannungen in den Bettungsfedern.
Nach der Verformung verbleiben dann grÃ¶ÃŸere Bereiche ohne Bettung.
Das ist aber auch gewÃ¼nscht, da man z.B. halt nicht will dass die horizontale StÃ¼tzung grÃ¶ÃŸer wird.
Denn die horizontale StÃ¼tzung ist ja die horizontale Last plus die zusÃ¤tzlich generierte horizontale Bettung!
Auch hier wird ja eine horizontale Bettung generiert so dass der horizontale Erddruck in der Berechnung
eigentlich angewachsen ist!
.
Manchmal will man aber einen groÃŸflÃ¤chen Zugausfall vermeinden und dann kann man die BetonverkÃ¼rzung
durch eine Betondehnung mit Lastfall 81 kompensieren.

$ Comments:
$ Without prestrain, a lot of quad beddings may crack and the stress in the bedding is 0.0.
$ To follow a nonlinear worklaw in the bedding this may not be what you want.
$ For this we can add a prestrain to the shell to create a prestress in the bedding -> LC 81.
$
$ But keep in mind that the total horizontal force acting on the shell is the bedding pressure plus the applied load.
$ And also in this analysis we get a horizontal pressure that is greater than the applied horizontal load!
$
$ Juergen Bellmann 24.5.2022

</TEXT>



END

$ With CTRL CONC V3+V4 in ASE the values can be adapted to a specific load case:
$  V3=   FCT  = Tensile strength for tension stiffening
$  V4=   FCTK = Tensile strength of bare concrete
$               " by ULS analysis set zero : then the concrete itself must not
$                 carry any tensile stress!
$ In SLS FCTK may be reduced due to damages from cold weather, temperature shocks
$        and construction loading (in reality the concrete is often pre-cracked)
$        Then the displacements better correlagte to measured values on site.
$ In ULS FCTK should be set to zere because then the concrete itself is not allowed to carry any tensile
$ Parallel OPEN-MP element analysis best with CTRL SOLV 4
$ see also CTRL CORE : limit number of processors
$   (or set this in SSD/TEDDY-SOFISTIK-globale_options-sofistik.def- parameter SOF_NUM_THREADS )

  LCC 3 FACT 1.00              $ Erddruck horizontal

!#!Info  Example:       Bedding Distribution P0-P3 and negative z Coordinates
!#!Info  Keyword:       pile; bedding; Bohrprofil
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ english file name: circular_variation.dat
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Bedding Distribution P0-P3 and negative z Coordinates
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
UNIT 0  $ Units in m
CONC 1 C  25  $ C25/30
STEE 2 S 500
SCIT 1 MNO 1 D 1[m]
$
BORE 1 Z -6 $ bore starts at Z=-6m, therefore 2 m over pile head
         BBAX 0  4        K0 100.0     $ first 4 m of bore
         BBAX 4  6+9.80-1 K0 100000.0  $ bore ends only upto  1m over pile foot
         BBLA 0  4        K0 100.0
         BBLA 4  6+9.80-1 K0 100000.0  P0 1 .7 .5 .3
BORE 2 Z -6
         BBAX 0  4        K1 100.0     $ first 4 m of bore
         BBAX 4  6+9.80-1 K1 100000.0  $ bore ends only upto  1m over pile foot
         BBLA 0  4        K1 100.0     $ square root parabel
         BBLA 4  6+9.80-1 K1 100000.0  P0 1 1 .4 1
BORE 3 Z -6
         BBAX 0  4        K2 100.0     $ first 4 m of bore
         BBAX 4  6+9.80-1 K2 100000.0  $ bore ends only upto  1m over pile foot
         BBLA 0  4        K2 100.0     $ linear distribution
         BBLA 4  6+9.80-1 K2 100000.0  P0 1 .4 1 .4
BORE 4 Z -6
         BBAX 0  4        K3 100.0     $ first 4 m of bore
         BBAX 4  6+9.80-1 K3 100000.0  $ bore ends only upto  1m over pile foot
         BBLA 0  4        K3 100.0     $ quadratic distribution
         BBLA 4  6+9.80-1 K3 100000.0  P0 .3 .3 1 1
$ P0 is the factor of bedding in local z direction of beam
$ P1 is the factor            in local y direction
$ P2 is the factor   in negative local z direction
$ P3 is the factor   in negative local y direction
$ see penultimate WINGRAF image
END
$ Determination of pile bedding K0:
$ Stiffness value of line bedding is required
$  1 m cross displacement produces a reaction force of
$    100000 kN/m (Force pro m pile length),
$    this is equivalent to a stiffness of c=K0= 100000 kN/m2  or kN/m/m
$
$ Line related stiffness K0, can be extracted simply out of pile bedding
$ module ks multiplied with the pile diameter D:
$            c=K0=DÂ·ks
$ Thereby under DIN 4014 the bedding module ks can be determined simply out of
$ stiffness modul of soil Es:
$            Ks=Es/D
$ For D>1.0m here D=1.0 m may be set. This results to:
$
$ Pile diameter D <= 1m:   c=K0=Es
$
$ Pile diameter D >  1m:   c=K0=Es*D
$
$ generally this value is set for cross bedding BBLA.
$ For longitudinal bedding BBAX line related stiffness c=K0 is required.
$ It can be extracted in a similar way from the reaction force per m in relation to the settelment.
$
$ same value can be set for BBAX as for BBLA if
$ BBAX is unknown.
+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD Bedding Distribution P0-P3 and negative z Coordinates
$
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIR POSZ GDIV 1000
NODE 1 0 0 -4.00         ; 3 7 ==  ; 5 14 ==  ; 7 21 ==
     2 0 0 -4.00+9.80 MZ ; 4 7 ==  ; 6 14 ==  ; 8 21 ==
$
BEAM (101 104 1) (1 2) (2 2) KR XX NCS 1 DIV 30 NP (1 1)
END

HEAD
LC 1 TYPE NONE
  NODE 1,3,5 PY  100
  NODE 1,3,5 PZ 1000
  NODE 7     PY   30
  NODE 7     PZ 1000
END

!#!Info  Example:       mantlefriction
!#!Info  Keyword:       pile; bedding; mantlefriction
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
!#!Info  Date:          09.04.2011


$ see also hase.dat\...\hase21.dat - hase23.dat piles in halfspace !

$ english file name: mantlefriction.dat
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD EXAMPLE Effect of skin friction
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
UNIT 0  $ Units in m
CONC 1 C  25  $ C25/30
STEE 2 S 500
SCIT 1 MNO 1 D 1[m]
$
BORE 1 ; BBAX 0.00 10.0 K0 100000.0 M0   0
         BBLA 0.00 10.0 K0 100000.0
BORE 2 ; BBAX 0.00 10.0 K0 100000.0 M0  50
         BBLA 0.00 10.0 K0 100000.0
BORE 3 ; BBAX 0.00 10.0 K0 100000.0 M0 100
         BBLA 0.00 10.0 K0 100000.0
END
$ Determination of pile bedding K0:
$ Stiffness value of line bedding is required
$  1 m cross displacement produces a reaction force of
$    100000 kN/m (Force pro m pile length),
$    this is equivalent to a stiffness of c=K0= 100000 kN/m2  or kN/m/m
$
$ Line related stiffness K0, can be extracted simply out of pile bedding
$ module ks multiplied with the pile diameter D:
$            c=K0=DÂ·ks
$ Thereby under DIN 4014 the bedding module ks can be determined simply out of
$ stiffness modul of soil Es:
$            Ks=Es/D
$ For D>1.0m here D=1.0 m may be set. This results to:
$
$ Pile diameter D <= 1m:   c=K0=Es
$
$ Pile diameter D >  1m:   c=K0=Es*D
$
$ generally this value is set for cross bedding BBLA.
$ For longitudinal bedding BBAX line related stiffness c=K0 is required.
$ It can be extracted in a similar way from the reaction force per m in relation to the settelment.
$
$ same value can be set for BBAX as for BBLA if
$ BBAX is unknown.
PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD EXAMPLE Effect of skin friction
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000
$
NODE 1   0 0  0
     101 0 0 10
NODE 2   4 0  0
     102 4 0 10
NODE 3   8 0  0
     103 8 0 10
BEAM 1 1 101 NCS 1 NP 1 DIV 10
BEAM 2 2 102 NCS 1 NP 2 DIV 10
BEAM 3 3 103 NCS 1 NP 3 DIV 10
END

PROG SOFILOAD urs:5
HEAD
LC 1 TYPE NONE
  NODE 1,2,3 PZ 1000.
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
PROG ASE URS:3
HEAD
LC  1
END

PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD
SYST PROB NONL
LC  5 ; LCC 1
END
END
$ Result:
$ Pile 1  (without skin friction) moves to upper face at 1.150 mm.
$ Pile 2  (with skin friction) moves only             at 0.650 mm.
$ Pile 3  (with skin friction) moves only             at 0.150 mm.
$ .
$ Reasons: In Pile2,is from program an upwards directed skin friction force of 50 kN/m to be set
$          which simulate in linear analysis a displacement of stress-strain-curve of axial
$          Pile bedding already.
$          Only a difference force of 500 kN (1000 - 10m*50kN/m) effects at the Pile
$          and the vertical displacement is correspondingly lesser.

$          The entire skin friction force in pile 3 with 1000 kN is equally as large as the single
$          load above., the lower node 103 does not move (vz=0.0 mm). The upper node due
$          to the elastic normal force moves a little.



$ see also hase.dat\...\hase21.dat - hase23.dat piles in halfspace !


$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?

!#!Info  Example:       SINGLE PILE
!#!Info  Keyword:       pile
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$
$

$ english file name: single_pile.dat
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X'
UNIT 0  $ Units in m
CONC 1 C 16   $ C16/20
STEE 2 S 500
SCIT 1 MNO 1 D 1[m]
$
BORE 1 ; BBAX 0.00 9.80 K0 100000.0  $ CONSTANT BEDDING
         BBLA 0.00 9.80 K0 100000.0
BORE 2 ; BBAX 0.00 9.80 K1 100000.0  $ ROOT-PARABEL
         BBLA 0.00 9.80 K1 100000.0
BORE 3 ; BBAX 0.00 9.80 K2 100000.0  $ LINEAR DISTRIBUTION
         BBLA 0.00 9.80 K2 100000.0
BORE 4 ; BBAX 0.00 9.80 K3 100000.0  $ QUADRILITERAL DISTRIBUTION
         BBLA 0.00 9.80 K3 100000.0
END
$ Determination of pile bedding K0:
$ Stiffness value of line bedding is required
$  1 m cross displacement produces a reaction force of
$    100000 kN/m (Force pro m pile length),
$    this is equivalent to a stiffness of c=K0= 100000 kN/m2  or kN/m/m
$
$ Line related stiffness K0, can be extracted simply out of pile bedding
$ module ks multiplied with the pile diameter D:
$            c=K0=DÂ·ks
$ Thereby under DIN 4014 the bedding module ks can be determined simply out of
$ stiffness modul of soil Es:
$            Ks=Es/D
$ For D>1.0m here D=1.0 m may be set. This results to:
$
$ Pile diameter D <= 1m:   c=K0=Es
$
$ Pile diameter D >  1m:   c=K0=Es*D
$
$ generally this value is set for cross bedding BBLA.
$ For longitudinal bedding BBAX line related stiffness c=K0 is required.
$ It can be extracted in a similar way from the reaction force per m in relation to the settelment.
$
$ same value can be set for BBAX as for BBLA if
$ BBAX is unknown.
PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD SINGLE PILE
$
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 1000
NODE 1 0 0 0.00    ; 3 7 ==  ; 5 14 ==  ; 7 21 ==

!#!Info  Example:       Spring overview
!#!Info  Keyword:       spring; spring worklaw; Isotropic Hardening; Kinematic Hardening
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$

+PROG TEMPLATE urs:1
HEAD

<TEXT>

Spring overview:
================================================================================================

Discussion of the spring work law variants AQUA-SMAT...MTYP PLAS-PISO-PKIN-HYPE:
===================================================================================

The four examples:
        ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_1_plas.dat
        ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_2_piso.dat
        ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_3_pkin.dat
        ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_4_hype.dat
work with the same work law AQUA-SMAT.
The work law for PKIN is the same in the beginning but ends with an increasing end tangent.
Normal plastic work laws should have a horizontal end tangent to clearly define the
final strength (MTYP PLAS+PISO+HYPE).
Please compare the URSULA-ASE-PLOTs and see additional remarks in the AQUA manual.

After a first plastification and unloading to sigma=0 for
PLAS+PISO+PKIN (except HYPE) a first remaining deformation is generated (damage).

PLAS Starting from the unloading point sigma=0 the work law follows the negative path.
     The negative path of the work law is shifted to this point.
     The postive and negative path store a separate hardening.
     This is done for PLAS with the justification that a damage in one direction partly
     destroys the damage in the other direction.

PISO Isotropic Hardening:
     Only one hardening is stored for both sides.
     So from sigma=0 PISO goes down up to the maximum reached strength of the first loading path.
     Then the common hardening is increased on deformations in the negative path.

PKIN Kinematic Hardening:
     For this the work law is slightly changed.
     For PKIN usually an increasing end-tangent is necessary.
     Usually the first linear part of the work law is important.
     It defines FY and the length of the linear unloading part.
     But PKIN also works on curved work laws without first linear part.
     Then the first yielding point FY is 0.0 - see spring_law_3_pkin_curve.dat

HYPE After plastification, on unloading HYPE goes back the same path as for loading
     (hyperelastic).

For multiple cyclic loading with increasing load factor PKIN shows the typical
kinematic hardening springforce-springdisplacement curve.

In the AQUA manual SMAT the curves are better shown with markers.

================================================================================================

GAP:
========

There are two possibilities:

- SFLA+GAP: The worklaw is defined without GAP.
                                                                                                        In SOFIMSHA-SPRI a GAP is added.
- GAP_in\SFLA: The GAP is directly defined in the work law.


For PLAS and PISO material types the first input with SFLA+GAP should be used.
The program stores a new GAP zero point if necessary. For PKIN no GAP is possible.
Example file: ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_1_plas_gap.dat

Only for HYPE material type also the second possibility with the GAP defined in the work law
can also be used.

The effect of a GAP is shown in the URSULA-ASE-PLOT.
================================================================================================

CRAC:
========

The work laws AQUA-SMAT...MTYP PLAS-PISO-HYPE
can be combined with SOFIMSHA-SPRI...CRAC.
An advantage of this (compared to a definition in the work law) is
that for SMAT+SPRI...CRAC the crack opening must be closed completely for further compression.
For this a separate damage parameter is stored to remember the deformation when the CRAC occured.
This better represents reality than the platic behavior of a work law.

Example file:
        ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_1_plas_crac.dat      -> URSULA-ASE-PLOT Graphik.
================================================================================================

YIEL:
========

It is not very senseful but the work laws AQUA-SMAT...MTYP PLAS-PISO-HYPE
can also be combined with SOFIMSHA-FEDE...YIEL, e.g. to better define
separate force limits for different springs.
================================================================================================
================================================================================================

Smeared line couplings:
===================================

Using spring work laws for line and area couplings,
the influence of the SOFIMSHA-FEDE-AR reference area is very important!
The width of a line coupling is input in SOFIMSHA-SPRI-AR.
To check the reference areas you can use a SOFIMSHA Export.

Example file:
        ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_smeared_line.dat
================================================================================================
================================================================================================

Finally a file ase.dat/../spring/spring_law_p_pt_m.dat exists to show multiple
nonlinear effekts in one spring.

================================================================================================
================================================================================================

For usage in dynamics please also look to the folder:
        ase.dat/../dynamics    Example     -spring... .dat
                               nice also   -ase_nstr_pld_pile_crash.dat
                               and         -step_bridge_nonl_lifting_support.dat

Examples to Moving Springs with moving contact points:
        ase.dat/../dynamics    movs_car_collision.dat

        ase.dat/../bridge      movs_incremental_launching_principle.dat

        in CSM:
        csm.dat/../incremental_launching      csm47_nonlinear_test.dat
================================================================================================
================================================================================================

Whether nonlinear effects occured can be seen in a tabel
at the end of a nonlinear ASE analysis:

Statistik nonlinear effekts
==============================
Statistic nonlinear effects of spring elements: no of elem.:       2
                             Number of longitudinal springs:       1
                             Number of torsional    springs:       1
        No. of longitudinal springs with activated      gap:       -
        No. of longitudinal springs                 cracked:       -
        No. of longitudinal springs                yielding:       -
         " in the nonlinear part of the stress strain curve:       -
        " in the nonlinear part of the spring worklaw curve:       1

JÃ¼rgen Bellmann SOFiSTiK AG 5.9.2013
================================================================================================


</TEXT>

    $ mm     kN
  -560.0 -500.0 $ must be defined long enough - and NOT horizontally !
  -200.0 -350.0
   -20.0 -200.0
     0.0    0.0
    20.0  200.0
   200.0  350.0
   560.0  500.0 $ must be defined lond enough - and NOT horizontally !

   $ Last part must NOT be horizontally because kinematic hardening only senseful with infinite tangent >0
   $ Last tangent is used for unloading part - cyclic loading !

  -200.0   '-U' $ for performance levels
   -20.0   '-S'
     0.0   '0'
    20.0   'S'
   200.0   'U'
SVAL 1 A 0.1 IY 1 IZ 1 MNO 1

!#!Info  Example:       stress strain curves for springs
!#!Info  Keyword:       Spring; stress strain curve
!#!Info  Program:       ASE
$

$ see also ase.dat\english\dynamics\spring ...

$-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA  urs:1 $ Material
$-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
HEAD Material
NORM 'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
ECHO MAT FULL
MATE 1 E 1E7 $ to get displacement controlled loading

SMAT                  NO 104 MTYP PKIN
SFLA   U      F    S  NO=104 TYPE=P $ axial spring
    $ mm     kN
     -600.0 -400.0        $ must be defined long enough - and NOT horizontally !
     -200.0 -300.0
     -120.0 -250.0    SPL
      -60.0 -150.0    SPL
        0.0    0.0
       60.0  150.0    SPL
      120.0  250.0    SPL
      200.0  300.0
      600.0  400.0        $ must be defined lond enough - and NOT horizontally !

   $ Last part must NOT be horizontally because kinematic hardening only senseful with infinite tangent >0
   $ Last tangent is used for unloading part - cyclic loading !

  -200.0   '-U' $ for performance levels
   -20.0   '-S'
     0.0   '0'
    20.0   'S'
   200.0   'U'

SVAL 1 A 0.1 IY 1 IZ 1 MNO 1
END

<TEXT> with a little wave to demonstrate the streching of the worklaw:
  -600.0 -400.0        $ must be defined long enough - and NOT horizontally !
  -200.0 -300.0
  -120.0 -250.0    SPL
   -80.0 -190.0    SPL
   -40.0 -130.0    SPL
     0.0    0.0
    40.0  130.0    SPL
    80.0  190.0    SPL
   120.0  250.0    SPL
   200.0  300.0
   600.0  400.0        $ must be defined lond enough - and NOT horizontally !
</TEXT>

$ +PROG ASE urs:8
HEAD Kinematic Hardening
ECHO FULL NO  ; ECHO SPRI FULL

sto#lf  0
sto#f1  0.0
sto#f2  230 ; let#nstep 25
#define step
  let#df (#f2-#f1)/#nstep
  loop#i0 #nstep
    let#f1 #f1+#df
    sto#lf #lf+1  ; SYST PROB NONL PLC #lf-1 ; LC #lf FACT #f1+0.001 ; LCC 901 ; END
  endloop
#enddef
#include step
sto#f2 -230 ; let#nstep 40
#include step
sto#f2  230 ; let#nstep 40
#include step
sto#f2  170 ; let#nstep 10
#include step
sto#f2  450 ; let#nstep 20  $ to stretch plot in y direction (looks nicer)
#include step

$ +PROG ASE urs:5
HEAD Plot after analysis
$ PLOT LC 1 TO #lf NO 1001 DIRE V TYPE LCNO

  PLOT LC 1 TO #lf NO 1001 DIRE NV
END

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation

HEAD Verschiedene Arbeitslinien fÃ¼r Federn
$ Head Different stress strain curves for springs

CONC 1 C  30
STEE 2 S 500
STEE 101 S 500
SREC NO 10 H .6[m] B .4[m]
$ FEDERKENNLINIEN   $ Spring Characteristic Curves
$ Eine Feder-Arbeitslinie kann gleichzeitig eine Senkfeder- und
$ eine zugehÃ¶rige Querfeder-Kennlinie haben:
$ A spring characteristic curve can have simultaneously an
$ axial spring characteristic curve and a relevant lateral
$ spring characteristic curve:
SFLA   U      F  NO=101 TYPE=P $ Senkfeder $ axial spring
    $ mm     kN
   -10.0 -100.0
    -3.0 -150.0
    -2.0 -140.0
    -1.0 -100.0
     0.0    0.0
     1.0  100.0
     2.0  150.0
     3.0  175.0
     4.0  155.0
     5.0   20.0
    10.0   10.0
SFLA   U      F  NO=101 TYPE=PT $ Querfederanteil der Senkfeder  $ lateral spring part of the axial spring
    $ mm     kN                $ wird aber evtl. noch durch die $ is limited, however, with the
     0.0    0.0                $ Reibung FEDE...MUE begrenzt !  $ friction SPRI...MUE !
     1.0   80.0                $
     3.0  140.0                $ Eine Querfeder hat immer eine     $ A lateral spring has always a
    10.0  100.0                $ positive Verschiebung (Vektor) !  $ positive displacement (vector) !
$ Eine Drehfederarbeitlinie erfordert aber immer eine eigene
$ Arbeitsliniennummer, hier 102.
$ A rotational spring characteristic curve requests always its own
$ charactersitic curve number, here 102
SFLA   U      F  NO=102 TYPE=M  $ Drehfeder  $ rotational spring
  $ mrad    kNm
   -10.0 -10.0
    -4.0 -10.0
    -3.0  -9.5
    -2.0  -8.5
    -1.0  -6.5
     0.0   0.0
     1.0   6.5
     2.0   8.5
     3.0   9.5
     4.0  10.0
    10.0  10.0
$ Die Arbeitslinien werden bei "echo quer" Ã¼ber Ursula geplottet.
$ The characteristic curves are plotted with "echo sect" via Ursula.
END

!#!Info  Example:       Timber slab
!#!Info  Keyword:       timber; layer
!#!Info  Program:       ASE

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Timber_slab
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
echo mat yes ; echo pict no
NORM 'DIN' 'en199x-200x'
TIMB NO OAL OAF   EP  E90    G G90    QH  QH90  GAM
      5  90  90 8000  300  900   5  0.05  0.30  6.0   $ stiff in x   top layer
      4   0  90 8000  300  900   5  0.05  0.30  6.0   $ stiff in  y
      3  90  90 8000  300  900   5  0.05  0.30  6.0
      2   0  90 8000  300  900   5  0.05  0.30  6.0   $ stiff in  y
      1  90  90 8000  300  900   5  0.05  0.30  6.0   $ stiff in x   bottom layer
sto#thick 40.0 30.0 40.0 30.0 40.0  $ mm slab thickness : thick(0:4) is an array with 5 elements
                                    $ see-> YOUTUBE https://youtu.be/naWzZJYTCpI   Teddy 3 Arrays and more

$ The soft rolling modulus is input very low here to trigger a soft connection between the layers
$ and to better see the effect that the timber boards shift among each other

END
<TEXT> BRIC-HOLZ relation
For BRIC the following relations are used:

EP  E in fiber direction
E90 transverse (soft)
G       shear from fiber direction to transverse   direction (membrane shear nxy and torsion mxy)
G90     slab shear from transverse direction to transverse direction (soft rolling modulus) (Rollschubmodul)
QH      mue effect from fiber direction to transverse (minor effect)
QH90    mue effect from transverse to transverse (minor effect)

 Dehnungs-Spannungsmatrix BRIC Holz:

| eps-x |   |     1/E90 -QH90/E90   -QH/EP  0  0  0 |   | sig-x |
| eps-y |   | -QH90/E90     1/E90   -QH/EP  0  0  0 |   | sig-y |
| eps-z | = |   -QH/EP    -QH/EP      1/EP  0  0  0 | * | sig-z | = z=fiber direction
| gam-xy|   |     0         0         0   G90  0  0 |   | tau-xy|
| gam-yz|   |     0         0         0     0  G  0 |   | tau-yz|
| gam-zx|   |     0         0         0     0  0  G |   | tau-zx|

For OAL=OAF=0 the strong fiber with E2 points into global Z direction!


For OAL=0  and OAF=90 the strong fiber points into global Y direction!
For OAL=90 and OAF=90 the strong fiber points into global X direction!
</TEXT>

+prog sofimshc urs:2
HEAD Timber_slab
echo geom,node,quad,bric,boun no
UNIT 5 ; SYST SPAC GDIV 10000 GDIR NEGZ
sto#lx 3.00    $ m length
sto#b  1.50    $ m width
sto#dx 0.08    $ m support distance

CTRL MESH 1 ; CTRL HMIN 0.12
SPT NO X     Y
     1 0     0       $ 1. edge node
     2 0     #b      $ 2. edge node
     3 #lx   0       $ 3. edge node
     4 #lx   #b      $ 4. edge node
SLN 1  1 2 ; SLNS DRZ -1 CA 1E5 CL 1
SLN 3  3 4 ; SLNS DRZ -1 CA 1E5 CL 1
SLN 2  1 3
SLN 4  2 4
SPT NO X     Y
    11 0+#dx     0+#dx       $ support
    12 0+#dx     #b-#dx      $ support
    13 #lx-#dx   0+#dx       $ support
    14 #lx-#dx   #b-#dx      $ support
SLN 11  11 12 ; SLNS DRZ -1 CA 1E5 CL 1
SLN 13  13 14 ; SLNS DRZ -1 CA 1E5 CL 1
$
SAR 1 T 0[mm] GRP 91 MNO 0 MCTL REGM  ; SARB OUT 1,2,3,4
END

$ Instead of SOFIMSHC you can also use a SOFIPLUS-mesh!
$ Just run SOFIMSHA after the SOFIPLUS export.

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:3
HEAD
echo node,quad,bric,boun no
CTRL NODE 50000 ; CTRL GTOL 0.001 $ 20 mm tolerance for nodes
syst rest ; ctrl rest 2
$
sto#totalthick 0
loop#i0 thick     $  loop runs for all elements of thick
  GRP 1+#i0 TITL 'bric layer'
  BRIC prop MNO 1+#i0
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 91+#i0 DNO - DZ #thick(#i0)[mm] PROP x1  $ Extrusion quad to bric
  GRP 92+#i0
  quad prop MNO 0 t 0[mm]
  TRAN QUAD INC GRP FROM 91+#i0 DNO - DZ #thick(#i0)[mm] $ copies next quad plane for next bric or loading
  sto#totalthick #totalthick+#thick(#i0)
endloop
prt#totalthick
END

+prog SOFILOAD urs:4
head
lc 901 TITL 'load'
  area ref qgrp proj ZZ wide 1[mm] type PG P1 12.0    x1 900[mm] y1 350[mm] z1 #totalthick[mm]     x2 dxy 1800[mm] 800[mm]
end

+prog ase urs:6
head
grp - ; grp (91 99 1) off
lc 1 dlz 1.00 TITL 'G+load'
  LCC 901
end

!#!Info  Example:       Timber slab
!#!Info  Keyword:       timber; layer
!#!Info  Program:       ASE

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Concrete on Timber_slab
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ECHO MAT full
NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1 C   30
STEE 2 S  500
TIMB NO OAL     EP E90   G G90   QH GAM
     11   0  12500 420 780  80 0.05 4.8
FLAY NO 101 T 140[mm] MNO  1 BETA  0 $ concrete
            T  30[mm] MNO 11 BETA  0 $ timber
            T  30[mm] MNO 11 BETA 90 $ material 11 with fiber direction 90 degree
            T  30[mm] MNO 11 BETA  0
            T  30[mm] MNO 11 BETA 90
            T  30[mm] MNO 11 BETA  0
$ mittleres gamma = (140mm*25 + 150mm*4.8) / 290mm = 14.55 [kN/m3]
let#1 (140*25+150*4.8)/290
prt#1
END

+prog sofimsha urs:2
HEAD Concrete on Timber_slab
SYST SPAC GDIV 10000
#define l=5.00    $ m length
#define h=4.00    $ m height
NODE NO  X       Y
    1   0       0
    2   0     $(h)[m]
    3 $(l)[m] $(h)[m]
    4 $(l)[m]   0
QUAD - 1 2 3 4 MNO 101 T 290[mm] M 12 N 20
BOUN 1 TITL R1 ; BOUN 1 4 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
BOUN 2 TITL R2 ; BOUN 2 3 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
BOUN 3 TITL R3 ; BOUN 1 2 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
BOUN 4 TITL R4 ; BOUN 4 3 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
                 BOUN 4 3 FIT TYPE cx,cy CA 0.1
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+prog ase urs:3
HEAD
$ Comments see example timber_quad_layer.dat
CTRL ILAY 20000  $ Stores inner layer stresses in LC +20000... (surface of an inner layer)
LC 1 FACD 1.0 titl 'G_1'
END

$ Open Animator, loadcase 1 and double klick a quad element

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?



!#!Info  Example:       Timber slab
!#!Info  Keyword:       timber; layer
!#!Info  Program:       ASE

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Timber_slab
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ECHO MAT full
NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
TIMB NO OAL     EP E90   G G90   QH GAM
     11   0  11900 200 390  50 0.00 4.8 $ !! values scaled in a way that stiffness acc. www.klhdesigner.at is nearly reached !!
                                        $ see also Q8x8 stiffness of GRP 101 in timber_8x8_matrix.dat
FLAY NO 101 T 30[mm] 11   0 TITL 'KLH 5s 150 TT slab plates'
            T 30[mm] 11  90 $ material 11 with fiber direction 90 degree
            T 30[mm] 11   0
            T 30[mm] 11  90 $ see  www.klhdesigner.at
            T 30[mm] 11   0

$ Example with concrete desk see timber_concrete_layer.dat
END

+prog sofimsha urs:2
HEAD Timber_slab
page UNII 0
SYST SPAC GDIV 10000
#define l=3.00    $ m length
#define h=3.00    $ m height
NODE NO  X       Y
    1   0       0
    2   0     $(h)[m]
    3 $(l)[m] $(h)[m]
    4 $(l)[m]   0
QUAD - 1 2 3 4 MNO 101 T 150[mm] M 12 N 20
BOUN 1 TITL R1 ; BOUN 1 4 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
BOUN 2 TITL R2 ; BOUN 2 3 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
BOUN 3 TITL R3 ; BOUN 1 2 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
BOUN 4 TITL R4 ; BOUN 4 3 FIT TYPE cz CA 1E5
                 BOUN 4 3 FIT TYPE cx,cy CA 0.1
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+prog ase urs:3
HEAD
<TEXT> On AQUA input:
TIMB NO OAL     EP E90   G G90   QH GAM
     11   0  12500 420 780  80 0.05 4.8

remarks:
EP  E in fiber direction
E90 transverse (soft)
G       shear from fiber direction to transverse direction (membrane shear nxy and torsion mxy)
FGXZ*G  slab shear xz from fiber direction to transverse z-direction (plate shear) FGXZ=control value in ASE
G90     slab shear yz from transverse direction to transverse direction (soft rolling modulus) (Rollschubmodul)

The quad membrane and bending stiffness use EP,E90,G,QH (first direction is the fiber direction)
   The transverse shear effect uses mue=QH (=poisson ration fiber-direction to transverse-direction)
   The quad membrane shear and the torsional bending stiffness use G
   Attention: using TIMB/HOLZ in AQUA, the QH poisson ratio is used ! QH90 from AQUA-TIMB/HOLZ is not used!

The slab shear stiffness uses FGXZ*G for a shear fiber-transverse (hard G modulus)
   and G90 for a shear transverse-transverse (soft rolling modulus) (Rollschubmodul)
   FGXZ*G and G90 can be increased or decreased due to glue effects

Scaling input values:
- with E, E90 and QH(mue) the main bending and normal components mxx,myy,nxx,nyy are well represented.
- with G you control mainly mxy+nxy,  vx+vy are also effected but can be adjusted with G90 and FGXZ.

For special use you can use the input of the 8x8 matrix with Q8x8, see timber_8x8_matrix
</TEXT>

echo mat full
CTRL FGXZ 0.85  $ extra factor for the slab shear in fiber direction (from fiber to z).
                $ but effect is small if G90 is small as weak layers dominate for shear!
                $ Please notice comments in legend of output table MLAY stiffness
CTRL ILAY 20000  $ Stores inner layer stresses in LC +20000... (surface of an inner layer)

LC 1  FACD 8.0  titl 'G_1*8'
END

+PROG RESULTS urs:4
HEAD
DIAG X "quad__la.sigx" Y "quad__la.__thick"  GDEF "quad__la.nr"
FLT 1 NAME "quad__la.nr" 127 $ 127= Element no.    11= Material no.
LC   NO 1  XI ALL
QUAD TYPE SXLA STYP ELEM REPR DIAG
END

$ Open Animator, loadcase 1 and double klick a quad element

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?

// ====================================================================================
//
// Worked example 3 - LTB. Page 3-54.
// PP 1990:2007. Structural Eurocodes.
// Extracts from the Structural Eurocodes for students of structural design
// Second edition, 2007. ISBN 978-0-580-68985-7
//
// Modeling: Program SOFiMSHA
// Analysis: Program ASE
//     - linear elastic
// Design: Program BDK
//     - in-plane buckling
//
// ==================================================================================

!#!Chapter Sytem
+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Material and Cross-section definition
NORM EN 199X-200X ! COUN 44 $ coun 44  Great Britain
$
STEE 1  S 275
$
SECT  1 MNO 1
PROF 1 TYPE 'UB' Z1 457 Z2 152 Z3 74 MNO 1
END

+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:7
HEAD Structural system
ECHO FULL NO
SYST 3D
CTRL MESH 1
CTRL HMIN 1.0
SPT    1 X 0.0  Y 0.0 Z 0.0 FIX PPMX
SPT    2 X 8.0  Y 0.0 Z 0.0 FIX XPMX
SLN NO 1 NPA 1 NPE 2 SNO 1 SDIV -8
END

!#!Chapter Loads
+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD Loading
ECHO FULL NO
LC  1  TYPE (D)
BEPL 1 TYPE MYY P -150 A 0.0
BEPL 8 TYPE MYY P  150 A 1.0
END

!#!Chapter Analysis
+PROG ASE urs:4
HEAD Linear analysis
CTRL OPT SOLV
ECHO FULL NO
LC 1
END

-PROG AQB urs:5
HEAD Design elastic - elastic + c/t
ECHO STRE extr
ECHO c2t extr             $ output for c/t-check  for all
BEAM SLN 1
LC 1
COMB GMAX LCST 901
STRE e f                  $ stresses, design case 901, with safety factor
END

!#!Chapter Buckling Checks
+PROG BDK urs:10
HEAD Check LTB
LC 1
CVA CB 0 CY fix CZ fix DX fix DY 0 DZ 0
CVE CB 0 CY fix CZ fix DX fix DY 0 DZ 0
CTRL OPT EN SCL 1  LCST 951
MEMB SLN 1
END

+PROG TEMPLATE urs:6
HEAD Summary

! Utilisation Level
@KEY 'DSLN_DE0' 951
sto#util (@27)          ! utilisation level (10) buckling
!TXB Utilisation Level #(#util,5.3)

  <text>
  Worked example 3 - LTB. Page 3-54.
  PP 1990:2007. Structural Eurocodes.
  Extracts from the Structural Eurocodes for students of structural design
  Second edition, 2007. ISBN 978-0-580-68985-7

  Result                                                  Reference        SOFiSTiK
  Utilisation Level acc. to EN 1993-1-1, Eq. 6.54         <b>1.061</b>            <b>#(#util,5.3)</b> (m-y)

  Deviation reasons:
  - in reference example the M-cr is taken from approximate formula, whereas SOFiSTiK exact - thus more precise.

  Notes:
  - M-cr according to exact formula of reference example is equal 154.17 kNm (SOFiSTiK - 154.06).

  Conclusion: SOFiSTiK results are reliable.
  </text>

END

!#!Info Example:    Design: member in major axis bending and axial compression
!#!Info Program:    BDK
!#!Info Keywords:   Stability, Buckling, Lateral Torsional Buckling

// ====================================================================================
//
// FassadenstÃ¼tze mit Biegebeanspruchung. Page 8-41.
// Schneider: Bautabellen fÃ¼r Ingenieure, 21. Auflage 2014,
// Bundesanzeiger Verlag. ISBN 978-8462-0304-0
//
// Modeling: Program SOFiMSHC
// Analysis: Program ASE
//     - linear elastic
//     - warping torsion
//     - buckling eigenvalues
// Design: Program BDK
//     - lateral torsional buckling
//     - interaction factors
//
// ==================================================================================

!#!Chapter System
+PROG AQUA urs:22
HEAD Cross section values
NORM 'DIN' 'en199x-200x'
STEE  1 S   235
SECT  1 MNO 1  ; PROF TYP HEA 200
$$ ROTATIONAL STIFFNESS FOR HALF BEAM
$STO#CMZ 4*21E6*1.336E-5/4.000    $ = 4EI/L
$STO#CMT 8.1E5*2.0526E-07/4.000   $ = GIt/L
END

  QUAD TYPE EYL UNIT -1003.273 SCHH 0.30 STYP ELEM FILL NO REPR DVEC AVER NO nd 2

  MOVE X DEL DTYP TEXT ; MOVE X 1 24 UNIT PR SCHH .5 C 1001 DTYP TEXT
  TEXT  main strain bottom - nonlinear ASE : much higher for 45 degree reinforcement
          QUAD TYPE EIL UNIT -1003.273 SCHH 0.30 STYP ELEM FILL NO REPR DVEC AVER NO nd 2
END

<TEXT> Comments Bellmann
As you see in the nonlinear ASE run, the bottom concrete strain on the right side
with the 45 degree reinforcement is more than double as high as the bottom concrete strain
on the left side with the reinforcement in direction of the span.

In the left part of the span the reinforcement direction is in the load-bearing direction:
    sigmax= 220 N/mm2, strain in reinforcement direction = 0.56 o/oo , in global x = 0.56 o/oo

In the right part the reinforcement direction is below 45 degrees:
    sigmax= 220/225 N/mm2, strain in reinforcement direction = 0.56/0.59 o/oo , in global x = 1.20 o/oo

That is, if you only look at the steel stress for the crack width
the crack width is greatly underestimated.
This is made much better with the new Eurocode prEN_1992-1-1, there the real
strain in span direction is used (addition of (esmx-ecmx)+(esmy-ecmy)).
Therefore, in ASE, by default, this calculation of the crack width is based on the
new Eurocode prEN_1992-1-1 with addition of (esmx-ecmx)+(esmy-ecmy).
 (But this can be switched off with CTRL BETO v9 0, but then old Eurocode is used
  and because of equation EN1992-1-1 7.3.4(4) usually the crack width is too small.
  CTRL BETO v9in ASE has the same meaning as BEMESS-CRISS-SAND,
  The default setting in ASE is 1 = more realistic but without |e2| )

However, in ASE the calculation of the crack width has no influence on stresses or displacements!

In BEMESS you can observe the same effect, switch with CRAC SAND.
</TEXT>

+sys del $(project).$d?

$ +PROG MAXIMA
$ HEAD Standard superpositioning without further input:
$ Then next maxima and the later SLS MAXIMA can be switched off !

+PROG MAXIMA urs:18
HEAD Manual Superposition ULS - Ultimate Limit State
ECHO FULL NO ; ECHO TABS YES
  COMB 1 DESI BASE 2100               $ desi = Superposition for Design LC 2100...
$ Without ACT and LC input MAXIMA combines the load cases automatically in
$ dependence on load TYPE. Please check the used load cases in the MAXIMA output.
$ The following input clearly defines that actions G and Q shall be taken
  ACT G
    $ LC 1 G      without LC input: Maxima takes all loadcases with action type G and G_1 G_2
  ACT Q
    $ LC 2,3,4  Q without LC input: Maxima takes all loadcases with action type Q and Q_A Q_B ....
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QUAD TYPE M     TITL 'ULS_QUAD' FROM -
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QNOD TYPE M     TITL 'ULS_QUAD' FROM -
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QUAD TYPE VX,VY TITL 'ULS_QUAD' FROM -
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QNOD TYPE VX,VY TITL 'ULS_QUAD' FROM -
  ECHO LOAD,FACT YES
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP NODE TYPE PZ    TITL 'ULS_NODE' FROM 4
  ECHO LOAD,FACT NO
  $ from: All nodes are superpositioned, however, a printout is done
  $ only for node 4.
  $ If BEAM elements are available, the next line is necessary:
  $
  $SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE N,MY,VZ TITL 'ULS_BEAM' FROM -
  $SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QUAD TYPE P       TITL 'GZT_QUAD' FROM -
  $ If QUAD beddings are available, the previous line is necessary,
  $ because the bedding stresses are necessary for punching.
END

+PROG BEMESS urs:9
HEAD Definition of reinforcement parameters and minimum reinforcement
$ normal area - inner roms:
GEOM - HA 25[mm] DHA 10[mm] HB 25[mm] DHB 10[mm] $ exposition class XC1
DIRE  0  0
PARA NOG - DU 10[mm] WKU 0.40[mm]        $ class F
$ WKU for crack witdh check acc. table bar diameter
$ If check shall be done for table bar distance, directly the steel stress
$ can be defined with PARA...SSU. For parallel input of
$ WKU and SSU, SSU is used for the check. WKU will always be used for
$ minimum reinforcement check!
$
$ Balcony:
GEOM - HA 40[mm] DHA 10[mm] HB 40[mm] DHB 10[mm] $ exposition class XC4
DIRE 90 90
PARA NOG 3 DU 20[mm] WKU 0.30[mm]        $ class E
$ 20 mm diameter only to get a result in the crack witdh check
$
$ Minimum reinforcement in corners via XMIN-XMAX input (or secondary groups from SOFIMSHA):
$   (for possible nonlinear analysis)

DIRE 0 0
GEOM - HA 25[mm] DHA 10[mm] HB 25[mm] DHB 10[mm] $ exposition class XC1
PARA ASU 377[mm2/m] 377[mm2/m]    XMIN  -   XMAX 1.60 YMIN  -   YMAX 1.60  $ TYP MOD TYPE MOD see manual
PARA ASU 377[mm2/m] 377[mm2/m]    XMIN 8.40 XMAX  -   YMIN  -   YMAX 1.60
$ PARA 'A1' You can also use secondary groups from SOFIMSHA or SOFIPLUS but an
$           Export in SOFIPLUS deletes all results - so PARA XMIN-XMAX ist easier.

PUNC   D 0.30[m] B 0.30[m] RO_V 1.50 $ default single column
PUNC TYPE WALL D 0.24[m]           $ default support wall
$ (All inputs for PUNC are saved in the database and must not be defined
$  anymore in the following BEMESS inputs!
$  But if you make PUNC input in following BEMESS, then input all inclusive these lines ! )
$
$ Please do not make input for the dimensions for punching, if these inputs
$ are done already in the grafical input SOFIPLUS (otherwise they are overwritten)!
$
$ With PUNC CHEC punching is only checked but BEMESS nevertheless takes into account
$ the minimum design moments an single supports.
$ In WINGRAF with INFO-necessary reinforcement the pure bending reinforcement
$ can be plotted!

END

+PROG BEMESS urs:14

$ Here a minimum reinforcement is not considered.

$
         $ ^without input to CTRL LCR, LCR=1 is used = design
         $ if crack design needs more reinforcement, LCR 1 is increased
         $ This can be checked in WINGRAF-"Controlling design" "Origin of max. values"
LC  PERM             $ load cases according to quasi-permament combination SLS
CRAC WK TAB          $ crack width check according to tables
$       alternative:   MREI FFCT 1.0 KC .4 K 1.0 $ minimum reinforcement for bending constraint
$       set only, if the constraint reaches the crack width internal forces and moments!
END

+PROG BEMESS urs:16

HEAD According EN 1992-1-1 : 9.2.1.1

LC 1
$ The robustness reinforcement is always below and only in case of tensile
$ stresses above. Here only the load case 1 is used for that tensile definition.
$ ctrl robu fctm may be input also additionally in a normal BEMESS calculation.
$ Here it is done in a separate run in order to show graphically the areas in
$ which the robustness check leads to an increase of the reinforcement.
$ The robustness reinforcement is inserted above about a length till a quarter
$ of the span.

END

$Determination of the definition of the load case numbers
$========================================================
$Results from MAXIMA:
$
$th : t = thousands place 1... = SLS = serviceability limit state
$                         2... = ULS = ultimate limit state
$     h = hundreds place  .1.. = rare combination               psi-0
$                         .2.. = non-frequent combination       psi-1'
$                         .3.. = frequent combination           psi-1
$                         .4.. = quasi-permanent combination    psi-2
$                         .5.. = accidental combination         psi-2
$                         .9.. = mounting, construction stage
$
$For units place and tens place it is provided:
$th01-..10 Quadforces       mx,my,mxy,vx,vy
$                           ..01=max-mx ..02=min-mx ..03=max-my ...
$..11-..16 Quadforces       nx,ny,nxy
$              -stresses    sigx,sigy,sigxy  for plain strain TALPA
$..18-..19 Beddingforces
$..21-..32 Beamforces       STN,STVY,STVZ,STMT,STMY,STMZ
$..41-..42 Trussforces
$..43-..44 Cableforces
$..45-..48 Springforces     P,M
$..51-..62 Supportforces    PX,PY,PZ,MXX,MYY,MZZ
$..63-..70 Boundaryforces   RPX,RPY,RPZ,RMN
$..71-..82 Displacements    u-x,u-y,u-z,PHIX,PHIY,PHIZ
$..83-..90 Boundaryforces   SRPX,SRPY,SRPZ,SRMN
$
$
$=============================================================
$=============================================================
$
$MAXIMA:
$Further common superpositions in dependence on the system:
$
$ QUAD internal forces and moments
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP quad TYPE M,VX,VY    TITL 'QUAD'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP qnod TYPE M,VX,VY    TITL 'QUAD'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP quad TYPE N          TITL 'QUAD'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP qnod TYPE N          TITL 'QUAD'
$
$ QUAD bedding
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP QUAD TYPE p          TITL 'BEDD'
$
$ STAB internal forces and moments
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP BEAM TYPE VZ,MT,MY   TITL 'BEAM'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP BEAM TYPE N,VY,MZ    TITL 'BEAM'
$
$ NODE support reactions
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP NODE TYPE px,py,mz   TITL 'NODE'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP NODE TYPE pz,mx,my   TITL 'NODE'
$
$ NODE displacments
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP NODE TYPE ux,uy      TITL 'NODE'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP NODE TYPE uz         TITL 'NODE'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP NODE TYPE phix       TITL 'NODE'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP NODE TYPE phiy       TITL 'NODE'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP NODE TYPE phiz       TITL 'NODE'
$
$ BOUN support reactions
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP BOUN TYPE px,py      TITL 'RAND'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP BOUN TYPE pz,m       TITL 'RAND'
$
$ Other elements
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP TRUS TYPE N          TITL 'TRUS'
$
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP CABL TYPE N          TITL 'CABL'
$
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP SPRI TYPE P          TITL 'SPRI'
$  SUPP 1 EXTR mami ETYP SPRI TYPE M          TITL 'SPRI'
$
$=============================================================
$=============================================================

+sys del $(project).$d?

STEE  7    S  '235' $ TMAX  0 $ structural steel for tubes, rolled steel ...
STEE 11    Y '1860A' $ prestessing steel
                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2
                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD Road Bridge as FE-Slab acc. EN 1992-1-1
$ The input of the statical system is - compared with the effort
$ Of the proofs - the least problem.
$ In order to show other ways of the input - in this case the slab is entered with a
$ raster formed elementing in SOFISHA.
$ The advantage of SOFIMSHA is that the node numbers can randomly be given out by the program
$ And only the compulsory points (bearing, edges) need to be defined with fixed numbers.
$ The inner nodes of the meshes are undetermined at first.
$ Tn the case of a different element division the numbering of the edge nodes
$ does not need to be changed!
UNIT 0 $ m fest
SYST SPAC GDIR POSZ GDIV 1000
ECHO FULL NO ; ECHO SYST YES

NODE  8 X 11  -8 0 $ left upper edge of the slab

      2   1   8   6.50 $ Edge of haunch

      4   1   8   2.50 $ Bearing axis 2

      6   1   8  -5.50 $ Bearing axis 4
      7   1   8  -6.50 $ Edge of haunch
TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 8 DNO 100 DX 0.80

TRAN NODE FROM 1 TO 8 DNO 300 DX 0.80+20.0+0.80
let#1 0.20 $ Thickness at cantilever end
let#2 0.40 $ Thickness at cantilever section
let#3 0.80 $ Thick slab area
QUAD N1  N2  N3  N4  M  N T1 T2 T3 T4 MNO=1 MRF=2 POSI=BELO
      1 101 102   2  1  2 #1 #1 #2 #2 $ Cantilever

!#!Kapitel Loading, Prestress
+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD actions and loads
$ actions bridge design
$ All actions should be defined here.
$ This can be done in a separate SOFILOAD run as shown here.
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ECHO ACT Full $ Please check GAMU factors, especially for L_U and L_T (in germany GAMU 1.35)
ACT G_1                                                              TITL 'dead load'
ACT G_2                                                              TITL 'dead load'
ACT P   GAMU 1.00 GAMF 1.00  PSI0 1.00 PSI1 1.00 PSI2 1.00           TITL 'prestress'
ACT C                                                                TITL 'C+S'
ACT ZC  GAMU 1.00 1 SUP PERM PSI0 1.00 PSI1 1.00 PSI2 1.00           TITL '                            life load creep part'
ACT L_T GAMU   -  0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
ACT L_U GAMU   -  0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
ACT L_1 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 1'
ACT L_2 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 2'
ACT L_3 GAMU 1.35 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL overload span 3'
$ The GAMU and PSI factores are taken from the .ini file depending on the design code (-> check)
$ You can also define them nanually here e.g. with:
$ ACT L_T GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.75 PSI1 0.75 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'TS Tandemsystem'
$ ACT L_U GAMU 1.35::1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'UDL basic load'
  $ Superposition with ELLA traffic loading see more\csm31_design_ella.dat
  $ here SUP COND=special case, since L_U is applied in MAXIMA/AQB without inter superposition!
  $ L_1 with multiple UDL over loads in transvers direction needs EXCL, because only one to be taken
ACT SL  GAMU 1.50 0 SUP COND PSI0 0.40 PSI1 0.40 PSI2 0.20 PS1S    - TITL 'loading during construction'
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT FAT GAMU 1.50 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'Fatigue LM3'
ACT SF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'possible settlement'
ACT ZF  GAMU 1.00 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'probable settlement'
  $ Acc. DIN FB 101 - C.2.3 for settlements GAMA=1.00.
ACT W                                                                TITL 'wind transvers'
ACT T   GAMU 0.81 0 SUP EXCL PSI0 0.80 PSI1 0.60 PSI2 0.50 PS1S    - TITL 'temperatur'
  $ In the ULS design you can usually take the temperature forces only with 60 %
  $ because the concrete may crack and will have only 60% stiffness for the temperature effect in ULS.
  $ Hence to simplify, set the ULS-gama-u value by 1.35 to 0.81 (0.81 = 1.35*0.60).
  $ So: safety factor = 1.35 but only with factor 0.6 due to reduced stiffness (60% stiffness)
  $---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACT R   GAMU 1.5  0        SUP COND PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'earthpressure traffic'
ACT B   GAMU 1.35 1 PART G SUP PERM PSI0 1 1 1                              TITL 'construction stage'
$
$ The signs SUP PERM,COND,EXCL are necessary and set itself according to
$ the definition of traffic load cases:
$    SUP EXCL - only one out of available load cases
$    SUP CONC - all of the available load cases, if acting unfavourable
           $ Meaning of PSI-Value:
           $
           $ Fraction :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
           $
           $ Rare    : 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
           $ frequent: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
           $ quasi   : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-all
           $ not     : PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
           $
           $ to  : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
           $ See MAXIMA - theoretical basics
$ G if as generic term effects G the under effects
$ G_1 and G_2 combined! alike L the L_U plus L_T combined!
$ not but Z the ZF and ZS, as no underline follows!
$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END
END

$ For the check of the limit state of the bearing capacity the possible soil movements
$ have to be taken into consideration, however for their determination
$ the 0.6 folded rigidities of state 1 can be disregarded for this check
$ (due to possible transition into state II). According to SOFiSTiK (Dr. Bellmann)
$ the superposition has then to be applied with a load safety coefficient g=1.35.
LC 81 TYPE SF TITL 'Possible Settlement 1+3'
   NODE NO 103,104,105,106  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm] $ corresponds to analysis with 0.6 folded rigidities
LC 82 TYPE SF TITL 'Possible Settlement 2'
   NODE NO 203,204,205,206 TYPE WZZ 1000*0.01*0.60[mm]
$ For checking the limit states of the fitnes of purpose the most probable
$ soil movements should always be applied as constant effects, therefore 1.0 folded,
$ see DIN FB 102 II-2.3.4(110)P  . Here the reduction of 0.4 is not allowed!
$ In the present analysis 1 com is applied as possible settlement and 0.5 cm are applied as probable settlement,
$ each per support axis and in the worst case superposed.
LC 83 TYPE ZF TITL 'Real Settlement 1+3' $
   NODE NO 103,104,105,106  TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]
LC 84 TYPE ZF TITL 'Real Settlement 2'
   NODE NO 203,204,205,206 TYPE WZZ 1000*0.005[mm]

SYSP NOPS MAT   ZV       AZ    LITZ MINR   BETA  MUE ECC  SP     DO
        1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 82[mm] $ csm3_parabel and csm32_slab, 12 wires

$ Max. perm. stress  po,max:

+PROG ASE -E urs:8

PUNC - D 0.45[m] B 0.45[m] RO_V 1.50 $ Voreinstellung Einzel-StÃ¼tzenabmessungen   $ default single column

+PROG BEMESS urs:18
HEAD Design Ultimate Limit State (ULS)
$ Tendon stress increase in ULS design:
$ For bonded tendons now the stress increase in the tendons is taken into account in the
$ ULS design. For this the tendons are smeared over a certain width.
$ The stress increase is limited by the strain in the height of the tendons and
$ by the material parameters. With CTRL SIGZ it can be limited e.g. CTRL SIGZ 180 to 180 N/mm2.
$ The tendon stress increase results in a lower longitudinal reinforcement which
$ can be checked in tke listing.
$ With  CTRL SIGZ 0 the feature can be switched off totally.
ECHO PUNC extr $ -> tendons at the punching perimeters
CTRL LCR 11 $ number of the reinforcement distribution
            $ Because the reinforcement distribution number 1 is reserved for
            $ the final result, the start is here with number 11!
LC   DESI   $ DESI = design = ultimate limit state
LC 4098 'perm'      $ Permanent state traffic opening (ASE LC necessary for exact analysis of the tendon stress)
CTRL RO_V 0.5 $ Up to this reinforcement ratio the program attempts not to use
              $ any shear reinforcement. The shear check increases possibly
              $ the bending reinforcement up to that value.
              $ It is possible to modify the value for the punching area.:
END
$ First calculate the robustness check, the crack checks and the steel range
$ check (fatigue) for increase of the reinforcement, then the following
$ stress checks are successful (NSTR CHKC...)!

+PROG BEMESS urs:19
HEAD Crack control check at serviceability limit State frequent
CTRL LCRI 11 LCR 12 $ number of the reinforcement distribution read from 11, write to 12
CTRL SLS RMOD SUPE
LC FREQ             $ Load cases according to frequent combinations SLS
                    $ Tabelle 4.118 > depending on structure: frequent combination!
LC 4098 'PERM'      $ Permanent state traffic opening (ASE LC necessary for exact analysis of the tendon stress)
                    $ In case the loadcases include pk-inf and pk-sup (here in LC FREQ), please notice in the tendon stresses:
                    $ The storage of the max. tendon stress for WINGRAF is done without pk-sup in the static determined part NP0, that means:
                    $       The permanent tendon stress from LC 4000 PERM does not include a change due to
                    $       pk-inf/pk-sup, only the little stress part from traffic includes a pk-inf/pk-sup part!
$ Minimum reinforcement see also bemess2.dat and bemess6_design.dat:
MREI FFCT 1.0 KC .4 K 1.0 $ minimum reinforcement for bending constraint
$       Alternative:    MREI FFCT 0.5 KC 1.0 - for centric constraint hydration heath
$ ^ use only, if the constraint loading reaches the crack internal forces and moments!
CRAC WK TAB         $ crack width check acc. to DIN-FB 4.4.2.3.   Tabelle (4.120)  Seite 176
                    $ see input PARA
$ The input   CRAC WK 0.20[mm] would do a direct calculation of the crack width
$ acc. to DIN-FB 4.4.2.4..  We recommend to use the check with the table 4.120/4.121
$ with CRAC WK TAB.   J. Bellmann
END

+PROG BEMESS urs:22
HEAD Fatigue verification for steel and concrete
$ For not prestressed bridges without welded reinforcement
$ a sufficient resistance agains fatigue can be assumed, if
$ under frequent effects the stress range remains bottom 70 mPa.
$ See EN 1992-1-1 6.8.6(1)
$ This could be succeeded with an entry
$     dehn sigs 70 sigt 70.
$ For this check load model LM 3 has to be applied.
$ In this case it was superposed in load case 1501-1510
$ together with the constant loads.
$
$ The fatigue design for concrete under pressure is done with sigma_c,perm
$ according EN 1992-2 NN.3.2 (NN.112)
$ It is requested with 'LC 'perm' for the permanent loadcase and an input
$   for the correction factors as product lambda_c1*lambda_c2*lambda_c3*lambda_c4
$   in NSTR ... LC14
$      (for lambda-c,1 value 0.85 is applicable in most cases,
$       for lambda-c,2,3,4 1.0, so together LC14 0.85 )
$ The maximum concrete pressure can be checked in WINGRAF with:
$   Area elements-dimensioning stresses-maximum concrete pressure
$ Singularity places should be interpretated by the engineers.
CTRL LCRI 12 LCR 13 $ Number of the reinforcement distribution read/write
CTRL SLS RMOD SUPE  $ Requesting a working load check
LC (1501 1510 1)    $ Load cases fatigue
LC 4098 'perm'      $ Permanent state traffic opening (ASE LC necessary for exact analysis of the tendon stress)
$ Coefficients see EN 1992-1-1:   6.8.4 and for road bridges
$                  EN 1992-2 NN.3.2 Tabelle NN.3
$   (old german DIN-Fachbericht 102 4.3.7.7 (101) table 4.116 ff)
NSTR SIGS 175 SIGT 0.454*175 SIGP 185                          $$
             LS_U 1.18 LS_L 1.44 LS_V 1.18 LS_P 1.30 LC14 0.85 $$
             FACU 1.40 FACL 1.40 FACV 1.40 FACP 1.40 CHKR 0.8
$ The increasing factors FACU... have to be used only for the axle load
$ of the load model 3 and not for g+p... .
$ Because g+p balance for prestressed bridge, the total internal force
$ from MAXIMA is multiplied here by the increase factors!
$ For more detailed checks the factors have to be considered already in MAXIMA
$ and used than in BEMESS with 1.00.
$ This happens in a design via CSM DSI - see csm32_slab_design.dat
$
$ Fatigue shear reinforcement is reduced onto 0.454*SIGS due to small
$ diameter of mandrel.
$ CHKR 0.8: It is recommended to limit the maximum steel stress (CHKR 0.8) additionally
$ to the stress amplitude, because the load cases have possibly fatigue of another
$ combination of internal forces and moments and full utilize the normally hardly
$ used small reinforcement.
$
$    For continuous systems with intermediate support we have to apply:
$            FACU 1.75 FACL 1.40 FACV 1.75 FACP 1.40
$
$ Determination of the coefficients also see page 13-27 in:
$   Examples for dimensioning according to DIN 1045-1
$   Volume 2: Ingenieurbau - engineering
$   Deutscher Beton- und Bautechnik-Verein E.V. - German concrete and building techniques Association
$   Verlag Ernst & Sohn   ISBN 3-433-02835-4
END

!#!Kapitel Robustness
+PROG BEMESS URS:65
HEAD Robustness Reinforcement for Saving of a Ductile Member Behaviour
head - refer to EN 1992-1-1  9.2.1.1(1)
CTRL SLS RMOD SUPE
CTRL LCRI 13 LCR 14 $ $ Number of the reinforcement distribution read from 13, write to 14
$
LC 2101,2156   $ load cases max-mx and min-PZ from ULS superposition:
MREI ROBU fctk $ robustness reinforcement with fctk,0.05 !!!!
$ Remark: Also the minimum reinforcement was activated here in the 2nd design calculation.
$         That is larger than the robustness reinforcement in the 1st layer. The 1st layer
$         is therefore not increased opposite the LCR 13.
$         The 2nd layer (main direction of effective span) has no minimum reinforcement
$         and is increased now due to the robustness reinforcement.
          $ The robutsness reinforcement is always applied at the bottom of a section.
          $ On top only in case of appearing tensile stresses.
          $ To make it easier we only anlayze load case 2101
          $ to determine tensiles.
          $ (LF 1 is not enough, as for missing prestresses to much reinforcement will be generated
          $  in the field middle)
          $ steu robu fctm can also be entered for a normal BEMESS-run -
          $ in this case we requeste to do it in a seperate run
          $ to be able to recognize graphical areas, where
          $ the robustness check requires an increase of the reinforcement.
          $ The robustness reinforcement on the top has to be placed over a length of
          $ up to a quarter of the span length.
END

HEAD Materiel
