NORM 'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1 C 35 FEQR 0.653 FEQT 0.408 $  values must be input new !
$--     Input of a stress strain curve at SLS
$--     It is not necessary to input the worklaw by hand but then you have more control
$--     Without explicit input of the worklaw, the E-modulus jumps at the zero point = not nice
SSLA SERV 1.0  $  First ARBL set defines type of stress strain curve
               $  Security 1.0 - All securities are contained in the following table!
$ Value accroding to type of stress strain curve sets an associated safety factor
SSLA    EPS     SIG     TYPE
       25.00    0.624          $ tensile zone
        3.50    0.998          $ values see below
        0.30    0.998
        0.07    3.21
        0       0               $-------------
       -2.25   -43.0    SPL     $ eps1 from table 3.1
       -3.5    -30.0            $  compressive zone

STEE 2 S 500
END
<TEXT> Nach dafstb-richtlinie-stahlfaserbeton_2021.pdf :
Querschnittsbemessung Bild R.2
z.B. Leistungsklasse L1 Tabelle R.3: z.B. Zeile 9 :
L1=2.4 fct0,L1 = 0.96 N/mm2 ; fctRL1 = 0.96 N/mm2 (mit kappaf=kappaG = 1.0)
max. sigma fctdL1 = alphac*fctRL1 / gamma  = 0.85*0.96/1.25 = 0.653 N/mm2 (= AQUA FEQR Eingabe)
L2=2.4 fct0,L2 = 0.60 N/mm2 ; fctRL2 = 0.60 N/mm2 (mit kappaf=kappaG = 1.0)
max. sigma fctdL2 = alphac*fctRL1 / gamma  = 0.85*0.60/1.25 = 0.408 N/mm2 (= AQUA FEQT Eingabe)

Gebrauch (nichtlineare Verfahren DEHN): Bild R.1
max. sigma fctm = 3.21 N/mm2
1.04*fctR,L1 = 1.04*0.96 = 0.998 N/mm2
1.04*fctR,L2 = 1.04*0.60 = 0.624 N/mm2

Daher wird hier eine Gebrauchsarbeitslinie mit Sicherheit 1.0 eingegeben, dann stimmen alle Werte mit der Handrechnung Ã¼berein.

 Nonlinear ASE see bemess.dat\..\steel_fibre_concrete.dat

</TEXT>

!#!Info  Example:       ULS Design of a cantilever column modelled by a structural line
!#!Info  Keyword:       Column design, Nominal Curvature Method
!#!Info  Program:       COLUMN
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2024

+prog aqua urs:1
head Cross-Section
page unii 0

norm 'din' 'en199x-200x' coun 49

conc 1  c '20' typr    b titl "=c 20/25 (en 1992)"

stee 2  b '500b' tmax 32 titl "=b 500 b (en 1992)"

srec 1 h 0.40 b 0.40 so 50 su 50 ss 50 mno 1 mrf 2 rtyp 'cu'

end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head  Column Geometry

page unii 0
echo full 0
syst 3d gdiv 10000 gdir posz
ctrl mesh 1
ctrl hmin 0.5
ctrl tolg 0.02

spt 1 x 0.00 0.00 0.00 fix ppmz
spt 2 x 0.00 0.00 -8.00 fix pypxmz

sln 1 npa 1 2 styp "oy" sno 1 titl "sln x-9"

end


+prog sofiload urs:3
head Characteristic Load Cases
echo full 0

act g
act q
act s

lc 1 type g titl "dead load"
 poin ref node 2 type pzz 2000.0

lc 2 type q titl "live load 1"
 poin ref node 2 type myy 50.00

lc 3 type s titl "live load 2"
 poin ref node 2 type pzz 800.0

end


+prog ase urs:6
head Linear 1st Oder Analysis of characteristic load cases
echo full no
lc 1,2,3
end

HEAD Combination Rules
PAGE UNII 0 LANO 0
echo full no

$ Optional pre-definition here

LC 1002 TYPE (D)
 copy 1 1.0
 copy 2 1.5
 copy 3 0.75

end

+prog column urs:5
head Column Design

echo mat
echo sect
echo syst
echo comb full
echo forc full
echo rein full

$   Design According to EN 1992-1-1:2004, 5.8.8

$ Design Group

dgrp no DG01 titl "S101 - X/8 - Cantilever Columns"

!*!Label General NCM constants

geom bety 1.00 betz 1.00 cy 10 cz 10

$imp amxy 1 amxz 1

!*!Label Combinations

$ Option 1: define new rules here

 copy no 1 fact 1.0

$ Option 2: reference predefined ones by 'lc'

$ forces of referenced Structural Lines (sln) will automatically be read

END

!#!Info  Example:       Span by span erection
!#!Info  Keyword:       construction stages; creep; shrinkage
!#!Info  Program:       CSM
$
$

$ english file name: csm1_4span_centering.dat
$
$ Overview examples for bridges see csm.dat\..\design\csm31_design.dat
$
$ Please run animator with first CS loadcase without vibration (animation speed=0)
$ and fixed magnitude (click into input-box magnitude and input  e.g. 50 ).
$ Then switch through the loadcases -
$ therefore you can use the keyboard button cursor-down to switch
$ to next loadcase (through the loadcases) or use the loadcase loop feature.
$
$ This example exists with camber computation as csm26_precamber_feldweise.dat

$  Description:
$  ============

$     A 4-span bridge is build in span by span construction stages:
$
$     First concrete : stressfree on formwork - here not calculated:
$             ------------------*
$             |||||||||||||||||||-formwork
$             ^   Span 1   ^
$
$   CS10: Construction stage 10: Deadload of CS 10 is activated after removal of formwork.
$
$             ------------------*
$             ^   Span 1   ^
$
$   CS15: Creep and shrinkage of concrete span 1 for 28 Days.
$
$   CS19: Next step is concreted, dead load still on formwork on ground
$
$             ------------------*----------------*
$                               ||||||||||||||||||-formwork on ground
$             ^   Span 1   ^    Span 2      ^
$
$   CS20: Formwork removed - deadload activated
$
$             ------------------*----------------*
$
$             ^   Span 1   ^    Span 2      ^
$
$   CS25: Creep and shrinkage of active spans 1+2 for 28 Days.
$
$   CS29: Next step is concreted, dead load still on formwork on ground
$
$             ------------------*----------------*-------------------------
$                                                |||||||||||||||||||||||||-formwork on ground
$             ^   Span 1   ^    Span 2      ^    Span 3      ^   Span 4   ^
$
$         As this stage does not give new forces it is not calculated here !
$
$   CS30: Formwork removed - deadload activated
$
$           ------------------*----------------*-------------------------
$
$           ^  1st Span  ^   2nd Span     ^   3rd Span     ^  4th Span  ^
$
$   CS32: Additional dead load g_2 activated
$
$   CS35: Creep and shrinkage till traffic opening
$
$   CS45: Creep and shrinkage till t-infinite

$ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Creep with construction stages for a 4-span bridge
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
CONC 1 C 35
STEE 2 S 500
STEE 7 S 235
SREC 1 H 1.20[m] B 0.60[m] HO 0.40[m] BO 2.80[m] MNO 1 MRF 2  $ A= 1.6mÂ² => g= 40kN/m
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:3
HEAD Creep with construction stages for a 4-span bridge
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST TYPE SPAC GDIV 1000
NODE (1 41 1) (0 2) 0 0
NODE 1 FIX ppmx
NODE 10,21,32,41 FIX xp
GRP 1
  BEAM (1 12 1) (1 1) (2 1) NCS 1
GRP 2
  BEAM (13 23 1) (13 1) (14 1) NCS 1
GRP 3
  BEAM (24 40 1) (24 1) (25 1) NCS 1

$ Group title for WINGRAF:
GRP   1,2,3 titl 'Superstructure'

END

+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:5
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
HEAD Axis for SOFILOAD load trains, SSD Tendons, Animator environment
SYST REST
GAX 'AX_1'
GAXB X1 0 0 0 X2 400 0 0  $ create axis from point 1 to point 2   (also with R)
$ GAX...TYPC SPLI and GAXC can create an axis through a set of points
end

!#!KAPITEL Loading and Settings
+PROG SOFILOAD URS:20
HEAD Definition of actions and loads
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ECHO ACT Full $ Please check GAMU factors
ACT G_1
ACT G_2
ACT P
ACT C
$
$ Loads used in CSM should get TYPE none because construction stages get an own type in CSM-CS
LC  2 TYPE 'none' TITL 'G_2'         $ NachtrÃ¤gliches Eigengewicht g2
                                 $ supplementary  deadload g2
  BEAM GRP 1,2,3 TYPE PZP PA 30
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG CSM URS:19
HEAD Construction stages
CTRL DL  AUTO  $ Deadload of gamma applied automatically
CTRL CANT 1    $ 1 = free cantilever erection with original inclination  $ 2 = tangential
               $ irrelevant when using CAMB precamber feature !
CS 10 TYPE G_1 TITL 'Stripping span 1'
CS 15 TYPE C_1 TITL 'Creep+shrinkage'                T    28          $ 4 Weeks= 28 Days
CS 19 TYPE G_1 TITL 'Concrete 20 on formwork' $ Please refer to csm.dat\optimize\csm26_precamber_spanbyspan.dat
CS 20 TYPE G_1 TITL 'Stripping span 2'
CS 25 TYPE C_1 TITL 'Creep+shrinkage'                T    28
CS 29 TYPE G_1 TITL 'Concrete 30 on formwork' $ not necessary as it does not result in a force change - only animation looks better
CS 30 TYPE G_1 TITL 'Stripping span 3+4'
CS 32 TYPE G_2 TITL 'add. dead load'
CS 34 TYPE C_1 TITL 'Creep+shrinkage'                T    28
CS 35 TYPE C_1 TITL 'C+S till traffic open'          T   100
CS 45 TYPE C_2 TITL 'C+S till t-infinite'            T 365*100   NCRE 4               $ In 4 Creep steps
$
GRP  NO  ICS1 ICSD  T0 TITL
       -    10   10   7 '10.CS'
       2    19   20   7 '20.CS'  $ Please refer to csm.dat\optimize\csm26_precamber_spanbyspan.dat
       3    29   30   7 '30.CS'
$
LC    NO ICS1 ATIL
       2 32    - $ active until t-infinite
SELE BEAM 1012 X 0[m]      $ Girder for AQB stress output.
END
$  Then let run the file $(NAME)_csm.dat will be done automatically via +apply
+apply "$(NAME)_csm.dat"

<TEXT> Comments:
Please also unconditionally look to example csm.dat\optimize\csm26_precamber_spanbyspan.dat
= formwork precamber linear

In case you do not want to precamber your segments
BUT     you want to add (weld) them tangentially  (CTRL CANT 2)
AND     you want to have the beams placed on the supports in the architectural position:
-->  csm26_tangential_without_precamber.dat
</TEXT>

+sys del $(project).$d?

       1    1    -  103    -  7   $ Hinge fixed since CS 3!

!#!Info  Example:       Two-span beam with in-situ-concrete deck

$ english file name: csm3_composite_beam.dat

$ Overview examples for bridges see csm.dat\..\design\csm31_design.dat
$
$ Please run animator with first CS loadcase without vibration (animation speed=0)
$ and fixed magnitude (click into input-box magnitude and input  e.g. 50 ).

$ to next loadcase (through the loadcases) or use the loadcase loop feature.
$

#define l1=24.50    $ l1
#define l2=24.50    $ l2
#define spaltA=0.30  $ Abstand der FT-TrÃ¤ger von Lagerachse am Anfang
                     $ Distance of beam by support axis (start)
#define spaltM=0.40  $ Abstand der FT-TrÃ¤ger von Mittelachse
                     $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle)
#define xlager=0.30 $ Abstand der Lagerung der FT-TrÃ¤ger im FT-Werk
                    $ Distance of beam by support axis (end) during fabrication
#define xlag_M=0.15 $ Abstand der Lagerung der FT-TrÃ¤ger bei Montage
                    $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle) during fabrication


$ more\csm3_Spannbett.dat = Variante mit sofortigem Verbund
$----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

$ more\csm3_casting_bed_method.dat = variant with immediate bond
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Two-span beam with in-situ-concrete deck
ECHO SECT FULL
NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
CONC  1  C   40      $ = C40/50
STEE  2,3 S 500                  $ standard reinforcement steel 500
CONC  4  C   30      $ = C30/37  in situ concrete
STEE  7    S  '235' $ TMAX  0 $ structural steel for tubes, rolled steel ...
STEE 11    Y '1860A' $ prestessing steel
                    $ fp0,1k = 1600 N/mm2
                    $ fpk    = 1860 N/mm2
                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max

SECT  1  MNO 1 MRF  2
let#zmax 1050 $ mm
CS  1  $   ----------------------------- Construction stage 1
$ do not use CS 0 here, CS 0 is always a complete cross section!
$ Best use CS 1 as first CS (do not start e.g. with CS 10)
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT TOP1  0     0 EXP  0.10 $ aeration only over asphalt
    1   1125     0 EXP  1.00 $ for all following QP!
    2   1125  0110
    3    300  0150
    4    275  #zmax
SPT    NO     Y      Z   MNO
     'TOP1'   0      0    1
     'BOT1'   0  #zmax    1
  let#ytop  250 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#ybot  210 $ [mm] y-value of Torsionsbox below
  let#ztop   80 $ [mm] z-value of Torsionsbox above
  let#zbot #zmax-110 $ "       of Torsionsbox below
LAY 0 'TORS' type min $ default for reinforcement layers
LAY 1 'BOT'  type opt $ 'bot' lower reinforcement 'bot'
LAY 2 'TOP'  type opt $ 'top' upper reinforcement 'top'
RF Y #ytop,-#ytop Z #ztop AS  4[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
RF Y #ybot,-#ybot Z #zbot AS  4[cm2] LAY 0 TORS acti D  12
$ bending reinforcement:
  let#ytop  800 $ [mm]
  let#ybot  230 $ [mm]
  let#ztop   60 $ [mm]
  let#zbot #zmax-60
RF Y #ytop,#ytop/2,-#ytop/2,0,-#ytop Z #ztop AS  4[cm2] LAY 2 TORS pass D  16 $ above
RF Y #ybot,#ybot/2,-#ybot/2,0,-#ybot Z #zbot AS  4[cm2] LAY 1 TORS pass D  16 $ below
CUT 1 ZB 210    MNO 1 MRF 2      LAY 0
CUT 2 ZB 350    MNO 1 MRF 2      LAY 0
$
CS 40  $   ----------------------------- Construction stage 40 : = complete cross section
POLY  OPZ MNO 4
VERT TOP4    0  -200 EXP  0.40 $ Aeration only over asphalt
VERT  11  1125  -200 EXP  1.00
VERT  12  1125     0 EXP  0.20 $ Areation down only as
VERT  13     0     0 EXP  0.20 $ $ contact support axis
SPT    NO     Y   Z   MNO
     'TOP4'   0 -200   4
     'BOT4'   0    0   4
  let#ztop -140 $ [mm]
RF Y #ytop,#ytop/2,-#ytop/2,0,-#ytop Z #ztop AS  4[cm2] LAY 3 MRF 3 TORS pass D  16 $ above
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:15
HEAD Two-span beam with in-situ-concrete deck
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 GDIR ZZ

#define l1=24.50    $ l1
#define l2=24.50    $ l2
#define spalt=0.40  $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle)
#define xlager=0.30 $ Distance of beam by support axis (end) during fabrication
#define xlag_M=0.15 $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle) during fabrication

let#1 $(l1) $ l1
let#2 $(l2) $ l2
NODE NO X  Y=0 Z=0
     1  0            ; let#xx $(spaltA)
     2 #xx
     3 #xx+$(xlag_M)
     4 #xx+$(xlager)
     5 #xx+#1/2
     6 #xx+#1-$(xlager)
     7 #xx+#1-$(xlag_M)
     8 #xx+#1
     9 #xx+#1+$(spaltM) ; let#xx #xx+#1+$(spaltM)+$(spaltM)
    10 #xx
    11 #xx+$(xlag_M)
    12 #xx+$(xlager)
    13 #xx+#2/2
    14 #xx+#2-$(xlager)
    15 #xx+#2-$(xlag_M)
    16 #xx+#2
    17 #xx+#2+$(spaltA)
NODE 2,16 FIX mx
$
GRP 10 $ Pre-fabricated beam
  BEAM  (2  7 1)  (2 1)  (3 1) NCS 1 NP -1
  BEAM (10 15 1) (10 1) (11 1) NCS 1 NP -1
  let#3 0.25*(#1+#2)
  BSEC NO 10004,10005,10012,10013 X #3/3   NCS 1 $ additional section at long grider
  BSEC NO 10004,10005,10012,10013 X #3/3*2 NCS 1
$
GRP 40 $ Connection to final support
  BEAM  1        1      2    NCS 1 NP -1 $ same cross section
  BEAM (8  9 1) (8 1)  (9 1) NCS 1 NP -1 $ same cross section
  BEAM 16       16     17    NCS 1 NP -1 $ same cross section
$
GRP 91 $ Support during fabrication and construction
  let#knr  3 ; SPRI #knr #knr DZ 1 CP 1E7 CT 1
  let#knr  7 ; SPRI #knr #knr DZ 1 CP 1E7 CT 1
  let#knr 11 ; SPRI #knr #knr DZ 1 CP 1E7 CT 1
  let#knr 15 ; SPRI #knr #knr DZ 1 CP 1E7 CT 1
$
GRP 92 $ Final support
  let#knr  1 ; SPRI #knr #knr DZ 1 CP 1E7 CT 1
  let#knr  9 ; SPRI #knr #knr DZ 1 CP 1E7 CT 1
  let#knr 17 ; SPRI #knr #knr DZ 1 CP 1E7 CT 1

$ Group title for WINGRAF:
GRP   10 titl 'Main beam'
GRP   40 titl 'mispan closure'
GRP   91 titl 'Temporary support'
GRP   92 titl 'Final support'

END

        1  11 2*2430[kN] 2*1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 1.41*82[mm] $ csm3_parabel and csm32_slab, 12 wires

        1     0   0.4     -

$        PROG CSM ->   SELE BEAM 10005 X 0[m]            $ beam for AQB/AQUP
$        .
$        If you want to add a final design, please refer to csm.dat\..\design\csm31_design.dat

$ ########################### Attention: #########################################
$ ##############################################################################
$ By the construction stage the components of cross section in AQUA
$ to be cautiously proffered if internal forces are interpreted
$
$ The forces of cross section to ASE in CDB refer always to the active
$ partial cross sections in ASE run. That's why they are entered in AQB as REF TEIL (= default in versions 21)
$
$ The load during transfer of load case 20 to load case 40 in this example does not change.
$ The precast girder - corss sections dead load is also activated in constructions stage 20
$ (see CSM-GRUP-Input ORTG = 20).
$ In construction stage 40 only the soft concrete of construction stage 20 will be now hardened !
$
$ Although no deformation and stress changes, the printed moment in load case 4040
$ in ASE is different as in load case 4020, because it is now calculated relative to another centre
$ of gravity, namely at the centre of gravity of now hardened ideal complete cross section
$
$ LC 4020 = sum of all moments which relates currently at an active stress
$           (g1+in situ concrete mass+ prestress) of ideal centre of gravity skill = partial
$           cross section 1.1 construction stage 1 of AQUA.
$ LC 4040 = sum of moments which relates of same loads at ideal centre of
$           gravity complete- composite section = AQUA No. 1.2 structure 40:
$
$                    SUMMARY OF CROSS SECTION VALUES OF AUQA
$  No         A[m2]  Iy             zs       gam
$            It[m4]       [m4]     [m]    [kN/m]
$   1    1.2384E+00  1.585E-01   0.231     31.80
$   1.1    BA     1
$        8.2200E-01  8.827E-02   0.399     20.55
$   1.2    BA    40                               d.h. delta-zs = 0.168 m
$        1.2385E+00  1.585E-01   0.231     31.80
$
$ Expression internal forces and moments expression with DBVIEW (= CDB content):
$
$  Forces at girder elements
$  Elem.      X  LC        N       VY       VZ       MT       MY       MZ
$     Nr    [m]  No     [kN]     [kN]     [kN]    [kNm]    [kNm]    [kNm]
$  10005  0.000 4020  -4935.6     0.00     0.00     0.00  -244.20     0.00
$               4040  -4935.6     0.00     0.25     0.00 -1071.70     0.00
$  Control:   delta-MY = N*delta-centriod location = -4935.6*0.168= -829 kNm OK.
$
$ Stored difference load case 6040 in ASE, deliver the moment difference of
$ the construction stage, it will be given with MY=0.0, as in reality the moment does not
$ change but in LC 4040 it's given only at another reference point!
$ DBVIEW's expression
$  Elem.      X  LC        N       VY       VZ       MT       MY       MZ
$     Nr    [m]  No     [kN]     [kN]     [kN]    [kNm]    [kNm]    [kNm]
$  10005  0.000 6040      0.0     0.00     0.26     0.00     0.23     0.00
$
$ Same effects can be observed naturally in the edition of forces of WinGraf!
$
$ Only the difference load case 6000
$ . are processed in AQB and from it generated stress will be imposed,
$ we will try to find the real equivalent stress again (-> AQUP). By transition from CS 20 to CS 40 the
$ stress does not change,that in construction stage 20 the soft situ concrete is only hardened in construction
$ stage 40, but it has no stress, because till now there isn't any additional deformations occurred.
$
$  Analysisi of section
$  Analysisi of section:  10005  X =       0.000   [m]
$  ------------------------------------------------------------------------
$  CROSS SECTION VALUES
$  QNo               A[m2]     Iy[m4]     Iz[m4]    Iyz[m4]   ys[m]   zs[m]
$    1 Brutto    1.238E+00  1.585E-01  3.072E-01  0.000E+00   0.000   0.231
$      BauAbs 3  8.454E-01  9.445E-02  1.316E-01  0.000E+00   0.000   0.413
$      BauAbs 4  1.262E+00  1.694E-01  3.072E-01  0.000E+00   0.000   0.244
$
$  NORMAL STRESS  [MPa]
$  Q  Load case                      N       MY PktFUMI  PktFOMI  PktOUMI  PktOOMI
$                                [kN]    [kNm]   [MPa]    [MPa]    [MPa]    [MPa]
$  3  FL 8015 AQB-Creep FT   322.0   163.11    1.59    -0.36     0.00     0.00
$  4  LF 6040 Solo_Harden OB    0.0     0.23    0.00     0.00     0.00     0.00
$
$  B  CS 20 G1 in-situ-concrete slab  -4613.7  -850.20   -7.66    -4.93     0.00     0.00
$  B  CS 40 Harden OB       -4613.7  -849.97   -7.66    -4.93     0.00     0.00
$
$ ^ B means here, the stress is applied at different partial cross sections or rather
$ said at different construction stage and the moment -850kNm out of moments of this program
$ therefore the section value is now related at the gross cross section expression:
$ Control:
$ M-Gross = M-CS3 + N*delta-zs = -244.20 -4613.7*(0.399-0.231) + 163.11 =  -855
$                                                                        =ca.850
$ (+163.11  due to AQBs-concrete inherent stress at creep
$         - AQB presses only the moment at that concrete).
$
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

$  will be done automatically via +apply
+apply "$(NAME)_csm.dat"

                    $            0.8*fpk    = 0.80*1860 = 1488 N/mm2
                    $            0.9*fp0,1k = 0.90*1600 = 1440 N/mm2
                    $ sigp,max = min(1488,1440)         = 1440 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 5.10.2.1(1) maximum stress
                    $ sigp,SLS = 0.65*fpk   = 0.65*1860 = 1209 N/mm2 EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)      on traffic opening permanent
                    $ sigp,rare= sigp,max

<TEXT>
Explanation to SIR-results by QUAD-Tendons:
(to simplify matters at statically determinate single span girder):

In principle at statically determined single span girder, the sum of the internal
forces and moments of all elements at all of the load cases P and C
is in average 0.0
Basic: Prestress and Creep+Shrinkage are here inherent stress conditions
       (without redistributed moment ).
       The concrete has a compressive force in load case P and the tendon
       an identical magnitude tension .
       The concrete stress sinks due to C+S in load case C, also
       in identical mass sinks the prestressing steel stress too.
       The sum of concrete proportion + prestressing steel is zero (inherent stress condition).

Only the concrete proportion is required for the AQB- design
(respectively for a SIR-check)by the prestress and creep + shrinkage.
(rather total internal forces and moments plus statically determined proportion of concrete).

For the load case prestress P is this in SIR with LC BAMI to be specified.

Following methods are for the load case creep + shrinkage C by CSM applications
implemented:

       ASE can compute the difference load cases out of the sum load cases (STEU DIFF ...).
       An additional information will be saved in ASE, in these difference load cases C+S by the
       creep and shrinkage analyses. Therewith the SIR can add once again the statically determined
       proportion of concrete of C+S (=Loss of concrete stress).

       Thus the SIR-results of the difference load cases are not consistent with the
       simple difference of output - (Sums-) load cases !

Example:
The construction stage C+S will be saved in stage of construction 15 (BA 15) in load case 4015
(LC 4015)(= load case of sums according to C+S).
Due to control LC DIFF 1000 in ASE, a difference load case will be automatically generated 5015
(LC 5015) (= difference load case C+S).  This load case contains the additional information,
that it is a C+S and in SIR the
statically determined proportion C+S should be added once again.

Following SIR-Results are generated:

 SECTION COMPONENT  SECTION     2 XS =    0.000
           LC  Typ           No     N[kN]     Vy[kN]     Vz[kN]    Mt[kNm]    My[kNm]    Mz[kNm]
         4010 Sum                     0.0       0.00       0.00       0.00    1233.97       0.00
         4011 Sum                     0.0       0.00      -0.01       0.00    1249.89       0.00
         4015 Sum                     0.0       0.00      -0.01       0.00    1258.49       0.00
         4020 Sum                     0.0       0.00      -0.01       0.00    1557.81       0.00
         4025 Sum                     0.0       0.00      -0.01       0.00    1557.77       0.00
         4026 Sum                     0.0       0.00      -0.01       0.00    1557.72       0.00
         4027 Sum                     0.0       0.00      -0.01       0.00    1557.65       0.00

         5010 Sum                     0.0       0.00       0.00       0.00    1233.97       0.00
         5011 Sum                 -4277.2       0.00      -0.01       0.00   -3833.26       0.00
         5015 Sum                   139.4       0.00       0.00       0.00     134.10       0.00
         5020 Sum                     0.0       0.00       0.00       0.00     299.32       0.00
         5025 Sum                   106.2       0.00       0.00       0.00      95.53       0.00
         5026 Sum                   116.8       0.00       0.00       0.00     105.11       0.00
         5027 Sum                   152.7       0.00       0.00       0.00     137.39       0.00
                                 ============
                          sum C+S = 515.1  (= 139.4 + 106.2 + 116.8 + 152.7)
                                  =  12% of -4277.2  -> to be input in an AQB design as loss due to C+S :
                                         Input in AQB COMB e.g.:  COMB MAXR MY  LC1 G  LC2 P 0.88  LC3 L
end


Please consider that the sums load cases 4000.. without BAMI have manipulation all
N=0.0 kN = none external normal force !

Contrary to it in LC 5011 the statically determined proportion of prestress contains N=-4277.2 kN
and in LC 5015 the loss of prestress in concrete proportion  delta-N= +139.4 kN

Therefore in SIR only the difference load cases
(LC 5000*) should be analysed for a better overview!
</text>

+PROG TENDON urs:9
HEAD Parabolic Prestress
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
$ Definition of prestressing system:
$ We recommend to input all data as user defined prestressing system.
$ For the static analysis the following values are sufficient:
SYSP NOPS MAT   ZV       AZ    LITZ MINR   BETA  MUE ECC  SP     DO
      $ 1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 82[mm] $ csm3_parabel and csm32_slab, 12 wires
      $ 1  11 3078[kN] 2250[mm2] 15 7.10[m] 0.3 0.20 4[mm] 3[mm] 92[mm] $            15 wires
        1  11 2*3848[kN] 2*2850[mm2] 19 6.50[m] 0.3 0.21 4[mm] 3[mm] 1.41*97[mm] $ csm31_beam 19 wires
      $       2* two tendons - better here than  TEND NSP 2
      $ 1  11 2430[kN] 1800[mm2] 12 6.50[m] 0.0 0.00 0[mm] 0[mm] 10[mm] $ csm3_casting_yard
$
$ reference axis and span definition:
AXES NOH 1 TYPE AUTO  117 17
TOPP NOH 1 KIND NODE S 117,17 SP 1,2
$ tendon geometry definition:  NOPS = prestressing system for max-min radius parameters + duct-excentricities
TGEO NOG 1 NOH 1 NOPS 1
let#1 0.15
$ Definition points of geometry:  (TYP=SPAN/FELD station via highpoints)
PTUV    S     U     V   DVS    RV   RL   TYPE=SPAN
        1     0   #1
        1.5   0   #1
        2     0   #1
$ prestress-procedure  $ Anspann-Vorgehen
PSIG 'RI' ANWS 9 KAPA - K3 1280 $
        $ k3 = estimated limit to reduce stress at traffic opening (after first creep+shrinkage)
        $      max-sigma-traffic opening in most cases (e.g. to EN-1992-1-1 7.2(5)) -> 0.65 fpk (or 0.75 depending on design code)

$ final tendon definition:
$.......................................................
CS ICS1 101 102
TEND NOT 101 NOG 1 NTEN 1 from 111 to 11 type NODE LC 101 LC0 0
  $ Spannglied 101 hat IBA1=101 und liegt im Bauabschnitt 101 und Lastfall 101
  $ Tendon 101 has IBA1=101 and lies in construction stage 101 and load case 101
  $ Zu Bauabschnitten bei Stabsystemen siehe auch railway.dat
  $ for construction stages by girder system see railway.dat file too

$.......................................................

let#5 2 $ Gruppennummer des Segmentes    $ Groupnumber of segment
$.......................................................
#define tendon

let#5 #5+1
let#IBA1 101+#5*10

CS ICS1 #IBA1 #IBA1+1

+PROG TENDON urs:9
HEAD Prestressing  top tendons
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
CTRL WARN 723,725,420 $ due to stresses fy - tendon.tab
$ Definition of prestressing system:
$ We recommend to input all data as user defined prestressing system.
$ For the static analysis the following values are sufficient:
SYSP NOPS MAT   ZV       AZ    LITZ MINR   BETA  MUE ECC  SP     DO
        1  11 3848[kN] 2850[mm2] 19 6.50[m] 0.3 0.21 2[mm] 6[mm] 97[mm] $ top tendons csm31_beam 19 wires
        2  11 3848[kN] 2850[mm2] 19 6.50[m] 0.3 0.21 2[mm] 6[mm] 97[mm] $ bottom tendons
        3  11 3848[kN] 2850[mm2] 19 6.50[m] 0.3 0.21 2[mm] 6[mm] 10[mm] $ external: no extra duct hole -> 10[mm]
$
#define tendonplot
  SIZE urs
  PLOT GEOE NO #not FACH  4 TYPG DUTE
#enddef

$ reference axis and span definition:
AXES NOH 1 TYPE AUTO 101 202

let#pier 1
let#piernode 119
let#nrloc 1 $ *10+1 gives construction stage number for top tendons
#define toptendon
  let#not   #pier*100+#nrloc
  let#ics1  #nrloc*10+1
  let#nn DIV(#nrloc,2) $ = #nrloc/2: 1->0 3->1 5->2 7->3...
  let#node1 #piernode-2-#nn   $ starting node of tendon
  let#node2 #piernode+2+#nn   $ ending   node of tendon
  let#beam1 (#node1-100)*10   $ starting beam of tendon
  let#beam2 (#node2-100-1)*10 $ ending   beam of tendon
  TGEO NOG #not NOH 1 NOPS 1
  PTUV  S        X      U      V        DVS  TYPE=beam
       #beam1    0.000  0.000  0.430
       #beam1+10 0.000  0.000  0.306     0
       #beam2    =      =      =         0
       #beam2+10 0.000  =      0.430
  if MOD(#not,2)==1
    PSIG 'RI' ANWS 9 KAPA 1.5 K3 1280
  else
    PSIG 'LE' ANWS 9 KAPA 1.5 K3 1280
  endif
  CS ICS1 #ics1 #ics1+1
  TEND #not NOG #not NTEN 2 LC #ics1
                      $   2 Attention: NTEN=2
  #include tendonplot
  let#nrloc #nrloc+2
#enddef
#include toptendon $ ICS1  11
#include toptendon $ ICS1  31
#include toptendon $ ICS1  51
#include toptendon $ ICS1  71
$

+PROG TENDON urs:8
head    external tendons
CTRL WARN 723,725,420
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
#include seth

#define extern
  let#node1 #centerleft-#nrloc-#addinside   $ left  Umlenksattel
  let#node2 #centerleft+#nrloc+1+#addinside $ right Umlenksattel
  let#beama (#pierleft-100)*10   $ beam x=0 pierleft
  let#beam1 (#node1-100)*10      $ beam x=0 left  Umlenksattel
  let#beam2 (#node2-100)*10      $ beam x=0 right Umlenksattel
  let#beame (#pierright-100)*10  $ beam x=0 pierright
  let#dzbot 0.50
  if #node2-#node1>9
    let#dzbot 0.90  $ damit in Feldmitte nicht unten rausschauen
  endif
  TGEO NOG #not NOH 1 NOPS 3
  PTSV  S        X      U      V          TYPE=beam
       #beama    0.000  0.000  0.600
       #beam1    0.000  0.000  #h(#node1)-#dzbot
       #beam2    0.000  0.000  #h(#node2)-#dzbot
       #beame    0.000  =      0.600
  PSIG 'RI' ANWS 1 KAPA 0 K3 1180
  CS ICS1 #ics1 ICS2 999 $  999 = external !

!#!Info  Example:       Free cantilever erection with CTRL CANT 3
!#!Info  Keyword:       construction stages; free cantilever erection
!#!Info  Program:       CSM
$
$

$ english file name: csm7_cant_3.dat

$ Feature CTRL CANT 3:                          JB 30.12.2008
$ Sometimes if the cantilever part consists of multiple elements
$ e.g. of two parallel beams, the prefabricated cantilever part does not fit to
$ the already created part (because this is distorted).
$ In reality the new element must be squeezed to the old one.
$ CTRL CANT 3  now takes the new part as one block and first
$ analyses a preliminary state CS+10000 where the new part is
$ predeformed to fit the deformation at the joint.
$ Adding this predeformed new part in the real construction stage, it will
$ expand and behave as if the old and new part would have been
$ added in one piece (in shop)
$ File csm7_cant_3.dat shows the effect on inserting a close segement
$ File csm8_cant_3.dat shows the effect on a prefabricated cantilever segement
$


$ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD CTRL CANT 3
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
CONC 1 C 35
STEE 2 S 500
STEE 7 S 235
SREC 1 H 1.20[m] B 0.60[m] HO 0.40[m] BO 2.80[m] MNO 1 MRF 2  $ A= 1.6mÂ² => g= 40kN/m
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:3
HEAD System
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST TYPE SPAC GDIV 1000
NODE (1 41 1) (0 2) 0 0
NODE 1 FIX ppmx
NODE 10,29,41 FIX xp
GRP 1
  BEAM (1 14 1) (1 1) (2 1) NCS 1
GRP 2
  BEAM (15 23 1) (15 1) (16 1) NCS 1
GRP 3
  BEAM (24 40 1) (24 1) (25 1) NCS 1
  spri na 41 dx 1 cp 1 cm 1

$ Group title for WINGRAF:
GRP   1,2,3 titl 'Superstructure'

END

!#!KAPITEL Variant CTRL CANT 1
+PROG CSM URS:19
head Variant CTRL CANT 1
CTRL CANT 1
cs 10 type G_1 titl 'Activate GRP 1'
cs 30 type G_1 titl 'Activate GRP 2'
cs 39 type G_1 titl 'Activate GRP 2 without dead load' $ Please refer to csm.dat\optimize\csm26_precamber_spanbyspan.dat
cs 40 type G_1 titl 'Activate dead load GRP 2'
$
GRP   NO  ICS1 ICSD
       -    09   10
       2    39   40
       3    29   30
SELE BEAM 1012 X 0[m]      $ Stab fÃ¼r die AQB Spannungsausgabe
CTRL STOR 0 ; SCAL AQ_S 0 $ no AQB check print
end
+apply "$(NAME)_csm.dat"

!#!KAPITEL Variant CTRL CANT 3
+PROG CSM URS:2
head Variant CTRL CANT 3
CTRL CANT 2 $ CANT 3+4 only allo2wed for single CS -> CS 339 CANT 3
CTRL STOR +64  $ do not delete old CSM sequence
cs 310 type G_1        titl 'Activate GRP 1'
cs 330 type G_1        titl 'Activate GRP 2'
cs 339 type G_1 CANT 3 titl 'Activate GRP 2 without dead load' $ Please refer to csm.dat\optimize\csm26_precamber_spanbyspan.dat
cs 340 type G_1        titl 'Activate dead load GRP 2'
$
GRP   NO  ICS1 ICSD
       -   309  310
       2   339  340
       3   329  330
SELE BEAM 1012 X 0[m]      $ Stab fÃ¼r die AQB Spannungsausgabe
end
+apply "$(NAME)_csm.dat"

!#!KAPITEL Variant CTRL CANT 4
+PROG CSM URS:4
head Variant CTRL CANT 4
CTRL CANT 2 $ CANT 3+4 only allo2wed for single CS -> CS 339 CANT 3
CTRL STOR +64  $ do not delete old CSM sequence
cs 410 type G_1        titl 'Activate GRP 1'
cs 430 type G_1        titl 'Activate GRP 2'
cs 439 type G_1 CANT 4 titl 'Activate GRP 2 without dead load' $ Please refer to csm.dat\optimize\csm26_precamber_spanbyspan.dat
cs 440 type G_1        titl 'Activate dead load GRP 2'
$
GRP   NO  ICS1 ICSD
       -   409  410
       2   439  440
       3   429  430
SELE BEAM 1012 X 0[m]      $ Stab fÃ¼r die AQB Spannungsausgabe
end
+apply "$(NAME)_csm.dat"

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?

!#!Info  Example:       Free cantilever erection with CTRL CANT 3
!#!Info  Keyword:       construction stages; free cantilever erection
!#!Info  Program:       CSM
$
$

$ english file name: csm7_cant_3.dat

$ Feature CTRL CANT 3:                          JB 30.12.2008
$ Sometimes if the cantilever part consists of multiple elements
$ e.g. of two parallel beams, the prefabricated cantilever part does not fit to
$ the already created part (because this is distorted).
$ In reality the new element must be squeezed to the old one.
$ CTRL CANT 3  now takes the new part as one block and first
$ analyses a preliminary state CS+10000 where the new part is
$ predeformed to fit the deformation at the joint.
$ Adding this predeformed new part in the real construction stage, it will
$ expand and behave as if the old and new part would have been
$ added in one piece (in shop)
$ File csm7_cant_3.dat shows the effect on inserting a close segement
$ File csm8_cant_3.dat shows the effect on a prefabricated cantilever segement
$

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD CTRL CANT 2
NORM 'NS' 'en199X-200X-BRIDGE'     CAT 'B'  $ road bridges
CONC 1   C   30
STEE 2   S  500
STEE 3   Y  '1860A'
STEE 4   S  235 TMAX 0
SECT   1 MNO 4 ; SV IT -10 ; PROF 1 HEA 1000
SECT   2 MNO 4 ;             PROF 701 HEA  500
$ Querschnitt Seile    $ section cables
SCIT 3 D 80[mm] MNO 4 $ cable

END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:2
HEAD CTRL CANT 2
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
SYST SPAC          GDIV   1000
NODE     NO                 X          Y
    (1     30     1)     (0 1.00)   +3.50
    (1+500 30+500 1)     (0 1.00)   -3.50

let#d 100 $ beam number increment to get each 10 beams in one group:
BEAM NO                 NA       NE      NCS=1 NP=-1
    (1*#d+1 29*#d+1 #d)  (1     1)     (2 1) $ longitudinal beams
    (1*#d+2 29*#d+2 #d)  (1+500 1) (2+500 1)
BEAM          NO                 NA       NE      NCS=2 NP=-1
 let#1   3 ; #1*#d+3 #1 #1+500 $ crossbeam #1=main node number
 let#1   8 ; #1*#d+3 #1 #1+500 $ crossbeam #1=main node number
 let#1  13 ; #1*#d+3 #1 #1+500 $ crossbeam #1=main node number
 let#1  18 ; #1*#d+3 #1 #1+500 $ crossbeam #1=main node number
 let#1  23 ; #1*#d+3 #1 #1+500 $ crossbeam #1=main node number
 let#1  28 ; #1*#d+3 #1 #1+500 $ crossbeam #1=main node number
NODE 1,501 FIX F
NODE 901 Z -14 FIX F
GRP 11
  CABL NO - NA 17,517 NE 901 NCS 3

$ Group title for WINGRAF:
GRP   0 titl 'Segment 0'
GRP   1 titl 'Segment 1'
GRP   2 titl 'Segment 2'
GRP  11 titl 'Cable'

END

+PROG SOFILOAD URS:3
HEAD Definition of actions and loads
UNIT 5 $ units: sections in mm, geometry+loads in m
ECHO ACT Full $ Please check GAMU factors
ACT G_1
ACT G_2
ACT P
ACT C
$
$ Loads used in CSM should get TYPE none because construction stages get an own type in CSM-CS
LC 17 TYPE none TITL Torsion_to_show_CANT_3_effect
  BEAM  601  901 100 TYPE MX PA -8
  BEAM  602  902 100 TYPE MX PA  8
LC 27 TYPE none TITL Torsion_to_show_CANT_3_effect
  BEAM 1101 1901 100 TYPE MX PA  4
  BEAM 1102 1902 100 TYPE MX PA  4
LC 20 TYPE none TITL 'shortening cable 1 mm'
  CABL GRP 11 TYPE WX PA -1[mm] $ 1 mm cable shortening - StabverkÃ¼rzung
END

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG CSM URS:4
HEAD
CTRL CANT 2 $ CANT 3 only allo2wed for single CS -> CS 18 CANT 3
            $ Then in that stage the new segments is pressed in with the prefabricated shape
$
CS    8        TYPE B          TITL 'First group positioned'
CS   10        TYPE G_1        TITL 'Activate dead load'
CS   17        TYPE B          TITL '+Torsional load'
CS   18        TYPE B   CANT 3 TITL 'Adjust new member'
CS   19        TYPE B          TITL 'Add cable'
CS   20        TYPE G_1        TITL 'Deadload+cableshortening'
CS   26        TYPE B          TITL 'Torsional load removed'
CS   27        TYPE B          TITL 'New unsymmetric load'
CS   28        TYPE B   CANT 3 TITL 'Adjust new member'
CS   30        TYPE G_1        TITL 'Activate dead load'
CS   36        TYPE B          TITL 'Unsymmetric load removed'

GRP  NO  ICS1 ICSD
       -    8   10
       1   18   20
      11   19   20
       2   28   30
$     12   29   30

LC    NO  ICS1 ATIL FACT
      17   17    25
      27   27    35
      20   20     -  5.0

SCAL 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 $ no plots, no AQB-check
END

$  Then let run the file $(NAME)_csm.dat
$  will be done automatically via +apply
+apply "$(NAME)_csm.dat"

$ Remarks:
$ Please look to animator speed=0 and magnitude=200 and switch
$ through all 4000-loadcases!
$ Please find that the analysis ends in stage 36 with a symmetric shape
$ although the new group 2 has been inserted in an unsymmetric stage!!!
$ The final stage 36 looks as if it would have been analyzed without
$ construction stages = as if it would have been analyzed as single loadcase!
$
$ Cable group 11 is inserted with CANT=2 to show the difference!
$   you can set CS 19 CANT=3   and see that then the cable works as
$   inserted with the original length (precurvature = prestrain)
$
$ Cable group 12 is not used here because with CANT=2 the
$ activation in the unsymmetric state would create different
$ cable length left and right!
$
$ Please play with different settings of CTRL CANT and CS CANT   !!
$           Pre curvature is applied only for stages with CANT=3 !!
$ In particular please make a copy and run the file with CANT=2 !!!
$           Then a buckled shape will appear in the end because
$           the jumps at the nonfitting gaps are frozen !

$

$ For detail see LC 10000 runs in the created _csm.dat"

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?

!#!Info  Example:       Multistorey-building
!#!Info  Keyword:       construction stages; creep; shrinkage; Multistorey building
!#!Info  Program:       CSM
$
$

$ english file name: csm9_multistorey1.dat

$ Overview examples for bridges see csm.dat\..\design\csm31_design.dat
$
$ Please run animator with first CS loadcase without vibration (animation speed=0)

!#!Info  Example:       Design of a continious beam according to Eurocode 2
!#!Info  Keyword:       Design elements, design sections, beam, moment smoothing, shear reduction
!#!Info  Program:       DECREATOR
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2026

$!#!Chapter System Definition
$!*!Label Cross sections


!#!Chapter Structural System

+prog aqua urs:1
head Materials and cross section
norm DIN EN199X-200X

conc 1 C 25
ssla eps ulti sig 1.5 type lim

stee 2 B 500B
ssla eps ulti sig 1.15 type lim

srec 2 h 400 b 400 so 50 mno 1 mrf 2 rtyp CORN dasu 12 daso 12

srec 1 h 800 b 400 so 60 mno 1 mrf 2 rtyp ASYM dasu 20 daso 10 AY 0[o/o] AZ 0[o/o] BCYZ '0'

end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head Structural model
syst 3D gdiv -1000
ctrl MESH 1
ctrl HMIN 0.5

spt 1 x  0 0 0 fix PPMX
spt 2 x  7 0 0 fix PP
spt 3 x 14 0 0 fix PP

sln 1 npa 1 2 sno 1
sln 2 npa 2 3 sno 1

end


+prog sofiload urs:3
head Loads
act G
act Q

lc 1 type G facd 0.0 titl "Dead load"
 line SLN 1,2 type PG 70.0

lc 2 type Q titl "Live load, span 1"
 line SLN 1 type PG 30.0

lc 3 type Q titl "Live load, span 2"
 line SLN 2 type PG 30.0
end

!#!Chapter Analysis

+prog ase urs:4
head Linear FE analysis
lc ALL
end


!#!Kapitel Input Templates

+prog template urs:6
head

!*!Label BEAM Definitions

#define DesignTwoSpanBeam

echo full  extr
echo sls no

ctrl smoo yes
ctrl amin yes

dsln no 10

pos titl "Axis a-c" plac "5"
   lpos x 0.0 "A1"
   lpos x 7.0 "B1"
   lpos x 14.0 "C1"

comb 1001 (d) "1.0G(1)"
 copy 1 fact 1.0

#enddef


!*!Label DSLN Definitions

#define DesignElementHeader

echo full full

$ Constants
let#esw  0.35    ! Exterior support width
let#isw  0.20    ! Interior support width
let#d    0.74    ! Effective depth

$
dsln 10 hdiv 0.25
 dgeo SLN 1,2

#enddef

$ support face & shear sections

#define DesignSectionsOnSpan1

 dslc ref STRT s 0.0     typm SUPP
 dslc ref STRT s #esw/2  typm CFAC
 dslc ref STRT s #esw/2+#d typm SHEA
 $dslc ref STRT S  2.56 typm SECT $ max My
 dslc ref STRT S  3.5 typm SECT $ midspan

#enddef

#define DesignSectionsOnSpan2

 dslc ref END S 3.5 typm SECT $ midspan
 $dslc ref END S  2.56 typm SECT $ max My
 dslc ref END  s #esw/2+#d typm SHEA
 dslc ref END  s #esw/2  typm CFAC
 dslc ref END  s 0.0     typm SUPP

#enddef


end



!#!Chapter Design Example 1: Articulated support

!*!Label Eurocode 2: 5.3.2.2 (4)
!*!Label Moment smoothing for hinged support

+prog decreator urs:10
head Design Element and sections

#include DesignElementHeader

#include DesignSectionsOnSpan1

$ Design sections at inner support

 dslc ref STRT s 7.0-#isw-#d typm SECT $ shear section

 dslc ref STRT s 7.0-#isw typm HFAC    $ inner support face on span 1
 dslc ref STRT s 7.0     typm SUPP    $ support section
 dslc ref STRT s 7.0+#isw typm HFAC    $ inner support face on span 2

 dslc ref STRT s 7.0+#isw+#d typm SECT $ shear section

#include DesignSectionsOnSpan2

$ Calculate all load cases
lc all

end


+prog beam urs:9
Head Continuous beam ULS design

#include DesignTwoSpanBeam

end

head

ctrl mesh 1
ctrl hmin 0.15

spt 2 x 8 +1 0

spt 4 x 0 -1 0

spt 11 x 0 0 0 fix pp
spt 12 x 8 0 0 fix pypzmx
spt 13 x 8 0 1
spt 14 x 0 0 1

sln 1 npa 1 2
sln 2 npa 2 3
sln 3 npa 3 4
sln 4 npa 4 1

sln 11 npa 11 12
sln 12 npa 12 13
sln 13 npa 13 14
sln 14 npa 14 11

sar 1 t 200[mm] mno 1 qref abov
sarb out 1,2,3,4

sar 2 t 200[mm] mno 1
sarb out 11,12,13,14

end

!#!Info  Example:       Design of a T-section out of quad and beam elements
!#!Info  Keyword:       Design Elements, Design Sections, Beam, Quad, Hybrid
!#!Info  Program:       DECREATOR
!#!Info  Version:       SOiSTiK 2026


!#!Chapter System Definition
+prog template urs:7
head Constants

$Geometric input for the cross section
sto#bw 260 $ [mm]
sto#h 720  $ [mm]
sto#cv 100 $ [mm] re-bar center
sto#d #h-#cv
sto#b 200 $ [mm] support width

end


+prog aqua urs:1
head Material and Section

page unii 5
norm DIN en199x-200x
conc 1    c 35
stee 2    b 500

$ Full Cross Section
sect  1  mno 1 mrf  2 zm -120
let#zmax #h  $ [mm]
let#ytop 100 $ [mm]
let#ybot 80  $ [mm]
let#ztop 30  $ [mm]
let#zbot #zmax-#cv
poly  opz mno 1 $symmetry
vert top1  0  0
    1   1200  0
    2   1200  120
    3    160  120
    4    100  #zmax
! basic reinforcement
lay 1 type MIN mrf 2
lay 2 type MIN mrf 2
lrf 11 70   670 -70   lay 1 mrf 2 d 20 a 5[-] dist full
lrf 12 70   620 -70   lay 1 mrf 2 d 20 a 5[-] dist full
lrf 15 1150 30  -1150 lay 2 mrf 2 d 10 a 100 dist full

! shear definitions
cut 21  -200   350  200     mno 1 mrf 2 lay 1 type web
cut 22  -200   120  200   mno 1 mrf 2 lay 2 type roug
cut 23   190   220  190 -50 mno 1 mrf 2 lay 3 type flan
cut 23  -190   -50 -190 220 mno 1 mrf 2 lay 3 type flan


$Beam Cross Section Only
sect  2  mno 1 mrf  2
poly  opz mno 1
vert top1  0     0
    1   160    0
    2   100  600
    3    0   600


$ Full Cross Section
sect  3  mno 1 mrf  2 zm -120
poly  opz mno 1 $symmetry
vert top1  0  0
    1   1200  0
    2   1200  120
    3    200  120
    4    150  820
! basic reinforcement
lay 1 type MIN mrf 2
lay 2 type MIN mrf 2
lrf 11 130   790 -130 lay 1 mrf 2 d 20 a 5[-] dist full
lrf 12 130   750 -130 lay 1 mrf 2 d 20 a 5[-] dist full
lrf 15 1150 30  -1150 lay 2 mrf 2 d 22 a 100 dist full



end


+prog sofimshc urs:2
head Geometric Definition

syst 3d gdiv 10000 posz
ctrl mesh 1
ctrl hmin 0.1
ctrl deln 0

let#t 120    $thickness
let#y2 14.40 $slab length
let#x2 1.2   $half interval/field width
let#z 0.0    $long-axis vertical position -0.120

spt       1 x       0.0       0.0       #z fix ppmy
spt       2 x       0.0       #y2       #z fix yp

spt       21 x       -#x2       0.0       0.0
spt       22 x       -#x2       #y2       0.0
spt       23 x       #x2       0.0       0.0
spt       24 x       #x2       #y2       0.0

sln 1 npa 1  2  sno 2

sar 1 t #t mno 1 qref abov
 sarb na 21,22,24,23 ne 22,24,23,21

end

!#!Info  Example:       Interpolation of tendon geometry only
!#!Info  Keyword:       Design elements, design sections, beam, tendon
!#!Info  Program:       DECREATOR
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2026


!#!Chapter System Definition
+prog aqua urs:1
HEAD
ECHO FULL 0
NORM DIN en199x-200x
CONC 1 C 30
STEE 2 B 500A
STEE 11 Y 1520 FY 1520 FT 1770
SREC 1 500 250 MNO 1
SREC 2 400 250 MNO 1
END


+prog sofimshc urs:2
HEAD
ECHO FULL 0
SYST 3D GDIV 1000
CTRL MESH 1
CTRL BSEC -1 $ ignore slsc records in meshing

SPT 1 X 0 0 0 FIX PPMX
SPT 2 X 5 0 0 FIX PYPZMX
SPT 3 X 9 0 0 FIX PYPZMX

SLN 1 1 2 SNO 1 GRP 1 SDIV -5
 SLSC REF STRT,END 0.3 TYPM HFAC HFAC
 SLSC REF STRT (0.0 5.0 1.0) TYPM SECT
 SLSC REF MID TYPM SECT

SLN 2 2 3 SNO 1 GRP 2 SDIV -5
 SLSC REF STRT,END 0.3 TYPM HFAC HFAC
 SLSC REF STRT (0.0 4.0 1.0) TYPM SECT
 SLSC REF MID TYPM SECT

+prog decreator urs:5

   dsel box $ select all finite elements
   dsel grp 4,5 $ filter selection by group
lc (9001 9010 1)

end


+prog dyna urs:59
head Modal Analysis: Calculation of the response spectrum
echo full no

ctrl styp 3
eige neig 10 type rest lc 9001

modd d 5.00/100
lc 901
lc 904

let#lf 8100

$ beam elements
extr n  #lf+2 styp cqc act e $ normal force
extr vy #lf+3 styp cqc act e $ shear force vy
extr vz #lf+4 styp cqc act e $ shear force vz
extr mt #lf+5 styp cqc act e $ torsion moment
extr my #lf+6 styp cqc act e $ bending moment my
extr mz #lf+7 styp cqc act e $ bending moment mz

$ quad elements
extr mxx  #lf+32 styp cqc act e $ bending moment m-xx
extr myy  #lf+33 styp cqc act e $ bending moment m-yy
extr mxy  #lf+34 styp cqc act e $ torsion moment m-xy
extr vxx  #lf+35 styp cqc act e $ shear force v-x
extr vyy  #lf+36 styp cqc act e $ shear force v-y
extr nxx  #lf+37 styp cqc act e $ membrane force n-xx
extr nyy  #lf+38 styp cqc act e $ membrane force n-yy
extr nxy  #lf+39 styp cqc act e $ membrane shear force n-xy

$ nodes
extr u #lf+81 styp cqc act e $ displacement
extr v #lf+82 styp cqc act e $ velocity
extr a #lf+83 styp cqc act e $ acceleration

end

!#!Info  Example:       Transfer of forces to design elements having variable cross sections, and group definition
!#!Info  Keyword:       Design element, Beam elements, Quad elements, Variable cross sections, Groups
!#!Info  Program:       DECREATOR
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2026

!#!Chapter System Definition

+prog aqua urs:1  $  Cross sections
head
echo full no
norm din en199x-200x

stee 2 s 235
stee 3 b 500b


$ rectangular section

srec 3 300 250 mno 1 ref z-

prof 13 type i 400 mno 2  ref z-


$ polygon: composite

let#sf 1.0

                   102  150 -150

                   202  140 -140

    1 yb -140  ye  140 mno 1 mrf 3
    1 yb  140  ye  150 mno 2

                   102  150*#sf -150*#sf
poly opz 1 ; vert  201  140*#sf  140*#sf
                   202  140*#sf -140*#sf
cut 1 yb -150*#sf  ye -140*#sf mno 2
    1 yb -140*#sf  ye  140*#sf mno 1 mrf 3
    1 yb  140*#sf  ye  150*#sf mno 2


$ polygon: hollow

     2 3.50*#sf 0.75*#sf
     3 5.00*#sf 0.60*#sf ; 4 7.00*#sf 0.40*#sf ; 5 7.00*#sf 0.00
     6 5.00*#sf 0.00
     7 0.45*#sf 0.00 ; 8 0.00 0.00

     12 2.50*#sf 3.50*#sf

vert 1 3.00*#sf 4.00*#sf
     2 3.50*#sf 0.75*#sf
     3 5.00*#sf 0.60*#sf ; 4 7.00*#sf 0.40*#sf ; 5 7.00*#sf 0.00
     6 5.00*#sf 0.00
     7 0.45*#sf 0.00 ; 8 0.00 0.00
poly opz mno 0
vert 11 2.75*#sf 0.50*#sf
     12 2.50*#sf 3.50*#sf

$ t-section large
srec 41 1100 200 HO 200 BO 2000 mno 1 ref Z-

$ t-section small
srec 42 600 200 HO 200 BO 1000 mno 1 ref Z-

end

!#!Chapter Design Elements

+prog decreator urs:4
head

echo dsln yes
echo forc yes

!*!Label Integration at design sections

$ design element

$ with intermediate sections at intervals of 0.25m maximum
dsln no 1  ncs 1 hdiv 0.25

 $ explicit sections, which are considered in case of ULS design
 dslc ref mid s 0.0,-10.0,10.0

 $ geometry along a secondary axis
 $ start and end stations on the axis [x1 x2]
 dgeo axis "A001.B" x1 0.0 x2 40.0

 $ combined selection of finite elements using
 $ 1 the cross section frame (NCS 1)
 dsel sec
 $ 2 group numbers
 dsel grp 1,2,3,4,40,50

lc 1
end

$       1. Base point of the load train is within the range SMIN/SMAX

$ However ELLA is not able to find the least negative hogging moment (see LC 11)

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA
HEAD Example for Boussinesq method - mue=0.5 - same system as hase12
$ Boussinesq Method. In this method, the input requires
$ E modulus and poisson ratio (AQUA-BLAY). The analysis of settlement then also takes
$ into account the sum of principal stresses and thus also the horizontal stress.
$ Especially for clay with poisson ratio up to 0.5 this method gives more realistic
$ settlements.
NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1   C  25
STEE 2 S 500
END

MAT 93 E  8000 MUE 0.3000

BLAY  0    MNO 91
BLAY 23.80 MNO 92 $ from 23.80-25.00 material 92 is used
BLAY 25.00 MNO 93
BLAY 30.00 MNO 94

                  $ MNR/MNO of this line is not used !!!!!
END

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Combined pile slab foundation with 9 piles
NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1 C 30
STEE 2 S 500
sto#d 0.80
SCIT 1 #d[m] $ pile diameter
$ Soil layers including X-Pile resistance properties (best to use only BLAY)
sto#r 0.400 $ m pile radius
sto#u #d*3.1416
sto#area #r*#r*3.1416
BORE 1 X -5 Y 0. Z 0.0
  BLAY S  0.00 ES 40000.0 C  20/#u  PMAX  800/#area  PMAL   0    $ ES   = soil Es-modulus for the halfspace
  BLAY S  2.80 ES 60000.0 C  50/#u  PMAX  800/#area  PMAL   5/#d $ C    = max. pile mantle friction, here 50kN/m -> 50/#u kN/m2
  BLAY S  8.80 ES 60000.0 C  80/#u  PMAX  800/#area  PMAL 400/#d $ PMAX = max. pile foot force/pressure, here 800kN -> 800/#area kN/m2
  BLAY S 30.00 ES 60000.0 C  80/#u  PMAX  800/#area  PMAL 400/#d $ PMAL = max. pile transverse force/pressure, here 400kN/m -> 800/#area kN/m2

BORE 2 X +5 Y 0. Z 0.0
  BLAY S  0.00 ES 40000.0 C  10/#u  PMAX  250/#area  PMAL   0
  BLAY S  2.80 ES 60000.0 C  20/#u  PMAX  250/#area  PMAL   5/#d
  BLAY S  8.80 ES 60000.0 C  40/#u  PMAX  250/#area  PMAL 400/#d $ PMAX and C  smaller on this side of the structure !
  BLAY S 30.00 ES 60000.0 C  40/#u  PMAX  250/#area  PMAL 400/#d

$ Please remember: the bottom node gets a maximum nodal reaction force of PMAX + C*=.5*last-beam-length !
END

$ Comment:
$ The piles are embedded in the halfspace and interact via the halfspace.
$ This means if one pile creates a reaction in the halfspace, this
$ simultaniously induces settlements in all other halfspace nodes.
$ (or horizontal deformations for horizontal bedding effects).
$
$ This is also done in the nonlinear analysis - where the nonlinear
$ pile reaction forces interact with each other.
$ This results in a very accurate stress and force distribution
$ even if some pile zones overcome their linear limits, defined
$ in their bore profile.
$
$ In the linear run (loadcase 1), the load is carried by the slab bedding
$ as well as by the piles -> see plot reaction forces load case 1.
$ The piles are embedded in the halfspace and carry much of the load
$ in the upper part of the pile through mantle friction
$ -> see plot axial pile bedding and normal forces.
$
$ In the nonlinear run (loadcase 13), the mantle friction is reduced with the
$ input of the bore profile - nonlinear contact parameters BLAY C and PMAX.
$ This reduces the mantle friction in the upper part, the pile sinks into
$ halfspace slightly and the pile foot as well as the bottom slab
$ get higher reactions.

$ Please note that there are two possibilities of defining the nonlinear pile parameters:
$ in hase21...dat BLAY is used and also the X-Pile resistance properties are set in BLAY.
$                 This is best when you must interpolate bore profiles in the ground view
$                 as demonstrated here with 2 bore profiles
$
$ in hase22...dat and hase22...dat the X-Pile resistance properties are set with BBAX and BBLA.
$                 Then you must give a bore profile number for the beams in SOFIMSHA (or SOFIPLUS) !
$                 The advantage is that you can give an individual force (and not a pressure)
$                 to every pile.


$ J. Bellmann SOFiSTiK AG  20.02.2009 - method with BLAY, 17.08.2020

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?

#define abutment
  let#dx cos(#alfa_bri) $ bridge direction
  let#dy sin(#alfa_bri) $
  let#tx cos(#alfa)     $ transvers support direction
  let#ty sin(#alfa)     $
  let#deltalfa #alfa-#alfa_bri $ deviation support angle (90 normally)
  let#long 1.0/sin(#deltalfa)  $ elongation of b1...

  $  top connection line: ..3201-..3211    Numbers see bridgebutment_plot.pdf
  let#s #b1*#long/10
  let#dkc 0 $ offset of quad center node
  let#ntop #node+#dkc $ top node in bridge center line
  let#nbut 100000+10000*#isupp+3206 $ ..3206 center node number at top of abutment wall
  TRAN NODE FROM #ntop DNO #nbut-#ntop DZ #h
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO -5 DX  5*#s*#tx DY  5*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO -4 DX  4*#s*#tx DY  4*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO -3 DX  3*#s*#tx DY  3*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO -2 DX  2*#s*#tx DY  2*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO -1 DX  1*#s*#tx DY  1*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO  1 DX -1*#s*#tx DY -1*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO  2 DX -2*#s*#tx DY -2*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO  3 DX -3*#s*#tx DY -3*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO  4 DX -4*#s*#tx DY -4*#s*#ty
  TRAN NODE FROM #nbut DNO  5 DX -5*#s*#tx DY -5*#s*#ty

  $ abutment wall: --------------------------------------------------
  let#no1 #nbut-5 $ ..3201
  let#no2 #nbut+5 $ ..3211
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1 #no2 DNO -1000 DZ #h3      $ h3
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1 #no2 DNO -2000 DZ #h1      $ h1
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1 #no2 DNO -3000 DZ #h1+#t2  $ bottom nodes
  $ wing nodes: ============================================================================
  let#s #c2-#c4
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1-2000,#no2-2000        DNO  100 DX  -#s*#dx DY  -#s*#dy $ ..1301,1311
  let#s #c3+#t1/2
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1-1000,#no2-1000        DNO  100 DX  -#s*#dx DY  -#s*#dy $ ..2301,2311
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1,#no2                  DNO  100 DX  -#s*#dx DY  -#s*#dy $ ..3301,3311
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1,#no2,#no1+100,#no2+100 DNO 1000 DZ -#h4                $ ..4301... top
  $ bottom slab: --------------------------------------------------
  let#no1 #no1-3000 $ ..0201
  let#no2 #no2-3000 $ ..0211
  let#s #b2*#long
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1 DNO -1 DX  #s*#tx DY  #s*#ty $ ..0200 quer y txty
  TRAN NODE FROM #no2 DNO +1 DX -#s*#tx DY -#s*#ty $ ..0212 quer y txty

  TRAN NODE FROM #no1-1 #no2+1 DNO -100 DX #c1*#dx DY #c1*#dy $ front nodes ..100-..112
  let#s #c2-#c4
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1-1,#no1,#no2,#no2+1 DNO  100 DX  -#s*#dx DY  -#s*#dy $ ..300
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1-1,#no1,#no2,#no2+1 DNO  200 DX -#c2*#dx DY -#c2*#dy $ ..400
  $ connection points at wing line + 5 = #n12 nodes
  NODE #no1+300,#no1+400,#no1+500,#no1+600 NR1 #no1 #no1+100 SS X 0.20,0.40,0.60,0.80
  NODE #no2+300,#no2+400,#no2+500,#no2+600 NR1 #no2 #no2+100 SS X 0.20,0.40,0.60,0.80
  $
  let#s #b5*#long
  TRAN NODE FROM #no1+100                DNO   1 DX  -#s*#tx DY  -#s*#ty $ ..302 quer y txty

$ Comments:     (halfspace pile interaction see also hase21...dat)
$ The big difference between the linear and nonlinear analysis comes from
$ the strong horizontal bedding of the slab in the linear run.
$
$ In the nonlinear run, horizontal bedding is limited to:
$         p-horizontal <= mue*p-vertical
$ mue is fixed/preset to 0.50 = friction coefficient
$ In addition the vertical bedding in the bottom slab has been limited to 300 kN/m2
$ ( HASE-PLAS input).
$
$ This leads to a high reduction of horizontal bedding in the bottom slab
$ and to a much higher horizontal loading of the piles.
$ As the pile bedding forces are also limited by the value input in
$ bore profile 4, a redistribution of bedding force occurs
$ in the piles, and the deformations increase as well.
$ Remark: the vertical bedding of the pile foot is not limited!
$
$ In hase23_pier_foundation.dat the top of halfspace is defined 100 mm beyond the
$ bottom slab so that it has no contact to the halfspace and no bedding.

$ Please note that there are two possibilities of defining the nonlinear pile parameters:
$ in hase21...dat BLAY is used and also the X-Pile resistance properties are set in BLAY.
$                 This is best when you must interpolate bore profiles in the ground view
$                 as demonstrated here with 2 bore profiles
$
$ in hase22...dat and hase22...dat the X-Pile resistance properties are set with BBAX and BBLA.
$                 Then you must give a bore profile number for the beams in SOFIMSHA (or SOFIPLUS) !
$                 The advantage is that you can give an individual force (and not a pressure)
$                 to every pile.


$ J. Bellmann SOFiSTiK AG  20.02.2009

$ Comment:     (halfspace pile interaction see also hase21...dat)
$ In a river pier foundation, the soil often is very soft
$ in the upper part.
$ The pile cap slab only distributes the load to the piles.
$ So in this analysis, the top of halfspace is defined 100 mm beyond the
$ bottom slab so that it has no contact to the halfspace and no bedding.
$
$ Results:
$ Especially in the results of pile transverse bedding, the effect of
$ the limitation AQUA-BORE-BBLA-PMA1+PMA2 in the nonlinear run
$ is shown clearly. This results in a deeper and higher pile bending moment.
$
$ Please note that there are two possibilities of defining the nonlinear pile parameters:
$ in hase21...dat BLAY is used and also the X-Pile resistance properties are set in BLAY.
$                 This is best when you must interpolate bore profiles in the ground view
$                 as demonstrated here with 2 bore profiles
$
$ in hase22...dat and hase22...dat the X-Pile resistance properties are set with BBAX and BBLA.
$                 Then you must give a bore profile number for the beams in SOFIMSHA (or SOFIPLUS) !
$                 The advantage is that you can give an individual force (and not a pressure)
$                 to every pile.

$ J. Bellmann SOFiSTiK AG  25.02.2009

+sys del $(project).$d?

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG HASE URS:8
HEAD Analysis without big stiffnessmatrix
$   With CTRL SOLV NONL in HASE you can save to invert the
$   flexibility matrix in HASE.
$   Then ASE has to iterate the halfspace effect also in a linear analysis
$   but can use e.g. the Sparse Solver much more effective and thus
$   can be much quicker over all.
$
$   Usage:
$   HASE : CTRL SOLV NONL
$   ASE  : calculate each loadcase separate:
$     linear:      mit    SYST PROB LINE   +  STEX OPT ITER
$     nichtlinear: mit    SYST PROB NONL   +  STEX OPT ITER
$
$   The advantage of a linear analysis is,
$   that these results can be superposed correctly in MAXIMA
CTRL SOLV NONL
HALF TYPE CONS Z 2.00 FAKX 1 1 1
BORE 3
LOAR BEAM 0.90 $ Foundation area of single columns on the halfspace
               $ Attention: support force is also limited with PLAS
PLAS 250       $ max. soil contact pressure in a nonlinear analysis
END

+prog sofiload urs:3 $ Loads
HEAD Loads
LC 1 FACD 1 TITL 'Linear'
  QUAD GRP 3 TYPE PZZ P 20

LC 2 FACD 1 TITL 'Nonlinear PLAS 250'
  QUAD GRP 3 TYPE PZZ P 20
END

+PROG ASE URS:4
HEAD
SYST PROB LINE
STEX OPT ITER
LC 1
END

+PROG ASE URS:9
HEAD
SYST PROB NONL
STEX OPT ITER
LC 2
END

+PROG WING URS:7
HEAD
VIEW STAN 5 -4 -2 POSZ
VISI HIDD LINE
LC 1 ; QUAD TYPE P SCHH 0.30 FILL NO REPR DISO
LC 2 ; QUAD TYPE P SCHH 0.30 FILL NO REPR DISO
END

+PROG HASE urs:5
KOPF Bric 1
LF 1
AUSP ZR 0,1,2,3,5,7.8
AUSP BRIC "hase2_3d_bric_1"
ENDE

+PROG HASE urs:6
KOPF Bric 2
LF 1
AUSP ZR 0,1,2,3,5,7.8
AUSP BRIC "hase2_3d_bric_2" DX 1 DY 1 HMIN 1.5
ENDE

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?



!#!Info  Example:       Uneven Halfspace surface - modeling structures on multilayer foundation
!#!Info  Keyword:       uneven halfspace; BRIC
!#!Info  Program:       HASE
!#!Info  Date:          12.01.2018

!#!KAPITEL Material and System generation
+prog aqua urs:1
HEAD Variable surface level

NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
CONC 1 C 35
STEE 2 S 500
$ For concrete you can input more parameter for creep and shrinkage in AQUA MEXT EIGE
$ see CSM\..\more\real_creep_creepparameter.dat
$ Here values for long term deflection in the soil MNO 99:
$ MEXT ... VAL1 = value beta-bc1 = factor on final creep value
CONC 99 C 35 ; MEXT 99 TYPE EIGE VAL1 1.70
$
$ bore profile with 2 layers  0-10 and 10-40 m

  BLAY S  0.0 ES  90000
  BLAY S 10.0 ES 200000
  BLAY S 40.0 ES 200000

!#!KAPITEL Analysis
+PROG HASE urs:4
HEAD
CTRL SOLV NONL $ may be quicker and more efficient on big systems
HALF TYPE CONS FAKX 0.4 0.4 1.0 Z 0
BORE 1
END

+PROG ASE urs:5
HEAD Linear Test loadcases on final system
STEX OPT ITER ; LC 10 ; END $ in quicker and more efficient mode, every loadcse must run separate
STEX OPT ITER ; LC 11 ; END $ because every loadcase must be iterated.
STEX OPT ITER ; LC 12 ; END $ This iteration fulfills the halfspace flexibility equations,
END                         $ in a linear way - no material nonlinearities are applied!

+PROG CSM urs:6
head Construction stage analysis
CTRL CANT 11 $ spurious deformations have no effect on forces - only a problem of precamber, see following CSM !
             $ STEX OPT ITER     will be inserted automatically in the _csm.dat file.
CS 10 TYPE G_1      ; GRP 10 ICS1 10 PHIF 1 ; GRP 0 ICS1 10 PHIF 1 $ PHIF 1 for halfspace creeping
CS 15 TYPE C T 28                                                  $ = soil longterm behavior
CS 20 TYPE G_1      ; GRP 20 ICS1 20                               $ Please notice:
CS 25 TYPE C T 14                                                  $ It makes no sense to let the concrete creep
CS 30 TYPE G_1      ; GRP 30 ICS1 30                               $ and the soil not !!!!
CS 35 TYPE C T 14                                                  $ That would cause unaccurate force redistribution!
CS 49 TYPE B        ; GRP 50 ICS1 49 ICSD 50 $ activate columns one stage earlier - looks better
CS 50 TYPE G_1
CS 55 TYPE C T 14
CS 60 TYPE G_1      ; GRP 60 ICS1 60
CS 65 TYPE C T 14
CS 69 TYPE B        ; GRP 70 ICS1 69 ICSD 70 $ activate roof slab one stage earlier - looks better
CS 70 TYPE G_1
CS 75 TYPE C T 365*50 NCRE 2
CTRL STOR 0 ; SCAL AQ_S 0 $ no AQB check print
end
+apply "$(NAME)_csm.dat"

+PROG CSM urs:7
HEAD Precamber analysis - without +apply !
CAMB CS 69   $ zero-target-stage by 69 to be achieved.
END
$ - without +apply !
$ Please notice that without the precamber run the deformations look a little bit spurious,
$ but this is only because the magnitude in animator is high.
$
$ With precamber, the deformations are modified to get zero displacement at target stage - here 69
$ This is done to avoid spurious animations - forces are not affected by the precamber!
$
+PROG WING urs:8
HEAD
VIEW TYPE DIRE X -0.222992 Y 0.938170 Z -0.264785 AXIS NEGZ ROTA 0
LC   NO 12 ; QUAD TYPE P UNIT DEFA SCHH NO STYP NODE FILL AREA REPR DISO AVER NO
END

+PROG RESULTS
HEAD
FLT 1 NAME "n_disp.nr"  104
LC all
NODE TYPE   UZ REPR DLST
END

$
$ ZVAR :
$
$ To check the effect of the ZVAR method in HASE please plot the bedding stress as iso-area of e.g. LC 4076.
$ You will notice that the upper bottom slab at z=0 has not support bedding near the walls.
$ That is because the noded of the bottom slab there lie in the shadow of the cellar bottom slab!
$ This shadowing is an important effect on using variable z levels (ZVAR).
$ The reason is that the soil in the angle of the cellar wall and the z=0-slab is rather inactive
$ because it just goes down (or up) with the rigid wall-slab concrete angle.
$ Also the soil there is usually only refilled and may be not so stiff.
$
$ Dr. Juergen Bellmann 15.01.2018

$ Clean file folder:
+sys del $(project).$d?


!#!Info Example:    3D concrete frame structure founded in a non-homogeneous layered soil
!#!Info Program:    HASE
!#!Info Keywords:   LAYR interpolation method, Bric-Grid, X-Piles
!#!Info Author:     Dipl.-Ing. Bojan Radmanovic M.Sc.

$|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
$| The following example is only intended to show the workflow for |
$| the new 2012 features â€“ LAYR interpolation method and BRIC-GRID |
$| post-processing.                                                |
$|                                                                 |
$| Soil domain is modeled as highly non-homogeneous. User should   |
$| bear in mind that as a rule, the more the defined soil differs  |
$| from the homogeneous, the more the solution deviates from the   |
$| analytical solution of the half-space theory.                   |
$|-----------------------------------------------------------------|

!#!Chapter Materials, Bore Profiles

+PROG AQUA URS:1 $ Material, Bore Profiles
head Material, Bore Profiles
NORM  'DIN' 'en199X-200X'
$ Materials
conc 1,2 C 30
conc 9 C 30 gam 0
$ Cross sections
srec 1 mno 1 H .4[m] B .4[m]
srec 2 mno 1 H .6[m] B .4[m]
scit 9 mno 9 d 0.80[m]     $ pile without deadload (gam=0)
$
let#fact 7
let#dx #fact*3; let#dy #fact*4.5;
$ Bore profiles
let#ES0  5000;          $ stiffness parameter   [kN/mÂ²]
$
let#ES 1*#ES0;
bore 10 x #fact*5-#dx y #fact*5-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 2*#ES0;
bore 20 x #fact*7-#dx y #fact*10-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 3*#ES0;
bore 30 x #fact*3-#dx y #fact*7-#dy z 2;
  blay 0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay 2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay 4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 4*#ES0;
bore 40 x #fact*1-#dx y #fact*4-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 5*#ES0;
bore 50 x #fact*5-#dx y #fact*6-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 6*#ES0;
bore 60 x #fact*9-#dx y #fact*2-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 7*#ES0;
bore 70 x #fact*8-#dx y #fact*0-#dy z 2
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 8*#ES0;
bore 80 x #fact*0-#dx y #fact*5-#dy z 2
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 9*#ES0;
bore 90 x #fact*1-#dx y #fact*6-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 10*#ES0;
bore 100 x #fact*9-#dx y #fact*10-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$
let#ES 11*#ES0;
bore 110 x #fact*1-#dx y #fact*8-#dy z 2;
  blay  0.0 ES #ES*1 vari para
  blay  2.0 ES #ES*2 vari line DES 0.5*#ES
  blay  4.0 ES #ES*3 vari cons
  blay 20.0 ES #ES*3;
$

+PROG WING URS:8

LC  1 ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; LOAD  ; AND ; COLO C5 4000 2000 2000 2000
LC  1 ; DEFO YES 100 ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; COLO C5 2000 2000 2000 2000
LC  2 ; DEFO YES 100 ; STRU 0 0 ; AND ; COLO C5 3001 2000 2000 2000
LC 92 ; DEFO YES 100 ; STRU 0 0
LC 100; DEFO YES 100 ; STRU 0 0 $ liefert gleiches Ergebnis wie 92!

DEFO NO
SIZE LP 50 MARG NO
LC 1 ; NODE SZ SCHH 0.2
LC 2 ; NODE SZ SCHH 0.2
VIEW STAN 0  0 -1 POSY
MOVE  5 -.5  ; DRAW  5 6.5   DTYP STAN
MOVE -.5 3   ; DRAW 10.5 3   DTYP STAN
MOVE -.5 5.99   ; DRAW 10.5 5.99   DTYP STAN

LC 1  ; SECT P 100 DTYP PPLA STYP NODE SCHH 0.45
LC 2  ; SECT P 100 DTYP PPLA STYP NODE SCHH 0.45
MOVE
MOVE   0 0   ; DRAW 10   6   DTYP STAN
LC 1  ; SECT UZ 10 DTYP PPLA STYP NODE SCHH 0.
HEAD LF-2 = UK-Bodenplatte  LF-92=OK-Halbraum
LC 2  ; SECT UZ 10 DTYP PPLA STYP NODE SCHH 0.   ; AND
LC 92 ; SECT UZ 10 DTYP PPLA STYP NODE SCHH 0.
SIZE LP 75 MARG NO SPLI 3x3 HLEG 1
LC 2 ; SECT P 100 DTYP PPLA STYP NODE SCHH 0.25
loop#1 8
LC 100+#1*2 ; SECT P 100 DTYP PPLA STYP NODE SCHH 0.25
endloop
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD Example for MAXIMA
HEAD Loads, Actions with Partial Factors and Combination Coefficients
ACT G  TITL 'Dead Load'
  LC 1 DLZ 1.0
  LINE REF SLN  1,2 TYPE PZZ P1 4.0
ACT W TITL 'Wind X+'
  LC 2 TYPE W
  LINE REF SLN 1 TYPE PZ P1 5.
  LINE REF SLN 2 TYPE PZ P1 -2.5
ACT S TITL 'Snow >1000 m sea level'
  LC 3  TYPE S
  LINE REF SLN 1 TYPE PZP P1 7.5
  LC 4  TYPE S
  LINE REF SLN 2 TYPE PZP P1 7.5
ECHO FULL NO
ECHO ACT FULL
END

HEAD Superposition Ultimate Limit State

  ADD G    FACU GAMU  FACF GAMF
  ADD {Q1} FACU GAMU  FACF 0                $  leading action
    ADA W,S                                 $  actions Q category B,C or S are used only
  ADD {QI} FACU PSIU  FACF 0                $  accompanying action
    ADA W,S                                 $  actions Q category B,C or S are used only

SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP NODE TYPE PX,PZ

+PROG MAXIMA urs:5
HEAD Example for MAXIMA
HEAD Superposition ULS - Ultimate Limit State
HEAD
ECHO CHCK

  COMB 1 EXTR expl TYPE desi  BASE 2100          $ desi = fundamental combination equation 6.10
    ADD G    FACU GAMU FACF GAMF
    ADD {Q1} FACU GAMU FACF 0                    $  leading action
      ADA Q_B,Q_C,S                              $  actions Q category B,C or S are used only
    ADD {QI} FACU PSIU FACF 0                    $  accompanying action
      ADA Q_B,Q_C,S                              $  actions Q category B,C or S are used only

  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QUAD TYPE M     TITL   'ULS_QUAD'
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QNOD TYPE M     TITL   'ULS_QUAD'
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QUAD TYPE VX,VY TITL   'ULS_QUAD'
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QNOD TYPE VX,VY TITL   'ULS_QUAD'
  SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP NODE TYPE PZ    TITL   'ULS_NODE'
    $ SUPP 1 EXTR MAMI ETYP QBED TYPE P     TITL 'ULS_QUAD'
    $
    $ If QUAD beddings are available, previous line has to be activated.
    $ Bedding stresses are necessary for punching!
END
END

$ up to this bending reinforcement ratio. The shear check
$ increases perhaps the bending reinforcement up to this value.

PUNC TYPE WALL D 240[mm]
$ selects all necessary load cases from MAXIMA-ULS-superposition
$ please check the selected load cases in the result file
LC   DESI

HEAD Serviceability Limit State Quasi-Permanent Combination
ECHO CHCK
  COMB 2 EXTR expl TYPE perm  BASE 1300
    ADD G    FACU 1    FACF 1
    ADD {QI} FACU PSI2 FACF 0                $  accompanying action
      ADA Q_B,Q_C,S                          $  actions Q category B,C or S are used only

  SUPP 2 EXTR MAMI ETYP QUAD TYPE M     TITL   'SLS_QUADperm'
  SUPP 2 EXTR MAMI ETYP QNOD TYPE M     TITL   'SLS_QUADperm'
  SUPP 2 EXTR MAMI ETYP QUAD TYPE VX,VY TITL   'SLS_QUADperm'
  SUPP 2 EXTR MAMI ETYP QNOD TYPE VX,VY TITL   'SLS_QUADperm'
  SUPP 2 EXTR MAMI ETYP NODE TYPE PZ    TITL   'SLS_NODEperm'
    $SUPP 2 EXTR MAMI TYPE QBED ZUST P     TITL 'SLS_QUADperm'
END
END

+PROG MAXIMA urs:6
HEAD Example for MAXIMA Intermediate Superposition
HEAD Combination 1 DESI  1st superposition
ECHO LOAD,FACT
$ 1st superposition COMB DESI with categories XY_A and XY_B
$ It is determined which load case of XY_A and which load case of XY_B is used -> SUP EXCL
COMB 1 EXPL TYPE NONE  BASE 1100
ADD G_1   FACU GAMU FACF GAMF
ADD G_2   FACU GAMU FACF GAMF
ADD {Q1}  FACU GAMU FACF 0                    $ \|Leiteinwirkung    1leading action
  ADA XY_A,XY_B,S
ADD {QI}  FACU PSIU FACF 0                    $ \|Folgeeinwirkung   1accompanying action
  ADA XY_A,XY_B,S
$SUPP 1 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY
SUPP 1 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY FROM 2 X 1[-]   $ 1st span middle beam 2 end
SUPP 1 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY FROM 9 X 1[-]   $ 2nd span middle beam 9 end
END

+PROG MAXIMA urs:7
HEAD Example for MAXIMA Intermediate Superposition
HEAD Combination 2 DESI  2nd superposition
ECHO LOAD,FACT
$ 2nd superposition COMB DESI with categories XY_C and XY_D
$ It is determined which load case of XY_C or XY_D is used -> SUP EXEX
COMB 2 EXPL TYPE NONE  BASE 1200
ADD G_1   FACU GAMU FACF GAMF
ADD G_2   FACU GAMU FACF GAMF
ADD {Q1}  FACU GAMU FACF 0                    $ \|Leiteinwirkung    1leading action
  ADA XY_C,XY_D,S
ADD {QI}  FACU PSIU FACF 0                    $ \|Folgeeinwirkung   1accompanying action
  ADA XY_C,XY_D,S
$SUPP 2 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY
SUPP 2 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY FROM 2 X 1[-]   $ 1st span middle beam 2 end
SUPP 2 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY FROM 9 X 1[-]   $ 2nd span middle beam 9 end
END

$ Combination 1 EXPL with internally calculated intermediate superposition, results equal to combination 2 DESI
$ In a first step it is calculated whether the two possible load cases of XY_A and XY_B (due to PART Q_1 SUP EXCL one LC from XY_A
$ and one LC from XY_B) or one load case from XY_C or XY_D (due to PART Q_2 and Q_3 and SUP EXEX: only one LC from XY_C
$ or XY_D) are used. Then in a second step the determined load cases from XY_ are combined with the other actions.
$
$ For comparison of the internally calculated intermediate superposition see file  maxima_intermediate-superposition.dat
$ example with explicit input of the intermediate superposition

+PROG MAXIMA urs:8
HEAD Example for MAXIMA Load Groups
HEAD Combination 1 EXPL
ECHO LOAD,FACT
COMB 1 EXPL TYPE DESI BASE 2100
 ADD {G}   FACU GAMU  FACF GAMF
 ADD {Q1}  FACU GAMU  FACF 0
 ADD {QI}  FACU PSIU  FACF 0
$SUPP 1 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY
SUPP 1 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY FROM 2 X 1[-]   $ 1st span middle beam 2 end
SUPP 1 MAMI ETYP BEAM TYPE MY FROM 9 X 1[-]   $ 2nd span middle beam 9 end
END

+PROG RESULTS
HEAD Cylindrical masonry dam  $ Input language is English
$ List of support forces with default properties
NODE TYPE S REPR DLST
$ Change the list properties
DBO 'n_disp.nr' OPTI OFF       $ Switch off this column
DBO 'n_disp.px' ND 2 WIDT 14   $ Change decimal precision and column width
DBO 'n_disp.py' titl 'supp PY' $ Change the title of column
DBO 'n_disp.pz' UNIT 'MN'      $ Change the dimension of column
$ List of support forces with changed properties
NODE TYPE S REPR DLST
DBO $ Reset the default properties
$ List of support forces with default properties
NODE TYPE S REPR DLST
$ Change the column order
DBO 'n_disp.px' POS 5
DBO 'n_disp.py' POS 4
DBO 'n_disp.pz' POS 3
NODE TYPE S REPR DLST
$ ascending sorting
DBO 'n_disp.pz' SORT ASCE
NODE TYPE S REPR DLST
$ Multiselection of load cases and results
DBO 'n_disp.ux' WIDT 12 $ Separate support forces and dispalcements
LC 1,2
NODE TYPE S,U REPR DLST
END
