+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD Cooling Tower
SYST SPAC GDIR NEGZ GDIV 10000
$ Meridian as Hyperbolic equation (r/r0)**2 - ((z-z0)/zz)**2 = 1
$   (r1/r0)**2 - (-z0/zz)**2    = 1  => (1/zz)**2 = ((r1/r0)**2-1.)/z0**2
$   (r2/r0)**2 - ((h-z0)/zz)**2 = 1
$ parameter:
let#H   160.0 $ Total Height
let#R0   30.0 $ smallest radius
let#R1   55.0 $ Radius at bottom
let#R2   35.0 $ Radius at top
let#D1    400 $ Thickness at bottom
let#D2    220 $ Thickness at top
let#1   SQR(#r1**2-#r0**2)
LET#Z0  #H*#1*(SQR(#R2**2-#R0**2)-#1)/(#R2**2-#R1**2)
let#zz  #z0/SQR((#r1/#r0)**2-1.0)
let#m    16   $ subdivision in height
let#n    32   $ subdivision in periphery (<50)
TXB Generation of a hyperbolic cooling tower with following parameters
TXB      height       radius      thickness
TXB         0.0    #(r1,9.1)      #(d1,9.3)
TXB   #(z0,9.1)    #(r0,9.1)
TXB    #(h,8.1)    #(r2,9.1)      #(d2,9.3)
TXB
TXB Parameter zz of hyperbolic equation = #(zz,9.3)
$
let#2 #H/#m   $ delta-z
LOOP#1 #m+1 ; let#z #1*#2
   NODE #1*50+1  #r0*sqr(1.+((#z-#z0)/#zz)**2) 0.0 #z
ENDLOOP
LOOP#1 #n-1
   TRAN NODE 1 1+(#m+1)*50 50 PHIZ (#1+1)*360/#n DNO (#1+1)
endloop
$
loop#1 #m ; let#2 #1*50  $ offset of reference corner
   let#d #d1+#1/#m*(#d2-#d1)
   loop#3 #n-1
      QUAD #2+1+#3  #2+1+#3  #2+2+#3 #2+52+#3 #2+51+#3 MNO 1 T #D
   endloop
   QUAD #2+#n #2+#n #2+1 #2+51 #2+#n+50 MNO 1 T #D
endloop
NODE (1001 1032 1) 2.50 NR1 (51 1)   (1 1)    'SS'
NODE (2001 2031 1) 0.50 NR1 (1001 1) (1002 1) 'SS'
NODE  2032         0.50 NR1  1032     1001    'SS'
NODE 999 0 0 0 $ reference node
GRP 1 TITL 'Inflow Region'
BEAM (  1  32 1)  (1 1) (2001 1) KR 999 NP -1 NCS 1
BEAM (101 131 1)  (2 1) (2001 1) KR 999 NP -1 NCS 1
BEAM  132          1     2032    KR 999 NP -1 NCS 1
GRP 2 TITL 'Connectors'
BEAM (51 82 1) (51 1) (1 1)  KR ZZ NP -1 NCS 99 $ due to inplane freedom of th shell
NODE (2001 2032 1) FIX pp
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:4
HEAD SOFILOAD - free defined load distribution areas for beam systems
<TEXT>
Free loadings on beams:
=======================
Free loadings on beams may be creates by a load distribution area.

A load distribution areas may be defined either in SOFIPLUS or in SOFILOAD with
LAR and its 4 corner points. it will be converted internally into a temporary
finite element mesh which is then used to distribut the loadings. The support
reactions of that mesh will be converted to beam loads of the integral system.

It is shown with this example to define the load distribution area with an extra
outer border to catch for loadings which might be on the pathway of a bridge and
should be also conevrted to beam loads.

It is recommended to keep the load distribution areas rather small to avoid
disturbancies like lifting corners. It is suggested to proceed like in this
example: one area for every span.

         Three Span Beam: three load distribution areas:
          LAR 1            LAR 2           LAR 3
    ---------------------------------------------------
    |                |                |               |
    |   O************O****************O***********O   |
    |   *            *                *           *   |
    |   *            |                |           *   |
    |   *   span 1   *    span 2      *  span  3  *   |
    |   *            |                |           *   |
    |   *            *                *           *   |
    |   O************O****************O***********O   |
    |                |                |               |
    ---------------------------------------------------

        ** = beams   O = supports

(If a single continous load distribution are is used, a point load in one
span will create lifting forces in the adjacent span)

For extrenal loadings on the cantilevers, it is however anavoidable to have
lifting forces in the interior.

Example in space see LAR_FRAM.dat
</TEXT>
SYST SPAC
NODE      1,2,3,4,5 X 0,5,10,15,20 Y 0 FIX pp
NODE 11,12,13,14,15 X 0,5,10,15,20 Y 5 FIX pp
BEAM (  1   4 1) ( 1 1) ( 2 1)
BEAM ( 11  14 1) (11 1) (12 1)
BEAM (101 105 1) ( 1 1) (11 1)
END

!#!Chapter Load Take Down from Level 01 to Level 00

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:8
HEAD LTD from Level 01 to Level 00 with N:M assignment

ECHO LTD FULL

$With N:M assignments every source geometry will be explicitly assigned to its target geometry(/ies)
$Elaborate approach with regard to many inputs, but easy to control!

LC 10 TYPE G TITL "LTD with N:M assignment"

LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
    LTD OPT SEL SRCT SLN SRC 1,2     $ Selection source support SLN No.1 and No.2
    LTD OPT SEL TRGT SLN TRG 1       $ Selection target support SLN No.1 and
    LTD OPT SEL TRGT SPT TRG 4       $           target support SPT No.4

LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
    LTD OPT SEL SRCT SLN SRC 3       $ Selection source support SLN No.3
    LTD OPT SEL TRGT SLN TRG 2,3     $ Selection target support SLN No.2 and No.3

LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
    LTD OPT SEL SRCT SPT SRC 1,2,3   $ Selection source support SPT No.1,2,3
    LTD OPT SEL TRGT SPT TRG 1,2,3   $ Selection target support SPT No.1,2,3

END



+PROG SOFILOAD urs:9
HEAD LTD from Level 01 to Level 00 with Fall Down
ECHO LTD FULL


$With Fall Down the support forces of the source system "drop" down onto the target system
$Attention: Loads over openings will be moved if possible, otherwise they get lost!
$Checking by the user is mandatory!

LC 11 TYPE G TITL "LTD with Falldown"

LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT FALL TYPE CONS TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"

$SRCT ALL ensures that all support loads from the source system are considered
$When modeling levels with storey height (Z coordinate), the Z offset must be specified with DZ

$TYPE CONS/TRAP/MOMT specifies how support loads are distributed
$TYPE CONS -> Constant line loads
$TYPE TRAP -> Trapezoidal line load (no lifting loads = tensile forces)
$TYPE MOMT -> Moment along the line is fully depicted, tensile forces may be generated if necessary.
END



+PROG SOFILOAD urs:10
HEAD LTD from Level 01 to Level 00 with automatic target selection
ECHO LTD FULL

$With automatic target selection, the program attempts to find a suitable target geometry for each source support
$Checking by the user is mandatory!

LC 12 TYPE G TITL "LTD with AUTO assignment"
LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"

END


+PROG SOFILOAD urs:11
HEAD LTD from Level 01 to Level 00 with automatic target selection and correction
ECHO LTD FULL

$If the automatic assignment is not successful, corrections can be made
$In the following example, the source support SPT no. 2 is redistributed to target support SPT no. 1 and 3

LC 13 TYPE G TITL "LTD with AUTO + IGN"
LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
    LTD OPT IGN SRCT SPT SRC 2                  $Remove source support from transfer

LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1                    TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
    LTD OPT SEL SRCT SPT SRC 2                  $Select removed source support
    LTD OPT SEL TRGT SPT TRG 1,3                $Redistribution to target support

END


+PROG SOFILOAD urs:12
HEAD LTD from Level 01 to Level 00 with MO
ECHO LTD FULL

$If the automatic assignment is not successful, corrections can be made
$With OPT MOD, 1:1 relations can be created in abbreviated form

LC 14 TYPE G TITL "LTD LTD with AUTO + MOD"
    LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
    LTD OPT MOD SRCT SPT SRC 2 TRGT SPT TRG 1  $Redistribution from source support SPT No.2 to target support SPT No.1

END


+PROG SOFILOAD urs:13
HEAD LTD from Level 01 to Level 00 with LTDG
ECHO LTD FULL

$Target geometries can be "drawn" manually with the LTDG record

LC 15 TYPE G TITL "LTD with LTDG"
LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TYPE TRAP TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
    LTDG  X1 3  -2.5   0                   $Input target point
    LTDG  X1 5  -5   0  X2  8  -5   0      $Input target line
    LTDG  X1 8  -5   0  X2  8  -2   0      $Input target line

END


+PROG SOFILOAD urs:15
HEAD LTD with subdivision length
ECHO LTD FULL


$Long walls can be subdivided using LMAX
$Example: The 4m long wall (SLN no. 1) is divided with LMAX 1.5
$         into 4/1.25 = 3.2 -> 4 pieces of equal length

LC 16 TYPE G TITL "LTD with subdivision length"
LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT FALL TYPE CONS TRGM INDI LMAX 1.25 FROM "Level 01.cdb"

$Compare also with  LC 11 (without LMAX)
END


+PROG SOFILOAD urs:14
HEAD Summation of SW load cases
ECHO LTD FULL

$To store the SW of the target storey with transferred loads of the source storey
$into an existing LC, the following record can be used:
$LC .. TYPE REST


LC 100 TYPE G TITL "Self Weight"       $ Create SW-LC in target system
   AREA REF SAR NO 1 PROJ ZZ TYPE PG P1 6.25

LC 100 TYPE REST TITL "LTD Sum"      $ Create LTD from source system
   LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO TYPE MOMT TRGM INDI FROM "Level 01.cdb"
END

PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD silo with volume loading
SYST SPAC  GDIV 10000
ECHO FULL NO
sto#rza  0.4/sqr(2.0)  $ components x=y of the sink radius
sto#rz   3.0/sqr(2.0)  $ components x=y of the cylinder radius for mesh generation
sto#rzl  3.0           $ radius cylinder for load generation
sto#hz  10.0           $ height cylinder
sto#hza  1.3           $ height sink zone
let#diva  4            $ subdivision sink  (even number necessary)
let#div  12            $ subdivision cylinder (even number necessary)
let#divi 14            $ subdivision inside sink zone
$
QUAD PROP MNO 1 T 250[mm] POSI BELO  $ silo properties
$ centre node
NODE  1  0  0  0
$ sink zone
$ corner points of the sink
NODE 12  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ   0
NODE 13  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ  90
NODE 14  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ 180
NODE 15  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ 270
$ centre nodes of the sink (for rounding off)
NODE 23  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ  45
NODE 34  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ 135
NODE 45  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ 225
NODE 52  #rza #rza 0 PHIZ 315
$ edges of the sink
BOUN 1 TITL '1st quadrant' ; BOUN NA 13 12 NM -23 DIV #diva
BOUN 2 TITL '2nd quadrant' ; BOUN NA 14 13 NM -34 DIV #diva
BOUN 3 TITL '3rd quadrant' ; BOUN NA 15 14 NM -45 DIV #diva
BOUN 4 TITL '4th quadrant' ; BOUN NA 12 15 NM -52 DIV #diva
$
$ cylinder zone
$ nodes at sink level  (in polar coordinates)
$ corner points of the cylinder
NODE 112  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ   0
NODE 113  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ  90
NODE 114  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 180
NODE 115  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 270
$ centre nodes of the czylinder (for rounding off)
NODE 116  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ  45
NODE 117  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 135
NODE 118  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 225
NODE 119  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 315
$
$ transformation of the cylinder nodes to the height bottom level of the cylinder
TRAN NODE 112 119 INC 1 DZ -#hza DNO 100   $ target numbers increased about 100
$ edges of the cylinder
BOUN 11 TITL '1st quadrant' ; BOUN NA 212 213  NM -216 DIV #div
BOUN 12 TITL '2nd quadrant' ; BOUN NA 213 214  NM -217 DIV #div
BOUN 13 TITL '3rd quadrant' ; BOUN NA 214 215  NM -218 DIV #div
BOUN 14 TITL '4th quadrant' ; BOUN NA 215 212  NM -219 DIV #div
$ inner edge between sink and cylinder
BOUN 21 TITL 'inner edge' ; BOUN NA 12 212  DIV #divi
$
$ element mesh of the sink zone
QUAD FIT N1 12 13 213 212 M12 216 KR 1
QUAD FIT N1 13 14 214 213 M12 217 KR 1
QUAD FIT N1 14 15 215 214 M12 218 KR 1
QUAD FIT N1 15 12 212 215 M12 219 KR 1
$
$ cylinder wall
QUAD PROP MNO 1 T 250[mm] POSI BELO $ properties of the cylinder wall
TRAN NODE 11,12,13,14 INC FIT PROP X20 DZ -#hz  $ 11..14 are the edge numbers, X20 the number of the subdivisions
$
$ boundary conditions
NODE 212,213,214,215 FIX f
END

+prog sofiload urs:3 $ EC8
head Response spectra an acceleration history
$
let#lc_int 100
lc #lc_int titl 'I(t)'
func s trap t 20.0 t2 2.0 t3 3.0
$
let#ag 4         $ ground acceleration
                 $ = 10.0 for UBC spectra
let#ag_simq -1.0 $ -1 = no scaling
$
let#lc 110
lc #lc type none titl 'Sa(T)-EC8-1-A-----------'
resp type ec-1 clas A mod - ag #ag ah 1 av 0
acce type dir ax 1.0
lc #lc+1 type none titl 'ag(t)'
simq lspe #lc lint #lc_int dt 0.01 Tmin 0.01 Tmax 3.0 nfre 400 $$
     iter 10 d 5[%] ag #ag_simq
acce type noda ax 1.0
$
lc #lc+2 type none titl 'Visualisation ag(t)->Sa(T)'
reva typt time type aa lfun #lc+1 Tmin 0 Tmax 3.0 $$
     Tdif 0.01 d1 5[%] ref1 #lc rid1 2001
$
lc #lc+3 type none titl 'Recreated spectra ag(t)->Sa(T)'
reva typt time type aa lfun #lc+1 Tmin 0 Tmax 3.0 $$
     Tdif 0.01 d1 2[%] 5[%] 10[%]
acce type noda ax 1.0
$
end

!#!Info  Example:       Irregular waves
!#!Info  Keyword:       Waves, Jonswap, TMA, Pierson-Moskowitz, Stretching
!#!Info  Program:       SOFiLOAD

+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD CROSS-SECTION
NORM DIN EN199X-200X
STEE 1 S 355
STEE 2 S 355 ; MEXT 2 TYPE KR 0.30 0.02
PROF 1 CHS 300 10 MNO 1
PROF 2 CHS 300 10 MNO 2
SECT 3 ; CIRC 1 R 150 ; 2 R 140 MNO 0
WPAR ICE 50 $ MARINE GROWTH
WIND - 0.70 CHYD 1.70
end

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD IRREGULAR WAVES
ECHO FULL NO
SYST 3D GDIV 100000 GDIR NEGZ
NODE 1 -120 -15  -0.125
     2  120 -15  -0.125
     3  120  15  -0.125
     4 -120  15  -0.125
GRP 9 ; QUAD MESH 1 2 3 4 M  240 N 50 NRA 0

GRP 1
NODE 100,200 X -20  Z -25,5 ; BEAM IMSH 100 200 DIV 50 NCS 1
NODE 300,400 X -10  Z -25,5 ; BEAM IMSH 300 400 DIV 50 NCS 2
NODE 500,600 X   0  Z -25,5 ; BEAM IMSH 500 600 DIV 50 NCS 3

END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
head IRREGULAR WAVES
echo LOAD EXTR
GRP 1 ; GRP 9  WAVE SHOW

LC 100 TITL 'Jonswap - dx,dy';                              $Jonswap with current
WAVE JONS H 0.175 T 5 NF 100 TMAX 8 UC 2.0 EXPU 0.18 DX 0.5 DY 0.2 RHO 1032

LC 200 TITL 'Jonswap - average';                            $Jonswap with average values gamma and alfa
WAVE JONS H 0.1 T 5 NF 300 DX 1.0  GAM 3.3 ALF 0.0081

LC 300 TITL 'Pierson-Moskowitz' ;                           $Pierson-Moskowitz: special case of Jonswap for gamma=1
WAVE JONS H 0.1 T 5 NF 300 DX 1.0 GAM 1.0   ALF 0.0081

LC 400 TITL 'Jonswap - irrational freq.';                   $Jonswap with irrational frequency
WAVE JONS:I H 0.1 T 5 NF 300 DX 1.0  GAM 3.3 ALF 0.0081

LC 500 TITL 'Jonswap - ir frq + Wheeler strch';          $Jonswap with irrational frequency and Wheeler stretching
WAVE JONS:IW H 0.1 T 5 NF 300 DX 1.0  GAM 3.3 ALF 0.0081 D 30.0

LC 600 TITL 'Jonswap';                                      $Jonswap
WAVE JONS H 0.175 T 5  NF 300 D 2.0 DX 1.0  GAM 3.3 ALF 0.0081

LC 601 TITL 'TMA - transformed LC 601 Jonswap';             $LC 601 Jonswap transformed to TMA
WAVE TMAS H 0.175 T 5  NF 300 D 2.0 DX 1.0  GAM 3.3 ALF 0.0081

LC 602 TITL 'TMA - default (Hughes)';                       $TMA with default parameters as calculated by Hughes formulas
WAVE TMAS H 0.175 T 5  NF 300 D 2.0 DX 1.0

LC 700 TITL 'TMA - ir. freq. + Wheeler strch';           $TMA with irrational frequency and Wheeler stretching
WAVE TMAS:IW H 0.175 T 5  NF 300 D 2.0 DX 1.0

end

$ Wind as dynamic load case will be analyzed with initial stress stiffness
$ of the primary load case, but the forces of the primary loadcase are not
$ added to the results of the beams. (cables only)

+PROG DYNA urs:12
HEAD STATIC WIND I AS PRIMARY LOAD CASE
LC 100 TITL 'Static Gust Wind' ; CTRL PLC 9 ; END
LC 101 TITL 'Static Mean Wind' ; CTRL PLC 9 ; END
END
+PROG DYNA urs:13
HEAD Integration wind history I
CTRL PLC 101
CTRL RLC 1000 7
$ AS OUR CABLES HAVE EIGENFREQUENCIES ABOUT 0.2 HERTZ
$ THE TIME STEP SIZE HAS TO BE TAKEN RATHER SMALL
$ delta-t = 0.02 WORKS FINE, BUT THE UNREFLECTED USE OF
$ STEP 600 1.0 MAY CREATE INCREASING INFINITE DISPLACEMENTS,
$ HOWEVER A VALUE DEL 0.52 WILL PREVENT THAT NUMERICAL NOISE
LET#1 5 ; STEP 600*#1 1.0/#1 #1 DEL 0.52
LC 101 ; HIST U 9,17,27,40,44 LCST 101
END

+PROG DYNA urs:14
HEAD STATIC WIND II AS PRIMARY LOAD CASE
LC 200 TITL 'Static Gust Wind' ; CTRL PLC 9 ; END
LC 201 TITL 'Static Mean Wind' ; CTRL PLC 9 ; END
END
+PROG DYNA urs:15
HEAD Integration wind history II
CTRL PLC 201
CTRL RLC 2000 7
LET#1 5 ; STEP 600*#1 1.0/#1 #1 DEL 0.52
LC 201 ; HIST U 9,17,27,40,44 LCST 101

END



!#!Info  Example:       Definition and usage of secondary groups
!#!Info  Keyword:       secondary groups
!#!Info  Program:       SOFiMSHA
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2014
!#!Info  Date:          06.05.2014


+prog aqua urs:2
head Material and sections
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 C 25
conc 2 C 30
conc 3 C 35

srec 1 b 0.10[m] h 0.3[m] mno 1
srec 2 b 0.15[m] h 0.3[m] mno 2
srec 3 b 0.20[m] h 0.3[m] mno 3
end


+prog sofimshc urs:1
head System
syst 3D gdiv -1000
ctrl mesh 1
ctrl hmin 0.5
ctrl OPTI 0

$ System axes
gax A1 type AXIS ; gaxb x1 0 -1 0 x2 0 11 0
gax A2 type AXIS ; gaxb x1 5 -1 0 x2 5 11 0
gax A3 type AXIS ; gaxb x1 10 -1 0 x2 10 11 0

$ Structural points
spt 1 x  0 0 0
spt 2 x  5 0 0
spt 3 x 10 0 0
spt 4 x  0 6 0
spt 5 x  5 6 0
spt 6 x 10 6 0
spt 7 x  0 12 0
spt 8 x  5 12 0
spt 9 x 10 12 0

$ Structural lines
sln 1 npa 1 3 fix PP
sln 2 npa 4 6 fix PP
sln 3 npa 7 9 fix PP

sln 4 npa 1 7 sno 1 grp 1
sln 5 npa 2 8 sno 2 grp 2
sln 6 npa 3 9 sno 3 grp 3

$ Structural areas
sar 1 t 200 grp 11 mno 1
sarb out na 1,2,5,4 ne 2,5,4,1

sar 2 t 220 grp 12 mno 1
sarb out na 2,3,6,5 ne 3,6,5,2

sar 3 t 200 grp 13 mno 2
sarb out na 4,5,8,7 ne 5,8,7,4

sar 4 t 220 grp 14 mno 2
sarb out na 5,6,9,8 ne 6,9,8,5

end


+prog sofimsha urs:3
head Secondary groups
syst REST

$ Selection by SBOX
$ Logical 'OR': elements are either in box a or box b 'ODER': alle Elemente in Box A oder Box B
grp "BXOR" titl "SBOX selection OR"
sbox a1x 5 b1x 10 opt OR
sbox a1y 5 b1y 10 opt OR

$ Logical 'AND': elements must be in box a and box b 'UND': Elemente in Box A und Box B
grp "BXAN" titl "SBOX selection AND"
sbox a1x 5 b1x 10 opt AND
sbox a1y 5 b1y 10 opt AND

$ Selection by Properties:
grp "PRB1" titl "Beams with NCS 1 or 3"
beam '==' ncs 1,3     $ all beams with section number 1 or 3

grp "PRQ1" titl "Quads with T=250 or MNO=1"
quad '==' T 220 mno 1 $ all elements with thickness = 250mm or material no 1


$ Selection of specific element types within SBOX
grp "BQUA" titl "Quads within SBOX"
sbox a1x 5 b1x 10 opt AND
quad              $ only quads in SBOX are selected

$ Selection by primary group number
grp "GSEL" titl "Quads in Group 12 and 14"
quad GRP 12,14

end


+prog sofimsha urs:5
head Change properties
syst REST

QUAD PROP T 210
MOD QUAD GRP 'GSEL'
end


+prog sofiload urs:4
head Load application
lc 1 titl "area and line loads on BXOR"
area QGRP 'BXOR' type PG 10.0
line BGRP 'BXOR' type PG 10.0
lc 2 titl "area and line loads on BXAN"
area QGRP 'BXAN' type PG 10.0
line BGRP 'BXAN' type PG 10.0
lc 3 titl "area loads on GSEL"
area QGRP 'GSEL' type PG 10.0
end


+prog ase urs:6
head Calculation
grp 'GSEL'
lc 3
end








!#!Info  Example:       SOFIMSHA-Manual Example 6, Circular Plate with Cylinder
!#!Info  Keyword:       Meshing; Circular plate; Cylinder
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHA
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2025-03-19 16:25:40 +0100 (Wed, 19 Mar 2025) $

+PROG AQUA urs:1
HEAD Circular Plate with Cylinder
NORM DIN 1045-2008
CONC 1 C 30
STEE 2 BST 500SA
END

#define hz = 10.0 $ height cylinder

PROG SOFIMSHA urs:2
HEAD Circular Plate with Cylinder
SYST SPAC  GDIV 10000
let#rz  3.0/sqr(2.0)  $ radius cylinder
$let#hz 10.0  $ height cylinder
let#rp  3.5/sqr(2.0)  $ radius circular plate
let#teil 10  $ subdivision
$
QUAD PROP MNO 1 T 1.0 POSI ABOV C 25000.   $ plate properties
$ central node
NODE  1  0  0  0
$ central square (in polar coordinates)
let#ab #rz/2  $ size of the central square = 1/2 of the cylinder radius
NODE  2  #ab #ab 0 PHIZ   0
NODE  3  #ab #ab 0 PHIZ  90
NODE  4  #ab #ab 0 PHIZ 180
NODE  5  #ab #ab 0 PHIZ 270
BOUN 3 2 DIV #teil
BOUN 3 4 ==
GRP 0
$ quadratic plate area inside cylinder
QUAD FIT 2 3 4 5
$ corner points of the cylindrical wall
NODE 12  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ   0
NODE 13  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ  90
NODE 14  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 180
NODE 15  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 270
$ central node of the cylindrical wall (for die rounding off)
NODE 23  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ  45
NODE 34  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 135
NODE 45  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 225
NODE 52  #rz #rz 0 PHIZ 315
$ edges of the cylindrical wall
BOUN 1 TITL '1st quarter' ; BOUN NA 13 12 NM -23 DIV #teil
BOUN 2 TITL '2nd quarter' ; BOUN NA 14 13 NM -34 DIV #teil
BOUN 3 TITL '3rd quarter' ; BOUN NA 15 14 NM -45 DIV #teil
BOUN 4 TITL '4th quarter' ; BOUN NA 12 15 NM -52 DIV #teil
$ edges plate within cylinder
BOUN 11 TITL 'edge_inside' ; BOUN NA 2 12 DIV #teil
$ residual plate area inside cylinder
QUAD FIT N1 12 13 3 2 M12 23 KR 1  $ with direction of local x axis to central node
QUAD FIT N1 13 14 4 3 M12 34 KR 1
QUAD FIT N1 14 15 5 4 M12 45 KR 1
QUAD FIT N1 15 12 2 5 M12 52 KR 1
$ corner points of the plate
NODE 112  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ   0
NODE 113  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ  90  FIX PXPY
NODE 114  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ 180
NODE 115  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ 270  FIX PXPY
$ central nodes of the plate (for die rounding off)
NODE 123  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ  45
NODE 134  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ 135
NODE 145  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ 225
NODE 152  #rp #rp 0 PHIZ 315
$ edges plate outside cylinder
BOUN 21 TITL 'edge_outside' ; BOUN NA 12 112 DIV #teil/4
$ plate outside cylinder
grp 1
QUAD FIT N1 112 113 13 12 M12 123 M34 23 KR 1  $ with direction of local x axis to central node
QUAD FIT N1 113 114 14 13 M12 134 M34 34 KR 1
QUAD FIT N1 114 115 15 14 M12 145 M34 45 KR 1
QUAD FIT N1 115 112 12 15 M12 152 M34 52 KR 1
$ cylinder wall
GRP 2
QUAD PROP MNO 1 T 0.25 POSI ABOV  $ properties of the cylinder wall
TRAN NODE 1,2,3,4 INC FIT PROP X20 DZ -$(hz)    $ 1..4 edge numbers, X20 number of subdivisions
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD Circular Plate with Cylinder
LC 1
VOLU QGRP 0,2 TYPE PZ Z -($(hz)-1) P1 -10
$
LC 2
QUAD GRP 2 TYPE PZ P 0.0 X 0.0 Y 0.0 Z -$(hz) DPZ 10  $ fluid lever upper edge cylinder
QUAD GRP 0 TYPE PZ P $(hz)*10
END

+PROG ASE urs:4
HEAD Circular Plate with Cylinder
LC 1
END

$
GRP 1
NODE PROP RC #R  YC 1.0 $ ALL NODES ON THAT SPHERE
NODE 1   #R    1.0+0     0
     2   0     1.0+#R    0
     3   0     1.0+0     #R
     4   #R    1.0+#R    0
     5   0     1.0+#R    #R
     6   #R    1.0+0     #R
     7   #R    1.0+#R    #R
NODE MESH 1 2 DIV #N FIX PZZM
     MESH 2 3 DIV #N FIX PXXM
     MESH 3 1 DIV #N FIX PYYM
NODE MESH 4 7 DIV #N/2
     MESH 5 7 DIV #N/2
     MESH 6 7 DIV #N/2
$ NODE FIX FREE
QUAD PROP T 50[mm]
QUAD FIT 1 4 7 6
     FIT 2 5 7 4
     FIT 3 6 7 5
$
$ COMPARISSON SPHERE WITH COONS PATCH GEOMETRY
GRP 2
NODE PROP RC #R  YC -1.0  $ ALL NODES ON THAT SPHERE
NODE 11   #R   -1.0-0     0
     12   0    -1.0-#R    0
     13   0    -1.0-0     #R
     14   #R   -1.0-#R    0
     15   0    -1.0-#R    #R
     16   #R   -1.0-0     #R
     17   #R   -1.0-#R    #R
NODE MESH 11 12 DIV #N FIX PZZM
     MESH 12 13 DIV #N FIX PXXM
     MESH 13 11 DIV #N FIX PYYM
NODE MESH 14 17 DIV #N/2
     MESH 15 17 DIV #N/2
     MESH 16 17 DIV #N/2
NODE PROP $ RESET THE NODAL MODE
QUAD PROP T 50[mm]
QUAD FIT 11 16 17 14
     FIT 12 14 17 15
     FIT 13 15 17 16
END

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:3
HEAD QUAD-meshing of a sphere
GRP 1,2
LC 1 ; NODE 1,11 PX 100.
LC 2 ; NODE 2,12 PY 100.
LC 3 ; NODE 3,13 PZ 100.
LC 4 ; QUAD 1 9999 1 PZ 100.0
END

+PROG ASE urs:4
HEAD QUAD-meshing of a sphere
ECHO NOST,ERIN NO ; ECHO DISP
GRP 1,2
LC 1,2,3,4
END

PROG WING urs:5
HEAD
SIZE -lp 0
SCHH H3 0.3 H4 0.3
VIEW STAN 1 1 1 NEGZ
STRU 1 1
COLO C5 6001 6001 6001 6001 ; DEFO 1 1000.0 ; STRU 0 0 ; AND
COLO C5 1002 1002 1002 1002 ; DEFO NO ; STRU 0 0
COLO C5 6001 6001 6001 6001 ; DEFO 2 1000.0 ; STRU 0 0 ; AND
COLO C5 1002 1002 1002 1002 ; DEFO NO ; STRU 0 0
COLO C5 6001 6001 6001 6001 ; DEFO 3 1000.0 ; STRU 0 0 ; AND
COLO C5 1002 1002 1002 1002 ; DEFO NO ; STRU 0 0
COLO C5 6001 6001 6001 6001 ; DEFO 4 2000.0 ; STRU 0 0 ; AND
COLO C5 1002 1002 1002 1002 ; DEFO NO ; STRU 0 0
END
END
!#!Info  Example:       Modeling of attribute regions and 'free' openings
!#!Info  Keyword:       Structural model; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-04-22 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
conc 2 C 30
end

+prog sofimshc urs:4
head attribute regions
syst PESS gdiv 10000 POSY $ 2D plain stress system

ctrl mesh 2     $ create quadrilateral elements
ctrl hmin 0.5   $ global mesh density

$ a region is defined on an entirely geometrical basis
sar 1 t 0.2 mno 1 grp 1
sarb out ; slnb x1  0 0 0  x2 12 0 0
sarb out ; slnb x1 12 0 0  x2 12 8 0
sarb out ; slnb x1 12 8 0  x2  0 8 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  0 8 0  x2  0 0 0

$ attribute region changing thickness and material
sar PROP t 0.5 mno 2
sarb out ; slnb x1  1 0 0  x2  3 0 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  3 0 0  x2  3 5 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  3 5 0  x2  1 5 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  1 5 0  x2  1 0 0

$ attribute region with reduced mesh size
sar PROP H1 0.25
sarb out ; slnb x1  5 8 0  x2  7 8 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  7 8 0  x2  7 3 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  7 3 0  x2  5 3 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  5 3 0  x2  5 8 0

$ 'free' opening cutting out a hole
sar VOID
sarb out ; slnb x1  9 0 0  x2 11 0 0
sarb out ; slnb x1 11 0 0  x2 11 5 0
sarb out ; slnb x1 11 5 0  x2  9 5 0
sarb out ; slnb x1  9 5 0  x2  9 0 0

end

!#!Info  Example:       Elastic coupling of two structural regions
!#!Info  Keyword:       elastic interface
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2010-03-26 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $


+prog aqua URS:2
head material definition
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 c 30
srec 1 500 250 mno 1
end

+prog sofimshc urs:1
head two regions
syst SPAC gdiv 10000
ctrl mesh 1 ; ctrl HMIN 1.0

spt 1 x -5 -5 0
spt 2 x +5 -5 0
spt 3 x +5 +5 0
spt 4 x -5 +5 0

spt 11 x -5 -5 .5
spt 12 x +5 -5 .5
spt 13 x +5 +5 .5
spt 14 x -5 +5 .5

sln 1,2,3,4 npa 1,2,3,4 npe 2,3,4,1
sln 11,12,13,14 npa 11,12,13,14 npe 12,13,14,11

$ structural region
sar 1 grp 1 t 200 mno 1
sarb out 1,2,3,4

$ second region with elastic bedding
sar 2 grp 2 t 200 mno 1 CB 2000.0 2000.0 h1 0.5
sarb out 11,12,13,14

end

+prog sofimsha urs:3
head elastic interface
syst REST

$ regions 1 and 2 are coupled with spring elements
spri QGRP 1 2 cp 2000.0 2000.0
end

+prog sofiload urs:4
head loads
lc 1 ; area GAR 1 Type PZ 1.0
end

+prog ase urs:5
head test calculation
lc 1
end





!#!Info  Example:       Definition of secondary groups
!#!Info  Keyword:       Secondary group
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2010
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-05 $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 TYPE C 35
srec 1 H 350 B 350 mno 1
end

+prog sofimshc urs:4
head system definition
syst SPAC gdiv -1000
ctrl MESH 1 ; ctrl HMIN 0.5

spt 1 x -4 -4  0 fix PP
    2 x +4 -4  0 fix PP
    3 x +4 +4  0 fix PP
    4 x -4 +4  0 fix PP

sln 1 npa 1 grp 1 sno 1 ; slnb x2 -4 -4  -10
sln 2 npa 2 grp 1 sno 1 ; slnb x2 +4 -4  -10
sln 3 npa 3 grp 1 sno 1 ; slnb x2 +4 +4  -10
sln 4 npa 4 grp 1 sno 1 ; slnb x2 -4 +4  -10

sar 1 t 300 mno 1
 sarb out ; slnb x1  -4 -4 -2  x2 +4 -4  -2
 sarb out ; slnb x1  +4 -4 -2  x2 +4 +4  -2
 sarb out ; slnb x1  +4 +4 -2  x2 -4 +4  -2
 sarb out ; slnb x1  -4 +4 -2  x2 -4 -4  -2

sar 2 t 300 mno 1
 sarb out ; slnb x1  -4 -4 -6  x2 +4 -4  -6
 sarb out ; slnb x1  +4 -4 -6  x2 +4 +4  -6
 sarb out ; slnb x1  +4 +4 -6  x2 -4 +4  -6
 sarb out ; slnb x1  -4 +4 -6  x2 -4 -4  -6

sar 3 t 300 mno 1
 sarb out ; slnb x1  -4 -4 -10  x2 +4 -4  -10
 sarb out ; slnb x1  +4 -4 -10  x2 +4 +4  -10
 sarb out ; slnb x1  +4 +4 -10  x2 -4 +4  -10
 sarb out ; slnb x1  -4 +4 -10  x2 -4 -4  -10


grp 'BX1' titl 'Spacial selection'
 bbox zmin -6.1 zmax -5.9

grp 'LN12' titl 'Two structural lines'
 sln 1
 sln 2

grp 'ARLN' titl 'Areas and lines'
 sar 3
 sln 3

end


+prog sofiload urs:2
head loads

lc 1 titl 'PG on group BX1'
quad GRP 'BX1' type PG 100.0

lc 2 titl 'MX on group LN12'
beam GRP 'LN12' type MX 10.0

lc 3 titl 'PY on group ARLN'
quad GRP 'ARLN' type PXX 1.0
beam GRP 'ARLN' type PXX 1.0

end

!#!Info  Example:       Modeling of two touching slabs
!#!Info  Keyword:       Structural model; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-04-22 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material and sections
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 S 235
srec 1 0.5 0.2 mno 1
scit 5 D 0.01  mno 2
end

+prog sofimshc urs:4
head two connected slabs
syst fram gdiv 1000 $ 2D Frame system

$ this first example shows two slabs which are adjacent at the common
$ boundary between point 0 -5 0 and 5 -5 0.
$ As the lines are defined on an entirely geometrical basis, they will
$ be merged at the common boundary, thus both regions will be connected.
sln 11          ; slnb x1 0 -5 0  x2 5 -5 0
sln 12          ; slnb x1 5 -5 0  x2 5  0 0
sln 13          ; slnb x1 5  0 0  x2 0  0 0
sln 14 fix PP   ; slnb x1 0  0 0  x2 0 -5 0

sar 11 grp 1 t 0.2 mno 1
sarb out 11,12,13,14


sln 21          ; slnb x1  0 -5 0  x2 10 -5 0
sln 22 fix PP   ; slnb x1 10 -5 0  x2 10  0 0
sln 23          ; slnb x1 10  0 0  x2  5  0 0
sln 24          ; slnb x1  5  0 0  x2  5 -5 0

sar 21 grp 1 t 0.2 mno 1
sarb out 21,22,23,24
end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head two separated slabs
syst rest       $ keep previously created system
ctrl mesh 2     $ create quadrilateral elements
ctrl hmin 0.5   $ mesh density

$ In order to separate the two structural regions at their common boundary
$ between point 5 -5 0 and 5 0 0the endpoints of the two adjacent lines
$ must be created separately.
$ Two explicitly defined structural points at the same location will not be
$ merged by SOFiMSHC.
spt 101 5 +1 0
spt 102 5 +6 0

spt 201 5 +1 0
spt 202 5 +6 0


$ As the two lines at the boundary have different endpoints they will be treated
$ as different lines in SOFiMSHC and thus the two structural regions will not
$ be connected.
sln 51  npe 101  ; slnb x1 0 +1 0
sln 52  npa 101 102
sln 53  npa 102  ; slnb x2 0 +6 0
sln 54  fix PP   ; slnb x1 0 +6 0 x2 0 +1 0

sar 51 grp 1 t 0.2 mno 1
sarb out 51,52,53,54

sln 61 npa 201 ; slnb x2 10 +1 0
sln 62 fix PP  ; slnb 10 +1 0  10 +6 0
sln 63 npe 202 ; slnb x1 10 +6 0
sln 64 npa 202 201

sar 61 grp 1 t 0.2 mno 1
sarb out 61,62,63,64
end

+prog ase urs:3
head test calculation
lc 1 dly 1.0
end



!#!Info  Example:       Varying thickness of elements in a structural region
!#!Info  Keyword:       Structural model; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-04-22 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
conc 2 C 30
end

+prog sofimshc urs:4
head varying thickness
syst SPAC gdiv 10000 POSZ $ 3D spacial system

ctrl mesh 2     $ create quadrilateral elements
ctrl hmin 1.0   $ global mesh density

$ structural lines defined geometrically
sln 1        ; slnb x1  0 0 0  x2 10 0 0
sln 2 fix PP ; slnb x1 10 0 0  x2 10 5 0
sln 3        ; slnb x1 10 5 0  x2  0 5 0
sln 4 fix PP ; slnb x1  0 5 0  x2  0 0 0

sln 5 fix PP ; slnb x1 10  5 0  x2 10 10 0
sln 6        ; slnb x1 10 10 0  x2  0 10 0  x3 5 10 -1.5
sln 7 fix PP ; slnb x1  0 10 0  x2  0  5 0

$ Two structural regions with linearly changing thickness
sar 1 t 0.1 mno 1 mctl 1
sarb out nl 1 t 0.2
sarb out nl 2
sarb out nl 3 t 0.8
sarb out nl 4

sar 2 t 0.1 mno 1 mctl 1
sarb out nl 3 t 0.2 $ thickness at line 3 independend of previous definition
sarb out nl 5
sarb out nl 6 t 0.8
sarb out nl 7
end

!#!Info  Example:       Varying thickness using points thicknesses
!#!Info  Keyword:       Structural model; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-04-22 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
conc 2 C 30
end

+prog sofimshc urs:4
head varying thickness
syst SPAC gdiv 10000 POSZ $ 3D spacial system

ctrl mesh 2     $ create quadrilateral elements
ctrl hmin 1.0   $ global mesh density

$ structural lines
sln 1        ; slnb x1  0 0 0  x2 10 0 0
sln 2 fix PP ; slnb x1 10 0 0  x2 10 5 0
sln 3        ; slnb x1 10 5 0  x2  0 5 0
sln 4 fix PP ; slnb x1  0 5 0  x2  0 0 0

sln 5 fix PP ; slnb x1 10  5 0  x2 10 10 0
sln 6        ; slnb x1 10 10 0  x2  0 10 0
sln 7 fix PP ; slnb x1  0 10 0  x2  0  5 0

sar 1 t 0.0 mno 1 $ thickness must be set explicitly to 0.0!
sarb out nl 1,2,3,4

sar 2 t 0.2 mno 1 mctl 1
sarb out nl 3,5,6,7

$ points in area 1 with thickness values
spt 101 x  0 0 0  T 0.2
spt 102 x 10 0 0  T 0.2
spt 103 x 10 5 0  T 0.2
spt 104 x  0 5 0  T 0.2

spt 105 x 5 1 0 T 1.2
spt 106 x 5 4 0 T 1.2
end
!#!Info  Example:       Bedding of beam elements
!#!Info  Keyword:       Beam elements; Betting
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $


+prog aqua urs:2
head material and sections
norm DIN '1045-2008'
echo sect
conc 1   C  25
stee 2 BST 500

srec 1 H 0.3 B 0.3 ref UM
end


+prog sofimshc urs:4
head bedding on structural lines
syst spac gdiv 1000 POSZ
ctrl mesh 1 ; ctrl hmin 1.0

sln 1 grp 1 styp 'B' fix PZ
 $ rotational bedding in local beam direction
 slns grp 2 cd 1000.0
 slnb 0 4 0  0 0 0  $ geometry

sln 2 grp 1
 $ axial bedding in global X and Y-direction
 slns grp 3 ca 100.0  drx +1.0
 slns grp 3 ca 100.0  dry -1.0
 slnb 0 0 0  6 0 0  $ geometry

sln 3 grp 1
 $ axial bedding in global Z-direction
 slns grp 2 ca 1000.0 drz 1.0
 slnb 6 0 0  6 4 0  $ geometry

sln 4 grp 1
 $ transversal bedding in global XY-plane
 slns grp 3 cl 100.0  drz 1.0
 slnb 0 4 0  6 4 0  $ geometry

sar 1 t 0.2 grp 1 mno 1
sarb out 1,2,3,4

end

+prog sofiload urs:5
head
lc 1 ; area GAR 1 Type PG 1.0
lc 2 ; area GAR 1 Type PY -0.1
end

+prog ase urs:1
head
 lc 1,2
end







!#!Info  Example:       Coupling of displacements and rotations between structrual lines
!#!Info  Keyword:       beam elements ; coupling
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $


prog aqua urs:1
head material and sections
echo full 0
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 C 35
srec 10 H 400 B 200
srec 11 H 300 B 150
end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head system definition
syst spac gdiv 1000
ctrl mesh 2 ; ctrl hmin 1.0

loop#i 6
 let#j 10*#i
 let#y  8*#i
 let#z  5*#i
 sar #j+1 t 300 mno 1
 sarb out ; slnb  0 0+#y #z  5 0+#y #z
 sarb out ; slnb  5 0+#y #z  5 6+#y #z
 sarb out ; slnb  5 6+#y #z  0 6+#y #z
 sarb out ; slnb  0 6+#y #z  0 0+#y #z

 sar #j+2 t 200 mno 1
 sarb out ; slnb  8 0+#y #z  12 0+#y #z
 sarb out ; slnb 12 0+#y #z  12 6+#y #z
 sarb out ; slnb 12 6+#y #z   8 6+#y #z
 sarb out ; slnb  8 6+#y #z   8 0+#y #z

 sln #j+101 fix LMXPZ ;  slnb  0 0+#y #z   0 6+#y #z
 slns ca 100.0 cl 1000.0

 sln #j+102 fix LMXPZ ; slnb 12 0+#y #z  12 6+#y #z
 slns ca 100.0 cl 1000.0

 sln #j+103 ; slnb  5 0+#y #z  5 6+#y #z
 sln #j+104 ; slnb  8 0+#y #z  8 6+#y #z
endloop


$ coupling conditions are added afterwards
sln -104 ; slns fix PX ref 103   $ coupling of x-displacements between line 104 and 103
sln -114 ; slns fix PY ref 113   $ coupling of y-displacements
sln -124 ; slns fix PZ ref 123   $ coupling of z-displacements
sln -134 ; slns fix MX ref 133   $ coupling of moments about global x
sln -144 ; slns fix MY ref 143   $ coupling of moments about global y
sln -154 ; slns fix MZ ref 153   $ coupling of moments about global z
end

+prog sofiload urs:5
head loads
echo full 0
lc 1 titl 'longitudinal'
 area GAR 1,11,21,31,41,51 Type PXX +1.0
lc 2 titl 'horizontal'
 area GAR 1,11,21,31,41,51 Type PYY +0.1
lc 3 titl 'vertical'
 area GAR 1,11,21,31,41,51 Type PZZ +1.0
end

+prog ase urs:6
head solution
ctrl SPRI 0
lc 1,2,3
end



!#!Info  Example:       Coupling of displacements and rotations between structrual points
!#!Info  Keyword:       beam elements ; coupling
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $


prog aqua urs:1
head material and sections
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 C 35
srec 10 H 400 b 150
$ srec 11 H 300 b 150
end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head system definition
syst spac gdiv 1000
ctrl mesh 1 ; ctrl hmin 1.0
echo full 0 ; echo node full

loop#i 6
 let#j 10*#i
 let#y  5*#i
 let#z  3*#i
 spt 1+#j  0  #y  #z fix MM ; sptp CX val 3000.0 3000.0 1000.0
 spt 2+#j  4  #y  #z
 spt 3+#j  6  #y  #z
 spt 4+#j  10 #y  #z fix MM ; sptp CX val 3000.0 3000.0 1000.0

 sln 1+#j  1+#j 2+#j sno 10 grp 1
 sln 2+#j  3+#j 4+#j sno 10 grp 1
endloop

$ coupling conditions are added afterwards
spt  -3 ; sptp KPPZ ref 2  grp 2   $ coupling of z-displacements between point 3 and 2
spt -13 ; sptp KPPY ref 12 grp 2   $ coupling of y-displacements
spt -23 ; sptp   KP ref 22 grp 2   $ coupling of all displacements
spt -33 ; sptp  KMX ref 32 grp 2   $ coupling of moments about global x
spt -43 ; sptp  KMY ref 42 grp 2   $ coupling of moments about global y
spt -53 ; sptp   KF ref 52 grp 2   $ coupling of moments and displacements (all fixed)

end

+prog sofiload urs:5
head loads
echo full 0
lc 1 titl 'horizontal'
 line GLN 1,11,21,31,41,51 Type PYY 5.0
lc 2 titl 'longitudinal'
 line GLN 1,11,21,31,41,51 Type PXX -5.0
lc 3 titl 'vertical'
 line GLN 1,11,21,31,41,51 Type PZZ 1.0
lc 4 titl 'rotational'
 line GLN 1,11,21,31,41,51 Type MX 1.0

end

+prog ase urs:6
head solution
lc 1,2,3,4
end



!#!Info  Example:       Two crossing cables within a structural region
!#!Info  Keyword:       Structural model; line elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material and sections
echo full 0
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 S 235
scit 11 D 0.01  mno 2
end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head crossing cables
syst fram gdiv 1000 POSY

ctrl mesh 2     $ activate mesher
ctrl hmin 1.0   $ mesh density

$ structural region
spt no   x  y
    1   -4   0
    2   +4   0
    3   +4  -5
    4   -4  -5

sln no npa npe fix
    1   1   2  PP
    2   2   3  -
    3   3   4  -
    4   4   1  -

$ structural region
sar 1 grp 1 t 0.15 mno 1 mctl 1
sarb out 1,2,3,4

$ create two crossing cables within the wall
$ styp C = create cable element
$ styp Z = create one single element without sections
$ styp W = do not intersect the structural line with others
sln 101 npa 1 3 sno 11 grp 2 styp CZW
sln 102 npa 2 4 sno 11 grp 2 styp CZW

end

+prog ase urs:3
head test calculation
lc 1 dlx 1.0
end
!#!Info  Example:       Orientation of local coordinate systems of beam elements
!#!Info  Keyword:       Beam elements; Orientation
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $


+prog aqua urs:2
head asymmetric section
norm DIN '1045-2008'
echo sect
conc 1   C  25
stee 2 BST 500

sect 01 titl 'asymm_section'
poly O
vert 10  Y  0.0   Z  0.0
     11  Y  0.8   Z  0.0
     12  Y  0.8   Z  0.4
     13  Y  0.4   Z  0.4
     14  Y  0.4   Z  1.5
     15  Y  0.0   Z  1.5
     16  Y  0.0   Z  0.4
     17  Y -0.1   Z  0.4
     18  Y -0.1   Z  0.0
cut  1 zb  S
end


+prog sofimshc urs:4
head orientation of beam coordinate systems
syst spac gdiv 1000 POSZ
ctrl mesh 1 ; ctrl hmin 1.0

spt 1001 0 0 0 $ structural point

$ local z-axis of beam elements is oriented towards gravity direction
$ (=POSZ, see SYST GDIR) if no direction is given explicitly
sln 1 sno 1 styp B sdiv 0.5
 slnb x1 -5 0 0 x2 +5 0 0  x3 0 -4 0

$ local z-axis of beam elements is explicitly given
sln 2 sno 1 styp B sdiv 0.5 drx 0 1 2
 slnb x1 -5 0 -4 x2 +5 0 -4  x3 0 -4 -4

$ structural line, local z-axis aligned with global y-direction
sln 3 sno 1 styp B sdiv 0.5 kr POSY
 slnb x1 -5 0 -8 x2 +5 0 -8  x3 0 -4 -8

$ structural line, local z-axis oriented towards given structural point
sln 4 sno 1 styp B sdiv 0.5 kr 1001
 slnb x1 -5 0 -12 x2 +5 0 -12  x3 0 -4 -12

$ structural line, local z-axis aligned with global z-direction and rotated by 30 deg
sln 5 sno 1 styp B sdiv 0.5 kr POSZ drot 30.0
 slnb x1 -5 0 -16 x2 +5 0 -16  x3 0 -4 -16

end




!#!Info  Example:       Possibilities of aligning springs on beam elements
!#!Info  Keyword:       Structural model; line elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material and sections
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 S 235
srec 10 0.5 0.25 mno 1
scit 11 D 0.2 0.01  mno 2
end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head system with springs
syst SPAC gdiv 1000 POSZ     $ type of system
ctrl MESH 1 ; ctrl HMIN 0.5  $ meshing parameters

loop#i 7
 spt #i*10+1 #i*4 0 0 fix PPMY
 spt #i*10+2 #i*4 5 0 fix PZ
endloop

$ axial bedding tangential to beam direction (=default)
sln  1  1  2 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 1 ca 1000.0

$ lateral bedding perpendicular to beam direction
sln 11 11 12 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 2 cl 1000.0

$ axial bedding in positive global X-direction
sln 21 21 22 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 3 ca 1000.0 kr POSX

$ lateral bedding perpendicular to global X-direction
sln 31 31 32 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 4 cl 1000.0 kr POSZ

$ axial bedding in negative global Z-direction
sln 41 41 42 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 5 ca 1000.0 kr NEGZ

$ axial bedding oriented globally in arbitrary direction
sln 51 51 52 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 5 ca 1000.0 drx 1 0 1

end

!#!Info  Example:       Possibilities of aligning springs on beam elements
!#!Info  Keyword:       Structural model; line elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+prog aqua urs:1
head material and sections
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 S 235
srec 10 0.5 0.25 mno 1
scit 11 D 0.2 0.01  mno 2
end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head system with springs
syst SPAC gdiv 1000 POSZ     $ type of system
ctrl MESH 1 ; ctrl HMIN 0.5  $ meshing parameters
ctrl LSUP 16                 $ control of support generation: +16= generate
                             $ always springs instead of boundary elements
loop#i 7
 spt #i*10+1 #i*4 0 0 fix PPMY
 spt #i*10+2 #i*4 5 0 fix PZ
endloop

$ axial springs oriented along beam axis (=default)
sln  1  1  2 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 1 ca 1000.0

$ axial springs oriented perpendicular to the beam axis in local y-direction
sln 11 11 12 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 2 ca 1000.0 kr LOCY

$ axial springs oriented locally in z-direction + rotation
sln 21 21 22 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 3 ca 1000.0 kr LOCZ drot 60

$ axial springs oriented globally in positive X-direction
sln 31 31 32 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 4 ca 1000.0 kr POSX

$ axial springs oriented globally in negative Z-direction
sln 41 41 42 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 5 ca 1000.0 kr NEGZ

$ axial springs oriented globally in arbitrary direction
sln 51 51 52 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 6 ca 1000.0 drx 1 0 1

$ springs with transversal (lateral) stiffness perpendicular to global Z
sln 61 61 62 sno 10 ; slnb R -8
 slns grp 7 cl 1000.0 kr POSZ

end

!#!Info  Example:       Definition of bridge axis with two secondary lines
!#!Info  Keyword:       Alignment axes; Bridge-design; Beam elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2014


+PROG AQUA URS:1
head template section with varying height and width
norm DIN EN199X-200X
ctrl STYP 0
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 B 500A

$ general sections
srec 10 h 1800 b 1000 ref UM

srec 20 h 3000 b 1800
srec 21 h 4000 b 1800

$ user defined cross section
sect 1 btyp 'BEAM' titl 'section'

$ variable
tvar HEIGHT 1200  CMNT 'Default height'
tvar WIDTH  2500  CMNT 'Default width'

$ (varying) reference points
  spt  OM     0       0           MNO 0
  spt  OL  '=#WIDTH'  0           MNO 0
  spt  UL  1000       '=#HEIGHT'  MNO 0
  spt  UR -1000       '=#HEIGHT'  MNO 0
  spt  OR '=-#WIDTH'  0           MNO 0
  spt  OM     0       0           MNO 0

$ polygonal definition of shape
poly O
vert 11     0   0 REFP OM
     12     0   0 REFP OL
     13     0 200 REFP OL
     14  1000 300 REFP OM
     15     0   0 REFP UL
     16     0   0 REFP UR
     17 -1000 300 REFP OM
     18     0 200 REFP OR
     19     0   0 REFP OR
     20     0   0 REFP OM

$ shear cut
cut  1 zb S
end


+prog sofimshc urs:2
head definition of axis
syst 3D gdiv 1000 posz
echo geom FULL
ctrl topo GAXP 3 $ generate structural points & lines along placements
ctrl mesh 1      $ activate meshing of structrual system into beam elements
ctrl hmin 1.0    $ mesh size: maximum length of beam elements

$ definition of axis in plan view
gax A1 type LANE titl "central axis"
 gaxa S  0.0  X -1 0 SX 1 0     $ start point
      L 10.0                    $ straight line
      L 10.0 RA   0.0 RE 100.0  $ transition curve
      L 20.0 R  100.0           $ circular arc
      L 10.0 RA 100.0 RE  0.0   $ transition curve

 $ secondary lines with point and group offset
 gaxs A1 ids A  y +2.75  spt +10 grp +1
 gaxs A1 ids B  y -2.75  spt +20 grp +2

 $ placements on main axis
 $ - all placements are aligned parallel
 gaxp A1 ids 0 s  0.0  type 'S' grp 10 ncs 0 spt 100 alf 0.0 idp AA
 gaxp A1 ids 0 s 25.0  type 'S' grp 10 ncs 0 spt 200 alf 0.0 idp BB
 gaxp A1 ids 0 s 50.0  type 'S' grp 10 ncs 0 spt 300 alf 0.0 idp CC

 $ placements on all secondary axes
 $ - as a cross section number is given structural elements are created
 gaxp A1 ids + s  0.0  type 'S' ncs 1
 gaxp A1 ids + s 25.0  type 'S' ncs 1
 gaxp A1 ids + s 50.0  type 'S' ncs 1

 $ distribution of height along axis
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s  0.0  v 1800[mm] type -
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s  2.5  v 1800[mm] type -
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 10.0  v 1200[mm] type D-
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 15.0  v 1200[mm] type D+
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 22.5  v 1800[mm] type -
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 27.5  v 1800[mm] type -
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 35.0  v 1200[mm] type D-
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 40.0  v 1200[mm] type D+
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 47.5  v 1800[mm] type -
 gaxv A1 'HEIGHT'  s 50.0  v 1800[mm] type -

 $ points and lines at 1st support
 spt 101 ref PT 110 z 1.8 fix F->110
  sptp CZ val 1.E+6 1.0
 spt 102 ref PT 120 z 1.8 fix F->120
  sptp CZ val 1.E+6 1.0

 sln 101 npa 100 110 sno 10
 sln 102 npa 100 120 sno 10

 $ points and lines at 2nd support
 spt 201 ref PT 200 x 0 0 +10.0  FIX F

 sln 201 npa 200 210 sno 10 styp B
 sln 202 npa 200 220 sno 10 styp B
 sln 203 npa 200 201 sno '20.21'

 $ points and lines at 3rd support
 spt 301 ref PT 310 z 1.8 fix F->310
  sptp CZ val 1.E+6 1.E+6
 spt 302 ref PT 320 z 1.8 fix F->320
  sptp CZ val 1.E+6 1.0

 sln 301 npa 300 310 sno 10
 sln 302 npa 300 320 sno 10

end


+prog aqua urs:3
head Interpolation of sections along axis
echo full 0
inte 0
end

+prog ase urs:21
head test calculation
lc 1 dlz 1
end
!#!Info  Example:       Definition of variables along an axis
!#!Info  Keyword:       Alignment axes; Bridge-Design; Variables
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2014


+PROG AQUA URS:1
head material and sections
norm DIN EN199X-200X
ctrl STYP 0
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 B 500A

$ user defined cross section
sect 1 btyp 'BEAM' titl 'section'
poly O $ polygonal definition of shape
vert 11     0    0
     12  3500    0
     13  3500  200
     14  1500  300
     15  1500 1500
     16 -1500 1500
     17 -1500  300
     18 -3500  200
     19 -3500    0
     20     0    0
cut  1 zb S  $ shear cut

$ rectangular section
srec 10 H 1600 B 1000 REF UM

end


+prog sofimshc urs:4
head definition of axis with variables
syst 3D gdiv 1000 POSZ
echo GEOM FULL

$ axis in plan view
gax A1 type LANE titl "central axis"
 gaxa S  0.0  X 0 0 SX 1 0 L 50.0   $ straight line

let#S_ACT 0.0 $ station variable

$ definition of different variable distributions (see Results output in Ursula)
gaxv A1 NAME VAR1 S 0.0 V '=1.00+#S_ACT/50' TYPE FUNC  $ linear distribution
gaxv A1 NAME VAR2 S 0.0 V '=#S_ACT*(#S_ACT-50)/62.5+3' TYPE FUNC  $ quadratic parabola

end


+prog sofimshc urs:5
head example: usage of variable
syst REST
ctrl TOPO GAXP 1+2  $ generate structural points & lines along placements
ctrl MESH 1   $ activate meshing of structrual system into beam elements
ctrl HMIN 2.0 $ mesh size: maximum length of beam elements

$ the quadratic parabola is used to define two secondary axes
gaxs A1 ids A Y +4.0 Z VAR2 spt 10
gaxs A1 ids B Y -4.0 Z VAR2 spt 20

$ main girder is created by defining two placements at start and end
gaxp 'A1' S   0.0 type 'S' ncs 1
gaxp 'A1' S  50.0 type 'S'

$ placements at start and end of the two secondary axes
gaxp 'A1' ids + S   0.0 type 'S' ncs 10
gaxp 'A1' ids + S  50.0 type 'S'

end

+prog sofimshc urs:4
head definition of axis with variables
syst 3D gdiv 1000 posz
echo geom full

$ axis in plan view
gax A1 type LANE titl "central axis"
 gaxa S  0.0  X 0 0 SX 1 0 L 50.0   $ straight line

$ parabolic distribution of variable VAR2 by definition of 3 points
$ (see printout in Ursula output)
gaxv A1 VAR1 S  0.0 V +3.0
gaxv A1 VAR1 S 25.0 V -7.0 dv 0.0 TYPE D*
gaxv A1 VAR1 S 50.0 V +3.0

$ In case that no horizontal tangent is given at the second point,
$ a linear distribution is obtained.
gaxv A1 VAR2 S  0.0 V +3.0
gaxv A1 VAR2 S 25.0 V -7.0
gaxv A1 VAR2 S 50.0 V +3.0

$ The inclination can be set differently on both sides
gaxv A1 VAR3 S  0.0 V +3.0
gaxv A1 VAR3 S 25.0 V -7.0 dv +0.2 type D-
gaxv A1 VAR3 S 25.0 V -7.0 dv -0.2 type D+
gaxv A1 VAR3 S 50.0 V +3.0

end

!#!Info  Example:       Definition of bridge with varying cross-section
!#!Info  Keyword:       Alignment axes; Placements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2014


+PROG AQUA URS:1
head template section with varying height
norm DIN EN199X-200X
ctrl STYP 0
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 B 500A

$ user defined cross section
sect 1 btyp 'BEAM' titl 'section'

$ height of cross section will be variable
tvar HEIGHT 1000  CMNT 'Total height'

$ (varying) reference points
  spt  OM     0  0  MNO 0
  spt  OL  3500  0  MNO 0
  spt  UL  1500  '=#HEIGHT'  MNO 0
  spt  UR -1500  '=#HEIGHT'  MNO 0
  spt  OR -3500  0  MNO 0
  spt  OM     0  0  MNO 0

$ polygonal definition of shape
poly O
vert 11     0   0 REFP OM
     12     0   0 REFP OL
     13     0 200 REFP OL
     14  1500 300 REFP OM
     15     0   0 REFP UL
     16     0   0 REFP UR
     17 -1500 300 REFP OM
     18     0 200 REFP OR
     19     0   0 REFP OR
     20     0   0 REFP OM

$ shear cut
cut  1 zb S

end


+prog sofimshc urs:4
head definition of axis in plan view and height
syst 3D gdiv 1000 posz
ctrl TOPO GAXP 1+2 $ create structural points and lines between placements
echo geom FULL

$ definition of axis in plan view
gax A1 type LANE titl "central axis"
 gaxa S  0.0  X -1 0 SX 1 0    $ start point
      L  5.0                   $ straight line
      L 15.0 RA  0.0 RE 60.0   $ transition curve
      L 10.0 R  60.0           $ circular arc
      L 15.0 RA 60.0 RE  0.0   $ transition curve
      L  5.0                   $ straight line

$ and height
 gaxh S  0.0 H 1.0
      S 20.0 H 2.0 R 200.0
      S 50.0 H 0.0

$ definition of placements of type 'support'
$ - point, group and section number to be used for the structural system
$ - placements of type support initializes an internal variable #S_XI() which
$   allows to set the axis parameter s in terms of span widths xi(i)
gaxp A1 S  0.0 Type 'S' spt 100 grp 1 ncs 1 idp AA
gaxp A1 S 25.0 Type 'S' spt 200 grp 1 ncs 1 idp BB
gaxp A1 S 50.0 Type 'S' spt 300 grp 1 ncs 1 idp CC


$ definition of variable 'HEIGHT' along axis
$ - using the internal variable #S_XI() the parameter s can be specified
$   relatively to span widths xi
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s  0.0  v 2000[mm] type -
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s  2.5  v 2000[mm] type -
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 10.0  v 1200[mm] type D-
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 15.0  v 1200[mm] type D+
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 22.5  v 2000[mm] type -
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 27.5  v 2000[mm] type -
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 35.0  v 1200[mm] type D-
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 40.0  v 1200[mm] type D+
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 47.5  v 2000[mm] type -
gaxv A1 name HEIGHT  s 50.0  v 2000[mm] type -

end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head definition of supports and system generation
syst rest
ctrl mesh 1   $ activate meshing of structrual system into beam elements
ctrl hmin 2.0 $ mesh size: maximum length of beam elements

let#LB  4.0 $ width of bearing
let#LH  2.5 $ height of bearing

coor GAXP id A1 idp AA
 spt 101 x 0 -#LB*0.5 #LH FIX F->100
  sptp CZ val 1.e6 valq 1.e3
 spt 102 x 0 +#LB*0.5 #LH FIX F->100
  sptp CZ val 1.e6 valq 1.e3

coor GAXP id A1 idp BB
 spt 201 x 0 -#LB*0.5 #LH FIX F->200
  sptp CZ val 1.e6 valq 1.e3
 spt 202 x 0 +#LB*0.5 #LH FIX F->200
  sptp CZ val 1.e6 valq 1.e3

coor GAXP id A1 idp CC
 spt 301 x 0 -#LB*0.5 #LH FIX F->300
  sptp CZ val 1.e6 valq 1.e3
 spt 302 x 0 +#LB*0.5 #LH FIX F->300
  sptp CZ val 1.e6 valq 1.e3


end

echo full 0

head test calculation

end



!#!Info  Example:       Bridge support parametrically connected with cross-section point
!#!Info  Keyword:       Alignment axes; Bridge-Design; Variables
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2014


+PROG AQUA URS:1
head template section with varying height and width
norm DIN EN199X-200X
ctrl STYP 0
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 B 500A

$ user defined cross section
sect 1 btyp 'BEAM' titl 'section'

$ variable
tvar HEIGHT 1.20  CMNT 'Default height'
tvar WIDTH  2.50  CMNT 'Default width'

$ (varying) reference points
  spt  OM     0             0    MNO 0
  spt  OL  2500             0    MNO 0
  spt  PL  '=+#WIDTH*0.5' 300    MNO 0
  spt  UL  '=+#WIDTH*0.5'  '=#HEIGHT'  MNO 0
  spt  UR  '=-#WIDTH*0.5'  '=#HEIGHT'  MNO 0
  spt  PR  '=-#WIDTH*0.5' 300    MNO 0
  spt  OR -2500             0    MNO 0
  spt  OM     0             0    MNO 0

$ polygonal definition of shape
poly O
vert 11  0   0 REFP OM
     12  0   0 REFP OL
     13  0 200 REFP OL
     14  0   0 REFP PL
     15  0   0 REFP UL
     16  0   0 REFP UR
     17  0   0 REFP PR
     18  0 200 REFP OR
     19  0   0 REFP OR
     20  0   0 REFP OM

$ shear cut
cut  1 zb S
end


+prog sofimshc urs:3
head definition of axis with variables
syst 3D gdiv -1000
ctrl TOPO GAXP 1+2  $ generate structural points & lines along placements
ctrl MESH 1         $ activate meshing of structrual system into beam elements
ctrl HMIN 0.5       $ mesh size: maximum length of beam elements
echo GEOM FULL

gax A1
gaxa s 0.0 x 0 0 sx 1
gaxa L 40.0 R 100.0

gaxp 'A1' S  0.0 type 'S' grp 1 ncs 1 spt 100 idp P1
gaxp 'A1' S 20.0 type 'S'             spt 200 idp P2
gaxp 'A1' S 40.0 type 'S'             spt 300 idp P3

gaxv  S    V    type ID=A1 NAME=HEIGHT
      0.0  1.6[m]   -
      2.0  1.6[m]   -
      8.0  1.2[m]   D-
     12.0  1.2[m]   D+
     18.0  1.9[m]   -
     22.0  1.9[m]   -
     28.0  1.2[m]   D-
     32.0  1.2[m]   D+
     38.0  1.6[m]   -
     40.0  1.6[m]   -

gaxv  S    V     ID=A1 NAME=WIDTH type=POLY
      0.0  1.8[m]
      2.0  1.8[m]
      8.0  1.8[m]
     12.0  1.8[m]
     18.0  1.8[m]
     22.0  1.8[m]
     28.0  1.8[m]
     32.0  1.8[m]
     38.0  2.5[m]
     40.0  2.5[m]

$
#define BLOCK
 $ both structural points refer to a section point defined in AQUA
 $ --> this keeps the point fixed to the same cross-section point
 spt #base+3 ref CSP 'UL' FIX F->#base
  spts type CZ CP 1.e7 1.e3

 spt #base+4 ref CSP 'UR' FIX F->#base
  spts type CZ CP 1.e7 1.e3
#enddef

$ set coordinate system to named placement
COOR GAXP 'A1' idp P1
let#base 100
#include BLOCK

$ set coordinate system to named placement
COOR GAXP 'A1' idp P2
let#base 200
#include BLOCK

$ set coordinate system to placement at parameter
COOR GAXP 'A1' idp P3
let#base 300
#include BLOCK

COOR WRLD $ reset coordinate system
end

prog aqua urs:2
head interpolation of sections along axis
inte 0
end


!#!Info  Example:       Definition of a cupola as surface of revolution
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $


+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material definition
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
stee 2 BST 500
srec 1 h 0.5 b 0.30
end

+prog sofimshc urs:1
head cupola
syst spac gdiv 10000
ctrl WARN 383

ctrl mesh 2   $ activate meshing
ctrl hmin 0.5 $ mesh density

$ sectional curve to be rotated defined
$ using a hermite interpolation scheme
sln 101
 slnp x  0 0 -4 dx 1 0 0 type HINT  $ create horizontal tangent
 slnp x +8 0  0 dx 1 0 2

$ structural regions defined by revolving sln 101 around the Z-axis
$ HINT: As topologically closed regions cannot be meshed, they
$ should be subdivided into at least two halfs.
sar 1 t 0.1 mno 1
 sarr type ROTA gid1 101 x 0 0 0 nz 1.0 vmin 0 +180
sar 2 t 0.1 mno 1
 sarr type ROTA gid1 101 x 0 0 0 nz 1.0 vmin 0 -180

$ support at the bottom
sln 1 sno 1 fix LPZ
 slnb x1 +8 0  0 xm 0 0 0
 slns CL 100.0

end

+prog ase urs:21
head test calculation
lc 1 dlz 1.0
end
!#!Info  Example:       Definition of a freeform surface through interpolation points
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $

+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material definition
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35 ; stee 2 BST 500
end


+prog sofimshc urs:1
head Freeform surface
syst SPAC gdiv -1000 NEGZ

ctrl mesh 2    $ create quadrilateral elements
ctrl hmin 1.0  $ mesh density

$ structural lines
sln 101 fix PP ; slnb  0  0 0  10  0 0
sln 102        ; slnb 10  0 0  10 10 0
sln 103 fix PP ; slnb 10 10 0   0 10 0
sln 104        ; slnb  0 10 0   0  0 0

$ structural region
sar 1 t 0.1 h1 0.25 mno 1

 $ structural lines of outer boundary
 sarb out 101,102,103,104

 $ inner boundary = opening
 sarb in ; slnb xm 5 5 2.5 nz 1 R 1.0

$ 4x4 data-points describing the surface geometry
$ - the points will be interpolated by bicubic B-Splines
 sarp SPLI   1  1  x  0  0  0
      SPLI   2  1  x  3  0  0
      SPLI   3  1  x  7  0  0
      SPLI   4  1  x 10  0  0

      SPLI   1  2  x  0  3  0
      SPLI   2  2  x  3  3  2
      SPLI   3  2  x  7  3  2
      SPLI   4  2  x 10  3  0

      SPLI   1  3  x  0  7  0
      SPLI   2  3  x  3  7  2
      SPLI   3  3  x  7  7  2
      SPLI   4  3  x 10  7  0

      SPLI   1  4  x  0 10  0
      SPLI   2  4  x  3 10  0
      SPLI   3  4  x  7 10  0
      SPLI   4  4  x 10 10  0

end


+prog ase urs:21
head test calculation
lc 1 dlz 1.0
end
!#!Info  Example:       Intersection of a cylinder with an inclined plane
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $


prog aqua urs:1
head material
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 C 30
end

+prog sofimshc urs:3
head intersection of cylinder with plane
syst SPAC gdiv 10000 gdir posz
ctrl mesh 2
ctrl hmin 0.25

let#R 1.0 $ radius of tube


$ cylindrical surface (split in two halfs)
gax R1 typc ARC ; gaxb x1 -5 0 -#R  x2 +5 0 -#R

gar T1 type ROTA ; gara R1 x 0 0 0 nx 1 0 0 vmin 0 +180
gar T2 type ROTA ; gara R1 x 0 0 0 nx 1 0 0 vmin 0 -180

$ a planar surface
gar PL
gars 1 1 x -2.5 -5 -2.5
gars 2 1 x +2.5 -5 +2.5
gars 1 2 x -2.5 +5 -2.5
gars 2 2 x +2.5 +5 +2.5

$ compute intersection lines
gax I1 sur1 PL T1 ; sln 1 ref I1
gax I2 sur1 PL T2 ; sln 2 ref I2

$ structural area referencing the planar surface
sar 1 grp 1 mno 1 t 200[mm] ref PL

$ opening referencing the intersection curves
sar VOID
 sarb in 1,2
end


!#!Info  Example:       Intersection of a tube with a curved surface
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $


prog aqua urs:2
head material
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 c 30
stee 2 bst 500
end

prog sofimshc urs:1
head system definition
syst spac gdiv 10000

ctrl mesh 2    $ activate meshing of elements
ctrl hmin 0.5  $ mesh density
ctrl warn 383  $ do not warn about unused lines

let#RU 10.0  $ radius at top and bottom of the halfshell
let#RM  8.0  $ radius in mid
let#H  16.0  $ height of shell

let#H2  6.0  $ elevation of tube axis
let#R2  2.5  $ radius of tube
let#L2 12.0  $ length of tube

$ two curves bounding the shell
gax G1 typc ARC ; gaxb x1 0 +#RU 0 x2 0 +#RU -#H x3 0 +#RM -0.5*#H
gax G2 typc ARC ; gaxb x1 0 -#RU 0 x2 0 -#RU -#H x3 0 -#RM -0.5*#H

$ geometry of surface by revolving G1 by 180Â° around global Z
gar S1 type ROTA
gara G1 x 0 0 0 nz -1.0 vmax 180.0

$ define the tube geometry crossing the surface
$ - the surface is split into two halfs in order to stabilize
$   geometric operations and to allow a more regular mesh
gax H1 typc ARC ; gaxb x1 0 0 -#H2+#R2 x2 #L2 0 -#H2+#R2
gax H2 typc ARC ; gaxb x1 0 0 -#H2-#R2 x2 #L2 0 -#H2-#R2

gar TB1 type ROTA ; gara H1 x 0 0 -#H2 nx 1.0 vmax 180.0
gar TB2 type ROTA ; gara H2 x 0 0 -#H2 nx 1.0 vmax 180.0

$ intersection of the two tubular halfs with surface S1
gax I1 sur1 S1 TB1
gax I2 sur1 S1 TB2


$ define the structural region on the shell geometry
sln 1 ref G1
sln 2 ref G2
sln 3 ; slnb x1 0 +#RU   0 x2 0 -#RU   0 x3 #RU 0   0
sln 4 ; slnb x1 0 +#RU -#H x2 0 -#RU -#H x3 #RU 0 -#H

sln 101 sdiv 0.5 ref I1 $ references the geometry of the intersection curve
sln 102 sdiv 0.5 ref I2 $ references the geometry of the intersection curve

sar 1 t 0.25 ref S1 mno 1
sarb out 1,2,3,4   $ lines on outer boundary
sarb in 101,102    $ structural lines forming the opening


$ define structural regions on the outer parts of the tube
sln 11 ref H1
sln 12 ref H2
sln 13 ; slnb x1 #L2 0 -#H2+#R2 x2 #L2 0 -#H2-#R2 x3 #L2 -#R2 -#H2
sln 14 ; slnb x1 #L2 0 -#H2-#R2 x2 #L2 0 -#H2+#R2 x3 #L2 +#R2 -#H2

sar 11 t 0.25 ref TB1
sarb out 11,12,13,101

sar 12 t 0.25 ref TB2
sarb out 11,12,14,102

end

!#!Info  Example:       definition of a NURBS surface with trimming boundary edges
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $


PROG SOFIMSHC urs:1
head NURBS surface
syst SPAC gdiv 10000 NEGZ
ctrl MESH 2 ; ctrl HMIN 1.0

sar - t 0.2 $ mctl 1
  $ GEOMETRY OF BOUNDARY
  $ first boundary curve given as cubic NURBS-curve

   slnn s   0.000000 degr   3  $ knot-vector
   slnn s   0.000000

   slnp x  -2.729712    5.000000    7.335983
   slnp x  -6.084722    5.000000    9.588157
   slnp x  -8.726326    5.000000   10.116109
   slnp x -10.047436    5.000000   10.114234

  $ rational (weights <> 1.0) NURBS-curve of degree 2

   slnn s   0.000000
   slnn s   7.853982
   slnn s   7.853982
   slnn s  15.707963
   slnn s  15.707963

   slnp x   0.000000    5.000000    0.000000  w  1.000000

  $ 2 knot-vectors of the surface-geometry in s- and t-direction

  sarn s   0.000000

  sarn s   5.963454

!#!Info  Example:       Definition of a planar region
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-11-23 $


+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 C 35
end

PROG sofimshc urs:3
head system
syst SPAC gdiv -1000
ctrl MESH 1 ; ctrl HMIN 0.5

sar 1 t 250 mno 1
sarr PLAN x 0 0 0 sx 4 3 0 tx 1.5 -2 0

sar 2 t 250 mno 1
sarr PLAN x 0 0 -2 sx 1 ty -1 umin -2.0 +4.0 vmin 0.0 3.0

sar 3 t 250 mno 1
sarr PLAN x 0 0 -4 nz -1 sx 1 1 umin -2.0 +2.0 vmin -2.0 +2.0


end

!#!Info  Example:       Definition of a surface of revolution
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $

+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material definition
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35 ; stee 2 BST 500
end

+prog sofimshc urs:1
head cooling tower
syst spac gdiv -100 posz

ctrl mesh 2   $ create quadrilateral elements
ctrl hmin 2.5 $ size of elements

$ define parameters
let#R1 22.0  $ radius at basement
let#R2 15.0  $ radius in mid
let#R3 18.0  $ radius at upper end
let#H  50.0  $ height

sln 1 ; slnb x1 +#R1 0 0 x2 +#R3 0 -#H x3 +#R2 0 -0.5*#H

sar 1 t 0.2 mno 1 mctl 1
sarr type ROTA gid1 1 x 0 0 0 nz 1.0 vmin 0.0 vmax 180.0

sar 2 t 0.2 mno 1 mctl 1
sarr type ROTA gid1 1 x 0 0 0 nz 1.0 vmin 0.0 vmax -180.0

sln 101
 slnb x1 +#R1 0 0 xm 0 0 0 nz 1.0
 slns CA 10000.0 CL 100.0 KR POSZ
end


!#!Info  Example:       Definition of a cupola as surface of revolution
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $


+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material definition
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
end

prog sofimshc urs:1
head spherical surface
syst spac gdiv 10000

ctrl mesh 2
ctrl tolg -0.01[m]
ctrl hmin 0.5[m] $ mesh density
ctrl efac 20
ctrl fine -1
ctrl prog 1.238

let#R 5.0 $ radius of sphere

$ sectional curve to be rotated
sln 1 ; slnb z1 -#R z2 #R xm 0 0 0 nx 0 1 0

$ two structural regions each forming a halfshell
$ HINT: As topologically closed regions cannot be meshed, they
$ must be subdivided into at least two halfs.
sar 1 t 0.25 mno 1
sarr type ROTA gid1 1 x 0 0 0 nz 1 vmin 0 +180
sar 2 t 0.25 mno 1
sarr type ROTA gid1 1 x 0 0 0 nz 1 vmin 0 -180
end

!#!Info  Example:       Definition of a sweep surface
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geometric modeling; area elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2011-08-01 $


+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35
end

PROG sofimshc urs:3
head system
syst SPAC gdiv -1000
ctrl MESH 1 ; ctrl HMIN 0.5

let#R 1.8
$ two cross-section curves
sln 1 ; slnb y1 -#R y2 +#R xm 0 0 0 nx 1
sln 2 ; slnb y1 +#R y2 -#R xm 0 0 0 nx 1

$ trajectory curve along which the cross section curves will be swept
$ The local z-Axis should be kept consistent along the whole axis
gax G1
 gaxb x1  0 0 0 x2  2 0 0 nz 1.0
 gaxb x1  2 0 0 x2  6 4 0 nz 1.0 R +4.0
 gaxb x1  6 4 0 x2 10 8 0 nz 1.0 R -4.0
 gaxb x1 10 8 0 x2 12 8 0 nz 1.0

$ structural areas defined by sweeping the section curves along the trajectory
sar 1 t 0.2 mctl 1
sarr SWEE gid1 1 gid2 G1

sar 2 t 0.2 mctl 1
sarr SWEE gid1 2 gid2 G1
end

!#!Info  Example:       Modeling of back-anchored, embedded wall
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geotechnics; Interface elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

// variables ========================================================================

+PROG TEMPLATE urs:1
HEAD Global parameters

$ central parameter for variation:
$   depth of foot of diaphragm wall measured from subsoil surface level
STO#T 11.0

$ system
STO#W 25.0        $ model width
STO#H 20.0        $ model height
STO#W_TRENCH  6.0 $ trench width
STO#X1_TLOAD  9.0 $ start of traffic load (left side)
STO#X2_TLOAD 15.0 $ end of traffic load (right side)

$ anchor
STO#Y_ANCHR   1.5  $ vertical position of anchor
STO#C_ANCHR 1.5E6  $ [kN/m] anchor stiffness
STO#ANGLE_ANCHR 35 $ [Â°] anchor angle
STO#L_ANCHR   4.0  $ [m] free anchor length
STO#L_GROUT   5.0  $ [m] length of grouting body

$ excavation depths
STO#T1 2.0
STO#T2 4.0
STO#T3 6.0

END


// system + materials ===============================================================

+PROG AQUA urs:2
HEAD Materials
NORM EN 199x-200x

$ diaphragm wall
MAT 1 E 3e7 MUE 0.18 GAM 24 TITL 'Wall'
SREC 1 H 800 B 1000  MNO 1

$ soil material
let#phi 27.5
let#coh 10.0
  MAT  2 E 30000 MUE 0.3  GAM 20  GAMA 19  TITL 'Soil'
  NMAT 2 MOHR P1 #phi P2 #coh P3 0 P4 0.0
  $MAT  2 E 90000 MUE 0.15  GAM 20  GAMA 19  TITL 'Soil'
  $NMAT 2 GRAN P1 #phi P2 #coh P3 0 P4 0.0  P5 30000 P6 0.6 P9 30000

$ interface definition
MAT  22 E 30000 MUE 0.3  GAM 20  GAMA 19  TITL 'Interface'
BMAT 22 MREF 22  H 0.4  MUE tan(2/3*#phi) COH #coh  CRAC 0.0

$ working law
SFLA 101 TYPE MYU F 500

$ grouting body
MAT    51   E  .3000E+08  MUE 0.20 GAM 25.00 GAMA 15.00
SVAL   51 MNO   51        A  .4550E-02       IY 1.E-5

END

+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:3
HEAD System
SYST PAIN GDIV 10000 GDIR POSY
ECHO SYST FULL

$ meshing parameters
CTRL MESH 2 ; CTRL HMIN 0.7


$ define the bulk body
SPT NO      X     Y
     1   0.0    0.0
     2   #W     0.0
     3   #W     #H
     4   0.0    #H

SLN  1 1 2
SLN  2 1 4 FIX PX

SLN  3 2 3 FIX PX
SLN  4 3 4 FIX PY

SAR  1  MNO 2  T 1.0[m]  GRP 1  H1 0.7
SARB OUT NL 1,2,3,4


$ define the excavation domains as attribute areas
                      SPT 102 X #W_TRENCH Y 0.0
SPT 201 X 0.0 Y #T1 ; SPT 202 X #W_TRENCH Y #T1
SPT 301 X 0.0 Y #T2 ; SPT 302 X #W_TRENCH Y #T2
SPT 401 X 0.0 Y #T3 ; SPT 402 X #W_TRENCH Y #T3
                      SPT 502 X #W_TRENCH Y #T

SAR PROP GRP 11 MNO 2
SARB OUT NA 1 102 ; SARB OUT NA 102 202 ; SARB OUT NA 202 201 ; SARB OUT NA 201 1

SAR PROP GRP 12 MNO 2
SARB OUT NA 201 202 ; SARB OUT NA 202 302 ; SARB OUT NA 302 301 ; SARB OUT NA 301 201

SAR PROP GRP 13 MNO 2
SARB OUT NA 301 302 ; SARB OUT NA 302 402 ; SARB OUT NA 402 401 ; SARB OUT NA 401 301

$ diaphragm wall
SLN 11 102 502 GRP 20 SNO 1 SDIV 0.15  $FIXA 101 FIXE 101 FIMA 101 FIME 101
SLNS  GRP 21 REFT *SAR  MNO 22 D 0.05  $ create interface layers on both sides

$ anchor + grouting body
SPT 1002 X #W_TRENCH Y #Y_ANCHR SX 1 0 0
SPT 2002 X #L_ANCHR  Y #ANGLE_ANCHR  REF PPOL 1002  $ relative to point 1002 in polar coordinates
SPT 3002 X #L_GROUT  Y #ANGLE_ANCHR  REF PPOL 2002  $ relative to point 2002 in polar coordinates

SLN NPA 1002 2002 GRP 50 STYP TZ SNO 51 SDIV 0.15  $ anchor (defined as truss element, not embedded in mesh)
SLN NPA 2002 3002 GRP 51 STYP CE SNO 51 SDIV 0.15  $ grouting body (defined as cable, embedded in mesh)

END

// external loading =================================================================

+PROG SOFILOAD urs:5
HEAD External loading
LC 101 TITL 'Permanent load'
LINE  TYPE PYY P1 10 0 0  P2 10 #W 0

LC 102 TITL 'Variable load'
LINE  TYPE PYY P1 50 #X1_TLOAD 0  P2 50 #X2_TLOAD 0

LC 103 TITL 'Prestressing'
TRUS  GRP 50 TYPE VX PA 100

END


// construction stages ==============================================================

-PROG TALPA urs:6
HEAD CSG
$ global control options (defined prior to 1st CS)
CSYS PROB NONL
CCRL ITER 30 0.005
CCRL WARN 7
CCRL BEAM DBM

CS NO 1  TITL 'In-situ'
    CGW    HW 9999                            $ ground water level
    CGRP   NO 1,11,12,13  ACT SITU K 0.5      $ lateral earth pressure coefficient
    CGRP   NO 21          ACT IN   ACT2 LINE  $ interface elements

CS NO 2  TITL  'Installation wall'
    CGRP   NO 21     ACT MODI ACT2 FULL       $ interface elements now nonlinear
    CGRP   NO 20     ACT IN                   $ activation of corresponding groups

CS NO 3  TITL  'Activation of surcharge loads'
    CLOA 101,102  OPT ACT

CS NO 4  TITL  '1st excavation step'
    CGRP   NO 11     ACT EX                   $ excavation

CS NO 5  TITL  '2nd excavation step'
    CCRL STEP 3 SAVE 0
    CGRP   NO 12     ACT EX                   $ excavation

CS NO 6  TITL  'Anchor + prestressing'
    CGRP   NO 50     ACT IN  PTYP FFIN        $ installation of anchor
    CGRP   NO 51     ACT IN                   $ installation of grouting body
    CLOA   NO 103    OPT TEMP

CS NO 7  TITL  '3rd excavation step'
    CCRL STEP 3 SAVE 0
    CGRP   NO 13     ACT EX                   $ excavation

END


-apply "$(NAME)_csg.dat"

!#!Info  Example:       Excavation pit with retaining wall as 3D-model
!#!Info  Keyword:       volume model ; extrusion to bric-elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2012
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2010-03-26 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $

+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material definition
norm din 1045-2008
conc 1 C 30
srec 1 0.5 0.25 mno 1
end

+prog sofimshc urs:1
head lines and surfaces
syst SPAC gdiv 50000
ctrl mesh 1 ; ctrl hmin 2.0

$ some parameters
let#b  5.0
let#r1 5.0
let#r2 5.25

$ points, lines and region of inner circle
spt 1 x +#r1 +#b 0
spt 2 x +#r1 -#b 0
spt 3 x -#r1 -#b 0
spt 4 x -#r1 +#b 0

sln 1 npa 1 2
sln 2 npa 2 3 ; slnb nz -1 xm 0 -#b 0
sln 3 npa 3 4
sln 4 npa 4 1 ; slnb nz -1 xm 0 +#b 0

sar 1 t 0.0 grp 1 h1 1.0
sarb out 1,2,3,4

$ points lines and region of second circle
spt 11 x +#r2 +#b 0
spt 12 x +#r2 -#b 0
spt 13 x -#r2 -#b 0
spt 14 x -#r2 +#b 0

sln 11 npa 11 12 ; slns ref 1
sln 12 npa 12 13 ; slns ref 2 ; slnb nz -1 xm 0 -#b 0
sln 13 npa 13 14 ; slns ref 3
sln 14 npa 14 11 ; slns ref 4 ; slnb nz -1 xm 0 +#b 0

sar 2 t 0.1 grp 2 h1 0.5
sarb out 11,12,13,14
sarb in 1,2,3,4

$ third circle
spt 21 x +25 +25 0
spt 22 x +25 -25 0
spt 23 x -25 -25 0
spt 24 x -25 +25 0

sln 21 npa 21 22
sln 22 npa 22 23
sln 23 npa 23 24
sln 24 npa 24 21

sar 3 t 0.0 grp 3
sarb out 21,22,23,24
sarb in 11,12,13,14

end


+prog sofimsha urs:3
head extrusion to bric mesh
syst REST

let#z1 10.0
let#z2  3.0
let#z3  5.0

$ structural lines are extruded to quad elements of the retaining wall
grp 21 ref 21
quad PROP T 0.2 mno 1
tran GLN 1,2,3,4 dz #z1 prop X10 dno 50
tran GLN 51,52,53,54 dz #z2 prop X5

$ quad-layer used for coupling
grp 22 ref 22
$ quad PROP T 0.0 nra 0
tran GLN 11,12,13,14 dz #z1 prop X20 dno 50
tran GLN 61,62,63,64 dz #z2 prop X5

$ quad elements on the ground level copied to different depths
grp 4 ; tran QUAD grp 1 dz #z1
grp 6 ; tran QUAD grp 3 dz #z1

grp 7 ; tran QUAD grp 1 dz #z1+#z2
grp 8 ; tran QUAD grp 2 dz #z1+#z2
grp 9 ; tran QUAD grp 3 dz #z1+#z2

grp 10 ; tran QUAD grp 1,2,3 dz #z1+#z2+#z3

$ set default parameter of brics
bric PROP mno 1

$ quad-elements are extruded to hexahedral mesh
grp 11
 tran QUAD grp 4 dz #z2 prop X5
 tran QUAD grp 7 dz #z3 prop X5

grp 12
 tran QUAD grp 8 dz #z3 prop X5

grp 13
 tran QUAD grp 3 dz #z1 prop X10
 tran QUAD grp 6 dz #z2 prop X5
 tran QUAD grp 9 dz #z3 prop X5


$ interface between retaining wall and soil body
grp 23 ; spri QREF 21 22 CP 1000.0

$ delete elements for better visualization
del QUAD 1 2 GRP
del QUAD 1 21 GRP xmin -30 -30 0 xmax -0.5 +30 20
del BRIC 11 13 GRP xmin -30 -30 0 xmax -0.5 +30 20
del SPRI 23 23 GRP xmin -30 -30 0 xmax -0.5 +30 20
end


!#!Info  Example:       Excavation pit with retaining wall as 3D-model
!#!Info  Keyword:       volume model ; extrusion to bric-elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2016
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2015-03-13 $


!#!Kapitel System

+prog aqua urs:1
kopf Material
echo VOLL VOLL
norm DIN EN199X-200X

beto 1 C 35

mat  nr    E   mue  gam  gama  bez
     11  100000 0.3   18   10   "Soil"

nmat nr    art    p1      p2
     11    mohr   30      10

bmat 11 c 50000 cq 10000 mue 0.5 coh 10
ende


+prog sofimshc urs:2
kopf master ground view
syst 3D gdiv 100000 POSZ
steu MESH 1
steu HMIN 5.0
steu PROG 1.1
steu DELN 0

spt 1 x -20 +20 0
spt 2 x +20 +20 0
spt 3 x +20 -20 0
spt 4 x -20 -20 0

let#ds 0.4

spt 11 x -5-#ds +5+#ds 0
spt 12 x +5+#ds +5+#ds 0
spt 13 x +5+#ds -5-#ds 0
spt 14 x -5-#ds -5-#ds 0

spt 21 x -5 +5 0
spt 22 x +5 +5 0
spt 23 x +5 -5 0
spt 24 x -5 -5 0

sln 1,2,3,4 npa 1,2,3,4 npe 2,3,4,1
sln 11,12,13,14 npa 11,12,13,14 npe 12,13,14,11

sln 21 npa 21 22
 slns grp 6 ref 11 mnr 11 drx 0 1 0

sln 22 npa 22 23
 slns grp 6 ref 12 mnr 11 drx 1 0 0

sln 23 npa 23 24
 slns grp 6 ref 13 mnr 11 drx 0 -1 0

sln 24 npa 24 21
 slns grp 6 ref 14 mnr 11 drx -1 0 0

$ structural areas as master
sar 1 t 0 mnr 0 grp 1
sarb out 1,2,3,4
sarb in 11,12,13,14

sar 2 t 0 mnr 0 grp 2 h1 1.0
sarb out 21
sarb out 22
sarb out 23
sarb out 24

$ Extrusion path
spt 101 x -20 +20 10
spt 201 x -20 +20 20

sln 101 npa 1 101  sdiv -10
sln 102 npa 101 201 sdiv -10

ende

+prog sofimsha urs:4
kopf Completion of master view
syst REST

$ Quads for filling the interface
grup 3
quad FIT 11 12 22 21 t 0
quad FIT 12 13 23 22 t 0
quad FIT 13 14 24 23 t 0
quad FIT 14 11 21 24 t 0
ende

+prog sofimsha urs:10
kopf extrusion to 3D
syst REST

$ diaphragm wall
quad PROP mnr 1 t 0.4[m] lage UNTE
grup 17 ; extr edge von 21 bis 24 path SLN 101

$ soil outside
bric PROP mnr 11
grup 11 ; extr quad von GRP 1 path SLN 101
grup 21 ; extr quad von GRP 1 path SLN 102 sref 1

$ soil inside
bric PROP mnr 11
grup 12 ; extr quad von GRP 2 path SLN 101
grup 13 ; extr quad von GRP 3 path SLN 101
grup 22 ; extr quad von GRP 2 path SLN 102 sref 1
grup 23 ; extr quad von GRP 3 path SLN 102 sref 1 $ brics to fill interface

$ interface
fede PROP mnr 11
grup 16 ; extr fede von GRP 6 path SLN 101

$ boundary conditions
mod knot xmin -20.01 xmax -19.99 fix px
mod knot ymin -20.01 ymax -19.99 fix py

mod knot xmin 19.99 xmax 20.01 fix px
mod knot ymin 19.99 ymax 20.01 fix py
mod knot zmin 19.99 zmax 20.01 fix pz

$ delete temporary elements
del QUAD 3 delt GRP

ende


!#!Kapitel Loads
+prog sofiload urs:6
kopf
lf 21 ; quad grp 1 typ PZZ 30.0
ende

kopf

steu solv 4

lf 1 egz 1.0  bez 'in-situ'

grup ALLE NEIN
grup  nr         wert   faks
      11,12,13   VOLL   1.0
      21,22,23   VOLL   1.0
ende
