+prog ase urs:5
kopf
$ Verformungen aus in-situ nicht berÃ¼cksichtigen -> fakv=0
syst prob NONL iter -  nmat ja  plf 1  fakv 0.0
steu solv 4

lf 2 egz 1.0 bez 'Installation diaphragm wall'

grup ALLE NEIN
grup  nr               wert   faks
     17                VOLL   1.0
     11,12,13          VOLL   1.0
     21,22,23          VOLL   1.0
ende


+prog ase urs:7
kopf
syst prob NONL iter -  nmat ja  plf 2
steu solv 4

lf 3 egz 1.0 bez 'Live load'
 lc 21

grup ALLE NEIN
grup  nr               wert   faks
     1                 VOLL   1.0
     17                VOLL   1.0
     16                VOLL   -
     11,12             VOLL   1.0
     21,22,23          VOLL   1.0
ende


+prog ase urs:9
kopf
syst prob NONL iter -  nmat ja  plf 3
steu solv 4

lf 4 egz 0 bez 'Excavation'
 lc 21

grup ALLE NEIN
grup  nr               wert   faks
     1                 VOLL   1.0
     17                VOLL   1.0

     11                VOLL   1.0
     21,22,23          VOLL   1.0

!#!Info  Example:       Modeling of a continuum embedded tunnel with implicit hinges
!#!Info                 and interface elements (see also examples in talpa.dat)
!#!Info  Keyword:       Geotechnics; implicit hinges; interface elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2009-03-31 02:04:38 +0200 (Di, 31 Mrz 2009) $


+PROG AQUA urs:2
HEAD Material and working law definition
NORM DIN EN199X-200X

$ working laws
SFLA   F 18  NO 111 TYPE MY  $ rotational spring
       $kNm

ECHO SECT

$ tunnel lining
CONC 1 C 30
SREC 1 0.25 1.00  MNO 1

$ soil material
MAT  2 E 100000 MUE 0.2  GAM 18  TITL 'Soil'
NMAT 2 MOHR P1 20 P2 0 P3 0
BMAT 2 MREF 2  H 0.2  MUE 0.5  CRAC 0.0

END

+PROG SOFIMSHC urs:1
HEAD System definition
SYST PAIN GDIV 10000 GDIR POSY
LET#W 50.0      $ model width
LET#H 50.0      $ model height
LET#D 20.0      $ depth tunnel axis
LET#R  5.0      $ tunnel radius

$ mesh control
CTRL MESH 2 ; CTRL HMIN 1.5


$ define the bulk body
SPT NO      X     Y
     1  -#W/2   0.0
     2   #W/2   0.0
     3   #W/2   #H
     4  -#W/2   #H

SLN  1 1 2
SLN  2 1 4 FIX PX
SLN  3 2 3 FIX PX
SLN  4 3 4 FIX PY

SAR  1  MNO 2  T 1.0  GRP 1
  SARB OUT NL 1,2,3,4


$ define the circular tunnel section as attribute area
$ - the two structural lines bounding the circular section must be given in same
$   clock-order in order to create interfaces layers on consistent sides.

 SLN 10 SDIV 0.4  SNO 1  FIXA 111 FIXE 111 FIMA 111 FIME 111 GRP 10
  SLNB  X1 -#R #D   X2 #R #D   X3 0.0  #D-#R

  $ create interface layer to the 'left' side of the line if viewed in curve direction
  SLNS  GRP 20 REFT -SAR  MNO 2 D 0.2 $ bedding parameters are taken from the material
  $ SLNS  GRP 30 REFT -SAR D 0.2  CA 1000.0 CL 100.0 $ linear parameters are given directly

SLN 11 SDIV 0.4  SNO 1  FIXA 111 FIXE 111 FIMA 111 FIME 111 GRP 11
  SLNB  X1 +#R #D   X2 -#R #D   X3 0.0  #D+#R

  $ interface layers:
  SLNS  GRP 20 REFT -SAR  MNO 2 D 0.2
  $SLNS  GRP 30 REFT -SAR D 0.2  CA 1000.0 CL 100.0

  $ tunnel section given as property region
SAR PROP GRP 2 MNO 2 H1 1.0
  SARB OUT NL 10,11

END

+PROG TALPA urs:3
HEAD Primary State
SYST PROB NONL
GRP 1,2   FULL FACD 1.0 K 0.6
GRP 20,21 LINE FACD 1.0
LC 1 TITL 'PRIMARY STATE'
END

-PROG TALPA urs:4
HEAD Relaxation
SYST PROB NONL
CTRL BEAM 3
PLC 1 TYPE ACTI
GRP 1     FULL FACD 1.0
GRP 2     FULL FACD 0.7 FACS 0.7 FACL 0.7
GRP 20,21 LINE FACD 1.0
LC 2 TITL 'RELAXATION'
END

-PROG TALPA urs:5
HEAD Excavation and Support
SYST PROB NONL
CTRL BEAM 3
CTRL ITER 30
PLC 2 TYPE FULL
GRP 1     FULL FACD 1.0
GRP 10,11 FULL FACD 1.0 PLC -
GRP 20,21 FULL FACD 1.0
LC 3 TITL 'EXCAVATION AND SUPPORT'
END

!#!Info  Example:       Extraction of a subsystem from a model
!#!Info  Keyword:       Subsystems
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2014
!#!Info  Date:          $Date: 2014-03-24


+prog aqua urs:3
head Material and sections
echo FULL FULL
norm DIN EN199X-200X
conc 1 C 35
srec 1 h 250 250 mno 1
end


!#!Kapitel Main System
+prog sofimshc urs:1
head Definition main system
syst 3D gdiv 10000

loop#n 5
 let#z (#n+1)*-3.0

 $ create slabs
 sar #n+1 t 300 mno 1 mctl 1
 sarb out fix MX ; slnb x1 0 0 #z x2 8 0 #z
 sarb out ; slnb x1 8 0 #z x2 8 6 #z
 sarb out ; slnb x1 8 6 #z x2 0 6 #z
 sarb out ; slnb x1 0 6 #z x2 0 0 #z

 $ create walls
 sar - t 200 mno 1
 sarb out ; slnb x1 0 0 #z x2 8 0 #z
 sarb out ; slnb x1 8 0 #z x2 8 0 #z+3
 sarb out ; slnb x1 8 0 #z+3 x2 0 0 #z+3
 sarb out ; slnb x1 0 0 #z+3 x2 0 0 #z

 $ fix horizontally
 spt - x 0 0 #z fix PY
 spt - x 8 0 #z fix PY

endloop

$ foundation supports
spt - x 0 0 0 fix PP
spt - x 8 0 0 fix PP
spt - x 8 6 0 fix PP
spt - x 0 6 0 fix PP

$ columns
sln 1 sno 1 ; slnb x1 0 0 0 x2 0 0 #z
sln 2 sno 1 ; slnb x1 8 0 0 x2 8 0 #z
sln 3 sno 1 ; slnb x1 8 6 0 x2 8 6 #z
sln 4 sno 1 ; slnb x1 0 6 0 x2 0 6 #z

end


+prog sofimshc urs:10
head Definition of subsystem and meshing
syst REST
ctrl MESH 1
ctrl HMIN 0.5

$ select members defining the subsystem using a bounding box
xsub type 3D fixa free free free free cdb "floor_02_xsub_01"
bbox zmin -6.01 zmax -5.99

$ specify kind of stiffness to be generated for downward connected members
xcon BELO fixa fix fixl 1.0 fixm 1.0 fixs free

end


+prog sofiload urs:8
head Loads
lc 1 facd 1.0
area SAR 1,2,3,4,5 type PG 20
end


+prog ase urs:4
head Calculation
lc ALL
end



+PROG WING urs:6
head Principal bending moments
CTRL OPT INP
CTRL OPT GSTR VAL DEFA
CTRL OPT AXIS VAL DEFA
$ graphics    1 | Picture    1 | Layer    1 : Principal bending moments  LC:    1
PAGE LANO 1 UNIO 0
SIZE TYPE URS SC 0 MARG NO FORM STAN
SIZ2
AND  POSI 1 POSL 0 POSR 100 POSD 0 POSU 100
SCH2 DIRE DEFA
LC   NO 1 DESI 1
BOX
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0 Y -1 Z 0 AXIS POSZ ROTA 0
BOX  XMIN -0.5 YMIN -0.5 ZMIN -5.8 XMAX 8.5 YMAX 6.5 ZMAX -6.2 TYPE BWIN OPER AND BGRP 0
$ bounding: BOX XMIN 0.000 YMIN 0.000 ZMIN -10.000 XMAX 8.000 YMAX 6.000 ZMAX -10.000
VIEW TYPE DIRE X 0 Y 0 Z 1 AXIS POSY ROTA 0
DEFO TYPE NO EXPO 0 SMOV NO
SELE NUMB 0 titl 'Main system: '
QUAD TYPE HM UNIT DEFA SCHH YES STYP NODE FILL NO REPR DVEC AVER NO
END

#define projekt="floor_02_xsub_01"

SIZ2

!#!Info  Example:       Solid Body meshed with hexahedral elements through lofting and extrusion
!#!Info  Keyword:       Meshing; Brics; Hexahedral elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC,SOFIMSHA
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2016


+prog aqua urs:1
head Materials

norm 'DIN' '1045-2008'
conc no 1 type 'C' fcn 30

end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head Guiding Lines and Cross Sections
syst 3d gdiv -10000 gdir negz
ctrl mesh 2+64
ctrl prog 1.25
ctrl tolg 0.0001
ctrl deln 0

sto#NS  5         ! number of base / capital sides (>=3)
sto#R   0.75 0.50 ! min radius at base / capital
sto#H   8.0       ! column height (excluding base / capital)
sto#N   6         ! number of column blocks
sto#SD  100       ! structural element number separator
sto#DA  180/#NS   ! base - capital rotation
sto#A   360.0/#NS   ! angle per side
sto#BF  #R(0)/#R(1) ! base - capital radius ration


! Circular cross sections at column
loop#J #N+1
  let#ISD #SD*#J                      ! element number base
  let#IR  #R(0)+(#J/#N)*(#R(1)-#R(0)) ! radius
  let#IH  (#J/#N)*#H                  ! height
  let#IDA (#J/#N)*#DA                 ! rotation

! Points
  loop#I #NS
    spt no #ISD+#I+1 x #IR*cos(#I*#A+#IDA) y #IR*sin(#I*#A+#IDA) z #IH
  endloop

! Lines
  loop#I #NS-1
    sln no #ISD+#I+1 npa #ISD+#I+1 npe #ISD+#I+2
    slnb r #IR nx 0 ny 0 nz 1
  endloop
  sln no #ISD+#NS npa #ISD+#NS npe #ISD+1
  slnb r #IR nx 0 ny 0 nz 1

! Area
  sar no #ISD+1 grp #J+1 mno 1 t 0 mctl auto h1 0.40*#IR h2 0.10*#IR
  sarb type out nl (#ISD+1 #ISD+#NS 1)
  if #J>0
! Generate similar meshes for all Cross Sections
    sars reft >SAR ref 1
  endif
endloop


! Polygonal cross sections at base / capital
loop#J 2
  let#ISD  #SD*(#N+1+#J) ! element number base
  let#ISDR #SD*(#J*#N)   ! reference element number base
  let#IR   2.0*#R(#J)    ! width of base / capital
  let#IDA  #J*#DA        ! rotation

  if #J==0               ! height
    let#IH 0-0.75*#IR    ! at base
  elseif #J==1
    let#IH #H+0.75*#IR   ! at capital
  endif

  if #J==0               ! curvature point
    let#Z3 -0.5*#IR      ! at base
  elseif #J==1
    let#Z3 #H+0.5*#IR    ! at capital
  endif

! Points
  loop#I #NS
    spt no #ISD+#I+1 x #IR*cos(#I*#A+#IDA) y #IR*sin(#I*#A+#IDA) z #IH
  endloop

! Lines
  loop#I #NS-1
    sln no #ISD+#I+1 npa #ISD+#I+1 npe #ISD+#I+2
  endloop
  sln no #ISD+#NS npa #ISD+#NS npe #ISD+1

! Area
  sar no #ISD+1 grp #N+#J+1 mno 1 t 0
  sarb type out nl (#ISD+1 #ISD+#NS 1)
! Generate similar meshes for all Cross Sections
  sars reft >SAR ref 1

! Curved guiding lines for lofting
  loop#I #NS
    sln no #ISD+#NS+#I+1 npa #ISDR+#I+1 npe #ISD+#I+1 sdiv -12
    slnb x3 0.5*(#R(#J)+#IR)*cos(#I*#A+#IDA) y3 0.5*(#R(#J)+#IR)*sin(#I*#A+#IDA) z3 #Z3
  endloop
endloop

end

+prog sofimsha urs:3
head Volume Mesh
syst rest

! Column blocks
loop#J #N
  let#ISDS #SD*#J     ! source element number base
  let#ISDT #SD*(#J+1) ! target element number base

  grp #J+1
  bric prop mno 1
! Loft between Cross Sections with linear interpolation
  loft type sar idsc #ISDS+1 idtg #ISDT+1 refs #ISDS+1 reft #ISDT+1 div 6*(#H/#N) ! 6 elements per meter
endloop

! Base / capital
loop#J 2
  let#ISDS #SD*(#J*#N)   ! source element number base
  let#ISDT #SD*(#N+1+#J) ! target element number base

  grp #N+#J+1
  bric prop mno 1
! Loft following guiding structural lines with curvature
  loft type sar idsc #ISDS+1 idtg #ISDT+1 refs #ISDS+1 reft #ISDT+1 opt 'E'

! Extrusion direction and distance
  let#IH 0.75*#R(#J)
  if #J==0
    let#IH -#IH
  endif
! Extrude
  extr type sar from #ISDT+1 path dir v1 0 v2 0 v3 #IH div 6
endloop

! Elastic bedding
grp 101
sbox a3z -3*0.75*#R(0)-0.001 b3z -3*0.75*#R(0)+0.001
spri sbox dx  0  0 -1 cp 42000 ct 28000

end

+prog sofimsha urs:4
head Interfaces
syst rest

loop#J #N+1
  let#ISD #SD*#J ! element number base

  grp 101+#J+1
  intf type spri reft sar no #ISD+1 cp 58000 ct 36000 d 0.025
endloop

end

+prog ase urs:5
head Eccentric Dead Load
ctrl solv 4

lc 1 dlx 0.5 dlz 1.5

end
!#!Info  Beispiel:      Extrusion von 1D elementen zu Quad-Netz
!#!Info  Schlagwort:    Netzgenerierung
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2016

+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material definition
mate 1 E 20000
end


+prog sofimshc urs:1
head section and extrusion curves
SYST 3D gdiv 10000
ctrl mesh 1
ctrl DELN 0

$ 'section' lines
sln 1 sdiv -10
 slnb x1 0 0 0 x2 0 0 -5 nx 1 0 0 R 2.5

sln 2 sdiv -10
 slnb x1 0 -5 0 x2 0 -5 -5 nx 1 0 0 R 2.5

$ extrusion paths
sln 11 sdiv -10
 slnb x1 0 0 0 x2 5 0 5 xm 0 0 5

sln 12 sdiv -10
 slnb x1 0 -5 0 x2 5 -5 5 xm 0 -5 5

end

+prog sofimsha urs:3
head extrusion to quads
syst REST

quad PROP mno 1 t 200[mm]

grp 2
extr SLN 1 path SLN 11 OPT -  $ extrusion without rotation of sectional curve

grp 3
extr SLN 2 path SLN 12 OPT R  $ extrusion with rotation of sectional curve

end


!#!Info  Beispiel:      Modellierung eines kreisfÃ¶rmigen Flansches mit BolzenÃ¶ffnungen
!#!Info  Schlagwort:    Geometriemodellierung; Volumenelemente
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC,SOFIMSHA
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2016


+prog aqua urs:1
head material
page UNII 7
norm DIN 18800
stee 1 S 355
end


+prog sofimshc urs:3
head master section and extrusion axes
syst 3D gdiv 20000 gdir NEGZ
page UNII 7
ctrl TOLG 0.001
ctrl MESH 1
ctrl HMIN 3[mm]
ctrl DELN 0

let#R1 150/2    $ inner radius of flange
let#R2 155/2
let#R3 180/2
let#R4 250/2    $ outer radius of flange
let#R5 #R4-15   $ radius at bolt axis
let#RB 5        $ radius of bolts

let#H1 40 $ heights
let#H2 35
let#H3 15


$ structural points defining the section
spt 1 x #R1 z #H1
spt 2 x #R2 z #H1
spt 3 x #R2 z #H2
spt 4 x #R3 z #H3
spt 5 x #R4 z #H3
spt 6 x #R4 z 0
spt 7 x #R3 z 0
spt 8 x #R1 z 0

spt 101 x #R1*cos(45) #R1*sin(45) #H1
spt 104 x #R3*cos(45) #R3*sin(45) #H3
spt 105 x #R4*cos(45) #R4*sin(45) #H3

spt 201 x (#R5-#RB)*cos(45/2) (#R5-#RB)*sin(45/2) #H3
spt 202 x (#R5+#RB)*cos(45/2) (#R5+#RB)*sin(45/2) #H3

$ structural lines
sln 1 npa 1 2
sln 2 npa 2 3
sln 3 npa 3 4
sln 4 npa 4 5
sln 7 npa 7 8
sln 8 npa 8 1
sln 9 npa 4 7

sln 101 npa 1 101 ; slnb xm 0 0 #H1
sln 104 npa 4 104 ; slnb xm 0 0 #H3
 slns ref 101 $ enforce common subdivision

sln 114 npa 104 105 ; slns ref 4 $ enforce common subdivision

sln 201 npa 201 202
 slnb xm #R5*cos(45/2) #R5*sin(45/2) #H3 nz 1

sln 202 npa 202 201
 slnb xm #R5*cos(45/2) #R5*sin(45/2) #H3 nz 1

$ structural areas
sar 1 t 0 titl "sectional area"
sarb out 1,2,3,7,8,9

sar 2 t 0 titl "upper face"
sarr ROTA 4 x 0 0 nz 1 vmin 0 vmax 45

sar VOID titl "bolt opening"
sarb out 201,202

end


+prog sofimsha urs:4
head extrusion & copying
syst REST

quad PROP t 0 kr NEGZ

grp 1
 extr QUAD from SAR 1 path SLN 104 opt R
 extr QUAD from SAR 2 path SLN 9
 tran BRIC GRP 1 phiz 45

grp 2
 quad PROP t 0
 extr EDGE from 201 to 202 path SLN 9
 tran QUAD grp 2 phiz 45

grp 3

 tran QUAD grp 3 phiz 45

grp 11
 tran BRIC GRP 1 phiz 90

grp 12
 tran QUAD grp 2 phiz 90

grp 21

grp 22
 tran QUAD grp 2,12 phiz 180

grp 23
 tran QUAD grp 3,13 phiz 180

$ fix quad elements at bolts
$ mod QUAD from 2,12,22 inc GRP fix PP
spri QGRP 2,12,22 CP 1000.0 CT 100.0

end

!#!Info  Example:       Solid Body with holes meshed with bric elements
!#!Info  Keyword:       Meshing; Brics; Hexahedral elements
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC,SOFIMSHA
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2016

+prog aqua urs:2
head Material
norm DIN 18800
stee 1 S 235
end

prog sofimshc m8000000 urs:1
head 2D Quad meshes
page UNII 7      $ mechanical units: all in [mm]

syst 3D gdiv 10000
ctrl TOLG 0.001  $ adapt geometric tolerance to model size
ctrl mesh 2      $ create mesh
ctrl hmin 8.0[mm] $ mesh size

$ Parameters
let#m  64,220,300,80,16  $ total dimensions = height,length,width,thick1,thick2

let#d  28             $ diameter of openings
let#h1 -60,0,60       $ x-position of openings in handle
let#h2 260            $ y-position of openings in cantilever

let#B  #m(1)/2,#m(1)/2-#m(4)

$ Points
spt 1   #(B+1) #(m+3)  0.0
    2   #(B+0) #(m+3)  0.0
    3   #(B+0)   0.0   0.0
    4  -#(B+0)   0.0   0.0
    5  -#(B+0) #(m+3)  0.0
    6  -#(B+1) #(m+3)  0.0
    7  -#(B+0) #(m+3)  #(m)
    8  -#(B+0) #(m+2)  #(m)
    9  -#(B+0) #(m+2)  0.0

$ Lines
sln 1 6 1
    2 1 2
    3 2 3
    4 3 4
    5 4 5
    6 5 6

sln 11 5 7
    12 7 8
    13 8 9
    14 9 5

$ Openings
sln 21 ; slnb xm #h1(0) #m(3)/2 R #d/2 nz 1
sln 22 ; slnb xm #h1(1) #m(3)/2 R #d/2 nz 1
sln 23 ; slnb xm #h1(2) #m(3)/2 R #d/2 nz 1

sln 31 fix PP ; slnb xm -#B #h2(0) #m(0)/2 R #d/2 nx 1

$ Structural areas
sar 100 t 0
sarb out 1,2,3,4,5,6
sarb in 21,22,23

sar 200 t 0
sarb out 11,12,13,14
sarb in 31
end

+prog sofimsha urs:3
head Extrusion to Bric mesh
syst REST

$ Extrusion of quad elements to brics
bric PROP mno 1
grp 11 ; extr QUAD from SAR 100 path SLN 11
grp 12 ; extr QUAD from SAR 200 path SLN 6
grp 13 ; extr QUAD from SAR 200 path SLN 2 sref 5

$ Extrusion of support conditions in opening of cantilever
extr FIX from SLN 31 path SLN 6
extr FIX from SLN 31 path SLN 2 sref 5
end

+prog aqua urs:2
head
mat 1 E 1.e6 0.3
mat 2 E 1.e3 0.4
end

+prog sofimshc urs:3
head modeling of surface
syst SPAC gdiv -1000
ctrl MESH 2     $ create surface mesh
ctrl HMIN 0.5   $ mesh density
ctrl WARN 383   $ ignore warnings about unconnected structural lines

let#L 10.0 $ length of body
let#W  5.0 $ width of body
let#H  2.0 $ height of body

let#R 1.0       $ radius of hole
let#C 5,2.5,1.0 $ center position of hole
let#alph 45.0   $ inclination of hole

gar P1 type PLAN ; gara x 0 0 0  nz 1.0 umin -#L +#L vmin -#L +#L
gar P2 type PLAN ; gara x 0 0 #H nz 1.0 umin -#L +#L vmin -#L +#L


gax G1 typc ARC
 gaxb x1 #C(0)-10*tan(#alph) #C(1)-#R #C(2)-10 x2 #C(0)+10*tan(#alph) #C(1)-#R #C(2)+10
gax G2 typc ARC
 gaxb x1 #C(0)-10*tan(#alph) #C(1)+#R #C(2)-10 x2 #C(0)+10*tan(#alph) #C(1)+#R #C(2)+10

gar R1 type ROTA
 gara G1 x #C(0) #C(1) #C(2) nx tan(#alph) nz 1.0 vmin 0.0 vmax 180.0

gar R2 type ROTA
 gara G2 x #C(0) #C(1) #C(2) nx tan(#alph) nz 1.0 vmin 0.0 vmax 180.0

gax P1R1 sur1 P1 sur2 R1
gax P1R2 sur1 P1 sur2 R2
gax P2R1 sur1 P2 sur2 R1
gax P2R2 sur1 P2 sur2 R2


spt 1 x  0  0 0
    2 x #L  0 0
    3 x #L #W 0
    4 x  0 #W 0
   11 x  0  0 #H
   12 x #L  0 #H
   13 x #L #W #H
   14 x  0 #W #H

$ lines defining the body
sln 1,2,3,4 npa 1,2,3,4 npe 2,3,4,1
sln 11,12,13,14 npa 11,12,13,14 npe 12,13,14,11
sln 21,22,23,24 npa 1,2,3,4 npe 11,12,13,14

$ lines defining the hole
sln 51 ref G1
sln 52 ref G2
sln 61 ref P1R1
sln 62 ref P1R2
sln 71 ref P2R1
sln 72 ref P2R2

$ structural areas
sar  1 grp 1 t 0 ; sarb out 1,2,3,4 ; sarb in 61,62
sar  2 grp 1 t 0 ; sarb out 1,11,21,22
sar  3 grp 1 t 0 ; sarb out 2,12,22,23
sar  4 grp 1 t 0 ; sarb out 3,13,23,24
sar  5 grp 1 t 0 fix F ; sarb out 4,14,24,21
sar  6 grp 1 t 0 ; sarb out 11,12,13,14 ; sarb in 71,72

sar 11 grp - ref R1 t 0 ; sarb out 51,52,61,71
sar 12 grp - ref R2 t 0 ; sarb out 51,52,62,72

end


+prog sofimsha urs:1
head volume meshing
syst REST

grp 10
bric PROP mno 2

umsh type TET
 ubnd type OUT sel QGRP n1 1
 ubnd type OUT QREF n1 11 12
end


!#!Info  Example:       volume body with with two materials
!#!Info  Keyword:       Meshing
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2016

+prog aqua urs:2
head
mat 1 E 10000 0.3
mat 2 E 10000 0.3
end

+prog sofimshc urs:1
head test 3d with two different materials
syst spac GDIV -1000
ctrl mesh 3  $ create volume mesh
ctrl hmin 0.5

$ structural points
spt  11,21  0.0 5.0 0.0,2.0
     12,22  8.0 5.0 0.0,2.0
     13,23 12.0 5.0 0.0,2.0
     14,24 12.0 0.0 0.0,2.0
     15,25  8.0 0.0 0.0,2.0
     16,26  0.0 0.0 0.0,2.0

$ structural lines
sln (11 16 1) (11 1) (21 1)
    100,200 12,22 15,25
    101,201 15,25 16,26
    102,202 16,26 11,21
    103,203 11,21 12,22
    111,211 12,22 13,23
    112,212 13,23 14,24
    113,213 14,24 15,25

$ boundary surfaces
sar  1 ; sarb OUT 15,101,16,201
sar  2 ; sarb OUT 16,102,11,202
sar  3 ; sarb OUT 11,103,12,203
sar  4 ; sarb OUT 12,111,13,211
sar  5 ; sarb OUT 13,112,14,212
sar  6 ; sarb OUT 14,113,15,213
sar 11 ; sarb OUT 100,101,102,103  ; sar 21 ; sarb OUT 200,201,202,203
sar 12 ; sarb OUT 100,111,112,113  ; sar 22 ; sarb OUT 200,211,212,213
sar 10 ; sarb OUT 100,12,200,15

$ first volume mesh defined by boundary surfaces
svo 1 grp 1 mno 1 ; svos 1,2,3,11,21,10
$ second volume defined by boundary surfaces
svo 2 grp 2 mno 2 ; svos 4,5,6,12,22,10
end


!#!Info  Beispiel:      Tetraedervernetzung eines KegelfÃ¶rmigen KÃ¶rpers
!#!Info  Schlagwort:    Geometriemodellierung; Volumenelemente
!#!Info  Program:       SOFIMSHC
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 2016

+PROG AQUA URS:2
head material definition
norm DIN 1045-2008
conc 1 C 35 ; stee 2 BST 500
end


+prog sofimshc urs:1
head definition of surface of cone
syst 3D gdiv -1000 gdir POSZ
ctrl mesh 2+32  $ create triangular mesh on surface
ctrl hmin 0.5

let#r    5.0  $ BASE RADIUS
let#h  -10.0  $ HEIGHT

$ point at apex with reduced meshsize
spt 1 x 0 0 #h bx 0.1 0.1

$ lines describing region boundaries
sln 1 ; slnb x1 +#r 0 0  x2 0 0 #h
sln 2 ; slnb x1 -#r 0 0  x2 0 0 #h
sln 11 ; slnb x1 +#r 0 0 x2 -#r 0 0 R #r nz +1
sln 12 ; slnb x1 -#r 0 0 x2 +#r 0 0 R #r nz +1

$ three structural regions
sar 1 nra 0 t 0.0
 sarr ROTA 1 x 0 0 0 nz +1 $ geometry: surface of revolution
 sarb out 1,2,11

sar 2 nra 0 t 0.0
 sarr ROTA 2 x 0 0 0 nz +1 $ geometry: surface of revolution
 sarb out 1,2,12

sar 3 mno 1  nra 0 t 0.0
sarb out 11,12
end


+prog sofimsha urs:3
head volume meshing
syst REST

grp 10
bric PROP mno 1

$ create volume mesh
umsh type TET hmax 0.5
 ubnd type out sel COOR x 0 0 -1 $ 'seed' point in interior
end


!#!Info  Example:       Prestressed bridge
!#!Info  Keyword:       prestress; tendon
!#!Info  Program:       TENDON
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 25
!#!Info  Date:          24.04.2009

+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Materials
echo mat full ; echo sect no
NORM DIN 'fb102-2009' CAT C $ DIN FACHBERICHT 102 vgl. Beispiel   DIN_FB_SOFiSTiK.pdf
                      $ DIN Special report German 102 campare example  DIN_FB_SOFiSTiK.pdf
CONC 1  C   40        $ = C40/50
STEE 2  BST 500SA
STEE 7    S 235
STEE 11 PST 1570S
$ STEE 11   Y 1770  $ for EUROCODE see csm.dat\..\mode\csm31_design_ec2.dat
END

+PROG AQUA URS:2
HEAD Template section with axis-variables
CTRL REST 0 $ alte Querschnitte lÃ¶schen  -  delete old sections
echo pict no

  STO#WIDTH   8.00  $ Total width    $ these two variables will change in
  STO#HEIGHT  1.50  $ Total height   $ axis development -> see SOFIMSHC - axis variables
$
SECT 1 MNO 1 MRF 2 TITL 'cross1'
SPT TOPP Y       0        Z 0          MNO 1 $ MNR 1 = for AQB-output material 1
SPT BOTT Y       0        Z '=#HEIGHT' MNO 1 $
SPT TOPR Y '=+#WIDTH*0.5' Z 0          MNO 0 $ MNR 0 = only construction
SPT TOPL Y '=-#WIDTH*0.5' Z 0          MNO 0 $ point - not used for AQB-output
POLY O
VERT 11  Y   0  Z 0  REFP TOPR
     12  Y   0  Z .2 REFP TOPR
     13  Y  2.0 Z .4
     14  Y  1.5 Z 0  REFP BOTT
    114  Y -1.5 Z 0  REFP BOTT
    113  Y -2.0 Z .4
    112  Y   0  Z .2 REFP TOPL
    111  Y   0  Z 0  REFP TOPL exp 0.50 $ BelÃ¼ftung nur Ã¼ber Asphalt $ aeration only over asphalt
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$ TOPL=111--------------------------------------------11=TOPR
$      112---       TL----------|----------TR     ----12
$            ----113 |          |          | 13---
$                 |  |          |          |  |
$                 |  |          |          |  |
$                 |  |          |          |  |
$                 | BL----------|----------BR |
$                114-------------------------14
let#c 0.07 $ m distance to surface - torsion box reinforcement
SPT TL REFP 113 Y  #c Z -0.40+#c  MNO 0
SPT TR REFP  13 Y -#c Z -0.40+#c  MNO 0
SPT BL REFP 114 Y  #c Z      -#c  MNO 0
SPT BR REFP  14 Y -#c Z      -#c  MNO 0
LRF  1 0 0 0 0 REFA TL REFE BL AS 0.1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  2 0 0 0 0 REFA BL REFE BR AS 0.1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  3 0 0 0 0 REFA BR REFE TR AS 0.1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  4 0 0 0 0 REFA TR REFE TL AS 0.1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12
$
let#d 0.09 $ m distance to surface - main reinforcement bars
LRF  5 #d  #d -#d  #d REFA TOPL REFE TOPR AS   - LAY 1 TORS PASS D  20  $ unten $ below
LRF  5 #d -#d -#d -#d REFA  114 REFE   14 AS   - LAY 2 TORS PASS D  20  $ oben  $ above
CUT 1 ZB 0.41     MNO 1        LAY 1
CUT 2 ZB S        MNO 1        LAY 1
CUT 3 YB 1.50     MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN
$
$ Sections for cross girders and piers:
SREC  7 H 1.8 B 1.2 REF UM $ QuertrÃ¤ger  -  cross girder
SREC  9 H 1.5 B 4          $ Pfeiler     -  piers
END

+PROG SOFIMSHC URS:3 $ Definition of the main axis, spans, main beam and axis variables
HEAD CABD - Parametric haunched prestressed bridge
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 POSZ
$ ------------------------------------- axis : ------------------------------
GAX 'AX_1'
  GAXA S  0 X 0 0 0 SX 1 0 0 $ first starting point with starting direction
  GAXA L 10 RA   0 RE   80
  GAXA L 10 R   80
  GAXA L 20 RA  80 RE -100
  GAXA L 80 R -100
$ a straight bridge with 100 m only requires:
$ GAXB X1 0 0 0 X2 100 0 0   $ create axis from point 1 to point 2   (also with R)
                             $ other curved bridge -> csm.dat\...\cabd\csm10_...cabd.dat
$
$ ------------------------------ definition of spans: S_XI table: ----- axis : ------------------------------

$ As this span definition is used often in the file, it is defined once and stored:
STO#S_XI(99) 0     $ allocate table
STO#S_XI(0)  0.00  $ start of bridge at left excess  -   am linken Ãœberstand
STO#S_XI(1)  1.00  $ first support                   -   erstes Lager
STO#S_XI(2) 31.00  $ 2.    support                   -   2.     Lager
STO#S_XI(3) 61.00  $ 3.    support                   -   3.     Lager
STO#S_XI(4) 62.00  $ end of bridge at right excess   -   am rechten Ãœberstand
$ please always define #X_XI(0) and #X_XI(right excess)
$ also if it is equal to support X_XI(0)=X_XI(1)=0.00
$
$ now you can access to the table also with interpolation:
$ s at span 2 at local xi=0.6 ->
$ let#s =S_XI(2.6)    gives s back with 49.00 m !!
STO#s_end =S_XI(4.0)  $ for SOFILOAD - end of bridge
TXB Testprint variable s_end =  #(s_end,8.3)   $ (8 characters and 3 digits)

$ ------------------------------------- main beam : ------------------------------
CTRL MESH 1 ; CTRL HMIN 1.0  $ meshing of beam elements
$ xi-span definition  $ Felddefinition - Lagerachsen
$ and beam element definition on that main axis $ gleichzeitig: Stabzug an der Hauptachse
GAXP 'AX_1' S =S_XI(0) TYPE 'A' GRP 1 NCS 1 SPT  90  $ defines  xi=0
GAXP 'AX_1' S =S_XI(1) TYPE 'S'             SPT 100  $ defines  xi=1
GAXP 'AX_1' S =S_XI(2) TYPE 'S' GRP 2       SPT 200  $ defines  xi=2
GAXP 'AX_1' S =S_XI(3) TYPE 'S'             SPT 300  $ defines  xi=3
GAXP 'AX_1' S =S_XI(4) TYPE 'E'             SPT 310  $ defines  xi=4
$
$ ------------------------------------- axis variables : ------------------------------
$ Variable HEIGHT via xi:
GAXV   S                V   TYPE ID='AX_1' NAME='HEIGHT'
       =#S_XI(0.0)      1.50   -
       =#S_XI(1.4)      1.50  D+  $ at xi=0.4 of span 1 !
       =#S_XI(2.0)-1.20 2.80  D+  $ 1.20 m vorm Mittelpfeiler
       =#S_XI(2.0)+1.20 2.80  D-  $ 1.20 m nach Mittelpfeiler
       =#S_XI(2.6)      1.50  D-
       =#S_XI(4.0)      1.50  D-

$ Variable WIDTH:
GAXV   S                V   TYPE ID='AX_1' NAME='WIDTH'
       =#S_XI(0.0)      8.00  POLY
       =#S_XI(2.0)-6.00 9.80  POLY  $ 6.00 m vorm Mittelpfeiler
       =#S_XI(2.0)-3.00 9.80  POLY  $ 3.00 m vorm Mittelpfeiler
       =#S_XI(2.0)+3.00 9.80  POLY  $ 3.00 m nach Mittelpfeiler
       =#S_XI(2.0)+6.00 9.80  POLY  $ 6.00 m nach Mittelpfeiler
       =#S_XI(4.0)      8.00  POLY
END
END
$ alternatively :
$ Variable HEIGHT via S:
GAXV    S   V   TYPE ID='AX_1' NAME='HEIGHT'
        0 1.20   -
       20 1.20  D+
       30 2.70  D+
       32 2.70  D-
       42 1.20  D-

+PROG AQUA URS:5
HEAD Create interpolated sections
$ echo pict no
INTE 0
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:6
HEAD Piers and support conditions [SOFIPLUS]
  $ Please always run also first SOFIMSHC parallel to this SOFIMSHA !!!
SYST REST ; CTRL REST 2
GRP 9
  $ The following block can be used for standard support constructs without changes
  $ Please only change the variables let#node ...  below !
  $ limitation: #node = node number in superstructure < 1000
#define support01
  let#dhspring        0 $ m bearing height
    $ bearing springs
    let#sy 0.5*#b0
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 51000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 53000 ; endif
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 52000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 54000 ; endif
    $ node on top of pier: node 49000...
             tran node #node                 dz #h dno 49000
             node #node+51000 FIX KF #node               $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+53000 FIX KF #node      ; endif  $ coupling
             node #node+52000 FIX KF #node+49000         $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+54000 FIX KF #node+49000 ; endif $ coupling
             SPRI #node+0 #node+51000 #node+52000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  $ vertical bearing
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+1 #node+53000 #node+54000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  ; endif
    $ transverse bearing springs:
             SPRI #node+3 #node+51000 #node+52000 dy 1 CP 1E6 $ transverse
    $ longitudinal bearing springs:
    let#cp_long 1.0                       $ weak - to get bearing displacements
    if #logitud ; let#cp_long 1E6 ; endif $ longitudinal fixed bearing
             SPRI #node+7 #node+51000 #node+52000 dx 1 CP #cp_long $ longitudinal
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+8 #node+53000 #node+54000 dx 1 CP #cp_long ; endif $ longitudinal
  $ node bottom of pier: node 50000...
  tran node #node dz #UKpier dno 50000
  BEAM #node 50000+#node 49000+#node NCS 9 KR YY
  node #node+50000 FIX F                 $ fixed support
#enddef
$
let#node         100 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            1.5 $ m cross section height
let#b0           2.6 $ m bearingspread
let#UKpier         7 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         200 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            2.7 $ m cross section height
let#UKpier        13 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        1 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         300 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            1.5 $ m cross section height
let#UKpier         7 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
END

+PROG TENDON urs:9
HEAD Prestressing

  SYSP NOPS 19 MAT 11 ZV 3848 AZ 2850 LITZ 19 MINR 6.80 BETA 0.30 MUE 0.21 ECC 0.0 SP 6 DO 97
$ for EUROCODE see csm.dat\..\mode\csm31_design_ec2.dat

$ reference axis and span definition:
AXES NOH 1 TYPE AUTO  90 310
TOPP NOH 1 KIND NODE S 90,100,200,300,310 SP 0,1,2,3,4
           $ S=100 = Knoten 100 ist der 1. Hochpunkt $ Node 100 is the 1. upper point
$ tendon geometry definition:
$ NOPS = prestressing system for max-min radius parameters + duct-excentricities
TGEO NOG 1 NOH 1 NOPS 19
$ Definition points of geometry:  (TYP=SPAN/FELD station via highpoints)
PTUV    S     U     V   DVS    RV   RL   TYPE=SPAN
        0     0   0.4     -    -     -
      1.4     -   1.35    0    -     -
        2     0   0.16    0    14    1.3
      2.6     -   1.35    0    -     -
        4     0   0.4     -    -     -
$ Additional values: construction stages:
CS ICS1 11 12
$ prestress-procedure  $ Anspann-Vorgehen
PSIG RI ANWS 'TS' KAPA 1.5 K3 1220 $ k3 = geschÃ¤tzte Begrenzung, damit Spannung bei VerkehrsÃ¼bergabe nicht zu hoch
                                   $      zul-sigma-VerkehrsÃ¼bergabe wegen DIN-FB 4.4.1.4 -> 0.65 fpk
                                   $ k3 = estimated limit to reduce stress at traffic opening
                                   $      zul-sigma-traffic opening due to DIN-FB 4.4.1.4 -> 0.65 fpk
$ final tendon definition:
TEND NOT 1 NOG 1 NTEN 8 LC 3
$ tendon plots:
ECHO PLOT full
SCHH h2 0.18 h4 0 h5 0 h6 0
PLOT GEOE NO 0 FACH  5 TYPG DUTE  DIA 65  PCS 1 $ 0 = all tendons
PLOT FACT NO 1 FACH 50
end

!#!Info  Example:       Two-span beam with in-situ-concrete deck
!#!Info  Keyword:       prestress
!#!Info  Program:       CSM
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 23/25
!#!Info  Date:          09.04.2009

#define l1=24.50    $ l1
#define l2=24.50    $ l2
#define spaltA=0.30  $ Abstand der FT-TrÃ¤ger von Lagerachse am Anfang
                     $ Distance of beam by support axis (start)
#define spaltM=0.40  $ Abstand der FT-TrÃ¤ger von Mittelachse
                     $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle)
#define xlager=0.30 $ Abstand der Lagerung der FT-TrÃ¤ger im FT-Werk
                    $ Distance of beam by support axis (end) during fabrication
#define xlag_M=0.15 $ Abstand der Lagerung der FT-TrÃ¤ger bei Montage
                    $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle) during fabrication


$ more\csm3_Spannbett.dat = Variante mit sofortigem Verbund
$----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

$ more\csm3_casting_bed_method.dat = variant with immediate bond
$--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

+PROG AQUA URS:1
HEAD Two-span beam with in-situ-concrete deck
ECHO SECT YES
NORM DIN 'fb102-2009' CAT C $ DIN FACHBERICHT 102 vgl. DIN_FB_SOFiSTiK Beispiel
                      $ DIN professional report 102 compare DIN_FB_SOFiSTiK example
CONC 1  C   40      $ = C40/50
STEE 2  BST 500SA TITL 'Stabstahl'        $ 'steel girder'
CONC 4  C   30      $ = C30/37  Ortbeton $ in situ concrete
STEE 7   S 235
STEE 11 PST 1570S REL1 1.7 REL2 1.7 $ vgl. Beispiel  DIN_FB_SOFiSTiK.doc - Relaxation
                                    $ compare example DIN_FB_SOFiSTiK.doc steel Relaxation values (1000h values)

SECT  1  MNO 1 MRF  2
let#zmax 1.05
CS  1  $   ----------------------------- Bauabschnitt 1 : $ Construction stage 1
$ hier nicht BA 0 verwenden: BA 0 ist immer der Gesamtquerschnitt !
$ do not use CS 0 here, CS 0 is always a complete cross section!
POLY  OPZ MNO 1
VERT TOP1 0.000  0.000 exp 0.10 $ BelÃ¼ftung nur Ã¼ber Asphalt $ aeration only over asphalt
    1   1.125  0.000 exp 1.00 $ fÃ¼r alle folgenden QP !    $ for all following QP!
    2   1.125  0.110
    3   0.300  0.150
    4   0.275  #zmax
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO
     'TOP1'   0.00  0.00    1
     'BOT1'   0.00  #zmax   1
$
CS 40  $   ----------------------------- Bauabschnitt 40 : = Gesamtquerschnitt
                                       $ Construction stage 40 : = complete cross section
POLY  OPZ MNO 4
VERT TOP4 0.000 -0.200 exp 0.40 $ BelÃ¼ftung nur bis Asphaltierung $ Aeration only over asphalt
VERT  11  1.125 -0.200 exp 1.00
VERT  12  1.125  0.000 exp 1.00
VERT  13  0.000  0.000 exp 0.20 $ BelÃ¼ftung unten nur als $ Areation down only as
                              $ Kontakt zu FT           $ contact support axis
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO
     'TOP4'   0.00 -0.20    4
     'BOT4'   0.00  0.00    4
CUT 1 ZB 0.21     MNO 1 MRF 2      LAY 0
CUT 2 ZB 0.35     MNO 1 MRF 2      LAY 0
$
$  Torsionsbox:  *---------------------> y
$                |         yo      yo2
$     *----------|----------*--------     #zo
$     |          |<---#yo-->|
$     |          |          |
$     |          |          |
$     |          |<---#yu-->|
$     *----------|----------*             #zu
$                z
let#yo  0.26 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
             $ y-Value of torsionbox upper
let#yu  0.22 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox unten
             $ y-Value of torsionbox lower
let#zo -0.10 $ z-Wert der Torsionsbox oben
             $ Z-Value of torsionbox upper
let#zu #zmax-0.08 $ " der Torsionsbox unten (Schwerpunkt Hauptbew. unten)
                  $ " the torsionbox lower
let#yo2 1.00 $ y-Wert HauptlÃ¤ngsbew. oben  $ Main flexural reinforcement upper

LRF 11  #yo #zo   #yu  #zu AS  7.5 LAY M3 TORS ACTI D  12   $ Durchm.12/15 $ diameter
LRF  1    -   -  -#yu  #zu AS 13.4 LAY M1 TORS ACTI D  16   $ Durchm.16/15 $ diameter
LRF 12    -   -  -#yo  #zo AS  7.5 LAY M3 TORS ACTI D  12
LRF  2    -   -   #yo  #zo AS 13.4 LAY M2 TORS ACTI D  16
LRF  3  #yo2 #zo  #yo  #zo AS 13.4 LAY M2 TORS PASS D  16   $ oben aussen
LRF  4 -#yo2 #zo -#yo  #zo AS 13.4 LAY M2 TORS PASS D  16   $ oben aussen
$ QW  IT  0.23*0.60*0.60*0.60*1.40/2     $ 50  % Torsions-IT
END

+PROG SOFIMSHA URS:15
HEAD Two-span beam with in-situ-concrete deck
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 GDIR ZZ

#define l1=24.50    $ l1
#define l2=24.50    $ l2
#define spalt=0.40  $ Abstand der FT-TrÃ¤ger in der Mitte
                    $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle)
#define xlager=0.30 $ Abstand der Lagerung der FT-TrÃ¤ger im FT-Werk
                    $ Distance of beam by support axis (end) during fabrication
#define xlag_M=0.15 $ Abstand der Lagerung der FT-TrÃ¤ger bei Montage
                    $ Distance of beam by support axis (middle) during fabrication

let#1 $(l1) $ l1
let#2 $(l2) $ l2
NODE NO X  Y=0 Z=0

$ ########################### Attention: #########################################
$ ##############################################################################
$ By the construction stage the components of cross section in AQUAÂ…QNRÂ….BA are
$ to be cautiously proffered if internal forces are interpreted
$
$ The forces of cross section to ASE in CDB refer always to the active
$ partial cross sections in ASE run. That's why they are entered in AQB as REF TEIL (= default in versions 21)
$
$ The load during transfer of load case 20 to load case 40 in this example does not change.
$ The precast girder - corss sections dead load is also activated in constructions stage 20
$ (see CSM-GRUP-Input ORTG = 20).
$ In construction stage 40 only the soft concrete of construction stage 20 will be now hardened !
$
$ Although no deformation and stress changes, the compressed moment in load case 4040
$ in ASE is different as in load case 4020, that it now emphasis of another centre
$ of gravity, namely at the centre of gravity of now hardened ideal complete cross section
$
$ LC 4020 = sum of all moments which relates currently at an active stress
$           (g1+in situ concrete mass+ prestress) of ideal centre of gravity skill = partial
$           cross section 1.1 construction stage 1 of AQUA.
$ LC 4040 = sum of moments which relates of same loads at ideal centre of
$           gravity complete- composite section = AQUA No. 1.2 structure 40:
$
$                    SUMMARY OF CROSS SECTION VALUES OF AUQA
$  No         A[m2]  Iy             zs       gam
$            It[m4]       [m4]     [m]    [kN/m]
$   1    1.2384E+00  1.585E-01   0.231     31.80
$   1.1    BA     1
$        8.2200E-01  8.827E-02   0.399     20.55
$   1.2    BA    40                               d.h. delta-zs = 0.168 m
$        1.2385E+00  1.585E-01   0.231     31.80
$
$ Expression internal forces and moments expression with DBVIEW (= CDB content):
$
$  Forces at girder elements
$  Elem.      X  LC        N       VY       VZ       MT       MY       MZ
$     Nr    [m]  No     [kN]     [kN]     [kN]    [kNm]    [kNm]    [kNm]
$  10005  0.000 4020  -4935.6     0.00     0.00     0.00  -244.20     0.00
$               4040  -4935.6     0.00     0.25     0.00 -1071.70     0.00
$  Control:   delta-MY = N*delta-centriod location = -4935.6*0.168= -829 kNm OK.
$
$ Stored difference load case 6040 in ASE, deliver the moment difference of
$ the construction stage, it will be given with MY=0.0, as in reality the moment does not
$ change but in LC 4040 it's given only at another reference point!
$ DBVIEW's expression
$  Elem.      X  LC        N       VY       VZ       MT       MY       MZ
$     Nr    [m]  No     [kN]     [kN]     [kN]    [kNm]    [kNm]    [kNm]
$  10005  0.000 6040      0.0     0.00     0.26     0.00     0.23     0.00
$
$ Same effects can be observed naturally in the edition of forces of WinGraf!
$
$ Only the difference load case 6000Â…. are processed in AQB and from it generated stress will be imposed,
$ we will try to find the real equivalent stress again (-> RESULTS). By transition from CS 20 to CS 40 the
$ stress does not change,that in construction stage 20 the soft situ concrete is only hardened in construction
$ stage 40, but it has no stress, because till now there isn't any additional deformations occurred.
$
$  Analysisi of section
$  Analysisi of section:  10005  X =       0.000   [m]
$  ------------------------------------------------------------------------
$  CROSS SECTION VALUES
$  QNo               A[m2]     Iy[m4]     Iz[m4]    Iyz[m4]   ys[m]   zs[m]
$    1 Brutto    1.238E+00  1.585E-01  3.072E-01  0.000E+00   0.000   0.231
$      BauAbs 3  8.454E-01  9.445E-02  1.316E-01  0.000E+00   0.000   0.413
$      BauAbs 4  1.262E+00  1.694E-01  3.072E-01  0.000E+00   0.000   0.244

$  3  FL 8015 AQB-Creep FT   322.0   163.11    1.59    -0.36     0.00     0.00
$  4  LF 6040 Solo_Harden OB    0.0     0.23    0.00     0.00     0.00     0.00
$
$  B  CS 20 G1 in-situ-concrete slab  -4613.7  -850.20   -7.66    -4.93     0.00     0.00
$  B  CS 40 Harden OB       -4613.7  -849.97   -7.66    -4.93     0.00     0.00

$ ^ B means here, the stress is applied at different partial cross sections or rather
$ said at different construction stage and the moment -850kNm out of moments of this program
$ therefore the section value is now related at the gross cross section expression:

$ M-Gross = M-CS3 + N*delta-zs = -244.20 -4613.7*(0.399-0.231) + 163.11 =  -855

+PROG SOFIMSHA urs:3
HEAD DIN-FB prestressed bridge - checks with the CSM-Design Module
SYST SPAC GDIV 1000 POSZ
NODE (101 121 1) X (0 21.4/10)
GRP 1
BEAM (101 110 1) (101 1) (102 1) NCS 1 NP -1
GRP 2
BEAM (111 120 1) (111 1) (112 1) NCS 1 NP -1
$
BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec A typm HFAC
BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec A typm SHEA
BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec E typm SHEA
BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec E typm HFAC
$
GRP 9
$ Den folgenden Block kÃ¶nnen Sie ohne Ã„nderung verwenden und nur die
$ darunter stehenden Variablen let#node ... setzen !
$ (Voraussetzung: Knotennummern im Ãœberbau < 1000)
#define support01
  let#dhspring        0 $ m bearing height
    $ bearing springs
    let#sy 0.5*#b0
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 51000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 53000 ; endif
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 52000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 54000 ; endif
    $ node on top of pier: node 49000...
             tran node #node                 dz #h dno 49000
             node #node+51000 FIX KF #node               $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+53000 FIX KF #node      ; endif  $ coupling
             node #node+52000 FIX KF #node+49000         $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+54000 FIX KF #node+49000 ; endif $ coupling
             SPRI #node+0 #node+51000 #node+52000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  $ vertical bearing
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+1 #node+53000 #node+54000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  ; endif
    $ transverse bearing springs:
             SPRI #node+3 #node+51000 #node+52000 dy 1 CP 1E6 $ transverse
    $ longitudinal bearing springs:
    let#cp_long 1.0                       $ weak - to get bearing displacements
    if #logitud ; let#cp_long 1E6 ; endif $ longitudinal fixed bearing
             SPRI #node+7 #node+51000 #node+52000 dx 1 CP #cp_long $ longitudinal
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+8 #node+53000 #node+54000 dx 1 CP #cp_long ; endif $ longitudinal
  $ node bottom of pier: node 50000...
  tran node #node dz #UKpier dno 50000
  BEAM #node 50000+#node 49000+#node NCS 9 KR YY
  node #node+50000 FIX F                 $ fixed support
#enddef
$
let#node         101 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            1.5 $ m cross section height
let#b0           3.5 $ m bearingspread
let#UKpier         7 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         111 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        1 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         121 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
END

$    SUP EXCL - only one out of available load cases
$    SUP CONC - all of the available load cases, if acting unfavourable
           $ Meaning of PSI-Value:
           $
           $ Fraction :(1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki)*GAMU-GAMF
           $
           $ Rare    : 1.00*Q-Leit + PSI0*Qki
           $ frequent: PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki
           $ quasi   : PSI2*Q-Leit + PSI2*Qki  =    PSI2*Q-all
           $ not     : PSI1*Q-Leit + PSI1*Qki
           $
           $ to  : (ING-BAY-Buba-S.15)
           $ See MAXIMA - theoretical basics
$ G if as generic term effects G the under effects
$ G_1 and G_2 combined! alike L the L_U plus L_T combined!
$ not but Z the ZF and ZS, as no underline follows!
$------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END
END

-PROG TEMPLATE urs:59
HEAD Concrete stress in the height of tendons for Deko loadcases 1901-1910

let#nr       183 $ element number
let#xi      0.35 $ location in section : xi=-1 = top of section
                 $                       xi= 0 = center line
                 $                       xi=+1 = bottom of section
let#lc1     1921 $ first loadcase number
let#lc2     1930 $ last  loadcase number

#define printxi
@KEY QUAD 0          $ Quad element info
LET#h  0
LET#h  @(#nr,THICK)  $ read Quad thickness
if #h>0
  let#maxsigxt -999 $ sigma-x
  let#maxsigxb -999 $ sigma-x
  let#maxsigxx -999 $ sigma-x
  let#maxtaux  -999 $ sigma-x
  let#maxsI_x  -999 $ main tensile tress (schiefe Hauptzugspannung) incl. shear

  $   Diese Texte TXE werden im Ergebnisfile gedruckt:
  TXE .
  TXE Element #nr thickness #(h,5.2) m: stresses at level xi= #(xi,5.2)
  TXE [level xi=-1=top , xi=0=center line , xi=+1=bottom]
  TXE ---------------------------------------------------------------
  TXE loadcase  sigxtop  sigxbot  tauxmax  sigx_xi  taux_xi   sIx_xi
  TXE           [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]
  TXE ---------------------------------------------------------------

  let#nlc #lc2-#lc1+1
  loop#1 #nlc            $ loop over loadcases
    let#lc #lc1+#1       $ actual loadcase
    @KEY QUAD_FOR #lc    $ Quadforces of loadcase #lc
    LET#mxx  @(#nr,mxx)  $ Quad Nr #nr , mxx
    LET#myy  @(#nr,myy)
    LET#mxy  @(#nr,mxy)
    LET#vx   @(#nr,vx)
    LET#vy   @(#nr,vy)
    LET#nx   @(#nr,nx)
    LET#ny   @(#nr,ny)
    LET#nxy  @(#nr,nxy)

    let#i 1.*#h*#h*#h/12     $ b*h^3 / 12
    let#zt  -1*#h/2
    let#zb  +1*#h/2
    let#zx #xi*#h/2
    let#sigxt (#nx/#h+#mxx/#i*#zt)/1000  $ N/A + M/w
    let#sigxb (#nx/#h+#mxx/#i*#zb)/1000  $ N/A + M/w
    let#sigxx (#nx/#h+#mxx/#i*#zx)/1000  $ N/A + M/w
    let#tauxmax 1.5*#vx/#h/1000   $ 1.5*V/h
    let#taux #tauxmax*(1-#xi*#xi) $ tau an der Stelle xi (quadratisch)
    let#sI_x 0.5*#sigxx+SQR(0.5*#sigxx*0.5*#sigxx+#taux*#taux) ! Hauptzugspannung
    TXE     #lc #(sigxt,8.3) #(sigxb,8.3) #(tauxmax,8.3) #(sigxx,8.3) #(taux,8.3) #(sI_x,8.3)
  $                                    ^Wert ^Format: 8 Stellen
  $                                               mit 2 Nachkommastellen
    if #sigxt>#maxsigxt  ; let#maxsigxt #sigxt  ; endif
    if #sigxb>#maxsigxb  ; let#maxsigxb #sigxb  ; endif
    if #tauxmax>#maxtaux ; let#maxtaux #tauxmax ; endif
    if #sigxx>#maxsigxx  ; let#maxsigxx #sigxx  ; endif
    if #sI_x>#maxsI_x    ; let#maxsI_x #sI_x    ; endif
  endloop
  TXE ---------------------------------------------------------------
    TXE Maximum  #(maxsigxt,8.3) #(maxsigxb,8.3) #(maxtaux,8.3) #(maxsigxx,8.3)          #(sI_x,8.3)
  TXE           [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]  [N/mm2]
  TXE ---------------------------------------------------------------
  TXE sigx    = nx/A + mxx/w     [nx,mxx = forces in element center -> DBVIEW]
  TXE tauxmax = 1.5*vx/h         [vx     = shearforce]
  TXE sigx_xi, taux_xi            values at level xi
  TXE sIx_xi                      main tensile stress:
  TXE    if sigx_xi is unter compression, the first main tensile stress
  TXE    will turn transverse to the section and get nearly 0.0
  TXE    which is the stress transverse to the slab!!
  TXE ---------------------------------------------------------------
endif
#enddef
#include printxi

let#nr        185 $ element number
let#xi      0.55 $ location in section : xi=-1 = top of section
#include printxi

let#nr        187 $ element number
let#xi      0.75 $ location in section : xi=-1 = top of section
#include printxi


END
END

$ der _csm Datei und der _desi Datei ansehen!                     $ _csm Datei und der _desi resulf file!



$ Tendon stress increase in ULS design:
$ For bonded tendons now the stress increase in the tendons is taken into account in the
$ ULS design. For this the tendons are smeared over a certain width.
$ The stress increase is limited by the strain in the height of the tendons and
$ by the material parameters. It leads to a reduction of normal reinforcement:
$
$ as_reduk= redukstress*redukhebelarm*as_z          mit:
$                      max_potential_Prestressing steel_raise stress
$    - redukstress   = -----------------------------------------   but not bigger as 1.0
$                      fy_Slack steel
$    - redukleverarm = Lever arm_Tendon/lever arm_Slack steel
$    - as-z          = capable blurred prestressing steel cross section
$                         at this point in cm2/m
$ With CTRL SIGZ it can be limited e.g. CTRL SIGZ 180 to 180 N/mm2.
$ The tendon stress increase results in a lower longitudinal reinforcement which
$ can be checked in tke listing.
$ With  CTRL SIGZ 0 in BEMESS the feature can be switched off totally.

$ Usage of SIR please see  csm4_quad_singlespan.dat

$ Comfortable is also the variant slab bridge in the SSD-bridge wizzard !

LC 5028
$ For C+S SIR SIR automatically adds the statically determined concrete
$ part so that the output gives the desired C+S loss in the concrete
$ comp.ASE.HTM Version 12.42

END
Explanation to SIR-results by QUAD-Tendons:
(to simplify matters at statically determinate single span girder):

In principle at statically determined single span girder, the sum of the internal
forces and moments of all elements at all of the load cases P and C
is in average 0.0
Basic: Prestress and Creep+Shrinkage are here inherent stress conditions
       (without redistributed moment ).
       The concrete has a compressive force in load case P and the tendon
       an identical magnitude tension .
       The concrete stress sinks due to C+S in load case C, also
       in identical mass sinks the prestressing steel stress too.
       The sum of concrete proportion + prestressing steel is zero (inherent stress condition).

Only the concrete proportion is required for the AQB- design
(respectively for a SIR-check)by the prestress and creep + shrinkage.
(rather total internal forces and moments plus statically determined proportion of concrete).

For the load case prestress P is this in SIR with LC BAMI to be specified.

Following methods are for the load case creep + shrinkage C by CSM applications
implemented:

       ASE can compute the difference load cases out of the sum load cases (STEU DIFF ...).
       An additional information will be saved in ASE, in these difference load cases C+S by the
       creep and shrinkage analyses. Therewith the SIR can add once again the statically determined
       proportion of concrete of C+S (=Loss of concrete stress).

       Thus the SIR-results of the difference load cases are not consistent with the
       simple difference of output - (Sums-) load cases !

Example:
The construction stage C+S will be saved in stage of construction 15 (BA 15) in load case 4015
(LC 4015)(= load case of sums according to C+S).
Due to control LC DIFF 1000 in ASE, a difference load case will be automatically generated 5015
(LC 5015) (= difference load case C+S).  This load case contains the additional information,
that it is a C+S and in SIR the
statically determined proportion C+S should be added once again.

Following SIR-Results are generated:

 SECTION COMPONENT  SECTION     2 XS =    0.000
   LC  Typ     No     N[kN]   Vy[kN]   Vz[kN]  Mt[kNm]   My[kNm]   Mz[kNm]  Mb[kNm2]
 4010 SUM               0.0     0.00     0.00     0.00   1232.04      0.00     0.00
 4011 SUM               0.0     0.00    -0.07     0.00   1255.15      0.00     0.00
 4015 SUM               0.0     0.00    -0.07     0.00   1263.14      0.00     0.00
 4020 SUM               0.0     0.00    -0.07     0.00   1462.70      0.00     0.00

 5010 SUM               0.0     0.00     0.00     0.00   1232.04      0.00     0.00
 5011 SUM           -4738.8     0.00     0.00     0.00  -4170.33      0.00     0.00
 5015 SUM             239.7     0.00     0.00     0.00    220.10      0.00     0.00
 5020 SUM               0.0     0.00     0.00     0.00    199.55      0.00     0.00

Please consider that the sums load cases 4000.. without BAMI have manipulation all
N=0.0 kN = none external normal force !

Contrary to it in LC 5011 the statically determined proportion of prestress contains N=-4738.8 kN
and in LC 5015 the loss of prestress in concrete proportion  delta-N= +239.7 kN

Therefore in SIR only the difference load cases
(LC 5000*) should be analysed for a better overview!
</text>

!#!Info  Example:       Prestressing of a rotational shell
!#!Info  Keyword:       prestress; tendon
!#!Info  Program:       TENDON
!#!Info  Version:       SOFiSTiK 27
!#!Info  Date:          26.04.2011

+prog aqua urs:1
head material & sections
norm DIN 'fb102-2009'
conc 1  C 40
stee 11 BST 500SA
stee 12 S 235
stee 21 PST 1570S $ rel1 1.7 rel2 1.7
srec 1 h 2.0 b 1.0
end

+prog sofimshc urs:2
head system generation
syst SPAC gdiv 1000
ctrl mesh 1 ; ctrl hmin 2.0
echo FULL 0

spt 1 x 0  0 0
spt 2 x 10 1.0102 0
spt 3 x 20 0 0

sln 1 npa 1 2 sno 1 ; slnb r 50 nz -1
sln 2 npa 2 3 sno 1 ; slnb r 50 nz -1
end

+prog tendon urs:16.1
head prestressing
echo full yes

$ Definition of prestressing system
SYSP NOPS 12 MAT 21 ZV 2268 AZ 1680 LITZ 12 MINR 6.10 BETA 0.30 MUE 0.2 ECC 11.7 SP 6 DO 82

$ Reference-axis defined along two structural lines
axes noh 1 type SLN val1 1,2

$ Tendon geometry
tgeo nog 1 noh 1 nops 12
 ptuv REFX s  0.0 v -0.3
 ptuv REFX s  5.0 v +0.3
 ptuv REFX s 10.0 v -0.3
 ptuv REFX s 15.0 v +0.3
 ptuv REFX s 20.0 v -0.3

psig kind LE TS
tend 1 nog 1 nten 1 lc 3 type SPAN

PLOT GEOE NO 0 FACH 5  TYPG DUTE DIA 100
PLOT GEOP NO 0 FACH 5  TYPG DUTE DIA 100
PLOT FACT NO 0 FACH 50 TYPG DUTE DIA 100

$ output of tendon geometry to external textfile
geox 1 from  0 to  8 inc 0.50 outp 'SUV' fach 10.0 expo TXT
geox 1 from  8 to 12 inc 0.25 outp 'SUV' fach 10.0 expo TXT
geox 1 from 12 to 20 inc 0.50 outp 'SUV' fach 10.0 expo TXT

$ output of tendon geometry to geometry axis in cdb
geox 1 inc 0.75 outp 'SV' fach 10.0 expo GAX 'TND1'

end


-prog template urs:3
head import text output in result-viewer
<text>
#include $(PROJECT)_GEO_1.uv
</text>
end

$ display of axis information in result viewer
+prog sofimshc urs:4
head print axis
echo GEOM EXTR
end

+prog sofimshc urs:3
HEAD Definition Tendon Axes
SYST REST

$ reference axes for horizontal tendons
$ pairwise rotated by 90Â°
GAX H0 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0  -4.99 X1  5.83          Z1  -4.99 NZ 1 S2 360.0
GAX H1 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0  -7.06          Y1  7.60 Z1  -7.06 NZ 1 S2 360.0
GAX H2 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0  -9.72 X1  9.52          Z1  -9.72 NZ 1 S2 360.0
GAX H3 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0 -11.87          Y1 10.44 Z1 -11.87 NZ 1 S2 360.0
GAX H4 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0 -15.89 X1 11.08          Z1 -15.89 NZ 1 S2 360.0
GAX H5 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0 -19.91          Y1 10.44 Z1 -19.91 NZ 1 S2 360.0
GAX H6 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0 -23.63 X1  8.51          Z1 -23.63 NZ 1 S2 360.0
GAX H7 TYPE TEND TYPC ARC ; GAXB XM 0 0 -26.50          Y1  5.83 Z1 -26.50 NZ 1 S2 360.0

$ reference axis for vertical tendons
loop#i 16
 let#alph #i*360/16
 GAX V#i TYPE TEND TYPC SPLI
  GAXC X  5.83*cos(#alph) Y  5.83*sin(#alph) Z  -4.99
  GAXC X  7.60*cos(#alph) Y  7.60*sin(#alph) Z  -7.06
  GAXC X  9.52*cos(#alph) Y  9.52*sin(#alph) Z  -9.72
  GAXC X 10.44*cos(#alph) Y 10.44*sin(#alph) Z -11.87
  GAXC X 11.08*cos(#alph) Y 11.08*sin(#alph) Z -15.89
  GAXC X 10.44*cos(#alph) Y 10.44*sin(#alph) Z -19.91
  GAXC X  8.51*cos(#alph) Y  8.51*sin(#alph) Z -23.63
  GAXC X  5.83*cos(#alph) Y  5.83*sin(#alph) Z -26.50
endloop

END


+prog tendon urs:4
HEAD Prestressing
CTRL WARN 600,601

SYSP NOPS 1 MAT 3 ZV 136 AZ 140 LITZ 1 MINR 4.80 BETA 0.50 MUE 0.15 ECC 0.0 SP 4 DO 26
SYSP NOPS 2 MAT 3 ZV 273 AZ 280 LITZ 2 MINR 4.80 BETA 0.40 MUE 0.20 ECC 0.0 SP 5 DO 45

$ geometry of horizontal tendons
loop#i 8
 AXES #i+1  TYPE REFX H#i KIND QUAD
 TGEO #i+1  NOH #i+1  NOPS 1
 PTUV REFX U -0.065 V 0
endloop

$ geometry of vertical tendons
loop#i 16
 AXES #i+11 TYPE REFX V#i KIND QUAD
 TGEO #i+11 NOH #i+11 NOPS 2
 PTUV REFX U 0 V 0
endloop

CS ICS1 11 12 0

$ horizontal tendons
PSIG RILE ANWS 9 KAPA 1.5 $ kapl Ja
$ vfak RELI anws 'AS' fak 1.130 faka 0.729 faks 0.629
loop#i 8
 TEND 101+#i NOG #i+1 NTEN 1 TYPE REFX FROM   0.0 TO 180.0
 TEND 111+#i NOG #i+1 NTEN 1 TYPE REFX FROM 180.0 TO 360.0
endloop

$ vertical tendons
$ vfak LI anws 'AS' fak 1.050 faka 1.180 faks 1.050 fake 1.000 fakf 1.000
loop#i 16
 TEND 201+#i NOG #i+11 NTEN 1 TYPE REFX LC 11
endloop

PLOT FACT 0 TYPG TEND FACH 10.0

END

$     |          |          |
$     |          |<---#yu-->|

let#yu  0.85 $ y-Wert der Torsionsbox unten $ y-value of Torsionsbox below

let#zu #zmax-0.06 $ " der Torsionsbox unten $ "       of Torsionsbox below

LRF  2   -   -  -#yu  #zu AS 0.1 LAY 0 TORS ACTI D  12

                                     $ By  x=3.80 m of the support above the tendon
CUT 2 ZB 0.70     MNO 1        LAY 1 $ Bei x=3.80 m von der StÃ¼tze unterhalb Spannglied
                                     $ By  x=3.80 m of the support underneath the tendon
CUT 3 YB 1.30     MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN  $ belt
CUT 4 YB 1.70     MNO 1        LAY 3 TYPE FLAN  $ belt
SPT    NO     Y      Z     MNO
     'BOT'   0.00  #zmax   1 $ Literal BOT muss in Grossbuchstaben
     'TOP'   0.00  0.00    1 $ eingegeben werden
                             $ input literal BOT in kapitel letters

BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec A typm HFAC
BSEC NO 1101,2111 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec A typm SHEA
BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 1.10 ncs 1 spec E typm SHEA
BSEC NO 1110,2120 X 0.30 ncs 1 spec E typm HFAC
$
GRP 9
$ Den folgenden Block kÃ¶nnen Sie ohne Ã„nderung verwenden und nur die
$ darunter stehenden Variablen let#node ... setzen !
$ (Voraussetzung: Knotennummern im Ãœberbau < 1000)
#define support01
  let#dhspring        0 $ m bearing height
    $ bearing springs
    let#sy 0.5*#b0
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 51000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 53000 ; endif
             TRAN node #node dy  #sy dz #h dno 52000
    if #b0 ; tran node #node dy -#sy dz #h dno 54000 ; endif
    $ node on top of pier: node 49000...
             tran node #node                 dz #h dno 49000
             node #node+51000 FIX KF #node               $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+53000 FIX KF #node      ; endif  $ coupling
             node #node+52000 FIX KF #node+49000         $ coupling
    if #b0 ; node #node+54000 FIX KF #node+49000 ; endif $ coupling
             SPRI #node+0 #node+51000 #node+52000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  $ vertical bearing
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+1 #node+53000 #node+54000 DZ 1 CP 1E7  ; endif
    $ transverse bearing springs:
             SPRI #node+3 #node+51000 #node+52000 dy 1 CP 1E6 $ transverse
    $ longitudinal bearing springs:
    let#cp_long 1.0                       $ weak - to get bearing displacements
    if #logitud ; let#cp_long 1E6 ; endif $ longitudinal fixed bearing
             SPRI #node+7 #node+51000 #node+52000 dx 1 CP #cp_long $ longitudinal
    if #b0 ; SPRI #node+8 #node+53000 #node+54000 dx 1 CP #cp_long ; endif $ longitudinal
  $ node bottom of pier: node 50000...
  tran node #node dz #UKpier dno 50000
  BEAM #node 50000+#node 49000+#node NCS 9 KR YY
  node #node+50000 FIX F                 $ fixed support
#enddef
$
let#node         101 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#h            1.5 $ m cross section height
let#b0           3.5 $ m bearingspread
let#UKpier         7 $ m bottom level pier
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         111 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        1 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
let#node         121 $ basenumber of node in superstructure
let#logitud        0 $ =1 bearing fixed in longitud. direction
#include support01
$
END
